chapter: Chapter on Zakat of Cattle
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd and al-Fudayl from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding cattle ,in every thirty cows, a yearling calf (tabi hawli) is due, and there is nothing due on fewer than that. In forty cows, an older cow (musinnah) is due, and there is nothing due between thirty and forty until it reaches forty. Then, when it reaches forty, an older cow (musinnah) is due on it. There is nothing due between forty and sixty cattle. Then, when it reaches sixty cattle, two yearling calves (tabian) are due, up to seventy. Then, when it reaches seventy, a yearling calf (tabi) and an older cow (musinnah) are due, up to eighty. Then, when it reaches eighty cattle, then for every forty, an older cow (musinnah) is due. Then, when it reaches ninety cattle, three yearling calves (hawliyyat) are due. Then, when it reaches one hundred and twenty cattle, then for every forty, an older cow (musinnah) is due. Then the cattle return according to their age categories. There is nothing due on the excess amount (al-nayyif), nothing due on fractions, and nothing due on working animals (al-awamil). Charity is only due on grazing, pasturing animals. And as for anything over which a full year has not passed while it is with its owner, there is nothing due on it until a full year passes over it. Then, when a full year passes over it, zakat becomes obligatory on it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ بُرَيْدٍ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ:» فِي اَلْبَقَرِ فِي كُلِّ ثَلاَثِينَ بَقَرَةً تَبِيعٌ حَوْلِيٌّ وَ لَيْسَ فِي أَقَلَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ وَ فِي أَرْبَعِينَ بَقَرَةً بَقَرَةٌ مُسِنَّةٌ وَ لَيْسَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ اَلثَّلاَثِينَ إِلَى اَلْأَرْبَعِينَ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ أَرْبَعِينَ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ أَرْبَعِينَ فَفِيهَا مُسِنَّةٌ وَ لَيْسَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ اَلْأَرْبَعِينَ إِلَى اَلسِّتِّينَ شَيْءٌ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتِ اَلسِّتِّينَ فَفِيهَا تَبِيعَانِ إِلَى سَبْعِينَ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتِ اَلسَّبْعِينَ فَفِيهَا تَبِيعٌ وَمُسِنَّةٌ إِلَى اَلثَّمَانِينَ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ ثَمَانِينَ فَفِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ مُسِنَّةٌ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ تِسْعِينَ فَفِيهَا ثَلاَثُ حَوْلِيَّاتٍ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ عِشْرِينَ وَ مِائَةً فَفِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ مُسِنَّةٌ ثُمَّ تَرْجِعُ اَلْبَقَرُ عَلَى أَسْنَانِهَا وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلنَّيِّفِ شَيْءٌ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْكُسُورِ شَيْءٌ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْعَوَامِلِ شَيْ ءٌإِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقَةُ عَلَى اَلسَّائِمَةِ اَلرَّاعِيَةِ وَ كُلُّ مَا لَمْ يَحُلْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَإِذَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَجَبَتْ فِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Burayd and al-Fudayl from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:

Then, when it reaches ninety cattle, three yearling calves (hawliyyat) are due. Then, when it reaches one hundred and twenty cattle, then for every forty, an older cow (musinnah) is due. Then the cattle return according to their age categories. There is nothing due on the excess amount (al-nayyif), nothing due on fractions, and nothing due on working animals (al-awamil). Charity is only due on grazing, pasturing animals. And as for anything over which a full year has not passed while it is with its owner, there is nothing due on it until a full year passes over it. chapter: Chapter on Zakat of Sheep or Goats
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir and Burayd al-Ijli and al-Fudayl from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding sheep, in every forty sheep, one sheep is due, and there is nothing due on fewer than forty. Then nothing further is due on them until they reach one hundred and twenty (sheep). When they reach 120 (sheep), the same ruling applies: one sheep is due. Then, if they increase beyond one hundred and twenty (sheep), two sheep are due on them, and nothing more than two sheep is due until they reach two hundred. Then, when they reach two hundred (sheep), the same ruling applies. Then, if they increase beyond two hundred (sheep) by one sheep, three sheep are due on them. Then nothing more than that is due until they reach three hundred (sheep). When they reach three hundred (sheep), the same ruling applies: three sheep are due. Then, if they increase by one, four sheep are due on them, until they reach 400 (sheep). Then, when four hundred (sheep) is complete, for every one hundred sheep, one sheep is due, and the previous calculation is dropped. Nothing is due on anything less than one hundred (sheep) after that, and nothing is due on the excess amount (al-nayyif).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ بُرَيْدٍ اَلْعِجْلِيِّ وَاَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:» فِي اَلشَّاةِ فِي كُلِّ أَرْبَعِينَ شَاةً شَاةٌ وَلَيْسَ فِيمَا دُونَ اَلْأَرْبَعِينَ شَيْءٌ ثُمَّ لَيْسَ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ عِشْرِينَ وَ مِائَةً فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ عِشْرِينَ وَ مِائَةً فَفِيهَا مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ شَاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ فَفِيهَا شَاتَانِ وَلَيْسَ فِيهَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ شَاتَيْنِ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ مِائَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتِ اَلْمِائَتَيْنِ فَفِيهَا مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ عَلَى اَلْمِائَتَيْنِ شَاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَفِيهَا ثَلاَثُ شِيَاهٍ ثُمَّ لَيْسَ فِيهَا شَيْ ءٌأَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ ثَلاَثَمِائَةٍ فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ ثَلاَثَمِائَةٍ فَفِيهَا مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ ثَلاَثُ شِيَاهٍ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ فَفِيهَا أَرْبَعُ شِيَاهٍ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ أَرْبَعَمِائَةٍ فَإِذَا تَمَّتْ أَرْبَعُمِائَةٍ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ مِائَةٍ شَاةٌ وَ سَقَطَ اَلْأَمْرُ اَلْأَوَّلُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَا دُونَ اَلْمِائَةِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ وَ لَيْسَ فِي اَلنَّيِّفِ شَيْءٌ« وَ قَالاَ» كُلُّ مَا لاَ يَحُولُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ فَإِذَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir and Burayd al-Ijli and al-Fudayl from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding sheep, in every forty sheep, one sheep is due, and there is nothing due on fewer than forty. Then nothing further is due on them until they reach one hundred and twenty (sheep). When they reach 120 (sheep), the same ruling applies: one sheep is due. Then, if they increase beyond one hundred and twenty (sheep), two sheep are due on them, and nothing more than two sheep is due until they reach two hundred. Then, when they reach two hundred (sheep), the same ruling applies. Then, if they increase beyond two hundred (sheep) by one sheep, three sheep are due on them. Then nothing more than that is due until they reach three hundred (sheep). When they reach three hundred (sheep), the same ruling applies: three sheep are due. Then, if they increase by one, four sheep are due on them, until they reach 400 (sheep). Then, when four hundred (sheep) is complete, for every one hundred sheep, one sheep is due, and the previous calculation is dropped. Nothing is due on anything less than one hundred (sheep) after that, and nothing is due on the excess amount (al-nayyif).”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of Sheep or Goats
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd, and al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing due on fewer than forty sheep. When they reach forty, one sheep is due on them, up to one hundred and twenty. Then, if they increase by one, two sheep are due on them, up to two hundred. Then, if they increase by one, three sheep are due on them, up to three hundred. Then, when the sheep become numerous, for every one hundred sheep, one sheep is due. An old animal is not to be taken, nor one with a defect, unless the collector of charity wishes. What is gathered together is not to be separated, and what is separated is not to be gathered together. Its young and its old are counted.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ فِيمَا دُونَ اَلْأَرْبَعِينَ مِنَ اَلْغَنَمِ شَيْءٌ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ أَرْبَعِينَ فَفِيهَا شَاةٌ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَ مِائَةٍ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ فَفِيهَا شَاتَانِ إِلَى اَلْمِائَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ فَفِيهَا ثَلاَثٌ مِنَ اَلْغَنَمِ إِلَى ثَلاَثِمِائَةٍ فَإِذَا كَثُرَتِ اَلْغَنَمُ فَفِي كُلِّ مِائَةٍ شَاةٌ وَ لاَ تُؤْخَذُ هَرِمَةٌ وَ لاَ ذَاتُ عَوَارٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَشَاءَ اَلْمُصَدِّقُ وَ لاَ يُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ وَ لاَ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ مُتَفَرِّقٍ وَ يَعُدُّ صَغِيرَهَا وَكَبِيرَهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd, and al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

Then, when the sheep become numerous, for every one hundred sheep, one sheep is due. An old animal is not to be taken, nor one with a defect, unless the collector of charity wishes. chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “Is there zakat upon the wealth of the orphan?” Imam (a.s) said: “If it is set aside, then there is no zakat upon it. But if you trade with it, then you are liable, and the profit belongs to the orphan.”

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “Is there zakat upon the wealth of the orphan?” Imam (a.s) said: “If it is set aside, then there is no zakat upon it. But if you trade with it, then you are liable, and the profit belongs to the orphan.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the wealth of the orphan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ فَقَالَ» لَيْسَ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the wealth of the orphan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 35

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ فِي مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) used to differ from the people regarding the wealth of the orphan: ‘there is no zakat upon it.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَحْمَدَ اِبْنَيِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ أَبِي يُخَالِفُ اَلنَّاسَ فِي مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) used to differ from the people regarding the wealth of the orphan: ‘there is no zakat upon it.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Abi Shubah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘the wealth of the orphan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon it unless it is traded with.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي شُعْبَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ فَقَالَ» لاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُعْمَلَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Abi Shubah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘the wealth of the orphan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon it unless it is traded with.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Said al-Samman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan unless it is traded with. If it is traded with, then the profit belongs to the orphan, and if there is a loss, then it is upon the one who trades with it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلسَّمَّانِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» لَيْسَ فِي مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ زَكَاةٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُتَّجَرَ بِهِ فَإِنِ اُتُّجِرَ بِهِ فَالرِّبْحُ لِلْيَتِيمِ وَ إِنْ وُضِعَ فَعَلَى اَلَّذِي يَتَّجِرُ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Said al-Samman, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan unless it is traded with. If it is traded with, then the profit belongs to the orphan, and if there is a loss, then it is upon the one who trades with it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:
I sent to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, a letter saying: “I have young brothers, so when does zakat become obligatory upon their wealth?” Imam (a.s) said: “When prayer becomes obligatory upon them, zakat becomes obligatory upon them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then as long as prayer has not become obligatory upon them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If it is traded with, then pay zakat on it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ لِي إِخْوَةً صِغَاراً فَمَتَى تَجِبُ عَلَى أَمْوَالِهِمُ اَلزَّكَاةُ قَالَ» إِذَا وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلزَّكَاةُ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَا لَمْ تَجِبْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلصَّلاَةُ قَالَ» إِذَا اُتُّجِرَ بِهِ فَزَكُّوهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I sent to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, a letter saying: “I have young brothers, so when does zakat become obligatory upon their wealth?” Imam (a.s) said: “When prayer becomes obligatory upon them, zakat becomes obligatory upon them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then as long as prayer has not become obligatory upon them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If it is traded with, then pay zakat on it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 36

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), about ‘young children who have wealth in the hand of their father or their brother, Is zakat obligatory upon their wealth?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is not obligatory in their wealth until it is traded with. So when it is traded with, zakat becomes obligatory. As for when it is held inactive, then there is no zakat upon it.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صِبْيَةٍ صِغَارٍ لَهُمْ مَالٌ بِيَدِ أَبِيهِمْ أَوْ أَخِيهِمْ هَلْ تَجِبُ عَلَى مَالِهِمْ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ تَجِبُ فِي مَالِهِمْ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يُعْمَلَ بِهِ فَإِذَا عُمِلَ بِهِ وَجَبَتِ اَلزَّكَاةُ فَأَمَّا إِذَا كَانَ مَوْقُوفاً فَلاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), about ‘young children who have wealth in the hand of their father or their brother, Is zakat obligatory upon their wealth?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is not obligatory in their wealth until it is traded with. So when it is traded with, zakat becomes obligatory. As for when it is held inactive, then there is no zakat upon it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 37

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Utarid al-Hannat, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘wealth of the orphan is with me, and I trade with it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If you move it, then its zakat is upon you.” I (narrator) asked: “I move it for eight months and leave it for four months.” Imam (a.s) said: “Its zakat is upon you.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعُطَارِدِ اَلْحَنَّاطِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع مَالُ اَلْيَتِيمِ يَكُونُ عِنْدِي فَأَتَّجِرُ بِهِ فَقَالَ» إِذَا حَرَّكْتَهُ فَعَلَيْكَ زَكَاتُهُ« قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي أُحَرِّكُهُ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَأَدَعُهُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ قَالَ» عَلَيْكَ زَكَاتُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Utarid al-Hannat, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘wealth of the orphan is with me, and I trade with it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If you move it, then its zakat is upon you.” I (narrator) asked: “I move it for eight months and leave it for four months.” Imam (a.s) said: “Its zakat is upon you.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 37

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Samaah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A man has the wealth of an orphan with him and trades with it. Is he liable for it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Then is there zakat upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, by my life, I do not combine two qualities upon him: liability and zakat.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ مَالُ اَلْيَتِيمِ وَ يَتَّجِرُ بِهِ أَيَضْمَنُهُ قَالَ »نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ فَعَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» لاَ لَعَمْرِي لاَ أَجْمَعُ عَلَيْهِ خَصْلَتَيْنِ اَلضَّمَانَ وَ اَلزَّكَاةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Samaah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A man has the wealth of an orphan with him and trades with it. Is he liable for it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Then is there zakat upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, by my life, I do not combine two qualities upon him: liability and zakat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 37

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali Mahbub, from Ahmad, from al-Hasan Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a man in whose hand there is wealth belonging to a brother of his who is an orphan, and he is his executor. Is it proper for him to work with it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may work with it as he works with the wealth of someone else, and the profit is between them both.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is there any liability upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, if he is acting with consideration for him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ جَرِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلرَّبِيعِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي يَدِهِ مَالٌ لِأَخٍ لَهُ يَتِيمٍ وَ هُوَ وَصِيُّهُ أَ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ بِهِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ يَعْمَلُ بِهِ كَمَا يَعْمَلُ بِمَالِ غَيْرِهِ وَ اَلرِّبْحُ بَيْنَهُمَا« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَهَلْ عَلَيْهِ ضَمَانٌ قَالَ» لاَ إِذَا كَانَ نَاظِراً لَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali Mahbub, from Ahmad, from al-Hasan Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a man in whose hand there is wealth belonging to a brother of his who is an orphan, and he is his executor. Is it proper for him to work with it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may work with it as he works with the wealth of someone else, and the profit is between them both.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is there any liability upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, if he is acting with consideration for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 38

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur al-Sayqal:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘the wealth of the orphan being worked with.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If you have wealth and you guarantee it, then the profit is yours, and you are liable for the wealth. But if you have no wealth and you work with it, then the profit belongs to the boy, and you are liable for the wealth.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ يُعْمَلُ بِهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ» إِذَا كَانَ عِنْدَكَ مَالٌ وَضَمِنْتَهُ فَلَكَ اَلرِّبْحُ وَ أَنْتَ ضَامِنٌ لِلْمَالِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لاَ مَالَ لَكَ وَ عَمِلْتَ بِهِ فَالرِّبْحُ لِلْغُلاَمِ وَ أَنْتَ ضَامِنٌ لِلْمَالِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur al-Sayqal:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘the wealth of the orphan being worked with.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If you have wealth and you guarantee it, then the profit is yours, and you are liable for the wealth. But if you have no wealth and you work with it, then the profit belongs to the boy, and you are liable for the wealth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 39

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The wealth of the orphan has nothing upon it in specie and silent wealth (al-samit). As for the yields, then charity upon them is obligatory.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ:» مَالُ اَلْيَتِيمِ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِي اَلْعَيْنِ وَ اَلصَّامِتِ شَيْءٌ فَأَمَّا اَلْغَلاَّتُ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهَا اَلصَّدَقَةَ وَاجِبَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The wealth of the orphan has nothing upon it in specie and silent wealth (al-samit). As for the yields, then charity upon them is obligatory.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan, and there is no prayer upon him, and there is no zakat upon all of his yields from date-palms, or crops, or produce. And if he (the orphan) reaches maturity, then there is no zakat upon him for what has passed, nor is there upon him for what is to come until he reaches maturity. So when he (the orphan) reaches maturity, one zakat becomes due upon him, and there is upon him the same as what is upon other people.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:» لَيْسَ فِي مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ زَكَاةٌ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةٌ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ غَلاَّتِهِ مِنْ نَخْلٍ أَوْ زَرْعٍ أَوْ غَلَّةٍ زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ بَلَغَ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَا مَضَى زَكَاةٌ وَ لاَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَا يَسْتَقْبِلُ حَتَّى يُدْرِكَ فَإِذَا أَدْرَكَ كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِثْلُ مَا عَلَى غَيْرِهِ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “There is no zakat in the wealth of the orphan, and there is no prayer upon him, and there is no zakat upon all of his yields from date-palms, or crops, or produce. And if he (the orphan) reaches maturity, then there is no zakat upon him for what has passed, nor is there upon him for what is to come until he reaches maturity. So when he (the orphan) reaches maturity, one zakat becomes due upon him, and there is upon him the same as what is upon other people.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl al-Basri:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), asking him about ‘the executor (of orphans wealth), Does he pay zakat al-fitrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?’ Imam (a.s) wrote: “There is no zakat upon the wealth of the orphan.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ اَلْبَصْرِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْوَصِيِّ يُزَكِّي زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ عَنِ اَلْيَتَامَى إِذَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مَالٌ فَكَتَبَ» لاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَى مَالِ اَلْيَتِيمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl al-Basri:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), asking him about ‘the executor (of orphans wealth), Does he pay zakat al-fitrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?’ Imam (a.s) wrote: “There is no zakat upon the wealth of the orphan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A woman from among our people is mentally confused (mukhtalitah), ‘Is there zakat upon her?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If it has been traded with, then zakat is upon her, and if it has not been traded with, then no.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اِمْرَأَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِنَا مُخْتَلِطَةٌ عَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ »إِ نْ كَانَ عُمِلَ بِهِ فَعَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُعْمَلْ بِهِ فَلاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A woman from among our people is mentally confused (mukhtalitah), ‘Is there zakat upon her?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If it has been traded with, then zakat is upon her, and if it has not been traded with, then no.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of Children and the Insane
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘an afflicted woman (musabah) who has wealth in the hand of her brother, Is there zakat upon it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If her brother trades with it, then zakat is upon it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اِمْرَأَةٍ مُصَابَةٍ وَ لَهَا مَالٌ فِي يَدِ أَخِيهَا فَهَلْ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ أَخُوهَا يَتَّجِرُ بِهِ فَعَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘an afflicted woman (musabah) who has wealth in the hand of her brother, Is there zakat upon it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If her brother trades with it, then zakat is upon it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 40

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers, from their father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam (a.s) said regarding ‘a man whose wealth is absent from him and he is not able to take possession of it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then there is no zakat upon him until it comes out. So when it comes out, he pays zakat on it for one year. But if he leaves it deliberately while he is able to take possession of it, then zakat is upon him for every one of the years that has passed over it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَخَوَيْهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْجَهْمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ مَالُهُ عَنْهُ غَائِبٌ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَخْذِهِ قَالَ» فَلاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ فَإِذَا خَرَجَ زَكَّاهُ لِعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ وَ إِنْ كَانَ يَدَعُهُ مُتَعَمِّداً وَ هُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَخْذِهِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ لِكُلِّ مَا مَرَّ بِهِ مِنَ اَلسِّنِينَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers, from their father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said regarding ‘a man whose wealth is absent from him and he is not able to take possession of it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then there is no zakat upon him until it comes out. So when it comes out, he pays zakat on it for one year. But if he leaves it deliberately while he is able to take possession of it, then zakat is upon him for every one of the years that has passed over it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 41

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no charity upon a debt, nor upon wealth that is absent from you, until it falls into your hands.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ صَدَقَةَ عَلَى اَلدَّيْنِ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْمَالِ اَلْغَائِبِ عَنْكَ حَتَّى يَقَعَ فِي يَدَيْكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no charity upon a debt, nor upon wealth that is absent from you, until it falls into your hands.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 41

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man whose wealth is absent from him for five years, then it comes to him, and the principal of the wealth is not returned to him. How much does he pay zakat on it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “For one year.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَغِيبُ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ خَمْسَ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يَأْتِيهِ وَ لاَ يُرَدُّ عَلَيْهِ رَأْسُ اَلْمَالِ كَمْ يُزَكِّيهِ قَالَ» سَنَةً وَاحِدَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man whose wealth is absent from him for five years, then it comes to him, and the principal of the wealth is not returned to him. How much does he pay zakat on it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “For one year.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Is there is no zakat in debt?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ لَيْسَ فِي اَلدَّيْنِ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Is there is no zakat in debt?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in debt unless the owner of the debt is the one who delays it. But if he is not able to take possession of it, then there is no zakat upon him until he receives it.”

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in debt unless the owner of the debt is the one who delays it. But if he is not able to take possession of it, then there is no zakat upon him until he receives it.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad and Muhammad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Maysarah, from Abd al-Aziz, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has a debt, Does he pay zakat on it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Every debt that he leaves, while if he wanted to take it he could take it, then its zakat is upon him. arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ مُحَمَّدٍ اِبْنَيِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْعَزِيزِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ اَلدَّيْنُ أَيُزَكِّيهِ قَالَ» كُلُّ دَيْنٍ يَدَعُهُ هُوَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَخْذَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ زَكَاتُهُ وَ مَا كَانَ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَخْذِهِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ«.

But whatever he is not able to take, then there is no zakat upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked regarding ‘a man who borrowed wealth, then a year passed over it while it was with him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If the one who lent it pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him, but if he does not pay it, the borrower pays it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ اِسْتَقْرَضَ مَالاً فَحَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ هُوَ عِنْدَهُ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ اَلَّذِي أَقْرَضَهُ يُؤَدِّي زَكَاتَهُ فَلاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يُؤَدِّي أَدَّى اَلْمُسْتَقْرِضُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked regarding ‘a man who borrowed wealth, then a year passed over it while it was with him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If the one who lent it pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him, but if he does not pay it, the borrower pays it.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who lends wealth to another man for one year, two years, three years, or whatever Allah (swt) wills. Thus, upon whom is the zakat, upon the lender or upon the borrower?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon the borrower, because its benefit belongs to him, so its zakat is upon him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُقْرِضُ اَلْمَالَ لِلرَّجُلِ اَلسَّنَةَ وَاَلسَّنَتَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثَ أَوْ مَا شَاءَ اَللَّهُ عَلَى مَنِ اَلزَّكَاةُ عَلَى اَلْمُقْرِضِ أَوْ عَلَى اَلْمُسْتَقْرِضِ فَقَالَ» عَلَى اَلْمُسْتَقْرِضِ لِأَنَّ لَهُ نَفْعَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ زَكَاتُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who lends wealth to another man for one year, two years, three years, or whatever Allah (swt) wills. chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man gave wealth to another man as a loan; upon whom is its zakat, upon the lender or upon the borrower?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather its zakat, if it has been placed with him for a year, is upon the borrower.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is its zakat not upon the lender?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Wealth is not paid zakat on from two sides in one year, and there is nothing upon the one who gives it, because there is nothing in his hand, for the wealth is in the hand of the other. So whoever has the wealth in his hand pays zakat on it.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Does he then pay zakat on the wealth of someone else from his own wealth?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is his wealth as long as it is in his hand, and that wealth does not belong to anyone other than him.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, have you considered the loss of that wealth and its profit, whose are they, and upon whom are they?” I (narrator) replied: “They belong to the borrower.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then the surplus belongs to him, and the deficiency is upon him, and he may clothe himself, marry, and eat from it. And it is not proper for him not to pay zakat on it. Rather, he should pay zakat on it, for it is upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ دَفَعَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مَالاً قَرْضاً عَلَى مَنْ زَكَاتُهُ أَ عَلَى اَلْمُقْرِضِ أَوْ عَلَى اَلْمُقْتَرِضِ قَالَ» لاَ بَلْ زَكَاتُهَا إِنْ كَانَتْ مَوْضُوعَةً عِنْدَهُ حَوْلاً عَلَى اَلْمُقْتَرِضِ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَلَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْمُقْرِضِ زَكَاتُهَا قَالَ» لاَ لاَ يُزَكَّى اَلْمَالُ مِنْ وَجْهَيْنِ فِي عَامٍ وَاحِدٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلدَّافِعِ شَيْءٌ لِأَنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِي يَدِهِ شَيْءٌ لِأَنَّ اَلْمَالَ فِي يَدِ اَلْآخَرِ فَمَنْ كَانَ اَلْمَالُ فِي يَدِهِ زَكَّاهُ« قَالَ قُلْتُ أَفَيُزَكِّي مَالَ غَيْرِهِ مِنْ مَالِهِ فَقَالَ» إِنَّهُ مَالُهُ مَا دَامَ فِي يَدِهِ وَ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَالُ لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» يَا زُرَارَةُ أَ رَأَيْتَ وَضِيعَةُ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَالِ وَ رِبْحُهُ لِمَنْ هُوَ وَ عَلَى مَنْ« قُلْتُ لِلْمُقْتَرِضِ قَالَ» فَلَهُ اَلْفَضْلُ وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلنُّقْصَانُ وَ لَهُ أَنْ يَلْبَسَ وَيَنْكِحَ وَ يَأْكُلَ مِنْهُ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ لاَ يُزَكِّيَهُ بَلْ يُزَكِّيهِ فَإِنَّهُ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man gave wealth to another man as a loan; upon whom is its zakat, upon the lender or upon the borrower?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather its zakat, if it has been placed with him for a year, is upon the borrower.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is its zakat not upon the lender?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Wealth is not paid zakat on from two sides in one year, and there is nothing upon the one who gives it, because there is nothing in his hand, for the wealth is in the hand of the other. So whoever has the wealth in his hand pays zakat on it.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Does he then pay zakat on the wealth of someone else from his own wealth?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is his wealth as long as it is in his hand, and that wealth does not belong to anyone other than him.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, have you considered the loss of that wealth and its profit, whose are they, and upon whom are they?” I (narrator) replied: “They belong to the borrower.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then the surplus belongs to him, and the deficiency is upon him, and he may clothe himself, marry, and eat from it. And it is not proper for him not to pay zakat on it. Rather, he should pay zakat on it, for it is upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Hisham ibn Ahmar: “I would like you to ask Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, for me: ‘There are loans belonging to some people with me, and they do not demand them from me; is there zakat upon me?’” Imam (a.s) said: “You do not repay, and you do not pay zakat? Pay zakat.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِهِشَامِ بْنِ أَحْمَرَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ تَسْأَلَ لِي أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ لِقَوْمٍ عِنْدِي قُرُوضاً لَيْسَ يَطْلُبُونَهَا مِنِّي أَفَعَلَيَّ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ تَقْضِي وَ لاَ تُزَكِّي زَكِّ«.

Pay zakat.”

chapter: Chapter on Zakat of the Wealth of the Absent Person, Debt, and Loan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said and al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there zakat upon debt?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, until he receives it.” I (narrator) asked: “Then when he receives it, does he pay zakat on it?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, until a year passes over it in his hands.”

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has a deposit and a debt, but he does not reach them, then he takes them. When does zakat become obligatory upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he takes them, then a year passes over them, he pays zakat.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي مَحْمُودٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ لَهُ اَلْوَدِيعَةُ وَ اَلدَّيْنُ فَلاَ يَصِلُ إِلَيْهِمَا ثُمَّ يَأْخُذُهُمَا مَتَى تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ قَالَ» إِذَا أَخَذَهُمَا ثُمَّ يَحُولُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ يُزَكِّي«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent, Is there zakat upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, until he arrives.” I (narrator) asked: “Does he pay zakat on it when he arrives?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَرِثَ مَالاً وَ اَلرَّجُلُ غَائِبٌ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَقْدَمَ« قُلْتُ أَ يُزَكِّيهِ حِينَ يَقْدَمُ قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent, Is there zakat upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, until he arrives.” I (narrator) asked: “Does he pay zakat on it when he arrives?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it.”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is upon silent wealth (al-mal al-samit) over which a year passes and which he has not moved.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: »اَلزَّكَاةُ عَلَى اَلْمَالِ اَلصَّامِتِ اَلَّذِي يَحُولُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ لَمْ يُحَرِّكْهُ«.

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man had two hundred dirhams minus one dirham with him for eleven months, then after that, in the twelfth month, he acquired one dirham, so that two hundred dirhams became complete with him; ‘Is their zakat upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it while it is two hundred dirhams. So if it was one hundred and fifty dirhams, then he acquired fifty after one month had passed, then there is no zakat upon him until a year passes over the two hundred.” I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he had two hundred dirhams minus one dirham with him, and some days passed over them before the month ended, then he acquired one dirham, and a year came over the dirhams together with the dirham, is there zakat upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. But if a full year has not passed over all of them together, then there is nothing upon him in them.” He (narrator) said that Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Any man who has wealth and a year passes over it, then he pays zakat on it.” I said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he gives it away as a gift one month or two days before its due time.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is never anything upon him.” He (narrator) said that Zurarah said from Imam (a.s) that he said: Imam (a.s) said: “This is only like a man who broke his fast in the month of Ramadan for one day while he was in his residence, then he goes out at the end of the day on a journey, intending by that journey to invalidate the expiation that had become obligatory upon him.” And Imam (a.s) said: “When he saw the twelfth crescent, zakat became obligatory upon him. But if he had given it away as a gift before that, it would have been permissible, and there would have been nothing upon him, like one who goes out and then breaks his fast. He only cannot prevent what a year has passed over. As for what a year has not passed over, he may prevent it, and it is not lawful for him to prevent the wealth of another in what has already become due upon it.” Zurarah said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man had two hundred dirhams, so he gave them as a gift to some of his brothers, or his children, or his family, fleeing thereby from zakat, and he did that one month before it became due.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When the twelfth month enters, then a year has passed over it, and zakat has become obligatory upon him in it.” So I (Zurarah) said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he does something with it before the year?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is permissible for him.” I (Zurarah) asked: “He fled thereby from zakat.” Imam (a.s) said: “What he has brought upon himself is greater than what he prevented from its zakat.” So I (Zurarah) said to Imam (a.s): “He is able to get it back.” Imam (a.s) said: “And what is it upon me that he is able to get it back, when it has gone out of his ownership?” I said: “Then he gave it to him upon a condition.” Imam (a.s) said: “When he names it a gift, the gift is valid, the condition falls away, and he is liable for the zakat.” I said to Imam (a.s): “And how does the condition fall away, the gift take effect, and he become liable for the zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “This is an invalid condition, and the guaranteed gift is effective, and the zakat is binding upon him as a punishment for him.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “That is only for him when he buys with it a house, or land, or estates.” Then Zurarah said: “I said to Imam (a.s): “Your father said to me: ‘Whoever flees thereby from zakat, then he must pay it.’” Imam (a.s) said: “My father (a.s), peace be upon him, spoke the truth. He must pay what has been made obligatory upon him, and what has not become obligatory upon him, then there is nothing upon him in it.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Have you considered, if a man were overcome by unconsciousness for a day and then died, so his prayer passed away, would it be upon him, while he has died, to perform it?” I (Zurarah) replied: “No, unless he had regained consciousness during his day.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “If a man became ill in the month of Ramadan and then died in it, would fasting be performed on his behalf?” I (Zurarah) replied: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “So likewise, the man does not pay from his wealth except that over which a year has passed.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ غَيْرَ دِرْهَمٍ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ شَهْراً ثُمَّ أَصَابَ دِرْهَماً بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلشَّهْرِ اَلثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ فَكَمَلَتْ عِنْدَهُ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ أَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاتُهَا قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ هِيَ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِائَةً وَ خَمْسِينَ دِرْهَماً فَأَصَابَ خَمْسِينَ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَمْضِيَ شَهْرٌ فَلاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَى اَلْمِائَتَيْنِ اَلْحَوْلُ« قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ عِنْدَهُ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ غَيْرَ دِرْهَمٍ فَمَضَى عَلَيْهَا أَيَّامٌ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْقَضِيَ اَلشَّهْرُ ثُمَّ أَصَابَ دِرْهَماً فَأَتَى عَلَى اَلدَّرَاهِمِ مَعَ اَلدِّرْهَمِ حَوْلٌ أَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَمْضِ عَلَيْهَا جَمِيعاً اَلْحَوْلُ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ فِيهَا« قَالَ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ مَالٌ وَ حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَإِنَّهُ يُزَكِّيهِ« قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ وَهَبَهُ قَبْلَ حَلِّهِ بِشَهْرٍ أَوْ بِيَوْمَيْنِ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ ءٌأَبَداً« قَالَ وَ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ عَنْهُ إِنَّهُ قَالَ» إِنَّمَا هَذَا بِمَنْزِلَةِ رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ يَوْماً فِي إِقَامَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ فِي آخِرِ اَلنَّهَارِ فِي سَفَرٍ فَأَرَادَ بِسَفَرِهِ ذَلِكَ إِبْطَالَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ اَلَّتِي وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ« وَ قَالَ» إِنَّهُ حِينَ رَأَى اَلْهِلاَلَ اَلثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ وَهَبَهَا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ لَجَازَ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ بِمَنْزِلَةِ مَنْ خَرَجَ ثُمَّ أَفْطَرَ إِنَّمَا لاَ يَمْنَعُ مَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ فَأَمَّا مَا لَمْ يَحُلْ عَلَيْهِ فَلَهُ مَنْعُهُ وَ لاَ يَحِلُّ لَهُ مَنْعُ مَالِ غَيْرِهِ فِيمَا قَدْ حَلَّ عَلَيْهِ« قَالَ زُرَارَةُ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ كَانَتْ لَهُ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ فَوَهَبَهَا لِبَعْضِ إِخْوَانِهِ أَوْ وُلْدِهِ أَوْ أَهْلِهِ فِرَاراً بِهَا مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ قَبْلَ حَلِّهَا بِشَهْرٍ فَقَالَ» إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلشَّهْرُ اَلثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ فَقَدْ حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ فِيهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ« فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ أَحْدَثَ فِيهَا قَبْلَ اَلْحَوْلِ قَالَ» جَازَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ« قُلْتُ إِنَّهُ فَرَّ بِهَا عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ» مَا أَدْخَلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَعْظَمُ مِمَّا مَنَعَ مِنْ زَكَاتِهَا« فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّهُ يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ فَقَالَ» وَ مَا عَلَيَّ إِنَّهُ يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهَا وَ قَدْ خَرَجَتْ مِنْ مِلْكِهِ« قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ دَفَعَهَا إِلَيْهِ عَلَى شَرْطٍ فَقَالَ» إِنَّهُ إِذَا سَمَّاهَا هِبَةً جَازَتِ اَلْهِبَةُ وَ سَقَطَ اَلشَّرْطُ وَ ضَمِنَ اَلزَّكَاةَ« قُلْتُ لَهُ وَ كَيْفَ يَسْقُطُ اَلشَّرْطُ وَ تَمْضِي اَلْهِبَةُ وَيَضْمَنُ اَلزَّكَاةَ فَقَالَ» هَذَا شَرْطٌ فَاسِدٌ وَ اَلْهِبَةُ اَلْمَضْمُونَةُ مَاضِيَةٌ وَ اَلزَّكَاةُ لَهُ لاَزِمَةٌ عُقُوبَةً لَهُ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ لَهُ إِذَا اِشْتَرَى بِهَا دَاراً أَوْ أَرْضاً أَوْ ضِيَاعاً« ثُمَّ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ أَبَاكَ قَالَ لِي» مَنْ فَرَّ بِهَا مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا« فَقَالَ» صَدَقَ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا مَا أُوجِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَ مَا لَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ فِيهِ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» أَ رَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً ثُمَّ مَاتَ فَذَهَبَتْ صَلاَتُهُ أَ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ مَاتَ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا« قُلْتُ لاَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ أَفَاقَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ» لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً مَرِضَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ مَاتَ فِيهِ أَ كَانَ يُصَامُ عَنْهُ« قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ» فَكَذَلِكَ اَلرَّجُلُ لاَ يُؤَدِّي عَنْ مَالِهِ إِلاَّ مَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man had two hundred dirhams minus one dirham with him for eleven months, then after that, in the twelfth month, he acquired one dirham, so that two hundred dirhams became complete with him; ‘Is their zakat upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it while it is two hundred dirhams. So if it was one hundred and fifty dirhams, then he acquired fifty after one month had passed, then there is no zakat upon him until a year passes over the two hundred.” I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he had two hundred dirhams minus one dirham with him, and some days passed over them before the month ended, then he acquired one dirham, and a year came over the dirhams together with the dirham, is there zakat upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. But if a full year has not passed over all of them together, then there is nothing upon him in them.” He (narrator) said that Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Any man who has wealth and a year passes over it, then he pays zakat on it.” I said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he gives it away as a gift one month or two days before its due time.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is never anything upon him.” He (narrator) said that Zurarah said from Imam (a.s) that he said: Imam (a.s) said: “This is only like a man who broke his fast in the month of Ramadan for one day while he was in his residence, then he goes out at the end of the day on a journey, intending by that journey to invalidate the expiation that had become obligatory upon him.” And Imam (a.s) said: “When he saw the twelfth crescent, zakat became obligatory upon him. But if he had given it away as a gift before that, it would have been permissible, and there would have been nothing upon him, like one who goes out and then breaks his fast. He only cannot prevent what a year has passed over. As for what a year has not passed over, he may prevent it, and it is not lawful for him to prevent the wealth of another in what has already become due upon it.” Zurarah said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man had two hundred dirhams, so he gave them as a gift to some of his brothers, or his children, or his family, fleeing thereby from zakat, and he did that one month before it became due.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When the twelfth month enters, then a year has passed over it, and zakat has become obligatory upon him in it.” So I (Zurarah) said to Imam (a.s): “Then if he does something with it before the year?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is permissible for him.” I (Zurarah) asked: “He fled thereby from zakat.” Imam (a.s) said: “What he has brought upon himself is greater than what he prevented from its zakat.” So I (Zurarah) said to Imam (a.s): “He is able to get it back.” Imam (a.s) said: “And what is it upon me that he is able to get it back, when it has gone out of his ownership?” I said: “Then he gave it to him upon a condition.” Imam (a.s) said: “When he names it a gift, the gift is valid, the condition falls away, and he is liable for the zakat.” I said to Imam (a.s): “And how does the condition fall away, the gift take effect, and he become liable for the zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “This is an invalid condition, and the guaranteed gift is effective, and the zakat is binding upon him as a punishment for him.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “That is only for him when he buys with it a house, or land, or estates.” Then Zurarah said: “I said to Imam (a.s): “Your father said to me: ‘Whoever flees thereby from zakat, then he must pay it.’” Imam (a.s) said: “My father (a.s), peace be upon him, spoke the truth. He must pay what has been made obligatory upon him, and what has not become obligatory upon him, then there is nothing upon him in it.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Have you considered, if a man were overcome by unconsciousness for a day and then died, so his prayer passed away, would it be upon him, while he has died, to perform it?” I (Zurarah) replied: “No, unless he had regained consciousness during his day.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “If a man became ill in the month of Ramadan and then died in it, would fasting be performed on his behalf?” I (Zurarah) replied: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “So likewise, the man does not pay from his wealth except that over which a year has passed.”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Both (Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim) said to Imam (a.s): “This land whose people we cultivate in partnership (sharecropping arrangement), what do you say concerning it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Every land that a ruler hands over to you, then whatever you cultivate from it, you are only liable for what Allah (swt) brings forth from it after fulfilling the share that he contracted with you upon. The tithe is not due upon everything that Allah (swt) brings forth from it. Rather, the tithe is only due upon what comes into your hand after his share has been taken from you.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ لَهُ هَذِهِ اَلْأَرْضُ اَلَّتِي نُزَارِعُ أَهْلَهَا مَا تَرَى فِيهَا فَقَالَ» كُلُّ أَرْضٍ دَفَعَهَا إِلَيْكَ سُلْطَانٌ فَمَا حَرَثْتَهُ فِيهَا فَعَلَيْكَ فِيمَا أَخْرَجَ اَللَّهُ مِنْهَا اَلَّذِي قَاطَعَكَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَا أَخْرَجَ اَللَّهُ مِنْهَا اَلْعُشْرُ إِنَّمَا اَلْعُشْرُ عَلَيْكَ فِيمَا يَحْصُلُ فِي يَدِكَ بَعْدَ مُقَاسَمَتِهِ لَكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Both (Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim) said to Imam (a.s): “This land whose people we cultivate in partnership (sharecropping arrangement), what do you say concerning it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Every land that a ruler hands over to you, then whatever you cultivate from it, you are only liable for what Allah (swt) brings forth from it after fulfilling the share that he contracted with you upon. The tithe is not due upon everything that Allah (swt) brings forth from it. Rather, the tithe is only due upon what comes into your hand after his share has been taken from you.”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah ibn Musa, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has an estate and pays its land-tax (kharaj), Is there a tithe upon him in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لَهُ اَلضَّيْعَةُ فَيُؤَدِّي خَرَاجَهَا هَلْ عَلَيْهِ فِيهَا عُشْرٌ قَالَ» لاَ«
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah ibn Musa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has an estate and pays its land-tax (kharaj), Is there a tithe upon him in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Abu Jafar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Kahmas, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever the ruler takes land-tax (kharaj) from, then there is no zakat upon him.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي كَهْمَسٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنْهُ اَلسُّلْطَانُ اَلْخَرَاجَ فَلاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Abu Jafar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Kahmas, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever the ruler takes land-tax (kharaj) from, then there is no zakat upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who both said:
We (Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad) mentioned to Imam (a.s) about ‘Kufa and what had been imposed upon it of land-tax (kharaj), and what the people of his house (Ahlul Bayt (a.s)) had followed concerning it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever embraces Islam willingly, his land is left in his hand, and the tithe is taken from him in what the sky and the rivers water, and half of the tithe in what is scarce (nadir) in what they cultivate of it. And whatever they do not cultivate of it, the Imam takes it and leases it (qabalah) to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And upon those who accept the ‘lease’, in their shares, is the tithe and half of the tithe. And in less than five awsaq there is nothing of zakat. And whatever is taken by the sword, that is for the Imam; he leases it according to what he sees, just as the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, did with Khaybar. He (saws) leased its ‘black’ and its ‘white’ (sawad and bayad), -meaning its land and its palm-trees. And the people say: ‘The leasing of land and palm-trees is not valid’, while the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him, leased Khaybar. And upon those who accept the lease, besides the lease payment of the land, is the tithe and half of the tithe in their shares.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The people of Taif embraced Islam, and He (saws) placed upon them the tithe and half of the tithe. And the people of Mecca, when the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, entered it by force, and they were captives in his hand, The Prophet (saws) released them and said: ‘Go, for you are the freed ones.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشْيَمَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالاَ: ذَكَرْنَا لَهُ اَلْكُوفَةَ وَ مَا وُضِعَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ اَلْخَرَاجِ وَ مَا سَارَ فِيهَا أَهْلُ بَيْتِهِ فَقَالَ» مَنْ أَسْلَمَ طَوْعاً تُرِكَتْ أَرْضُهُ فِي يَدِهِ وَ أُخِذَ مِنْهُ اَلْعُشْرُ فِيمَا سَقَتِ اَلسَّمَاءُ وَاَلْأَنْهَارُ وَ نِصْفُ اَلْعُشْرِ فِيمَا كَانَ نَادِراً فِيمَا عَمَرُوهُ مِنْهَا وَ مَا لَمْ يَعْمُرُوهُ مِنْهَا أَخَذَهُ اَلْإِمَامُ فَقَبَّلَهُ مِمَّنْ يَعْمُرُهُ وَ كَانَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ عَلَى اَلْمُتَقَبِّلِينَ فِي حِصَصِهِمُ اَلْعُشْرُ وَ نِصْفُ اَلْعُشْرِ وَ لَيْسَ فِي أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ أَوْسَاقٍ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ وَ مَا أُخِذَ بِالسَّيْفِ فَذَلِكَ إِلَى اَلْإِمَامِ يُقَبِّلُهُ بِالَّذِي يَرَاهُ كَمَا صَنَعَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَ بِخَيْبَرَ قَبَّلَ سَوَادَهَا وَبَيَاضَهَا يَعْنِي أَرْضَهَا وَ نَخْلَهَا وَ اَلنَّاسُ يَقُولُونَ لاَ تَصْلُحُ قَبَالَةُ اَلْأَرْضِ وَ اَلنَّخْلِ وَ قَدْ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ خَيْبَرَ وَ عَلَى اَلْمُتَقَبِّلِينَ سِوَى قَبَالَةِ اَلْأَرْضِ اَلْعُشْرُ وَنِصْفُ اَلْعُشْرِ فِي حِصَصِهِمْ« وَقَالَ» إِنَّ أَهْلَ اَلطَّائِفِ أَسْلَمُوا وَجَعَلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ اَلْعُشْرَ وَنِصْفَ اَلْعُشْرِ وَإِنَّ أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ لَمَّا دَخَلَهَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ ص عَنْوَةً وَ كَانُوا أُسَرَاءَ فِي يَدِهِ فَأَعْتَقَهُمْ وَ قَالَ» اِذْهَبُوا فَأَنْتُمُ اَلطُّلَقَاءُ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who both said:
thaqalaynMatn: We (Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad) mentioned to Imam (a.s) about ‘Kufa and what had been imposed upon it of land-tax (kharaj), and what the people of his house (Ahlul Bayt (a.s)) had followed concerning it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever embraces Islam willingly, his land is left in his hand, and the tithe is taken from him in what the sky and the rivers water, and half of the tithe in what is scarce (nadir) in what they cultivate of it. And whatever they do not cultivate of it, the Imam takes it and leases it (qabalah) to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And upon those who accept the ‘lease’, in their shares, is the tithe and half of the tithe. And in less than five awsaq there is nothing of zakat. And whatever is taken by the sword, that is for the Imam; he leases it according to what he sees, just as the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, did with Khaybar. He (saws) leased its ‘black’ and its ‘white’ (sawad and bayad), -meaning its land and its palm-trees. And the people say: ‘The leasing of land and palm-trees is not valid’, while the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him, leased Khaybar. And upon those who accept the lease, besides the lease payment of the land, is the tithe and half of the tithe in their shares.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The people of Taif embraced Islam, and He (saws) placed upon them the tithe and half of the tithe. And the people of Mecca, when the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, entered it by force, and they were captives in his hand, The Prophet (saws) released them and said: ‘Go, for you are the freed ones.’”

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding the zakat of land, when the Prophet (saws), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, or the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, leases it (qabbalaha) for half, or a third, or a quarter, then its zakat is upon him, And there is no zakat upon the one who accepts the lease (al-mutaqabbil), unless the owner of the land stipulates that the zakat is upon the one who accepts the lease. If he (the one who leases) stipulates it, then the zakat is upon them. And there is no zakat upon the people of the land today, except upon one in whose hand there is something from what the Messenger (saws), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, granted as a land allotment.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَخَوَيْهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» فِي زَكَاةِ اَلْأَرْضِ إِذَا قَبَّلَهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَوِ اَلْإِمَامُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِالنِّصْفِ أَوِ اَلثُّلُثِ أَوِ اَلرُّبُعِ فَزَكَاتُهَا عَلَيْهِ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْمُتَقَبِّلِ زَكَاةٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَشْتَرِطَ صَاحِبُ اَلْأَرْضِ أَنَّ اَلزَّكَاةَ عَلَى اَلْمُتَقَبِّلِ فَإِنِ اِشْتَرَطَ فَإِنَّ اَلزَّكَاةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْأَرْضِ اَلْيَوْمَ زَكَاةٌ إِلاَّ عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ فِي يَدِهِ شَيْءٌ مِمَّا أَقْطَعَهُ اَلرَّسُولُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding the zakat of land, when the Prophet (saws), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, or the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, leases it (qabbalaha) for half, or a third, or a quarter, then its zakat is upon him, And there is no zakat upon the one who accepts the lease (al-mutaqabbil), unless the owner of the land stipulates that the zakat is upon the one who accepts the lease. If he (the one who leases) stipulates it, then the zakat is upon them. And there is no zakat upon the people of the land today, except upon one in whose hand there is something from what the Messenger (saws), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, granted as a land allotment.”
