chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), recalling: “The companions of my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) came to him and asked him about ‘what the ruler takes’, so he felt compassion for them, while he certainly knew that zakat is not lawful except for its people. So he (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) commanded them to count it as such, and by Allah (swt), that was valid for them.” So I (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) asked: “O my father, if they hear that, no one will pay zakat.” So Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O son, it’s a truth that Allah (swt) loved to make manifest.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ أَبِي أَتَوْهُ فَسَأَلُوهُ عَمَّا يَأْخُذُهُ اَلسُّلْطَانُ فَرَقَّ لَهُمْ وَ إِنَّهُ لَيَعْلَمُ أَنَّ اَلزَّكَاةَ لاَ تَحِلُّ إِلاَّ لِأَهْلِهَا فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَحْتَسِبُوا بِهِ فَجَازَ ذَا وَ اَللَّهِ لَهُمْ فَقُلْتُ أَيْ أَبَهْ إِنَّهُمْ إِنْ سَمِعُوا ذَلِكَ لَمْ يُزَكِّ أَحَدٌ فَقَالَ» أَيْ بُنَيَّ حَقٌّ أَحَبَّ اَللَّهُ أَنْ يُظْهِرَهُ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), recalling: “The companions of my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) came to him and asked him about ‘what the ruler takes’, so he felt compassion for them, while he certainly knew that zakat is not lawful except for its people. So he (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) commanded them to count it as such, and by Allah (swt), that was valid for them.” So I (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) asked: “O my father, if they hear that, no one will pay zakat.” So Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O son, it’s a truth that Allah (swt) loved to make manifest.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 52

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tawil, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding zakat, whatever Banu Umayyah have taken from you, count it as such (zakat). And do not give them anything as much as you are able, for wealth cannot remain such that it is paid as zakat twice.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلطَّوِيلِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ فَقَالَ» مَا أَخَذَهُ مِنْكُمْ بَنُو أُ مَيَّةَ فَاحْتَسِبُوا بِهِ وَ لاَ تُعْطُوهُمْ شَيْئاً مَا اِسْتَطَعْتُمْ فَإِنَّ اَلْمَالَ لاَ يَبْقَى عَلَى هَذَا أَنْ يُزَكِّيَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tawil, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding zakat, whatever Banu Umayyah have taken from you, count it as such (zakat). And do not give them anything as much as you are able, for wealth cannot remain such that it is paid as zakat twice.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 53

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of wealth that the ruler takes.’ Imam (a.s) said: “I do not command you to repeat it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْمَالِ يَأْخُذُهَا اَلسُّلْطَانُ فَقَالَ» لاَ آمُرُكَ أَنْ تُعِيدَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of wealth that the ruler takes.’ Imam (a.s) said: “I do not command you to repeat it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 53

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Uthman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Usamah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, these collectors of charity (al-musaddiqin) come to us and take charity from us, so we give it to them; does it suffice on our behalf?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. These are only a people who have usurped from you,” or Imam (a.s) said: “They have wronged you regarding your wealth, and charity is only for its people.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ اَلْمُصَدِّقِينَ يَأْتُونَّا فَيَأْخُذُونَ مِنَّا اَلصَّدَقَةَ فَنُعْطِيهِمْ إِيَّاهَا أَ تُجْزِي عَنَّا فَقَالَ» لاَ إِنَّمَا هَؤُلاَءِ قَوْمٌ غَصَبُوكُمْ« أَوْ قَالَ» ظَلَمُوكُمْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ وَ إِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقَةُ لِأَهْلِهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Uthman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Usamah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, these collectors of charity (al-musaddiqin) come to us and take charity from us, so we give it to them; does it suffice on our behalf?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. These are only a people who have usurped from you,” or Imam (a.s) said: “They have wronged you regarding your wealth, and charity is only for its people.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 53

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Any man who has cultivation or fruit, and he gives its charity, then there is nothing upon him in it if a year passes over it while it is with him, unless he converts it into wealth. If he does so, and a year passes over it while it is with him, then he must pay zakat on it, otherwise there is nothing upon him, even if it remains for a thousand years, so long as it is itself. Rather, upon him is the charity of the tithe. So when he has paid it once, there is nothing upon him until it is converted into wealth and a year passes over it while it is with him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ:» أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ حَرْثٌ أَوْ ثَمَرَةٌ فَصَدَّقَهَا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِيهِ شَيْ ءٌإِنْ حَالَ عَلَيْهَا اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُحَوِّلَهُ مَالاً وَ إِنْ فَعَلَ فَحَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُزَكِّيَهُ وَ إِلاَّ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَوْ ثَبَتَ أَلْفَ عَامٍ إِذَا كَانَ بِعَيْنِهِ وَ إِنَّمَا عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةُ اَلْعُشْرِ فَإِذَا أَدَّاهَا مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يُحَوَّلَ مَالاً وَ يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَهُوَ عِنْدَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Any man who has cultivation or fruit, and he gives its charity, then there is nothing upon him in it if a year passes over it while it is with him, unless he converts it into wealth. If he does so, and a year passes over it while it is with him, then he must pay zakat on it, otherwise there is nothing upon him, even if it remains for a thousand years, so long as it is itself. Rather, upon him is the charity of the tithe. So when he has paid it once, there is nothing upon him until it is converted into wealth and a year passes over it while it is with him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn Ayan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir, Burayd al-Ijli, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon working camels and cattle. Charities are only upon grazing, pasturing livestock. And everything over which a year has not passed while it is with its owner, then there is nothing upon him in it. But when a year has passed over it, it becomes obligatory upon him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْجُهَنِيِّ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ بُرَيْدٍ اَلْعِجْلِيِّ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ:» لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْعَوَامِلِ مِنَ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ اَلْبَقَرِ شَيْ ءٌإِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقَاتُ عَلَى اَلسَّائِمَةِ اَلرَّاعِيَةِ وَ كُلُّ مَا لَمْ يَحُلْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ فَلاَ شَيْءَ فِيهِ عَلَيْهِ فَإِذَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn Ayan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Abu Basir, Burayd al-Ijli, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon working camels and cattle. Charities are only upon grazing, pasturing livestock. And everything over which a year has not passed while it is with its owner, then there is nothing upon him in it. But when a year has passed over it, it becomes obligatory upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in anything of animals other than these three categories: camels, cattle, and sheep. And everything from these categories, from domesticated animals and working animals, there is nothing in them until a year passes over them from the day they are born.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْحَيَوَانِ زَكَاةٌ غَيْرِ هَذِهِ اَلْأَصْنَافِ اَلثَّلاَثَةِ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ اَلْبَقَرِ وَ اَلْغَنَمِ وَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ اَلْأَصْنَافِ مِنَ اَلدَّوَاجِنِ وَ اَلْعَوَامِلِ فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ مُنْذُ يَوْمِ يُنْتَجُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat in anything of animals other than these three categories: camels, cattle, and sheep. And everything from these categories, from domesticated animals and working animals, there is nothing in them until a year passes over them from the day they are born.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 55

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked him about ‘camels belonging to a camel-driver, and which are in some of the towns. Does zakat apply to them as it applies to grazing livestock in the wilderness?’ He said: “Yes.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْإِبِلِ تَكُونُ لِلْجَمَّالِ وَ تَكُونُ فِي بَعْضِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ أَ تَجْرِي عَلَيْهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ كَمَا تَجْرِي عَلَى اَلسَّائِمَةِ فِي اَلْبَرِّيَّةِ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about ‘camels belonging to a camel-driver, and which are in some of the towns. Does zakat apply to them as it applies to grazing livestock in the wilderness?’ He said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ishaq:
I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘working camels, Is there zakat upon them?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is zakat upon them.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْإِبِلِ اَلْعَوَامِلِ عَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ عَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ishaq:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘working camels, Is there zakat upon them?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is zakat upon them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘camels belonging to a camel-driver (jammal), or which are in some of the towns. Does zakat apply to them as it applies to grazing livestock in the wilderness?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْإِبِلِ تَكُونُ لِلْجَمَّالِ أَوْ تَكُونُ فِي بَعْضِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ أَ تَجْرِي عَلَيْهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ كَمَا تَجْرِي عَلَى اَلسَّائِمَةِ فِي اَلْبَرِّيَّةِ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘camels belonging to a camel-driver (jammal), or which are in some of the towns. Does zakat apply to them as it applies to grazing livestock in the wilderness?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing in the young of camels, cattle, and sheep except that over which a year has passed while it is with the man, and there is nothing in their offspring until a year passes over it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ فِي صِغَارِ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ اَلْبَقَرِ وَ اَلْغَنَمِ شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ مَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ لَيْسَ فِي أَوْلاَدِهَا شَيْءٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing in the young of camels, cattle, and sheep except that over which a year has passed while it is with the man, and there is nothing in their offspring until a year passes over it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Samaah, from a man, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Nothing is paid as zakat from camels, cattle, and sheep except that over which a year has passed. And whatever a year has not passed over is as though it did not exist.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصُّهْبَانِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ يُزَكَّى مِنَ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ اَلْبَقَرِ وَ اَلْغَنَمِ إِلاَّ مَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ مَا لَمْ يَحُلْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَكَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Samaah, from a man, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Nothing is paid as zakat from camels, cattle, and sheep except that over which a year has passed. And whatever a year has not passed over is as though it did not exist.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has wealth with him; does he pay zakat on it when half the year has passed?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, but rather until a year passes over it and it becomes due upon him. No one may perform a prayer except at its time, and likewise zakat. And no one fasts the month of Ramadan except in its month, except as a make-up, and every obligation is only performed when it becomes due.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ اَلْمَالُ أَ يُزَكِّيهِ إِذَا مَضَى نِصْفُ اَلسَّنَةِ قَالَ» لاَ وَ لَكِنْ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ تَحِلَّ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ صَلاَةً إِلاَّ لِوَقْتِهَا وَ كَذَلِكَ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ لاَ يَصُومُ أَحَدٌ شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ إِلاَّ فِي شَهْرِهِ إِلاَّ قَضَاءً وَ كُلُّ فَرِيضَةٍ إِنَّمَا تُؤَدَّى إِذَا حَلَّتْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has wealth with him; does he pay zakat on it when half the year has passed?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, but rather until a year passes over it and it becomes due upon him. No one may perform a prayer except at its time, and likewise zakat. And no one fasts the month of Ramadan except in its month, except as a make-up, and every obligation is only performed when it becomes due.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Does a man pay zakat on his wealth when one third of the year has passed?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Do you perform the first prayer before midday?”
arabicText: حَمَّادٌ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يُزَكِّي اَلرَّجُلُ مَالَهُ إِذَا مَضَى ثُلُثُ اَلسَّنَةِ قَالَ» لاَ أَ تُصَلِّي اَلْأُولَى قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Does a man pay zakat on his wealth when one third of the year has passed?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Do you perform the first prayer before midday?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man upon whom zakat becomes due in the month of Ramadan, so he delays it until Muharram.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘But it does not become due except in Muharram, so he hastens it in the month of Ramadan.’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ تَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَيُؤَخِّرُهَا إِلَى اَلْمُحَرَّمِ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَحِلُّ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْمُحَرَّمِ فَيُعَجِّلُهَا فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man upon whom zakat becomes due in the month of Ramadan, so he delays it until Muharram.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘But it does not become due except in Muharram, so he hastens it in the month of Ramadan.’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man to whom a needy person comes, so he gives him from his zakat at the beginning of the year.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he is needy, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَأْتِيهِ اَلْمُحْتَاجُ فَيُعْطِيهِ مِنْ زَكَاتِهِ فِي أَوَّلِ اَلسَّنَةِ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ مُحْتَاجاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man to whom a needy person comes, so he gives him from his zakat at the beginning of the year.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he is needy, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in hastening zakat by two months and delaying it by two months.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُونُسَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِتَعْجِيلِ اَلزَّكَاةِ شَهْرَيْنِ وَ تَأْخِيرِهَا شَهْرَيْنِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in hastening zakat by two months and delaying it by two months.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from some of our companions, from Abu Said al-Mukari, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who hastens his zakat before the due time.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When eight months have passed, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ اَلْمُكَارِي عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُعَجِّلُ زَكَاتَهُ قَبْلَ اَلْمَحِلِّ فَقَالَ» إِذَا مَضَتْ ثَمَانِيَةُ أَشْهُرٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from some of our companions, from Abu Said al-Mukari, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who hastens his zakat before the due time.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When eight months have passed, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Ahwal:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who hastened the zakat of his wealth, then the one who was given became well-off before the beginning of the year.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The giver repeats the zakat.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْأَحْوَلِ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَجَّلَ زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ ثُمَّ أَيْسَرَ اَلْمُعْطَى قَبْلَ رَأْسِ اَلسَّنَةِ قَالَ» يُعِيدُ اَلْمُعْطِي اَلزَّكَاةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Ahwal:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who hastened the zakat of his wealth, then the one who was given became well-off before the beginning of the year.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The giver repeats the zakat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated this narration from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ahwal:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (narrated) the like of the first (hadith.117).
arabicText: وَ رَوَى هَذَا اَلْحَدِيثَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَ اَلْأَوَّلِ.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated this narration from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ahwal:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, (narrated) the like of the first (hadith.117).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked regarding ‘a man who takes out his zakat, then distributes part of it, while some remains, seeking the proper places for it, and there is between its beginning and its end three months.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُخْرِجُ زَكَاتَهُ فَيَقْسِمُ بَعْضَهَا وَ يَبْقَى بَعْضٌ يَلْتَمِسُ لَهَا اَلْمَوَاضِعَ فَيَكُونُ بَيْنَ أَوَّلِهِ وَ آخِرِهِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked regarding ‘a man who takes out his zakat, then distributes part of it, while some remains, seeking the proper places for it, and there is between its beginning and its end three months.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Jafar, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “My zakat becomes due upon me for a month; is it proper for me to withhold something from it, fearing that someone who asks me may come to me, so that it may be a reserve with me?” Imam (a.s) said: “When the year has passed, then take it out from your wealth and do not mix it with anything, and give it however you wish.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if I write it down and record it, is that valid for me?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, it will not harm you.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ زَكَاتِي تَحِلُّ عَلَيَّ شَهْراً فَيَصْلُحُ لِي أَنْ أَحْبِسَ مِنْهَا شَيْئاً مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يَجِيئَنِي مَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي يَكُونُ عِنْدِي عُدَّةً فَقَالَ» إِذَا حَالَ اَلْحَوْلُ فَأَخْرِجْهَا مِنْ مَالِكَ وَ لاَ تَخْلِطْهَا بِشَيْءٍ وَ أَعْطِهَا كَيْفَ شِئْتَ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ أَنَا كَتَبْتُهَا وَ أَثْبَتُّهَا يَسْتَقِيمُ لِي قَالَ» نَعَمْ لاَ يَضُرُّكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Jafar, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “My zakat becomes due upon me for a month; is it proper for me to withhold something from it, fearing that someone who asks me may come to me, so that it may be a reserve with me?” Imam (a.s) said: “When the year has passed, then take it out from your wealth and do not mix it with anything, and give it however you wish.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if I write it down and record it, is that valid for me?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, it will not harm you.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who informed him, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) ‘regarding zakat, a man sends it to a town other than his own town’. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in sending a third or a quarter.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ دُرُسْتَ بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ يَبْعَثُ بِهَا اَلرَّجُلُ إِلَى بَلَدٍ غَيْرِ بَلَدِهِ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يَبْعَثَ بِالثُّلُثِ أَوِ اَلرُّبُعِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who informed him, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) ‘regarding zakat, a man sends it to a town other than his own town’. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in sending a third or a quarter.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb al-Haddad, from the righteous servant (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man from among us is in an isolated land; what should he do with the zakat of his wealth?” Imam (a.s) said: “He places it among his brothers and the people of his wilayah.” So I (narrator) asked: “Then if none of them is present with him there?” Imam (a.s) said: “He sends it to them.” I asked: “Then if he does not find anyone to carry it to them?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives it to one who does not show hostility (la yansib).” I asked: “Then others besides them?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing for others besides them except stone.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ اَلْأَنْصَارِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ اَلْحَدَّادِ عَنِ اَلْعَبْدِ اَلصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنَّا يَكُونُ فِي أَرْضٍ مُنْقَطِعَةٍ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ بِزَكَاةِ مَالِهِ قَالَ» يَضَعُهَا فِي إِخْوَانِهِ وَ أَهْلِ وَلاَيَتِهِ« فَقُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَحْضُرْهُ مِنْهُمْ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ قَالَ» يَبْعَثُ بِهَا إِلَيْهِمْ« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ مَنْ يَحْمِلُهَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ» يَدْفَعُهَا إِلَى مَنْ لاَ يَنْصِبُ« قُلْتُ فَغَيْرُهُمْ قَالَ» مَا لِغَيْرِهِمْ إِلاَّ اَلْحَجَرُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb al-Haddad, from the righteous servant (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man from among us is in an isolated land; what should he do with the zakat of his wealth?” Imam (a.s) said: “He places it among his brothers and the people of his wilayah.” So I (narrator) asked: “Then if none of them is present with him there?” Imam (a.s) said: “He sends it to them.” I asked: “Then if he does not find anyone to carry it to them?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives it to one who does not show hostility (la yansib).” I asked: “Then others besides them?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing for others besides them except stone.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jafar and others, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), about ‘a man who takes his zakat out from one town to another town and spends it among his brothers. Is that permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَمْزَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُخْرِجُ زَكَاتَهُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ آخَرَ وَيَصْرِفُهَا فِي إِخْوَانِهِ فَهَلْ يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jafar and others, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), about ‘a man who takes his zakat out from one town to another town and spends it among his brothers. Is that permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “When a man takes zakat out from his wealth, then names it for a people, and it is lost, or sends it to them and it is lost, then there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا أَخْرَجَ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلزَّكَاةَ مِنْ مَالِهِ ثُمَّ سَمَّاهَا لِقَوْمٍ فَضَاعَتْ أَوْ أَرْسَلَ بِهَا إِلَيْهِمْ فَضَاعَتْ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When a man takes zakat out from his wealth, then names it for a people, and it is lost, or sends it to them and it is lost, then there is nothing upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Bukayr ibn Ayan, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who sends his zakat, and it is stolen or lost.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ بُكَيْرِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَبْعَثُ بِزَكَاتِهِ فَتُسْرَقُ أَوْ تَضِيعُ فَقَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Bukayr ibn Ayan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who sends his zakat, and it is stolen or lost.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man sent the zakat of his wealth so that it would be distributed, and it was lost; is he liable for it until it is distributed?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he finds a place for it and does not give it, then he is liable for it until he gives it. But if he does not find anyone to whom he can give it, and he sends it to its people, then there is no liability upon him, because it has gone out of his hand. And likewise, the executor who is appointed by will is liable for what is handed over to him if he finds its owner, the one whom he was commanded to hand it over to. But if he does not find him, then there is no liability upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ بَعَثَ بِزَكَاةِ مَالِهِ لِتُقْسَمَ فَضَاعَتْ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ ضَمَانُهَا حَتَّى تُقْسَمَ فَقَالَ» إِذَا وَجَدَ لَهَا مَوْضِعاً فَلَمْ يَدْفَعْهَا فَهُوَ لَهَا ضَامِنٌ حَتَّى يَدْفَعَهَا فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ لَهَا مَنْ يَدْفَعُهَا إِلَيْهِ فَبَعَثَ بِهَا إِلَى أَهْلِهَا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ ضَمَانٌ لِأَنَّهَا قَدْ خَرَجَتْ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَ كَذَلِكَ اَلْوَصِيُّ اَلَّذِي يُوصَى إِلَيْهِ يَكُونُ ضَامِناً لِمَا دُفِعَ إِلَيْهِ إِذَا وَجَدَ رَبَّهُ اَلَّذِي أُمِرَ بِدَفْعِهِ إِلَيْهِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ ضَمَانٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man sent the zakat of his wealth so that it would be distributed, and it was lost; is he liable for it until it is distributed?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he finds a place for it and does not give it, then he is liable for it until he gives it. But if he does not find anyone to whom he can give it, and he sends it to its people, then there is no liability upon him, because it has gone out of his hand. And likewise, the executor who is appointed by will is liable for what is handed over to him if he finds its owner, the one whom he was commanded to hand it over to. But if he does not find him, then there is no liability upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Hastening Zakat and Delaying It Beyond the Times in Which It Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man to whom a brother of his sent zakat so that he would distribute it, and it was lost.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no liability upon the messenger, nor upon the one who pays it.” So I (narrator) asked: “Then if he does not find people entitled to it, and it spoils and changes, is he liable for it?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. But if he knows people entitled to it, and it perishes or spoils, then he is liable for it from the time he delayed it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ بَعَثَ إِلَيْهِ أَخٌ لَهُ زَكَاةً لِيَقْسِمَهَا فَضَاعَتْ فَقَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلرَّسُولِ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْمُؤَدِّي ضَمَانٌ« فَقُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ لَهَا أَهْلاً فَفَسَدَتْ وَ تَغَيَّرَتْ أَيَضْمَنُهَا قَالَ» لاَ وَ لَكِنْ إِنْ عَرَفَ لَهَا أَهْلاً فَعَطِبَتْ أَوْ فَسَدَتْ فَهُوَ لَهَا ضَامِنٌ مِنْ حِينَ أَخَّرَهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man to whom a brother of his sent zakat so that he would distribute it, and it was lost.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no liability upon the messenger, nor upon the one who pays it.” So I (narrator) asked: “Then if he does not find people entitled to it, and it spoils and changes, is he liable for it?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. But if he knows people entitled to it, and it perishes or spoils, then he is liable for it from the time he delayed it.”

chapter: Chapter on Categories of the People of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Said, from Zurah, from Samaah:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘zakat, for whom is it proper to take it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is lawful for those whom Allah (swt), described in His Book: ‘(Alms-tax) is only for the poor and the needy, for those employed to administer it, for those whose hearts are to be attracted (to the faith), for (freeing) slaves, for those in debt, for Allah’s (swt) cause, and for (needy) travellers. (This is) an obligation from almighty Allah (swt).’ (Surah At-Tawbah 9:60) And zakat may be lawful for the owner of seven hundred, and unlawful for the owner of fifty dirhams.” So I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “How can this be?” Imam (a.s) said: “If the owner of the seven hundred has many dependants, and if he were to divide it among them it would not suffice him, then let him restrain himself from it and let him take it for his dependants. As for the owner of the fifty, it is unlawful for him if he is alone and is a craftsman who works with it, and he obtains from it what suffices him, if Allah (swt) wills.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘zakat, Is it proper for the owner of a house and a servant?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, unless his house is a house of yield, and from its yield dirhams come out for him that suffice him for himself and his dependants. But if the yield is not enough for himself and his dependants in their food, their clothing, and their needs, without extravagance, then zakat has become lawful for him. But if its yield suffices them, then no.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ لِمَنْ يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا قَالَ» هِيَ تَحِلُّ لِلَّذِينَ وَصَفَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ» لِلْفُقَرٰاءِ وَ اَلْمَسٰاكِينِ وَاَلْعٰامِلِينَ عَلَيْهٰا وَ اَلْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَ فِي اَلرِّقٰابِ وَ اَلْغٰارِمِينَ وَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهَِ وَ اِبْنِ اَلسَّبِيلِ فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللهَِ« وَ قَدْ تَحِلُّ اَلزَّكَاةُ لِصَاحِبِ سَبْعِمِائَةٍ وَتَحْرُمُ عَلَى صَاحِبِ خَمْسِينَ دِرْهَماً« فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ هَذَا فَقَالَ» إِذَا كَانَ صَاحِبُ اَلسَّبْعِمِائَةِ لَهُ عِيَالٌ كَثِيرَةٌ فَلَوْ قَسَمَهَا بَيْنَهُمْ لَمْ تَكْفِهِ فَلْيُعِفَّ عَنْهَا نَفْسُهُ وَلْيَأْخُذْهَا لِعِيَالِهِ وَ أَمَّا صَاحِبُ اَلْخَمْسِينَ فَإِنَّهَا تَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ وَ هُوَ مُحْتَرِفٌ يَعْمَلُ بِهَا وَ هُوَ يُصِيبُ فِيهَا مَا يَكْفِيهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ« قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ هَلْ تَصْلُحُ لِصَاحِبِ اَلدَّارِ وَ اَلْخَادِمِ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ دَارُهُ دَارَ غَلَّةٍ فَيَخْرُجُ لَهُ مِنْ غَلَّتِهَا دَرَاهِمُ تَكْفِيهِ لِنَفْسِهِ وَعِيَالِهِ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنِ اَلْغَلَّةُ تَكْفِيهِ لِنَفْسِهِ وَعِيَالِهِ فِي طَعَامِهِمْ وَكِسْوَتِهِمْ وَحَاجَتِهِمْ فِي غَيْرِ إِسْرَافٍ فَقَدْ حَلَّتْ لَهُ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ غَلَّتُهَا تَكْفِيهِمْ فَلاَ«.

chapter: Chapter on Categories of the People of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim:
They both (Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Have you considered the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: ‘(Alms-tax) is only for the poor and the needy, for those employed to administer it, for those whose hearts are to be attracted (to the faith), for (freeing) slaves, for those in debt, for Allah’s (swt) cause, and for (needy) travellers. (This is) an obligation from almighty Allah (swt).’ (Surah At-Tawbah 9:60) Are all of these given, even if he does not recognize?” Imam (a.s) said: “The Imam gives all of these, as they acknowledge obedience to him.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if they do not recognize?’” Imam (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, if he were to give to the one who recognizes and not to the one who does not recognize, no place would be found for it. Rather, he gives to the one who does not recognize so that he may desire the religion and remain firm upon it. As for today, then neither you nor your companions should give it except to one who recognizes. So whoever you find among these Muslims as one who recognizes, give it to him rather than the people.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “The share of those whose hearts are to be reconciled and the share of freeing slaves are general, and the rest are specific.” He (narrator) said: “I said to Imam (a.s): ‘Then if they are not found?’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no obligation that Allah (swt), the Exalted, has imposed except that people entitled to it are found.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if the charities are not enough for them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Allah (swt) has obligated for the poor in the wealth of the rich that which suffices them. If Allah (swt) had known that this would not suffice them, Allah (swt) would have increased it for them. They have not been deprived because of the obligation of almighty Allah (swt), but they have been deprived because of the withholding of those who withheld their right from them, not because of what Allah (swt) obligated for them. If the people had paid their rights, they would have lived in goodness.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ: أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ رَأَيْتَ قَوْلَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» إِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقٰاتُ لِلْفُقَرٰاءِ وَ اَلْمَسٰاكِينِ وَاَلْعٰامِلِينَ عَلَيْهٰا وَ اَلْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَ فِي اَلرِّقٰابِ وَ اَلْغٰارِمِينَ وَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهَِ وَ اِبْنِ اَلسَّبِيلِ فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللهَِ« أَ كُلُّ هَؤُلاَءِ يُعْطَى وَ إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يَعْرِفُ فَقَالَ» إِنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ يُعْطِي هَؤُلاَءِ جَمِيعاً لِأَنَّهُمْ يُقِرُّونَ لَهُ بِالطَّاعَةِ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ كَانُوا لاَ يَعْرِفُونَ فَقَالَ» يَا زُرَارَةُ لَوْ كَانَ يُعْطِي مَنْ يَعْرِفُ دُونَ مَنْ لاَ يَعْرِفُ لَمْ يُوجَدْ لَهَا مَوْضِعٌ وَإِنَّمَا يُعْطِي مَنْ لاَ يَعْرِفُ لِيَرْغَبَ فِي اَلدِّينِ فَيَثْبُتَ عَلَيْهِ فَأَمَّا اَلْيَوْمَ فَلاَ تُعْطِهَا أَنْتَ وَ أَصْحَابُكَ إِلاَّ مَنْ يَعْرِفُ فَمَنْ وَجَدْتَ مِنْ هَؤُلاَءِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ عَارِفاً فَأَعْطِهِ دُونَ اَلنَّاسِ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» سَهْمُ اَلْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَ سَهْمُ اَلرِّقَابِ عَامٌّ وَ اَلْبَاقِي خَاصُّ« قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُوجَدُوا قَالَ» لاَ يَكُونُ فَرِيضَةٌ فَرَضَهَا اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِلاَّ أَنْ يُوجَدَ لَهَا أَهْلٌ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسَعْهُمُ اَلصَّدَقَاتُ فَقَالَ» إِنَّ اَللَّهَ فَرَضَ لِلْفُقَرَاءِ فِي مَالِ اَلْأَغْنِيَاءِ مَا يَسَعُهُمْ وَ لَوْ عَلِمَ اَللَّهُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ لاَ يَسَعُهُمْ لَزَادَهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ لَمْ يُؤْتَوْا مِنْ قِبَلِ فَرِيضَةِ اَللَّهِ وَ لَكِنْ أُوتُوا مِنْ مَنْعِ مَنْ مَنَعَهُمْ حَقَّهُمْ لاَ مِمَّا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَ لَوْ أَنَّ اَلنَّاسَ أَدَّوْا حُقُوقَهُمْ لَكَانُوا عَائِشِينَ بِخَيْرٍ«.

chapter: Chapter on Categories of the People of Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim mentioned in the Book of Tafsir the detailed explanation of these eight categories, and he (Ali ibn Ibrahim) said:
The Scholar, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, explained them and said: (First category) “‘The poor’ are those who do not ask, because of the saying of almighty Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in Surah al-Baqarah (and Surah At-Tawbah 9:60): ‘(Charity is) for the needy who are too engaged in the cause of Allah (swt) to move about in the land (for work). Those unfamiliar with their situation will think they are not in need (of charity) because they do not beg. You can recognize them by their appearance. They do not beg people persistently. Whatever you give in charity is certainly well known to Allah (swt).’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:273) (Second category) “And ‘the needy’ are the people of religions; men, women, and children have entered into them.” (Third category) “And ‘those who work over it’ are the collectors and gatherers in taking it, collecting it, and preserving it until they deliver it to the one who distributes it.” (Fourth category) “And ‘those whose hearts are to be reconciled,’ they are a people who professed the oneness of Allah (swt) and cast off the worship of those besides the almighty Allah (swt), but the recognition had not entered their hearts that Prophet Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to reconcile them, teach them, and make them recognize, so that they might recognize. Thus He (saws) assigned for them a share in the charities so that they might recognize and become inclined.” (Fifth category) “And ‘in the necks’ refers to a people upon whom expiations have become obligatory in accidental killing, in zihar, in oaths, and in killing game within the sanctuary, and they do not have that with which they may expiate, while they are believers. So Allah (swt) assigned for them a share in the charities so that expiation may be made on their behalf.” (Sixth category) “And ‘the debtors’ are a people upon whom debts have fallen, which they spent in obedience to Allah (swt) without extravagance. Thus it is obligatory upon the Imam to pay on their behalf and release them from the wealth of the charities.” (Seventh category) “And ‘in the way of Allah (swt)’ refers to a people who go out for jihad and do not have that by which they may gain strength, or a people from among the believers who do not have that by which they may perform Hajj, or in all paths of good. Therefore, it is upon the Imam to give them from the wealth of the charities until they become able for Hajj and jihad.” (Eight category) “And ‘the son of the way’ refers to the needy travellers of the road (wayfarers), those who are in journeys in obedience to Allah (swt), then they are cut off and their wealth is lost. Therefore, it is upon the Imam to return them to their homelands from the wealth of the charities.”
arabicText: وَ ذَكَرَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ فِي كِتَابِ اَلتَّفْسِيرِ تَفْصِيلَ هَذِهِ اَلثَّمَانِيَةِ اَلْأَصْنَافِ فَقَالَ فَسَّرَهُمُ اَلْعَالِمُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ:» اَلْفُقَرَاءُ هُمُ اَلَّذِينَ لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ لِقَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي سُورَةِ اَلْبَقَرَةِ» لِلْفُقَرٰاءِ اَلَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهَِ لاٰ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْباً فِي اَلْأَرْضِ يَحْسَبُهُمُ اَلْجٰاهِلُ أَغْنِيٰاءَ مِنَ اَلتَّعَفُّفِ تَعْرِفُهُمْ بِسِيمٰاهُمْ لاٰ يَسْئَلُونَ اَلنّٰاسَ إِلْحٰافاً« وَ اَلْمَسَاكِينُ هُمْ أَهْلُ اَلدِّيَانَاتِ قَدْ دَخَلَ فِيهِمُ اَلرِّجَالُ وَ اَلنِّسَاءُ وَ اَلصِّبْيَانُ» وَاَلْعٰامِلِينَ عَلَيْهٰا« هُمُ اَلسُّعَاةُ وَاَلْجُبَاةُ فِي أَخْذِهَا وَجَمْعِهَا وَحِفْظِهَا حَتَّى يُؤَدُّوهَا إِلَى مَنْ يَقْسِمُهَا وَاَلْمُؤَلَّفَةُ» قُلُوبُهُمْ«« قَالَ» هُمْ قَوْمٌ وَحَّدُوا اَللَّهَ وَخَلَعُوا عِبَادَةَ مَنْ دُونَ اَللَّهِ وَ لَمْ تَدْخُلِ اَلْمَعْرِفَةُ قُلُوبَهُمْ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَكَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمْ وَيُعَرِّفُهُمْ كَيْمَا يَعْرِفُوا فَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ نَصِيباً فِي اَلصَّدَقَاتِ لِكَيْ يَعْرِفُوا وَيَرْغَبُوا» وَفِي اَلرِّقٰابِ« قَوْمٌ لَزِمَتْهُمْ كَفَّارَاتٌ فِي قَتْلِ اَلْخَطَإِ وَفِي اَلظِّهَارِ وَفِي اَلْأَيْمَانِ وَفِي قَتْلِ اَلصَّيْدِ فِي اَلْحَرَمِ وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُمْ مَا يُكَفِّرُونَ وَ هُمْ مُؤْمِنُونَ فَجَعَلَ اَللَّهُ لَهُمْ سَهْماً فِي اَلصَّدَقَاتِ لِيُكَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ» وَ اَلْغٰارِمِينَ« قَوْمٌ قَدْ وَقَعَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ دُيُونٌ أَنْفَقُوهَا فِي طَاعَةِ اَللَّهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِسْرَافٍ فَيَجِبُ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ عَنْهُمْ وَ يَفُكَّهُمْ مِنْ مَالِ اَلصَّدَقَاتِ »وَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهَِ« قَوْمٌ يَخْرُجُونَ فِي اَلْجِهَادِ وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُمْ مَا يَتَقَوَّوْنَ بِهِ أَوْ قَوْمٌ مِنَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُمْ مَا يَحُجُّونَ بِهِ أَوْ فِي جَمِيعِ سُبُلِ اَلْخَيْرِ فَعَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُمْ مِنْ مَالِ اَلصَّدَقَاتِ حَتَّى يَقْوَوْا عَلَى اَلْحَجِّ وَ اَلْجِهَادِ وَ اِبْنُ» اَلسَّبِيلِ« أَبْنَاءُ اَلطَّرِيقِ اَلَّذِينَ يَكُونُونَ فِي اَلْأَسْفَارِ فِي طَاعَةِ اَللَّهِ فَيُقْطَعُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ يَذْهَبُ مَالُهُمْ فَعَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمْ إِلَى أَوْطَانِهِمْ مِنْ مَالِ اَلصَّدَقَاتِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim mentioned in the Book of Tafsir the detailed explanation of these eight categories, and he (Ali ibn Ibrahim) said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Scholar, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, explained them and said: (First category) “‘The poor’ are those who do not ask, because of the saying of almighty Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in Surah al-Baqarah (and Surah At-Tawbah 9:60): ‘(Charity is) for the needy who are too engaged in the cause of Allah (swt) to move about in the land (for work). Those unfamiliar with their situation will think they are not in need (of charity) because they do not beg. You can recognize them by their appearance. They do not beg people persistently. Whatever you give in charity is certainly well known to Allah (swt).’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:273) (Second category) “And ‘the needy’ are the people of religions; men, women, and children have entered into them.” (Third category) “And ‘those who work over it’ are the collectors and gatherers in taking it, collecting it, and preserving it until they deliver it to the one who distributes it.” (Fourth category) “And ‘those whose hearts are to be reconciled,’ they are a people who professed the oneness of Allah (swt) and cast off the worship of those besides the almighty Allah (swt), but the recognition had not entered their hearts that Prophet Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, used to reconcile them, teach them, and make them recognize, so that they might recognize. Thus He (saws) assigned for them a share in the charities so that they might recognize and become inclined.” (Fifth category) “And ‘in the necks’ refers to a people upon whom expiations have become obligatory in accidental killing, in zihar, in oaths, and in killing game within the sanctuary, and they do not have that with which they may expiate, while they are believers. So Allah (swt) assigned for them a share in the charities so that expiation may be made on their behalf.” (Sixth category) “And ‘the debtors’ are a people upon whom debts have fallen, which they spent in obedience to Allah (swt) without extravagance. Thus it is obligatory upon the Imam to pay on their behalf and release them from the wealth of the charities.” (Seventh category) “And ‘in the way of Allah (swt)’ refers to a people who go out for jihad and do not have that by which they may gain strength, or a people from among the believers who do not have that by which they may perform Hajj, or in all paths of good. Therefore, it is upon the Imam to give them from the wealth of the charities until they become able for Hajj and jihad.” (Eight category) “And ‘the son of the way’ refers to the needy travellers of the road (wayfarers), those who are in journeys in obedience to Allah (swt), then they are cut off and their wealth is lost. Therefore, it is upon the Imam to return them to their homelands from the wealth of the charities.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 65

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamzah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “It has been narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that He (saws) said: ‘Charity is not lawful for a rich person, nor for one possessing strength and soundness.’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not proper for a rich person.” He (narrator) said: “Then I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man has three hundred dirhams in merchandise, and he has dependents. If he turns to it, his dependents would consume it, and they would not be sufficed by its profit.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should look at what surplus he obtains from it, and he should eat from it, he and whoever among them that suffices; and he should take for those among his dependents whom it does not suffice.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ حَمْزَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ» لاَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّدَقَةُ لِغَنِيٍّ وَلاَ لِذِي مِرَّةٍ سَوِيٍّ« فَقَالَ» لاَ تَصْلُحُ لِغَنِيٍّ« قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ لَهُ ثَلاَثُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فِي بِضَاعَةٍ وَ لَهُ عِيَالٌ فَإِنْ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا أَكَلَهَا عِيَالُهُ وَ لَمْ يَكْتَفُوا بِرِبْحِهَا قَالَ» فَلْيَنْظُرْ مَا يَسْتَفْضِلُ مِنْهَا فَيَأْكُلَهُ هُوَ وَ مَنْ يَسَعُهُ ذَلِكَ وَ لْيَأْخُذْ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَسَعْهُ مِنْ عِيَالِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “It has been narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that He (saws) said: ‘Charity is not lawful for a rich person, nor for one possessing strength and soundness.’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not proper for a rich person.” He (narrator) said: “Then I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man has three hundred dirhams in merchandise, and he has dependents. If he turns to it, his dependents would consume it, and they would not be sufficed by its profit.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then he should look at what surplus he obtains from it, and he should eat from it, he and whoever among them that suffices; and he should take for those among his dependents whom it does not suffice.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 66

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim. Zurarah said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “If there is more than one in the city?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then give to all of them, if you are able.” He (narrator) said: “Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘It is not lawful for one who has forty dirhams with him, upon which a year passes while they are with him, to take it; and if he takes it, he has taken it unlawfully.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ اِبْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَإِنْ كَانَ بِالْمِصْرِ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ قَالَ» فَأَعْطِهِمْ إِنْ قَدَرْتَ جَمِيعاً« قَالَ ثُمَّ قَالَ» لاَ تَحِلُّ لِمَنْ كَانَتْ عِنْدَهُ أَرْبَعُونَ دِرْهَماً يَحُولُ عَلَيْهَا اَلْحَوْلُ عِنْدَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا وَ إِنْ أَخَذَهَا أَخَذَهَا حَرَاماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim. Zurarah said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “If there is more than one in the city?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then give to all of them, if you are able.” He (narrator) said: “Then Imam (a.s) said: ‘It is not lawful for one who has forty dirhams with him, upon which a year passes while they are with him, to take it; and if he takes it, he has taken it unlawfully.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man while he thinks that he is in difficulty, then he finds him to be well-off.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It does not suffice on his behalf.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ يُعْطِي زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ رَجُلاً وَ هُوَ يَرَى أَنَّهُ مُعْسِرٌ فَوَجَدَهُ مُوسِراً قَالَ» لاَ يُجْزِي عَنْهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man while he thinks that he is in difficulty, then he finds him to be well-off.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It does not suffice on his behalf.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from more than one person, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
The Imams (a.s) were asked about ‘a man who has a house, a servant, and a slave. May he accept zakat?’ They both (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed the house and the servant are not property.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْجُهَنِيِّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُمَا سُئِلاَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لَهُ دَارٌ وَخَادِمٌ وَعَبْدٌ يَقْبَلُ اَلزَّكَاةَ فَقَالاَ» نَعَمْ إِنَّ اَلدَّارَ وَاَلْخَادِمَ لَيْسَا بِمِلْكٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from more than one person, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Imams (a.s) were asked about ‘a man who has a house, a servant, and a slave. May he accept zakat?’ They both (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed the house and the servant are not property.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 69

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Yahya ibn Isa, from Said ibn Yasar, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Zakat is lawful for the owner of a house and a servant,” Because Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, did not regard the house and the servant as anything (that eliminates the receiver from Zakat).
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» تَحِلُّ اَلزَّكَاةُ لِصَاحِبِ اَلدَّارِ وَ اَلْخَادِمِ« لِأَنَّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَرَى اَلدَّارَ وَ اَلْخَادِمَ شَيْئاً.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Yahya ibn Isa, from Said ibn Yasar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Zakat is lawful for the owner of a house and a servant,” Because Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, did not regard the house and the servant as anything (that eliminates the receiver from Zakat).

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is for the people of wilayah; Allah (swt) has clarified for you its place in His (azj) Book.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَاِبْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ:» اَلزَّكَاةُ لِأَهْلِ اَلْوَلاَيَةِ قَدْ بَيَّنَ اَللَّهُ لَكُمْ مَوْضِعَهَا فِي كِتَابِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is for the people of wilayah; Allah (swt) has clarified for you its place in His (azj) Book.”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:
Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih said to me: “Convey my greetings of peace to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and inform him that fright befalls me in my sleep.” He (narrator) said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): “Shihab conveys greetings of peace to you and says: ‘Fright befalls me in my sleep.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Say to Shihab: ‘Let him give zakat on his wealth.’” He (narrator) said: “So I conveyed that to Shihab, and Shihab said to me, ‘Will you convey from me to him?’” So I (narrator) said: “Yes.” He (Shihab) said: “Say to Imam (a.s) that indeed, children, let alone men, know that I give zakat.’” He (narrator) said: “So I conveyed it to Imam (a.s), and Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: ‘Say to Shihab; Indeed, you take it out, but you do not place it in its proper places.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ بْنِ صَبِيحٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي شِهَابُ بْنُ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ أَقْرِئْ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِّي اَلسَّلاَمَ وَ أَعْلِمْهُ أَنَّهُ يُصِيبُنِي فَزَعٌ فِي مَنَامِي قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ شِهَاباً يُقْرِئُكَ اَلسَّلاَمَ وَ يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ يُصِيبُنِي فَزَعٌ فِي مَنَامِي قَالَ» قُلْ لَهُ فَلْيُزَكِّ مَالَهُ« قَالَ فَأَبْلَغْتُ شِهَاباً ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِي فَتُبْلِغُهُ عَنِّي فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ قُلْ لَهُ إِنَّ اَلصِّبْيَانَ فَضْلاً عَنِ اَلرِّجَالِ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي أُزَكِّي قَالَ فَأَبْلَغْتُهُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» قُلْ لَهُ إِنَّكَ تُخْرِجُهَا وَ لاَ تَضَعُهَا مَوَاضِعَهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih said to me: “Convey my greetings of peace to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and inform him that fright befalls me in my sleep.” He (narrator) said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): “Shihab conveys greetings of peace to you and says: ‘Fright befalls me in my sleep.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Say to Shihab: ‘Let him give zakat on his wealth.’” He (narrator) said: “So I conveyed that to Shihab, and Shihab said to me, ‘Will you convey from me to him?’” So I (narrator) said: “Yes.” He (Shihab) said: “Say to Imam (a.s) that indeed, children, let alone men, know that I give zakat.’” He (narrator) said: “So I conveyed it to Imam (a.s), and Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: ‘Say to Shihab; Indeed, you take it out, but you do not place it in its proper places.’”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Sad al-Ashari, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘zakat, Is it to be placed among one who does not recognize?’ – meaning wilayah. Imam (a.s) said: “No, nor the zakat of al-fitrah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ هَلْ تُوضَعُ فِيمَنْ لاَ يَعْرِفُ قَالَ» لاَ وَ لاَ زَكَاةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Sad al-Ashari, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘zakat, Is it to be placed among one who does not recognize?’ – meaning wilayah. Imam (a.s) said: “No, nor the zakat of al-fitrah.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘one who drinks wine, Is he given anything from zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ شَارِبِ اَلْخَمْرِ يُعْطَى مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ شَيْئاً قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘one who drinks wine, Is he given anything from zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Ibrahim al-Awsi, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said that I heard my father (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)) saying: “I was with my father (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) one day, when a man came to him and said: ‘I am a man from the people of al-Rayy, and I have zakat, so to whom should I pay it?’ He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “To us.” So the man asked: “Is charity not forbidden for you?” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Yes. When you pay it to our Shia, then you have paid it to us.” So the man asked: “I do not know anyone for it.” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Wait with it for one year.” The man said: “If I do not find anyone for it?” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Wait with it for two years,” until Imam (a.s) reached four years. Then he (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said to the man: “If you do not find anyone for it, then tie it into bundles and throw it into the sea, for Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden our wealth and the wealth of our Shia to our enemy.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُمْهُورٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْأَوْسِيِّ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي يَقُولُ: »كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي يَوْماً فَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلرَّيِّ وَ لِي زَكَاةٌ فَإِلَى مَنْ أَدْفَعُهَا قَالَ» إِلَيْنَا« فَقَالَ أَلَيْسَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ مُحَرَّمَةً عَلَيْكُمْ فَقَالَ» بَلَى إِذَا دَفَعْتَهَا إِلَى شِيعَتِنَا فَقَدْ دَفَعْتَهَا إِلَيْنَا« فَقَالَ إِنِّي لاَ أَعْرِفُ لَهَا أَحَداً فَقَالَ »اِنْتَظِرْ بِهَا إِلَى سَنَةٍ« قَالَ فَإِنْ لَمْ أُصِبْ لَهَا أَحَداً قَالَ» اِنْتَظِرْ بِهَا إِلَى سَنَتَيْنِ حَتَّى بَلَغَ أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ« ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ» إِنْ لَمْ تُصِبْ لَهَا أَحَداً فَصُرَّهَا صِرَاراً وَاِطْرَحْهَا فِي اَلْبَحْرِ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَرَّمَ أَمْوَالَنَا وَ أَمْوَالَ شِيعَتِنَا عَلَى عَدُوِّنَا««.
thaqalaynSanad: Sad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Ibrahim al-Awsi, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said that I heard my father (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)) saying: “I was with my father (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) one day, when a man came to him and said: ‘I am a man from the people of al-Rayy, and I have zakat, so to whom should I pay it?’ He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “To us.” So the man asked: “Is charity not forbidden for you?” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Yes. When you pay it to our Shia, then you have paid it to us.” So the man asked: “I do not know anyone for it.” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Wait with it for one year.” The man said: “If I do not find anyone for it?” He (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “Wait with it for two years,” until Imam (a.s) reached four years. Then he (Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)) said to the man: “If you do not find anyone for it, then tie it into bundles and throw it into the sea, for Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden our wealth and the wealth of our Shia to our enemy.”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s) asking: “Is it permissible for me to pay the zakat of wealth and charity to a needy person who is not from my companions?” Imam (a.s) wrote: “Do not give charity and zakat except to your companions.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ أَدْفَعَ زَكَاةَ اَلْمَالِ وَ اَلصَّدَقَةَ إِلَى مُحْتَاجٍ غَيْرِ أَصْحَابِي فَكَتَبَ» لاَ تُعْطِ اَلصَّدَقَةَ وَ اَلزَّكَاةَ إِلاَّ لِأَصْحَابِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s) asking: “Is it permissible for me to pay the zakat of wealth and charity to a needy person who is not from my companions?” Imam (a.s) wrote: “Do not give charity and zakat except to your companions.”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘charity upon the Nussab (Nawasib) and upon the Zaydiyyah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give charity to them with anything, and do not give them water to drink, if you are able.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Zaydiyyah are the Nussab.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّدَقَةِ عَلَى اَلنُّصَّابِ وَ عَلَى اَلزَّيْدِيَّةِ قَالَ» لاَ تَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِشَيْءٍ وَ لاَ تَسْقِهِمْ مِنَ اَلْمَاءِ إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْتَ« وَ قَالَ» اَلزَّيْدِيَّةُ هُمُ اَلنُّصَّابُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘charity upon the Nussab (Nawasib) and upon the Zaydiyyah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give charity to them with anything, and do not give them water to drink, if you are able.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Zaydiyyah are the Nussab.”
