chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, what do you say ‘concerning zakat, for whom is it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is for your companions.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is anything from it given to beggars?’” He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “No, by Allah (swt), except dust, unless you have mercy on him. So if you have mercy on him, then give him a fragment.” Then Imam (a.s) gestured with his hand and placed his thumb upon the roots of his fingers.
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ لِمَنْ هِيَ قَالَ فَقَالَ» هِيَ لِأَصْحَابِكَ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ فَضَلَ عَنْهُمْ فَقَالَ »فَأَعِدْ عَلَيْهِمْ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ فَضَلَ عَنْهُمْ قَالَ» فَأَعِدْ عَلَيْهِمْ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ فَضَلَ عَنْهُمْ قَالَ» فَأَعِدْ عَلَيْهِمْ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَيُعْطَى اَلسُّؤَّالُ مِنْهَا شَيْئاً قَالَ فَقَالَ» لاَ وَ اَللَّهِ إِلاَّ اَلتُّرَابَ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَرْحَمَهُ فَإِنْ رَحِمْتَهُ فَأَعْطِهِ كِسْرَةً« ثُمَّ أَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ فَوَضَعَ إِبْهَامَهُ عَلَى أُصُولِ أَصَابِعِهِ.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, what do you say ‘concerning zakat, for whom is it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is for your companions.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then if there is surplus beyond them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then return it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then is anything from it given to beggars?’” He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “No, by Allah (swt), except dust, unless you have mercy on him. So if you have mercy on him, then give him a fragment.” Then Imam (a.s) gestured with his hand and placed his thumb upon the roots of his fingers.

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Zakat Due to Poverty and Destitution from Among the Categories
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, Bukayr, al-Fudayl, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd al-Ijli, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who is upon some of these doctrines: the Haruriyyah (Kharijites), the Murjiah (Murji'ites), the Uthmaniyyah (adherents to Uthman), and the Qadariyyah (Sufi inclied tariqa), then he repents, recognizes this matter, and his view becomes good. Thus, must he repeat every prayer he prayed, or fast, or zakat, or Hajj, or is there no repetition of any of that upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no repetition of anything from that upon him except zakat, and he must certainly pay it, because he placed zakat in other than its proper place, and its proper place is only the people of wilayah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ بُكَيْرٍ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ بُرَيْدٍ اَلْعِجْلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي بَعْضِ هَذِهِ اَلْأَهْوَاءِ اَلْحَرُورِيَّةِ وَ اَلْمُرْجِئَةِ وَاَلْعُثْمَانِيَّةِ وَاَلْقَدَرِيَّةِ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ وَ يَعْرِفُ هَذَا اَلْأَمْرَ وَ يَحْسُنُ رَأْيُهُ أَ يُعِيدُ كُلَّ صَلاَةٍ صَلاَّهَا أَوْ صَوْمٍ أَوْ زَكَاةٍ أَوْ حَجٍّ أَوْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ غَيْرِ اَلزَّكَاةِ وَ لاَ بُدَّ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا لِأَنَّهُ وَضَعَ اَلزَّكَاةَ فِي غَيْرِ مَوْضِعِهَا وَإِنَّمَا مَوْضِعُهَا أَهْلُ اَلْوَلاَيَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, Bukayr, al-Fudayl, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd al-Ijli, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who is upon some of these doctrines: the Haruriyyah (Kharijites), the Murjiah (Murji'ites), the Uthmaniyyah (adherents to Uthman), and the Qadariyyah (Sufi inclied tariqa), then he repents, recognizes this matter, and his view becomes good. Thus, must he repeat every prayer he prayed, or fast, or zakat, or Hajj, or is there no repetition of any of that upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no repetition of anything from that upon him except zakat, and he must certainly pay it, because he placed zakat in other than its proper place, and its proper place is only the people of wilayah.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Jafar, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man from among your mawali has relatives, all of whom profess belief in you (wilayah), and he has zakat. Is it permissible for him to give them all of his zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَمْزَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ مَوَالِيكَ لَهُ قَرَابَةٌ كُلُّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ بِكَ وَ لَهُ زَكَاةٌ أَ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُمْ جَمِيعَ زَكَاتِهِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Jafar, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man from among your mawali has relatives, all of whom profess belief in you (wilayah), and he has zakat. Is it permissible for him to give them all of his zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who places all of his zakat among the people of his household, while they have wilayah toward you (the Imams (a.s)).’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَضَعُ زَكَاتَهُ كُلَّهَا فِي أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ هُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَكَ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who places all of his zakat among the people of his household, while they have wilayah toward you (the Imams (a.s)).’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna, from Abu Basir, who said:
A man asked Imam (a.s) while I was listening, and he asked: “May I give my relatives from the zakat of my wealth, while they do not recognize you?” – meaning wilayah. He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give zakat except to a Muslim, and give them from other than that.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Do you think that there is nothing due in wealth except zakat alone? What Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in wealth besides zakat is greater than what you give from it to relatives and to those who come before you from among those who ask you, so you give to them, so long as you do not know them to be upon hostility (nasb/nawasib). But when you know him to be upon hostility (nasb), then do not give him, unless you fear his tongue, so you purchase your religion and your honor from him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ مُثَنًّى عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ فَقَالَ أُعْطِي قَرَابَتِي مِنْ زَكَاةِ مَالِي وَ هُمْ لاَ يَعْرِفُونَكَ قَالَ فَقَالَ» لاَ تُعْطِ اَلزَّكَاةَ إِلاَّ مُسْلِماً وَأَعْطِهِمْ مِنْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ« ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» أَتَرَوْنَ إِنَّمَا فِي اَلْمَالِ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَحْدَهَا مَا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي اَلْمَالِ مِنْ غَيْرِ اَلزَّكَاةِ أَكْثَرُ مِمَّا تُعْطِي مِنْهُ اَلْقَرَابَةَ وَاَلْمُعْتَرِضَ لَكَ مِمَّنْ يَسْأَلُكَ فَتُعْطِيهِ مَا لَمْ تَعْرِفْهُ بِالنَّصْبِ فَإِذَا عَرَفْتَهُ بِالنَّصْبِ فَلاَ تُعْطِهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَخَافَ لِسَانَهُ فَتَشْتَرِيَ دِينَكَ وَعِرْضَكَ مِنْهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked Imam (a.s) while I was listening, and he asked: “May I give my relatives from the zakat of my wealth, while they do not recognize you?” – meaning wilayah. He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give zakat except to a Muslim, and give them from other than that.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Do you think that there is nothing due in wealth except zakat alone? What Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in wealth besides zakat is greater than what you give from it to relatives and to those who come before you from among those who ask you, so you give to them, so long as you do not know them to be upon hostility (nasb/nawasib). But when you know him to be upon hostility (nasb), then do not give him, unless you fear his tongue, so you purchase your religion and your honor from him.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has relatives, mawali, and orphans who love the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, but do not recognize the master of this matter (rightful Imam of the time). Are they to be given from zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لَهُ قَرَابَةٌ وَمَوَالٍ وَأَيْتَامٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ لَيْسَ يَعْرِفُونَ صَاحِبَ هَذَا اَلْأَمْرِ أَ يُعْطَوْنَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has relatives, mawali, and orphans who love the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, but do not recognize the master of this matter (rightful Imam of the time). Are they to be given from zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zurah, from Samaah, and Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has zakat due upon him, and he has needy relatives who are not recognizers (of wilayah). Should he give them from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, and no honor. He must not make zakat a protection for his wealth. He may give them from other than zakat, if he wishes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ لَهُ قَرَابَةٌ مُحْتَاجُونَ غَيْرُ عَارِفِينَ أَ يُعْطِيهِمْ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَقَالَ» لاَ وَ لاَ كَرَامَةَ لاَ يَجْعَلُ اَلزَّكَاةَ وِقَايَةً لِمَالِهِ يُعْطِيهِمْ مِنْ غَيْرِ اَلزَّكَاةِ إِنْ أَرَادَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zurah, from Samaah, and Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has zakat due upon him, and he has needy relatives who are not recognizers (of wilayah). Should he give them from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, and no honor. He must not make zakat a protection for his wealth. He may give them from other than zakat, if he wishes.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “I have relatives and I spend on some of them and prefer some of them over others. Then the time of zakat comes to me, may I give them from it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Are they entitled to it?” I (narrator) replied: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are better than others (non-relatives); give them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then who is it among my relatives whose maintenance is binding upon me, so that I may not count zakat upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Your father and your mother.” I (narrator) asked: “My father and my mother?” Imam (a.s) said: “The parents and the child.”

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

Then the time of zakat comes to me, may I give them from it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Are they entitled to it?” I (narrator) replied: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are better than others (non-relatives); give them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then who is it among my relatives whose maintenance is binding upon me, so that I may not count zakat upon him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Your father and your mother.” I (narrator) asked: “My father and my mother?” Imam (a.s) said: “The parents and the child.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Five are not to be given anything from zakat; the father, the mother, the child, the owned slave, and the wife. And that is because they are his dependents, bound to him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ:» خَمْسَةٌ لاَ يُعْطَوْنَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ شَيْئاً اَلْأَبُ وَاَلْأُمُّ وَاَلْوَلَدُ وَاَلْمَمْلُوكُ وَاَلْمَرْأَةُ وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ عِيَالُهُ لاَزِمُونَ لَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Five are not to be given anything from zakat; the father, the mother, the child, the owned slave, and the wife. And that is because they are his dependents, bound to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 75

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “In zakat; the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt are given from it. But the grandfather is not given, nor the grandmother.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ وَغَيْرِهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ يُعْطَى مِنْهَا اَلْأَخُ وَ اَلْأُخْتُ وَاَلْعَمُّ وَاَلْعَمَّةُ وَاَلْخَالُ وَاَلْخَالَةُ وَ لاَ يُعْطَى اَلْجَدُّ وَ لاَ اَلْجَدَّةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “In zakat; the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt are given from it. But the grandfather is not given, nor the grandmother.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him: “I have children, men and women; is it permissible for me to give them from zakat?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “That is permissible for you.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عِمْرَانَ اَلْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ لِي وُلْداً رِجَالاً وَ نِسَاءً أَفَيَجُوزُ أَنْ أُعْطِيَهُمْ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» أَنَّ ذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ لَكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him: “I have children, men and women; is it permissible for me to give them from zakat?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “That is permissible for you.”

chapter: Chapter on Relatives for Whom Zakat Is Lawful and for Whom It Is Unlawful
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give from zakat to anyone whom you maintain.” And he (narrator) asked: “If a man has five hundred dirhams and his dependents are many.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon him; he spends it on his dependents, increasing it in their maintenance, in their clothing, and in food which they had not been eating. And if he does not have dependents and is alone, then let him distribute it among people in whom there is no harm, chaste from asking, who do not ask anyone for anything.” And Imam (a.s) said: “You must not give all of the zakat to your relatives, but give them some and distribute some among the rest of the Muslims.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is lawful for the owner of a house and a servant, and for one who has five hundred dirhams, provided that he has dependents. And he makes the zakat of the five hundred an increase in the maintenance of his dependents, expanding upon them.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تُعْطِ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ أَحَداً مِمَّنْ تَعُولُ« وَ قَالَ إِذَا كَانَ لِرَجُلٍ خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ وَ كَانَ عِيَالُهُ كَثِيراً قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ يُنْفِقُهَا عَلَى عِيَالِهِ يَزِيدُهَا فِي نَفَقَتِهِمْ وَ فِي كِسْوَتِهِمْ وَ فِي طَعَامٍ لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَطْعَمُونَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ عِيَالٌ وَ كَانَ وَحْدَهُ فَلْيَقْسِمْهَا فِي قَوْمٍ لَيْسَ بِهِمْ بَأْسٌ أَعِفَّاءَ عَنِ اَلْمَسْأَلَةِ لاَ يَسْأَلُونَ أَحَداً شَيْئاً« وَ قَالَ» لاَ تُعْطِيَنَّ قَرَابَتَكَ اَلزَّكَاةَ كُلَّهَا وَ لَكِنْ أَعْطِهِمْ بَعْضاً وَاِقْسِمْ بَعْضاً فِي سَائِرِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ« وَ قَالَ» اَلزَّكَاةُ تَحِلُّ لِصَاحِبِ اَلدَّارِ وَ اَلْخَادِمِ وَمَنْ كَانَ لَهُ خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ عِيَالٌ وَيَجْعَلُ زَكَاةَ اَلْخَمْسِمِائَةِ زِيَادَةً فِي نَفَقَةِ عِيَالِهِ يُوَسِّعُ عَلَيْهِمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give from zakat to anyone whom you maintain.” And he (narrator) asked: “If a man has five hundred dirhams and his dependents are many.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon him; he spends it on his dependents, increasing it in their maintenance, in their clothing, and in food which they had not been eating. And if he does not have dependents and is alone, then let him distribute it among people in whom there is no harm, chaste from asking, who do not ask anyone for anything.” And Imam (a.s) said: “You must not give all of the zakat to your relatives, but give them some and distribute some among the rest of the Muslims.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat is lawful for the owner of a house and a servant, and for one who has five hundred dirhams, provided that he has dependents. And he makes the zakat of the five hundred an increase in the maintenance of his dependents, expanding upon them.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, some people from Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and asked Him (saws) to appoint them over the charities of the livestock. They said: “This share which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has assigned for those who work over it would be for us, and we are more entitled to it.” So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, charity is not lawful for Me (saws) nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Bear witness, the Prophet (saws) was certainly promised it (intercession). So what do you think, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the gate of Paradise? Do you see me preferring others over you?”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِنَّ أُنَاساً مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ أَتَوْا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَسَأَلُوهُ أَنْ يَسْتَعْمِلَهُمْ عَلَى صَدَقَاتِ اَلْمَوَاشِي وَ قَالُوا يَكُونُ لَنَا هَذَا اَلسَّهْمُ اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِلْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا فَنَحْنُ أَوْلَى بِهِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ اَلْمُطَّلِبِ إِنَّ اَلصَّدَقَةَ لاَ تَحِلُّ لِي وَ لاَ لَكُمْ وَ لَكِنِّي قَدْ وُعِدْتُ اَلشَّفَاعَةَ«« ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» اِشْهَدُوا لَقَدْ وُعِدَهَا فَمَا ظَنُّكُمْ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ اَلْمُطَّلِبِ إِذَا أَخَذْتُ بِحَلْقَةِ بَابِ اَلْجَنَّةِ أَتَرَوْنِي مُؤْثِراً عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَكُمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, some people from Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and asked Him (saws) to appoint them over the charities of the livestock. They said: “This share which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has assigned for those who work over it would be for us, and we are more entitled to it.” So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, charity is not lawful for Me (saws) nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Bear witness, the Prophet (saws) was certainly promised it (intercession). So what do you think, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the gate of Paradise? Do you see me preferring others over you?”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who both said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, charity is the impurities of the hands of the people, and indeed Allah (swt) has forbidden for me from it, and from other than it, what He (azj) has forbidden. For charity is not lawful for Banu Abd al-Muttalib.” Then the Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, by Allah (swt), if I were to stand at the gate of Paradise and then take hold of its ring, you would certainly know that I do not prefer others over you. So be pleased for yourselves with what Allah (swt) and His Messenger (saws) are pleased with for you.” They (Banu Abd al-Muttalib) said: “We are pleased.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ:» قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» إِنَّ اَلصَّدَقَةَ أَوْسَاخُ أَيْدِي اَلنَّاسِ وَ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ حَرَّمَ عَلَيَّ مِنْهَا وَ مِنْ غَيْرِهَا مَا قَدْ حَرَّمَهُ فَإِنَّ اَلصَّدَقَةَ لاَ تَحِلُّ لِبَنِي عَبْدِ اَلْمُطَّلِبِ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» أَمَا وَ اَللَّهِ لَوْ قَدْ قُمْتُ عَلَى بَابِ اَلْجَنَّةِ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ بِحَلْقَتِهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ أَنِّي لاَ أُوثِرُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَارْضَوْا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ بِمَا رَضِيَ اَللَّهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ لَكُمْ« قَالُوا رَضِينَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who both said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Indeed, charity is the impurities of the hands of the people, and indeed Allah (swt) has forbidden for me from it, and from other than it, what He (azj) has forbidden. For charity is not lawful for Banu Abd al-Muttalib.” Then the Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, by Allah (swt), if I were to stand at the gate of Paradise and then take hold of its ring, you would certainly know that I do not prefer others over you. So be pleased for yourselves with what Allah (swt) and His Messenger (saws) are pleased with for you.” They (Banu Abd al-Muttalib) said: “We are pleased.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity which was forbidden for Banu Hashim, what is it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is zakat.” I (narrator) asked: “Then is the charity of some of them (Banu Hashim) lawful for others among them (other Banu Hashim)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّدَقَةِ اَلَّتِي حُرِّمَتْ عَلَى بَنِي هَاشِمٍ مَا هِيَ فَقَالَ» هِيَ اَلزَّكَاةُ« قُلْتُ فَتَحِلُّ صَدَقَةُ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity which was forbidden for Banu Hashim, what is it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is zakat.” I (narrator) asked: “Then is the charity of some of them (Banu Hashim) lawful for others among them (other Banu Hashim)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Fadl ibn Salih, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity which was forbidden for them (Banu Hashim).’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is the obligatory zakat, and the charity of some of us (Banu Hashim) to others among us (Banu Hashim) has not been forbidden for us.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّدَقَةِ اَلَّتِي حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالَ» هِيَ اَلزَّكَاةُ اَلْمَفْرُوضَةُ وَ لَمْ تُحَرَّمْ عَلَيْنَا صَدَقَةُ بَعْضِنَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Fadl ibn Salih, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity which was forbidden for them (Banu Hashim).’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is the obligatory zakat, and the charity of some of us (Banu Hashim) to others among us (Banu Hashim) has not been forbidden for us.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Charity is not lawful for the children of al-Abbas, nor for their counterparts from Banu Hashim.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّدَقَةُ لِوُلْدِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ وَ لاَ لِنُظَرَائِهِمْ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Charity is not lawful for the children of al-Abbas, nor for their counterparts from Banu Hashim.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Their mawali (owned slaves) are from them, and charity from a stranger is not lawful for their mawali, and there is no harm in the charities of their mawali being given to them.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, if justice existed, no ‘Hashimi’ (Banu Hashim) nor ‘Muttalibi’ (Banu Abd al-Muttalib) would need charity. Indeed, Allah (swt) has placed for them in His (swt) Book (Quran) that wherein there is their sufficiency.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, when a man does not find anything, carrion and charity become lawful for him; and it is not lawful for any one of them unless he does not find anything and is among those for whom carrion is lawful.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَوَالِيهِمْ مِنْهُمْ وَ لاَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّدَقَةُ مِنَ اَلْغَرِيبِ لِمَوَالِيهِمْ وَلاَ بَأْسَ بِصَدَقَاتِ مَوَالِيهِمْ عَلَيْهِمْ« ثُمَّ قَالَ »إِنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ اَلْعَدْلُ مَا اِحْتَاجَ هَاشِمِيٌّ وَ لاَ مُطَّلِبِيٌّ إِلَى صَدَقَةٍ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ جَعَلَ لَهُمْ فِي كِتَابِهِ مَا كَانَ فِيهِ سَعَتُهُمْ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ إِذَا لَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئاً حَلَّتْ لَهُ اَلْمَيْتَةُ وَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ وَ لاَ تَحِلُّ لِأَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ لاَ يَجِدَ شَيْئاً وَ يَكُونَ مِمَّنْ تَحِلُّ لَهُ اَلْمَيْتَةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Their mawali (owned slaves) are from them, and charity from a stranger is not lawful for their mawali, and there is no harm in the charities of their mawali being given to them.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, if justice existed, no ‘Hashimi’ (Banu Hashim) nor ‘Muttalibi’ (Banu Abd al-Muttalib) would need charity. Indeed, Allah (swt) has placed for them in His (swt) Book (Quran) that wherein there is their sufficiency.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, when a man does not find anything, carrion and charity become lawful for him; and it is not lawful for any one of them unless he does not find anything and is among those for whom carrion is lawful.”

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): “Is charity lawful for Banu Hashim?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Is it lawful for their mawali?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is lawful for their mawali, but it is not lawful for them, except the charities of some of them to others among them.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ تَحِلُّ لِبَنِي هَاشِمٍ اَلصَّدَقَةُ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ تَحِلُّ لِمَوَالِيهِمْ قَالَ» تَحِلُّ لِمَوَالِيهِمْ وَ لاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُمْ إِلاَّ صَدَقَاتُ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): “Is charity lawful for Banu Hashim?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Is it lawful for their mawali?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is lawful for their mawali, but it is not lawful for them, except the charities of some of them to others among them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 78

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for the report which Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Give from zakat to Banu Hashim, whoever among them wants it, for it is lawful for them. It is only forbidden for the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and for the Imam (a.s) who comes after him, and for the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا اَلْخَبَرُ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» أَعْطُوا مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ مَنْ أَرَادَهَا مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّهَا تَحِلُّ لَهُمْ وَإِنَّمَا تَحْرُمُ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ اَلَّذِي يَكُونُ بَعْدَهُ وَ عَلَى اَلْأَئِمَّةِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for the report which Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Give from zakat to Banu Hashim, whoever among them wants it, for it is lawful for them. It is only forbidden for the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and for the Imam (a.s) who comes after him, and for the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi, who said:
I (narrator) sent dinars to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, on behalf of some of my family, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) informing him that among them was zakat, seventy-five, and the remainder was a gift. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received it.” And I (narrator) sent to Imam (a.s) dinars belonging to me and to others, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) that they were from the fitrah of the dependents. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ: بَعَثْتُ إِلَى اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِدَنَانِيرَ مِنْ قِبَلِ بَعْضِ أَهْلِي وَ كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّ فِيهَا زَكَاةً خَمْسَةً وَ سَبْعِينَ وَ اَلْبَاقِيَ صِلَةٌ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِخَطِّهِ »قَبَضْتُ وَبَعَثْتُ إِلَيْهِ دَنَانِيرَ لِي وَلِغَيْرِي« وَكَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهَا مِنْ فِطْرَةِ اَلْعِيَالِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِخَطِّهِ» قَبَضْتُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) sent dinars to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, on behalf of some of my family, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) informing him that among them was zakat, seventy-five, and the remainder was a gift. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received it.” And I (narrator) sent to Imam (a.s) dinars belonging to me and to others, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) that they were from the fitrah of the dependents. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to ask Shihab for some of his zakat for his mawali, “and zakat was only forbidden for them (the Imams (a.s)), not for their mawali.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَسْأَلُ شِهَاباً مِنْ زَكَاتِهِ لِمَوَالِيهِ» وَ إِنَّمَا حُرِّمَتِ اَلزَّكَاةُ عَلَيْهِمْ دُونَ مَوَالِيهِمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, used to ask Shihab for some of his zakat for his mawali, “and zakat was only forbidden for them (the Imams (a.s)), not for their mawali.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 79

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “The charities of Banu Hashim, of some of them to others among them, are they lawful for them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The charity of the Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is lawful for all people, from Banu Hashim and others besides them. And the charities of some of them (Banu Hashim) to others among them are lawful for them, but the charities of a stranger (non Banu Hashim) are not lawful for them.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ صَدَقَاتُ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ تَحِلُّ لَهُمْ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ صَدَقَةُ اَلرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ تَحِلُّ لِجَمِيعِ اَلنَّاسِ مِنْ بَنِي هَاشِمٍ وَ غَيْرِهِمْ وَ صَدَقَاتُ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ تَحِلُّ لَهُمْ وَ لاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُمْ صَدَقَاتُ إِنْسَانٍ غَرِيبٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “The charities of Banu Hashim, of some of them to others among them, are they lawful for them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The charity of the Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is lawful for all people, from Banu Hashim and others besides them. And the charities of some of them (Banu Hashim) to others among them are lawful for them, but the charities of a stranger (non Banu Hashim) are not lawful for them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam (a.s) said: “If charity had been forbidden for us (Banu Hashim), it would not be lawful for us to go out to Mecca, because every water between Mecca and Madinah is charity.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:» لَوْ حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْنَا اَلصَّدَقَةُ لَمْ يَحِلَّ لَنَا أَنْ نَخْرُجَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ لِأَنَّ كُلَّ مَاءٍ بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ وَ اَلْمَدِينَةِ فَهُوَ صَدَقَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If charity had been forbidden for us (Banu Hashim), it would not be lawful for us to go out to Mecca, because every water between Mecca and Madinah is charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on What Is Lawful for Banu Hashim and Unlawful from Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Jafar ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said: “Is charity lawful for Banu Hashim?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is only the obligatory charity upon the people; it is not lawful for us (Banu Hashim). As for other than that, there is no harm in it. And if it were like that, they (Banu Hashim) would not be able to go out to Mecca; these waters, most of them, are charity.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّدَقَةُ لِبَنِي هَاشِمٍ فَقَالَ» إِنَّمَا تِلْكَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ اَلْوَاجِبَةُ عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ لاَ تَحِلُّ لَنَا فَأَمَّا غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ وَ لَوْ كَانَ كَذَلِكَ مَا اِسْتَطَاعُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا إِلَى مَكَّةَ هَذِهِ اَلْمِيَاهُ عَامَّتُهَا صَدَقَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Jafar ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said: “Is charity lawful for Banu Hashim?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is only the obligatory charity upon the people; it is not lawful for us (Banu Hashim). As for other than that, there is no harm in it. And if it were like that, they (Banu Hashim) would not be able to go out to Mecca; these waters, most of them, are charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 80

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “No one is to be given from zakat less than five dirhams, and it is the least of what Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory from zakat in the wealth of the Muslims. So do not give anyone less than five dirhams and upwards.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي وَلاَّدٍ اَلْحَنَّاطِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:» لاَ يُعْطَى أَحَدٌ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ دَرَاهِمَ وَ هُوَ أَقَلُّ مَا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فِي أَمْوَالِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلاَ تُعْطُوا أَحَداً أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ دَرَاهِمَ فَصَاعِداً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “No one is to be given from zakat less than five dirhams, and it is the least of what Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory from zakat in the wealth of the Muslims. So do not give anyone less than five dirhams and upwards.”

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “It is not permissible for zakat to be paid as less than five dirhams, for it is the least amount of zakat.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ اَلْأَنْصَارِيِّ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:» لاَ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُدْفَعَ اَلزَّكَاةُ أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ دَرَاهِمَ فَإِنَّهَا أَقَلُّ اَلزَّكَاةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “It is not permissible for zakat to be paid as less than five dirhams, for it is the least amount of zakat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 81

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is it permissible for me, my master, to give a man from among my brothers two dirhams and three dirhams from zakat? This has become unclear to me.” Imam (a.s) wrote: “That is permissible.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصُّهْبَانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لِي يَا سَيِّدِي أَنْ أُعْطِيَ اَلرَّجُلَ مِنْ إِخْوَانِي مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ اَلدِّرْهَمَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلدَّرَاهِمِ فَقَدِ اِشْتَبَهَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيَّ فَكَتَبَ» ذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is it permissible for me, my master, to give a man from among my brothers two dirhams and three dirhams from zakat? This has become unclear to me.” Imam (a.s) wrote: “That is permissible.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 81

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Said ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): How much is one man to be given from zakat? Imam (a.s) said: “Give him from zakat until you make him self-sufficient.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ غَزْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ كَمْ يُعْطَى اَلرَّجُلُ اَلْوَاحِدُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ» أَعْطِهِ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ حَتَّى تُغْنِيَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Said ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): How much is one man to be given from zakat? Imam (a.s) said: “Give him from zakat until you make him self-sufficient.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 82

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Give him one thousand dirhams.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» أَعْطِهِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Give him one thousand dirhams.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 82

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Saqr, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I give a man one hundred dirhams from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Two hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) replied: “Three hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Four hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Five hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, until you make him self-sufficient.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلصَّقْرِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَللُّؤْلُؤِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُعْطِي اَلرَّجُلَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ مِائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ مِائَتَيْنِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ ثَلاَثَمِائَةٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ أَرْبَعَمِائَةٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ خَمْسَمِائَةٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ حَتَّى تُغْنِيَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Saqr, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I give a man one hundred dirhams from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Two hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) replied: “Three hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Four hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Five hundred (dirhams)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, until you make him self-sufficient.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 82

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I give a man eighty dirhams from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and increase him.” I (narrator) asked: “May I give him one hundred dirhams?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and make him self-sufficient, if you are able to make him self-sufficient.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أُعْطِي اَلرَّجُلَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ ثَمَانِينَ دِرْهَماً قَالَ» نَعَمْ وَزِدْهُ« قُلْتُ أُعْطِيهِ مِائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ وَ أَغْنِهِ إِنْ قَدَرْتَ عَلَى أَنْ تُغْنِيَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I give a man eighty dirhams from zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and increase him.” I (narrator) asked: “May I give him one hundred dirhams?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and make him self-sufficient, if you are able to make him self-sufficient.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 82

chapter: Chapter on What Must Be Given Out from Charity and the Least Amount That Is Given
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked, “How much is a man to be given from zakat?” He (narrator) said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘When you give, then make him self-sufficient.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ كَمْ يُعْطَى اَلرَّجُلُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» إِذَا أَعْطَيْتَ فَأَغْنِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked, “How much is a man to be given from zakat?” He (narrator) said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘When you give, then make him self-sufficient.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 83

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of All Grains in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘cultivation, what of it is given zakat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Wheat, barley, corn (al-dhurrah), millet (al-dukhn), rice, sult (hulless barley), lentils, and sesame; all of this is given zakat, and what resembles it.”
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن علي بن ابراهيم عن ابيه عن حماد بن عيسى عن حريز عن محمد بن مسلم قال: سألته عليه السلام عن الحرث ما يزكى منه فقال: البر والشعير والذرة والدخن والارز والسلت والعدس والسمسم كل هذا يزكى وأشباهه
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘cultivation, what of it is given zakat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Wheat, barley, corn (al-dhurrah), millet (al-dukhn), rice, sult (hulless barley), lentils, and sesame; all of this is given zakat, and what resembles it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 83

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of All Grains in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: the like of it.
And Imam (a.s) said: “Everything that is measured by the sa’ and reaches the awsaq in which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is due upon it.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, placed charity in everything that the earth produces, except vegetables, herbs, and everything that spoils within its day.”
arabicText: حَرِيزٌ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ : مِثْلَهُ وَ قَالَ »كُلُّمَا كِيلَ بِالصَّاعِ فَبَلَغَ اَلْأَوْسَاقَ اَلَّتِي يَجِبُ فِيهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ« وَقَالَ» جَعَلَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ اَلصَّدَقَةَ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْبَتَتِ اَلْأَرْضُ إِلاَّ اَلْخُضَرَ وَ اَلْبُقُولَ وَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ يَفْسُدُ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: the like of it.
thaqalaynMatn: And Imam (a.s) said: “Everything that is measured by the sa’ and reaches the awsaq in which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is due upon it.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, placed charity in everything that the earth produces, except vegetables, herbs, and everything that spoils within its day.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of All Grains in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there anything due on millet (al-dhurrah)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Millet (al-dhurrah), lentils, barley-like grain (al-sult), and grains, in them is the like of what is in wheat and barley. And everything that is measured by the sa’ and reaches the awsaq in which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is due upon it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلذُّرَةِ شَيْءٌ قَالَ» اَلذُّرَةُ وَاَلْعَدَسُ وَاَلسُّلْتُ وَ اَلْحُبُوبُ فِيهَا مِثْلُ مَا فِي اَلْحِنْطَةِ وَ اَلشَّعِيرِ وَ كُلُّ مَا كِيلَ بِالصَّاعِ فَبَلَغَ اَلْأَوْسَاقَ اَلَّتِي تَجِبُ فِيهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ فَعَلَيْهِ فِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there anything due on millet (al-dhurrah)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Millet (al-dhurrah), lentils, barley-like grain (al-sult), and grains, in them is the like of what is in wheat and barley. And everything that is measured by the sa’ and reaches the awsaq in which zakat becomes obligatory, then zakat is due upon it.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibrahim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there anything due on rice?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Madinah at that time was not a land of rice, so that it would be mentioned regarding it. But it has indeed been placed in it, and how could there not be anything due on it, when most of the land tax (kharaj) of Iraq is from it?”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ فِي اَلْأَرُزِّ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» إِنَّ اَلْمَدِينَةَ لَمْ تَكُنْ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَرْضَ أَرُزٍّ فَيُقَالَ فِيهِ وَ لَكِنَّهُ قَدْ جُعِلَ فِيهِ وَ كَيْفَ لاَ يَكُونُ فِيهِ وَ عَامَّةُ خَرَاجِ اَلْعِرَاقِ مِنْهُ«.

But it has indeed been placed in it, and how could there not be anything due on it, when most of the land tax (kharaj) of Iraq is from it?”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Vegetables in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon vegetables, nor upon melons, nor upon herbs and their like, except what has gathered with you from its yield and remains with you for a year.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْخُضَرِ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْبِطِّيخِ وَ لاَ عَلَى اَلْبُقُولِ وَأَشْبَاهِهِ زَكَاةٌ إِلاَّ مَا اِجْتَمَعَ عِنْدَكَ مِنْ غَلَّتِهِ فَبَقِيَ عِنْدَكَ سَنَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no zakat upon vegetables, nor upon melons, nor upon herbs and their like, except what has gathered with you from its yield and remains with you for a year.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Vegetables in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, exempted vegetables.” I (narrator) asked: “And what are vegetables?” The both Imams (a.s) said: “Everything that does not have permanence: herbs, melons, fruits, and the like of that from what spoils quickly.” Zurarah said: “I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘Is there anything due on reeds?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ:» عَفَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ عَنِ اَلْخُضَرِ« قُلْتُ وَ مَا اَلْخُضَرُ قَالاَ» كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لاَ يَكُونُ لَهُ بَقَاءٌ اَلْبَقْلُ وَ اَلْبِطِّيخُ وَاَلْفَوَاكِهُ وَشِبْهُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَكُونُ سَرِيعَ اَلْفَسَادِ« قَالَ زُرَارَةُ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ فِي اَلْقَصَبِ شَيْءٌ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, exempted vegetables.” I (narrator) asked: “And what are vegetables?” The both Imams (a.s) said: “Everything that does not have permanence: herbs, melons, fruits, and the like of that from what spoils quickly.” Zurarah said: “I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘Is there anything due on reeds?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Vegetables in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘vegetables, Is there zakat in them, even if they are sold for a great amount of wealth?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, until a year passes over it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلْخُضَرِ فِيهَا زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ بِيعَ بِالْمَالِ اَلْعَظِيمِ فَقَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘vegetables, Is there zakat in them, even if they are sold for a great amount of wealth?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, until a year passes over it.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Vegetables in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is due on greenery?” Imam (a.s) said: “And what is it?” I (narrator) said: “Reeds, melons, and the like of it from vegetables.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon it, unless its like is sold for wealth, and a year passes over it; then charity is due in it.” (The narrator asked) “And regarding the trees of al-ghadah, of peaches, nectarines (al-firsik), and their like. ‘Is there zakat in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Its value?” – meaning the value gained from selling such. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever a year passes over from its price, then give zakat on it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا فِي اَلْخُضْرَةِ قَالَ» وَ مَا هِيَ« قُلْتُ اَلْقَصَبُ وَ اَلْبِطِّيخُ وَ مِثْلُهُ مِنَ اَلْخُضَرِ فَقَالَ» لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُبَاعَ مِثْلُهُ بِمَالٍ فَيَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَفِيهِ اَلصَّدَقَةُ« وَ عَنْ شَجَرِ اَلْغَضَاةِ مِنَ اَلْخَوْخِ وَاَلْفِرْسِكِ وَأَشْبَاهِهِ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ قِيمَتُهُ قَالَ» مَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ مِنْ ثَمَنِهِ فَزَكِّهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is due on greenery?” Imam (a.s) said: “And what is it?” I (narrator) said: “Reeds, melons, and the like of it from vegetables.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon it, unless its like is sold for wealth, and a year passes over it; then charity is due in it.” (The narrator asked) “And regarding the trees of al-ghadah, of peaches, nectarines (al-firsik), and their like. ‘Is there zakat in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Its value?” – meaning the value gained from selling such. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever a year passes over from its price, then give zakat on it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Ruling Concerning Horses in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from both of Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
The Imams (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, placed upon noble grazing horses, for every horse in every year, two dinars, And the Imam (a.s) placed upon draft horses one dinar.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ زُرَارَةَ عَنْهُمَا جَمِيعاً عَلَيْمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ:» وَضَعَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى اَلْخَيْلِ اَلْعِتَاقِ اَلرَّاعِيَةِ فِي كُلِّ فَرَسٍ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ دِينَارَيْنِ وَ جَعَلَ عَلَى اَلْبَرَاذِينِ دِينَاراً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from both of Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Imams (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, placed upon noble grazing horses, for every horse in every year, two dinars, And the Imam (a.s) placed upon draft horses one dinar.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 87

chapter: Chapter on the Ruling Concerning Horses in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there anything due upon mules?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” So I (narrator) asked: “How has it become due upon horses but not become due upon mules?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because mules do not conceive, while female horses give birth, and there is nothing due upon male horses.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Is there anything due upon a horse or a camel which belongs to a man and which he rides?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No. There is nothing due upon that which is fed with fodder. Charity is only upon freely grazing livestock (al-saimah), released in its pasture during the year in which the man keeps it. As for other than that, there is nothing due in it.”
arabicText: حَمَّادٌ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ عَلَى اَلْبِغَالِ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ« فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ صَارَ عَلَى اَلْخَيْلِ وَ لَمْ يَصِرْ عَلَى اَلْبِغَالِ فَقَالَ» لِأَنَّ اَلْبِغَالَ لاَ تَلْقَحُ وَ اَلْخَيْلُ اَلْإِنَاثُ يُنْتِجْنَ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْخَيْلِ اَلذُّكُورِ شَيْءٌ« قَالَ قُلْتُ هَلْ عَلَى اَلْفَرَسِ أَوِ اَلْبَعِيرِ يَكُونُ لِلرَّجُلِ يَرْكَبُهَا شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَا يُعْلَفُ شَيْءٌ إِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقَةُ عَلَى اَلسَّائِمَةِ اَلْمُرْسَلَةِ فِي مَرْجِهَا عَامَهَا اَلَّذِي يَقْتَنِيهَا فِيهِ اَلرَّجُلُ فَأَمَّا مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is there anything due upon mules?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” So I (narrator) asked: “How has it become due upon horses but not become due upon mules?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because mules do not conceive, while female horses give birth, and there is nothing due upon male horses.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Is there anything due upon a horse or a camel which belongs to a man and which he rides?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No. There is nothing due upon that which is fed with fodder. Charity is only upon freely grazing livestock (al-saimah), released in its pasture during the year in which the man keeps it. As for other than that, there is nothing due in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu al-Rabi al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who bought goods, and his goods became unsold upon him, while he had already given zakat on his wealth before buying with it. Is zakat due upon him, or only when he sells it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he kept it seeking an increase over the capital, then zakat is due.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلرَّبِيعِ اَلشَّامِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ اِشْتَرَى مَتَاعاً فَكَسَدَ عَلَيْهِ مَتَاعُهُ وَ قَدْ كَانَ زَكَّى مَالَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَ بِهِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ أَوْ حَتَّى يَبِيعَهُ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ أَمْسَكَهُ اِلْتِمَاسَ اَلْفَضْلِ عَلَى رَأْسِ اَلْمَالِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu al-Rabi al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who bought goods, and his goods became unsold upon him, while he had already given zakat on his wealth before buying with it. Is zakat due upon him, or only when he sells it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he kept it seeking an increase over the capital, then zakat is due.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who bought goods and they became unsold upon him, while he had given zakat on his wealth before buying the goods, when should he give zakat on them?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he kept his goods seeking thereby his capital, then there is no zakat upon him. But if he withheld them after he found his capital, then zakat is due upon him after he kept them beyond the capital.” He (narrator) said: “And I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man with whom wealth is placed, and he works with it.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When a year passes over it, let him give zakat on it.”

thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who bought goods and they became unsold upon him, while he had given zakat on his wealth before buying the goods, when should he give zakat on them?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he kept his goods seeking thereby his capital, then there is no zakat upon him. But if he withheld them after he found his capital, then zakat is due upon him after he kept them beyond the capital.” He (narrator) said: “And I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man with whom wealth is placed, and he works with it.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When a year passes over it, let him give zakat on it.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
Said al-Araj asked Imam (a.s) while I was present, listening, and he said: “We press oil and clarified butter (al-samn) with us, seeking trade through it, and it may remain with us for a year or two years. Is there zakat upon it?” He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “If you profit anything in it, or you find your capital, then zakat is due upon you in it. But if you are only waiting with it because you find nothing except a loss, then there is no zakat upon you until it becomes gold or silver. Then when it becomes gold or silver, give zakat on it for the year in which you trade with it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ سَعِيدٌ اَلْأَعْرَجُ وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ أَسْمَعُ فَقَالَ إِنَّا نَكْبِسُ اَلزَّيْتَ وَاَلسَّمْنَ عِنْدَنَا نَطْلُبُ بِهِ اَلتِّجَارَةَ فَرُبَّمَا مَكَثَ عِنْدَنَا اَلسَّنَةَ وَاَلسَّنَتَيْنِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كُنْتَ تَرْبَحُ فِيهِ شَيْئاً أَوْ تَجِدُ رَأْسَ مَالِكَ فَعَلَيْكَ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ إِنَّمَا تَرَبَّصُ بِهِ لِأَنَّكَ لاَ تَجِدُ إِلاَّ وَضِيعَةً فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ ذَهَباً أَوْ فِضَّةً فَإِذَا صَارَ ذَهَباً أَوْ فِضَّةً فَزَكِّهِ لِلسَّنَةِ اَلَّتِي تَتَّجِرُ فِيهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Said al-Araj asked Imam (a.s) while I was present, listening, and he said: “We press oil and clarified butter (al-samn) with us, seeking trade through it, and it may remain with us for a year or two years. Is there zakat upon it?” He (narrator) said, so Imam (a.s) said: “If you profit anything in it, or you find your capital, then zakat is due upon you in it. But if you are only waiting with it because you find nothing except a loss, then there is no zakat upon you until it becomes gold or silver. Then when it becomes gold or silver, give zakat on it for the year in which you trade with it.”
