chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated that from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A man buys a young female slave and keeps her with him so that she may increase in value, while he intends to sell her; is there zakat upon her price?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until he sells her.” I (narrator) asked: “Then if he sells her, should he give zakat on her price?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it while it is in his hand.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَشْتَرِي اَلْوَصِيفَةَ يُثْبِتُهَا عِنْدَهُ لِتَزِيدَ وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ بَيْعَهَا أَ عَلَى ثَمَنِهَا زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَبِيعَهَا« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ بَاعَهَا أَ يُزَكِّي ثَمَنَهَا قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ وَ هُوَ فِي يَدِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated that from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A man buys a young female slave and keeps her with him so that she may increase in value, while he intends to sell her; is there zakat upon her price?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until he sells her.” I (narrator) asked: “Then if he sells her, should he give zakat on her price?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until a year passes over it while it is in his hand.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 90

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Sindi ibn Muhammad, from al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Goods by which I do not obtain my capital; ‘Is there zakat upon me in them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “I keep them for two years, then I sell them; ‘what is due upon me?’” Imam (a.s) said: “One year.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ سِنْدِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلْمَتَاعُ لاَ أُصِيبُ بِهِ رَأْسَ اَلْمَالِ عَلَيَّ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ أُمْسِكُهُ سَنَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ أَبِيعُهُ مَاذَا عَلَيَّ قَالَ» سَنَةً وَاحِدَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Sindi ibn Muhammad, from al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Goods by which I do not obtain my capital; ‘Is there zakat upon me in them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “I keep them for two years, then I sell them; ‘what is due upon me?’” Imam (a.s) said: “One year.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, Ubayd, and a group of our companions, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “There is no zakat in wealth that is being traded with.” So his son Ismail (ibn Ja’far) said to him: “O my father (a.s), may I be made your ransom, you have destroyed the poor among your companions.” Imam (a.s) said: “O my son, it is a right which Allah (swt) intended to bring out, so it came out.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ وَ عُبَيْدٍ وَ جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالُوا قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» لَيْسَ فِي اَلْمَالِ اَلْمُضْطَرَبِ بِهِ زَكَاةٌ« فَقَالَ لَهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ اِبْنُهُ يَا أَبَتِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَهْلَكْتَ فُقَرَاءَ أَصْحَابِكَ فَقَالَ» أَيْ بُنَيَّ حَقٌّ أَرَادَ اَللَّهُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَهُ فَخَرَجَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, Ubayd, and a group of our companions, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “There is no zakat in wealth that is being traded with.” So his son Ismail (ibn Ja’far) said to him: “O my father (a.s), may I be made your ransom, you have destroyed the poor among your companions.” Imam (a.s) said: “O my son, it is a right which Allah (swt) intended to bring out, so it came out.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a man who had abundant wealth, so he bought goods with it. Then he placed them aside and said: ‘These are goods placed aside; when I wish, I will sell them, and my capital and more than it will return to me.’ Is charity due upon him in it while it is goods?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until he sells it.” He (narrator) asked: “Then must he pay on its behalf, if he sells it, for what has passed while it was goods?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ مَالٌ كَثِيرٌ فَاشْتَرَى بِهِ مَتَاعاً ثُمَّ وَضَعَهُ فَقَالَ هَذَا مَتَاعٌ مَوْضُوعٌ فَإِذَا أَحْبَبْتُ بِعْتُهُ فَيَرْجِعُ إِلَيَّ رَأْسُ مَالِي وَ أَفْضَلُ مِنْهُ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ فِيهِ صَدَقَةٌ وَ هُوَ مَتَاعٌ قَالَ» لاَ حَتَّى يَبِيعَهُ« قَالَ فَهَلْ يُؤَدِّي عَنْهُ إِنْ بَاعَهُ لِمَا مَضَى إِذَا كَانَ مَتَاعاً قَالَ» لاَ«
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a man who had abundant wealth, so he bought goods with it. Then he placed them aside and said: ‘These are goods placed aside; when I wish, I will sell them, and my capital and more than it will return to me.’ Is charity due upon him in it while it is goods?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, not until he sells it.” He (narrator) asked: “Then must he pay on its behalf, if he sells it, for what has passed while it was goods?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Trade Goods in Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
I was sitting with Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, and there was no one with him except his son, Imam Ja’far (al-Sadiq). Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, indeed Abu Dharr, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, and Uthman (ibn Affan) disputed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Uthman said: ‘Every wealth of gold or silver that is circulated, worked with, and traded with, zakat is due in it when a year passes over it.’ But Abu Dharr, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, said: ‘As for that which is traded with, circulated, and worked with, there is no zakat in it. Zakat is only in it when it is buried treasure (rikaz) or a treasure placed aside; then when a year passes over it, zakat is due in it.’ So they disputed about that before the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said, “So Prophet (saws) said: ‘The (correct) statement is what Abu Dharr said.’” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “What do you intend by bringing out something like this, so that the people will refrain from giving to their poor and their needy?” So his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Leave me to it; I find no way around it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: كُنْتُ قَاعِداً عِنْدَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُ اِبْنِهِ جَعْفَرٍ فَقَالَ» يَا زُرَارَةُ إِنَّ أَبَا ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اَللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَ عُثْمَانَ تَنَازَعَا عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَقَالَ عُثْمَانُ كُلُّ مَالٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ فِضَّةٍ يُدَارُ بِهِ وَ يُعْمَلُ بِهِ وَ يُتَّجَرُ بِهِ فَفِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ إِذَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَقَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اَللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَمَّا مَا اُتُّجِرَ بِهِ أَوْ دِيرَ وَ عُمِلَ بِهِ فَلَيْسَ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ إِنَّمَا اَلزَّكَاةُ فِيهِ إِذَا كَانَ رِكَازاً أَوْ كَنْزاً مَوْضُوعاً فَإِذَا حَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْحَوْلُ فَفِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ فَاخْتَصَمَا فِي ذَلِكَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ» اَلْقَوْلُ مَا قَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ«« فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لِأَبِيهِ» مَا تُرِيدُ إِلَى أَنْ تُخْرِجَ مِثْلَ هَذَا فَيَكُفَّ اَلنَّاسُ أَنْ يُعْطُوا فُقَرَاءَهُمْ وَمَسَاكِينَهُمْ« فَقَالَ أَبُوهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ »إِلَيْكَ عَنِّي لاَ أَجِدُ مِنْهَا بُدّاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was sitting with Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, and there was no one with him except his son, Imam Ja’far (al-Sadiq). Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O Zurarah, indeed Abu Dharr, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, and Uthman (ibn Affan) disputed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Uthman said: ‘Every wealth of gold or silver that is circulated, worked with, and traded with, zakat is due in it when a year passes over it.’ But Abu Dharr, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, said: ‘As for that which is traded with, circulated, and worked with, there is no zakat in it. Zakat is only in it when it is buried treasure (rikaz) or a treasure placed aside; then when a year passes over it, zakat is due in it.’ So they disputed about that before the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” He (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said, “So Prophet (saws) said: ‘The (correct) statement is what Abu Dharr said.’” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “What do you intend by bringing out something like this, so that the people will refrain from giving to their poor and their needy?” So his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Leave me to it; I find no way around it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 91

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Everyone whom you include among your dependents, whether free or owned, then it is upon you to pay al-fitrah on his behalf.” Imam (a.s) said: “Giving al-fitrah before prayer is better, and after prayer, it is charity.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كُلُّ مَنْ ضَمَمْتَ إِلَى عِيَالِكَ مِنْ حُرٍّ أَوْ مَمْلُوكٍ فَعَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُؤَدِّيَ اَلْفِطْرَةَ عَنْهُ« قَالَ »فَإِعْطَاءُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَفْضَلُ وَ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ صَدَقَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Everyone whom you include among your dependents, whether free or owned, then it is upon you to pay al-fitrah on his behalf.” Imam (a.s) said: “Giving al-fitrah before prayer is better, and after prayer, it is charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat) al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, on behalf of every person, one sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» عَلَى اَلصَّغِيرِ وَ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَ اَلْحُرِّ وَ اَلْعَبْدِ عَنْ كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ صَاعٌ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat) al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, on behalf of every person, one sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 92

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, raising it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “A man pays his zakat on behalf of his contracted slave (mukatab), the slaves of his wife, his Christian slave, his Magian slave, and whatever his door has closed upon.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يُؤَدِّي اَلرَّجُلُ زَكَاتَهُ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ وَ رَقِيقِ اِمْرَأَتِهِ وَعَبْدِهِ اَلنَّصْرَانِيِّ وَاَلْمَجُوسِيِّ وَ مَا أَغْلَقَ عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, raising it to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “A man pays his zakat on behalf of his contracted slave (mukatab), the slaves of his wife, his Christian slave, his Magian slave, and whatever his door has closed upon.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has a guest from among his brothers staying with him, and the day of al-Fitr arrives, does he pay al-fitrah on his behalf?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Al-fitrah is obligatory upon everyone whom he maintains, whether male or female, young or old, free or owned.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ اَلضَّيْفُ مِنْ إِخْوَانِهِ فَيَحْضُرُ يَوْمُ اَلْفِطْرِ يُؤَدِّي عَنْهُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ قَالَ» نَعَمْ اَلْفِطْرَةُ وَاجِبَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْ يَعُولُ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى صَغِيرٍ أَوْ كَبِيرٍ حُرٍّ أَوْ مَمْلُوكٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has a guest from among his brothers staying with him, and the day of al-Fitr arrives, does he pay al-fitrah on his behalf?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Al-fitrah is obligatory upon everyone whom he maintains, whether male or female, young or old, free or owned.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ibn Abi Umayr, Muawiyah ibn Ammar:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a newborn who was born on the night of al-Fitr, Is al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, the month has already ended.” And I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a Jew who accepted Islam on the night of al-Fitr, Is al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ مَوْلُودٍ وُلِدَ لَيْلَةَ اَلْفِطْرِ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةٌ قَالَ» لاَ قَدْ خَرَجَ اَلشَّهْرُ« وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ يَهُودِيٍّ أَسْلَمَ لَيْلَةَ اَلْفِطْرِ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةٌ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, Ibn Abi Umayr, Muawiyah ibn Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a newborn who was born on the night of al-Fitr, Is al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, the month has already ended.” And I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a Jew who accepted Islam on the night of al-Fitr, Is al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 93

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it has been narrated: “That if a baby is born before midday (of al-Fitr), al-fitrah is to be taken out on his behalf, and likewise one who accepts Islam before midday.”
arabicText: وَ قَدْ رُوِيَ:» أَنَّهُ إِنْ وُلِدَ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ تُخْرَجُ عَنْهُ اَلْفِطْرَةُ وَ كَذَلِكَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ«.
thaqalaynMatn: And it has been narrated: “That if a baby is born before midday (of al-Fitr), al-fitrah is to be taken out on his behalf, and likewise one who accepts Islam before midday.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ibrahim (a.s): “Is zakat al-fitrah due upon a needy man?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no fitrah upon him.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى اَلرَّجُلِ اَلْمُحْتَاجِ زَكَاةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ibrahim (a.s): “Is zakat al-fitrah due upon a needy man?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no fitrah upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazid ibn Farqad, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon the needy person?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى اَلْمُحْتَاجِ صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazid ibn Farqad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon the needy person?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who takes from zakat, Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَأْخُذُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who takes from zakat, Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Yazid ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
He (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “Whoever takes from zakat, there is no fitrah upon him.” He (narrator) said that Ibn Ammar said: “Indeed Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘There is no fitrah upon one who has taken zakat.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَهُ يَقُولُ:» مَنْ أَخَذَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةٌ«. قَالَ وَ قَالَ اِبْنُ عَمَّارٍ إِنَّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ فِطْرَةَ عَلَى مَنْ أَخَذَ اَلزَّكَاةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Yazid ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “Whoever takes from zakat, there is no fitrah upon him.” He (narrator) said that Ibn Ammar said: “Indeed Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘There is no fitrah upon one who has taken zakat.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “For whom is al-fitrah lawful?” Imam (a.s) said: “For the one who does not possess enough (poor/needy person). And whoever it is lawful for (to receive zakat al-fitrah), it is not lawful upon him (not obligatory for him to pay it); And whoever it is lawful upon (person upon whom zakat al-fitrah is obligatory), it is not lawful for him (not allowed to receive it).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ لِمَنْ تَحِلُّ اَلْفِطْرَةُ قَالَ» لِمَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ وَ مَنْ حَلَّتْ لَهُ لَمْ تَحِلَّ عَلَيْهِ وَ مَنْ حَلَّتْ عَلَيْهِ لَمْ تَحِلَّ لَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “For whom is al-fitrah lawful?” Imam (a.s) said: “For the one who does not possess enough (poor/needy person). And whoever it is lawful for (to receive zakat al-fitrah), it is not lawful upon him (not obligatory for him to pay it); And whoever it is lawful upon (person upon whom zakat al-fitrah is obligatory), it is not lawful for him (not allowed to receive it).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 94

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And by this chain of transmission, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is zakat due upon one who has accepted zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who has accepted the zakat of wealth, then zakat al-fitrah is due upon him, but no zakat is due upon him for what he has accepted. And there is no fitrah upon one who accepts al-fitrah.”
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ عَلَى مَنْ قَبِلَ اَلزَّكَاةَ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» أَمَّا مَنْ قَبِلَ زَكَاةَ اَلْمَالِ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَا قَبِلَهُ زَكَاةٌ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ يَقْبَلُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ فِطْرَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And by this chain of transmission, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is zakat due upon one who has accepted zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who has accepted the zakat of wealth, then zakat al-fitrah is due upon him, but no zakat is due upon him for what he has accepted. And there is no fitrah upon one who accepts al-fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar:
I said to Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is zakat al-fitrah due upon a needy man?” Imam (a.s) said: There is no fitrah upon him.
arabicText: سعد بن عبد الله عن ابي جعفر عن الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان بن يحيى عن إسحاق بن عمار قال: قلت لابي ابراهيم عليه السلام على الرجل المحتاج زكاة الفطرة؟ قال: ليس عليه فطرة
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him: “Is zakat al-fitrah due upon a needy man?” Imam (a.s) said: There is no fitrah upon him.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yazid ibn Farqad al-Nahdi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who accepts zakat, Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ اَلنَّهْدِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَقْبَلُ اَلزَّكَاةَ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yazid ibn Farqad al-Nahdi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who accepts zakat, Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Is zakat due upon one who has accepted zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who has accepted the zakat of wealth, then zakat al-fitrah is due upon him, and there is no fitrah upon one who has accepted al-fitrah.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ هَلْ عَلَى مَنْ قَبِلَ اَلزَّكَاةَ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» أَمَّا مَنْ قَبِلَ زَكَاةَ اَلْمَالِ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ قَبِلَ اَلْفِطْرَةَ فِطْرَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Is zakat due upon one who has accepted zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who has accepted the zakat of wealth, then zakat al-fitrah is due upon him, and there is no fitrah upon one who has accepted al-fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 95

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The poor person upon whom charity is given, is sadaqat al-fitrah obligatory upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he gives from what is given to him in charity.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْفَقِيرُ اَلَّذِي يُتَصَدَّقُ عَلَيْهِ هَلْ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ يُعْطِي مِمَّا يُتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The poor person upon whom charity is given, is sadaqat al-fitrah obligatory upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he gives from what is given to him in charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Numan and Sayf ibn Amirah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man does not have anything of al-fitrah except what he would pay on behalf of himself alone from al-fitrah; should he give it to a stranger, or should he and his dependents eat it?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives it to some of his dependents, then the other gives it on behalf of himself. They pass it around among themselves, and it becomes one fitrah on behalf of all of them.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ وَسَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ لاَ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ إِلاَّ مَا يُؤَدِّي عَنْ نَفْسِهِ مِنَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَحْدَهَا يُعْطِيهِ غَرِيباً أَوْ يَأْكُلُ هُوَ وَ عِيَالُهُ فَقَالَ» يُعْطِي بَعْضَ عِيَالِهِ ثُمَّ يُعْطِي اَلْآخَرُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ يُرَدِّدُونَهَا فَتَكُونُ عَنْهُمْ جَمِيعاً فِطْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Numan and Sayf ibn Amirah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man does not have anything of al-fitrah except what he would pay on behalf of himself alone from al-fitrah; should he give it to a stranger, or should he and his dependents eat it?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives it to some of his dependents, then the other gives it on behalf of himself. They pass it around among themselves, and it becomes one fitrah on behalf of all of them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Sadaqat al-fitrah is upon every head from your household, the young and the old, the free and the owned, the rich and the poor; on behalf of every person, half a sa’ of wheat or barley, or one sa’ of dates or raisins, for the poor of the Muslims.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are the most beloved of that to me.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ عَلَى كُلِّ رَأْسٍ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ اَلصَّغِيرِ وَاَلْكَبِيرِ وَاَلْحُرِّ وَاَلْمَمْلُوكِ وَاَلْغَنِيِّ وَاَلْفَقِيرِ عَنْ كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ زَبِيبٍ لِفُقَرَاءِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ« وَ قَالَ» اَلتَّمْرُ أَحَبُّ ذَلِكَ إِلَيَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Sadaqat al-fitrah is upon every head from your household, the young and the old, the free and the owned, the rich and the poor; on behalf of every person, half a sa’ of wheat or barley, or one sa’ of dates or raisins, for the poor of the Muslims.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are the most beloved of that to me.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
Imams (a.s) said: “Zakat al-fitrah is one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of dried curd (aqit), on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no hardship upon one who does not find that with which he may give charity.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» زَكَاةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنَ اَلْأَقِطِ عَنْ كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ حُرٍّ أَوْ عَبْدٍ صَغِيرٍ أَوْ كَبِيرٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ مَا يَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ حَرَجٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: What al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: Imams (a.s) said: “Zakat al-fitrah is one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of dried curd (aqit), on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no hardship upon one who does not find that with which he may give charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 96

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from al-Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat) al-fitrah, when is it due?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Before the prayer on the day of al-Fitr.” I (narrator) asked: “Then if something of it remains after the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm. We give our dependents from it, then it remains, so we distribute it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ مَتَى هِيَ فَقَالَ» قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ نَحْنُ نُعْطِي عِيَالَنَا مِنْهُ ثُمَّ يَبْقَى فَنَقْسِمُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from al-Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat) al-fitrah, when is it due?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Before the prayer on the day of al-Fitr.” I (narrator) asked: “Then if something of it remains after the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm. We give our dependents from it, then it remains, so we distribute it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: ‘Successful indeed are those who purify themselves, remember the Name of their Lord (azj), and pray.’ (Surah Al-A’la 87:14-15) Imam (a.s) said: “He goes to the open prayer-ground (al-jabbanah) and prays.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى »قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكّٰى` وَ ذَكَرَ اِسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلّٰى« فَقَالَ» يَرُوحُ إِلَى اَلْجَبَّانَةِ فَيُصَلِّي«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: ‘Successful indeed are those who purify themselves, remember the Name of their Lord (azj), and pray.’ (Surah Al-A’la 87:14-15) Imam (a.s) said: “He goes to the open prayer-ground (al-jabbanah) and prays.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 97

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Fitrah, if you give it before you go out to the Eid, then it is Fitrah; and if it is after you go out to the Eid, then it is charity.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» اَلْفِطْرَةُ إِنْ أَعْطَيْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ إِلَى اَلْعِيدِ فَهِيَ فِطْرَةٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ مَا تَخْرُجُ إِلَى اَلْعِيدِ فَهِيَ صَدَقَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Fitrah, if you give it before you go out to the Eid, then it is Fitrah; and if it is after you go out to the Eid, then it is charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayan, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Muawiyah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
Imams (a.s) said: “It is upon a man to give on behalf of everyone whom he supports, from free person and slave, young and old. He gives on the Day of Fitr, and that is better, and he has leeway to give it from the first day that enters in the month of Ramadan until its end. So if he gives dates, then it is one sa’ for every head; and if he does not give dates, then half a sa’ for every head of wheat or barley. Wheat and barley are the same; whatever wheat suffices for, barley suffices.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ بُكَيْرٍ اِبْنَيْ أَعْيَنَ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالاَ:» عَلَى اَلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَ عَنْ كُلِّ مَنْ يَعُولُ مِنْ حُرٍّ وَ عَبْدٍ صَغِيرٍ وَ كَبِيرٍ يُعْطِي يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَ هُوَ فِي سَعَةٍ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهَا فِي أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ يَدْخُلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ إِلَى آخِرِهِ فَإِنْ أَعْطَى تَمْراً فَصَاعٌ لِكُلِّ رَأْسٍ وَإِنْ لَمْ يُعْطِ تَمْراً فَنِصْفُ صَاعٍ لِكُلِّ رَأْسٍ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ شَعِيرٍ وَ اَلْحِنْطَةُ وَ اَلشَّعِيرُ سَوَاءٌ مَا أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ اَلْحِنْطَةُ فَالشَّعِيرُ يُجْزِي«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayan, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Muawiyah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imams (a.s) said: “It is upon a man to give on behalf of everyone whom he supports, from free person and slave, young and old. He gives on the Day of Fitr, and that is better, and he has leeway to give it from the first day that enters in the month of Ramadan until its end. So if he gives dates, then it is one sa’ for every head; and if he does not give dates, then half a sa’ for every head of wheat or barley. Wheat and barley are the same; whatever wheat suffices for, barley suffices.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Dhibyan ibn Hakim, from al-Harith, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in delaying the Fitrah until the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ ذُبْيَانَ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنِ اَلْحَارِثِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُؤَخِّرَ اَلْفِطْرَةَ إِلَى هِلاَلِ ذِي اَلْقَعْدَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Dhibyan ibn Hakim, from al-Harith, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in delaying the Fitrah until the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 98

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding the Fitrah, when you set it aside while you are seeking the proper place for it, or waiting with it for a man, then there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :»فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ إِذَا عَزَلْتَهَا وَ أَنْتَ تَطْلُبُ بِهَا اَلْمَوْضِعَ أَوْ تَنْتَظِرُ بِهَا رَجُلاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Regarding the Fitrah, when you set it aside while you are seeking the proper place for it, or waiting with it for a man, then there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar and others, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When you set it aside, it does not harm you whenever you give it, before the prayer or after the prayer.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ وَ غَيْرِهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» إِذَا عَزَلْتَهَا فَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ مَتَى أَعْطَيْتَهَا قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَوْ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar and others, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When you set it aside, it does not harm you whenever you give it, before the prayer or after the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on Time of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn Ayan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who took out his Fitrah and set it aside until he finds people worthy of it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he has taken it out from his liability, then he has become free of responsibility; otherwise, he is liable for it until he delivers it to its owners.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أَخْرَجَ فِطْرَتَهُ فَعَزَلَهَا حَتَّى يَجِدَ لَهَا أَهْلاً فَقَالَ» إِذَا أَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ ضَمَانِهِ فَقَدْ بَرِئَ وَ إِلاَّ فَهُوَ ضَامِنٌ لَهَا حَتَّى يُؤَدِّيَهَا إِلَى أَرْبَابِهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn Ayan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who took out his Fitrah and set it aside until he finds people worthy of it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he has taken it out from his liability, then he has become free of responsibility; otherwise, he is liable for it until he delivers it to its owners.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I be made your ransom, is the Fitrah upon the people of the deserts?” He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) said: ‘The Fitrah is upon everyone who subsists upon a staple food, so he must pay from that staple food.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ هَلْ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْبَوَادِي اَلْفِطْرَةُ قَالَ فَقَالَ» اَلْفِطْرَةُ عَلَى كُلِّ مَنِ اِقْتَاتَ قُوتاً فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلْقُوتِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I be made your ransom, is the Fitrah upon the people of the deserts?” He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) said: ‘The Fitrah is upon everyone who subsists upon a staple food, so he must pay from that staple food.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Fitrah is upon every people from that with which they nourish their dependents, from milk, or raisins, or other than it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلْفِطْرَةُ عَلَى كُلِّ قَوْمٍ مِمَّا يَغْذُونَ عِيَالاَتِهِمْ مِنْ لَبَنٍ أَوْ زَبِيبٍ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Fitrah is upon every people from that with which they nourish their dependents, from milk, or raisins, or other than it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 99

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man in the desert who is not able to give the Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should give in charity four artal of milk.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ بِالْبَادِيَةِ لاَ يُمْكِنُهُ اَلْفِطْرَةُ فَقَالَ» تَصَدَّقَ بِأَرْبَعَةِ أَرْطَالٍ مِنْ لَبَنٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man in the desert who is not able to give the Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should give in charity four artal of milk.”

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in the value in the Fitrah.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِالْقِيمَةِ فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in the value in the Fitrah.”

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Ali ibn Uthman, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The neighbors are more entitled to it, and there is no harm in giving the value of that in silver.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» اَلْجِيرَانُ أَحَقُّ بِهَا وَ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَ قِيمَةَ ذَلِكَ فِضَّةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Ali ibn Uthman, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The neighbors are more entitled to it, and there is no harm in giving the value of that in silver.”

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Zakat al-Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: the like of it,
And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in giving him its value as a dirham.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَهُ وَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُ قِيمَتَهَا دِرْهَماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: the like of it,
thaqalaynMatn: And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in giving him its value as a dirham.”

chapter: Chapter on Distinguishing the Fitrah of the People of Cities
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Hatim al-Qazwini said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said:
The narrations differed regarding the Fitrah, so I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan, the companion of al-Askar (a.s), peace be upon him, asking him about that, so he wrote: “The Fitrah is one sa’ from the staple food of your land. Upon the people of Makkah, Yemen, al-Taif, the outskirts of al-Sham, al-Yamamah, al-Bahrayn, the two Iraqs, Persia, al-Ahwaz, and Kirman, it is dates; And upon the people of the middle regions of al-Sham, it is raisins; And upon the people of al-Jazirah, al-Mawsil, and all of al-Jibal, it is wheat or barley; And upon the people of Tabaristan, it is rice; And upon the people of Khurasan, it is wheat, except the people of Marw and al-Rayy, for upon them is raisins; And upon the people of Egypt, it is wheat; And whoever is besides that, then upon them is what prevails as their staple food. And whoever from Bedouins dwells in deserts, then upon them is dried yoghurt (aqit). And the Fitrah is upon you and upon all the people, and upon whoever you support, whether male or female, young or old, free or slave, weaned or suckling. You pay it by weight as six artal according to the ratl of al-Madinah, and the ratl is one hundred and ninety-five dirhams, so the Fitrah is one thousand one hundred and seventy dirhams.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ اَلْقَزْوِينِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِيِّ عَ نْ إِ بْ رَ ا هِ ي مَ بْ نِ مُ حَ مَّ دٍ اَ لْ هَ مَ ذَ ا نِ يِّ قَ ا لَ: اِ خْ تَ لَ فَ تِ اَ ل رِّ وَ ا يَ ا تُ فِ ي اَ لْ فِ طْ رَ ةِ فَكَتَبْتُ إِ لَ ى أَ بِ ي اَ لْ حَ سَ نِ صَ ا حِ بِ اَ لْعَسْكَرِ عَ لَ يْ هِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَكَتَبَ» أَنَّ اَلْفِطْرَةَ صَاعٌ مِنْ قُوتِ بَلَدِكَ عَلَى أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ وَ اَلْيَمَنِ وَ اَلطَّائِفِ وَ أَطْرَافِ اَلشَّامِ وَ اَلْيَمَامَةِ وَ اَلْبَحْرَيْنِ وَ اَلْعِرَاقَيْنِ وَ فَارِسَ وَ اَلْأَهْوَازِ وَ كِرْمَانَ تَمْرٌ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ أَوْسَاطِ اَلشَّامِ زَبِيبٌ وَعَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْجَزِيرَةِ وَ اَلْمَوْصِلِ وَ اَلْجِبَالِ كُلِّهَا بُرٌّ أَوْ شَعِيرٌ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ طَبَرِسْتَانَ اَلْأَرُزُّ وَعَلَى أَهْلِ خُرَاسَانَ اَلْبُرُّ إِلاَّ أَهْلَ مَرْوَ وَ اَلرَّيِّ فَعَلَيْهِمُ اَلزَّبِيبُ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ مِصْرَ اَلْبُرُّ وَ مَنْ سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَعَلَيْهِمْ مَا غَلَبَ قُ و تَ هُ مْ وَ مَنْ سَكَنَ اَلْبَوَادِيَ مِنَ اَلْأَعْرَابِ فَعَلَيْهِمُ اَلْأَقِطُ وَاَلْفِطْرَةُ عَلَيْكَ وَ عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ كُلِّهِمْ وَ مَنْ تَعُولُ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ كَانَ أَوْ أُنْثَى صَغِيراً أَوْ كَبِيراً حُرّاً أَوْ عَبْداً فَطِيماً أَوْ رَضِيعاً تَدْفَعُهُ وَزْناً سِتَّةَ أَرْطَالٍ بِرِطْلِ اَلْمَدِينَةِ وَ اَلرِّطْلُ مِائَةٌ وَ خَمْسَةٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ دِرْهَماً تَكُونُ اَلْفِطْرَةُ أَلْفاً وَ مِائَةً وَ سَبْعِينَ دِرْهَماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Hatim al-Qazwini said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The narrations differed regarding the Fitrah, so I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan, the companion of al-Askar (a.s), peace be upon him, asking him about that, so he wrote: “The Fitrah is one sa’ from the staple food of your land. Upon the people of Makkah, Yemen, al-Taif, the outskirts of al-Sham, al-Yamamah, al-Bahrayn, the two Iraqs, Persia, al-Ahwaz, and Kirman, it is dates; And upon the people of the middle regions of al-Sham, it is raisins; And upon the people of al-Jazirah, al-Mawsil, and all of al-Jibal, it is wheat or barley; And upon the people of Tabaristan, it is rice; And upon the people of Khurasan, it is wheat, except the people of Marw and al-Rayy, for upon them is raisins; And upon the people of Egypt, it is wheat; And whoever is besides that, then upon them is what prevails as their staple food. And whoever from Bedouins dwells in deserts, then upon them is dried yoghurt (aqit). And the Fitrah is upon you and upon all the people, and upon whoever you support, whether male or female, young or old, free or slave, weaned or suckling. You pay it by weight as six artal according to the ratl of al-Madinah, and the ratl is one hundred and ninety-five dirhams, so the Fitrah is one thousand one hundred and seventy dirhams.”

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa’ad ibn Sa’ad al-Ashari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, how much is to be paid for every head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins?’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ according to the sa’ of the Prophet (saws), Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ كَمْ تُدْفَعُ عَنْ كُلِّ رَأْسٍ مِنَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ وَ اَلشَّعِيرِ وَ اَلتَّمْرِ وَ اَلزَّبِيبِ قَالَ» صَاعٌ بِصَاعِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa’ad ibn Sa’ad al-Ashari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, how much is to be paid for every head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins?’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ according to the sa’ of the Prophet (saws), Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 102

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat of) al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon the young and the old, the free and the slave; on behalf of every person, a sa’ of wheat, or a sa’ of dates, or a sa’ of raisins.”
arabicText: وعنه عن عدة من أصحابنا عن احمد بن محمد عن ابن ابي نجران وعلي بن الحكم عن صفوان الجمال قال: سألت ابا عبد الله عليه السلام عن الفطرة فقال: على الصغير والكبير والحر والعبد عن كل إنسان صاع من بر أو صاع من تمر أو صاع من زبيب
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘(zakat of) al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon the young and the old, the free and the slave; on behalf of every person, a sa’ of wheat, or a sa’ of dates, or a sa’ of raisins.”

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ is given from wheat, one sa’ from barley, and one sa’ from dried yoghurt (aqit).”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» يُعْطَى مِنَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ صَاعٌ وَ مِنَ اَلشَّعِيرِ صَاعٌ وَ مِنَ اَلْأَقِطِ صَاعٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ is given from wheat, one sa’ from barley, and one sa’ from dried yoghurt (aqit).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 102

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The owners of camels, cattle, and sheep give, in the Fitrah, one sa’ of dried yoghurt (aqit).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يُعْطِي أَصْحَابُ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ اَلْبَقَرِ وَ اَلْغَنَمِ فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ مِنَ اَلْأَقِطِ صَاعاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The owners of camels, cattle, and sheep give, in the Fitrah, one sa’ of dried yoghurt (aqit).”
