chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
(Imam (a.s) said) “Zakat al-fitrah is a sa’ of dates, or a sa’ of raisins, or a sa’ of barley, or a sa’ of dried curd (aqit), on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no hardship upon one who does not find anything to give in charity.”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن حماد بن عيسى عن عبد الله بن ميمون عن ابي عبد الله عن ابيه عليهما السلام قال: زكاة الفطرة صاع من تمر أو صاع من زبيب أو صاع من شعير أو صاع من أقط عن كل إنسان حر أو عبد صغير أو كبير، وليس على من لا يجد ما يتصدق به حرج
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) said) “Zakat al-fitrah is a sa’ of dates, or a sa’ of raisins, or a sa’ of barley, or a sa’ of dried curd (aqit), on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no hardship upon one who does not find anything to give in charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 102

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Qulawayh, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masud, from Jafar ibn Maruf, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu Bakr al-Radhi regarding ‘Zakat al-Fitrah’, and we asked him to write concerning that to our master, meaning Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him. So al-Radhi wrote that this had already come out to Ali ibn Mahziyar: “That one sa’ is to be taken out from everything: dates, wheat (burr), and other than it.” And after his answer to us regarding that, there is no disagreement among us.
arabicText: اِبْنُ قُولَوَيْهِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلرَّازِيِّ فِي زَكَاةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَسَأَلْنَاهُ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ فِي ذَلِكَ إِلَى مَوْلاَنَا يَعْنِي عَلِيَّ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَكَتَبَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ خَرَجَ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ »أَنَّهُ يُخْرَجُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ اَلتَّمْرِ وَ اَلْبُرِّ وَ غَيْرِهِ صَاعٌ« وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا بَعْدَ جَوَابِهِ عَلَيْنَا فِي ذَلِكَ اِخْتِلاَفٌ.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Qulawayh, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masud, from Jafar ibn Maruf, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu Bakr al-Radhi regarding ‘Zakat al-Fitrah’, and we asked him to write concerning that to our master, meaning Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him. So al-Radhi wrote that this had already come out to Ali ibn Mahziyar: “That one sa’ is to be taken out from everything: dates, wheat (burr), and other than it.” And after his answer to us regarding that, there is no disagreement among us.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon everyone whom the man supports, upon the free person and the slave, the young and the old, is one sa’ of dates, or half a sa’ of wheat (burr), and the sa’ is four mudds (amdad).”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْ يَعُولُ اَلرَّجُلُ عَلَى اَلْحُرِّ وَاَلْعَبْدِ وَاَلصَّغِيرِ وَاَلْكَبِيرِ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ بُرٍّ وَ اَلصَّاعُ أَرْبَعَةُ أَمْدَادٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon everyone whom the man supports, upon the free person and the slave, the young and the old, is one sa’ of dates, or half a sa’ of wheat (burr), and the sa’ is four mudds (amdad).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Give charity on behalf of all whom you support, whether young or old, free or owned slave. Upon every person is half a sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, and the sa’ is four mudds (amdad).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» تَصَدَّقْ عَنْ جَمِيعِ مَنْ تَعُولُ مِنْ صَغِيرٍ أَوْ كَبِيرٍ أَوْ حُرٍّ أَوْ مَمْلُوكٍ عَلَى كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ وَ اَلصَّاعُ أَرْبَعَةُ أَمْدَادٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Give charity on behalf of all whom you support, whether young or old, free or owned slave. Upon every person is half a sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, and the sa’ is four mudds (amdad).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Charity, for one who does not find wheat and barley, wheat (qamh), lentils, and maize suffice for him, half a sa’ from all of that, or one sa’ of dates or raisins.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» اَلصَّدَقَةُ لِمَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ اَلْحِنْطَةَ وَ اَلشَّعِيرَ يُجْزِي عَنْهُ اَلْقَمْحُ وَاَلْعَدَسُ وَ اَلذُّرَةُ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ زَبِيبٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Charity, for one who does not find wheat and barley, wheat (qamh), lentils, and maize suffice for him, half a sa’ from all of that, or one sa’ of dates or raisins.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 103

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, and Burayd, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
We asked the both Imams (a.s), peace be upon them both, about ‘Zakat al-Fitrah.’ They (a.s) both said: “One sa’ of dates, or raisins, or barley, or half of all of that as wheat, or flour, or parched flour, or maize, or a type of barley without husk (sult), on behalf of the young and the old, the male and the female, the adult, and those whom you support; in that they are the same.”
arabicText: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْأَحْمَرِيُّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ وَ بُرَيْدٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالُوا: سَأَلْنَاهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ زَكَاةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالاَ» صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ زَبِيبٍ أَوْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ نِصْفُ ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ حِنْطَةٌ أَوْ دَقِيقٌ أَوْ سَوِيقٌ أَوْ ذُرَةٌ أَوْ سُلْتٌ عَنِ اَلصَّغِيرِ وَ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَ اَلذَّكَرِ وَ اَلْأُنْثَى وَاَلْبَالِغِ وَ مَنْ تَعُولُ فِي ذَلِكَ سَوَاءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, and Burayd, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) and Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon them both, said:
thaqalaynMatn: We asked the both Imams (a.s), peace be upon them both, about ‘Zakat al-Fitrah.’ They (a.s) both said: “One sa’ of dates, or raisins, or barley, or half of all of that as wheat, or flour, or parched flour, or maize, or a type of barley without husk (sult), on behalf of the young and the old, the male and the female, the adult, and those whom you support; in that they are the same.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Salamah Abu Hafs, from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The charity of al-Fitrah is upon every young and old, free person or slave, on behalf of everyone whom you support, meaning whom you spend upon: one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of raisins. Then when it was in the time of Uthman, he changed it to two mudds (muddayn) of wheat (qamh).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ سَلَمَةَ أَبِي حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ عَلَى كُلِّ صَغِيرٍ وَ كَبِيرٍ حُرٍّ أَوْ عَبْدٍ عَنْ كُلِّ مَنْ تَعُولُ يَعْنِي مَنْ تُنْفِقُ عَلَيْهِ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي زَمَنِ عُثْمَانَ حَوَّلَهُ مُدَّيْنِ مِنْ قَمْحٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Salamah Abu Hafs, from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The charity of al-Fitrah is upon every young and old, free person or slave, on behalf of everyone whom you support, meaning whom you spend upon: one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of raisins. Then when it was in the time of Uthman, he changed it to two mudds (muddayn) of wheat (qamh).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadhdha, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) mentioned “the charity of al-Fitrah, that it is upon every young and old, from free person or slave, male or female. It is one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of maize.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Then when it was in the time of Muawiyah (may Allah (swt) curse him) and the people became prosperous, the people turned away from that to half a sa’ of wheat.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْمَغْرَاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ اَلْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ ذَكَرَ» صَدَقَةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ أَنَّهَا عَلَى كُلِّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مِنْ حُرٍّ أَوْ عَبْدٍ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ ذُرَةٍ« قَالَ» فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي زَمَنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ« لَعَنَهُ اَللَّهُ» وَخَصَبَ اَلنَّاسُ عَدَلَ اَلنَّاسُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ إِلَى نِصْفِ صَاعٍ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadhdha, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) mentioned “the charity of al-Fitrah, that it is upon every young and old, from free person or slave, male or female. It is one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of maize.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Then when it was in the time of Muawiyah (may Allah (swt) curse him) and the people became prosperous, the people turned away from that to half a sa’ of wheat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 104

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Regarding the Fitrah, the Sunnah was established as one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley. Then when it was in the time of Uthman and wheat became abundant, the people assessed its value. So Uthman said, ‘Half a sa’ of wheat (burr) is equal to one sa’ of barley.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ جَرَتِ اَلسُّنَّةُ بِصَاعٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ صَاعٍ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ أَوْ صَاعٍ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي زَمَنِ عُثْمَانَ وَ كَثُرَتِ اَلْحِنْطَةُ قَوَّمَهُ اَلنَّاسُ فَقَالَ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ بُرٍّ بِصَاعٍ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Regarding the Fitrah, the Sunnah was established as one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of raisins, or one sa’ of barley. Then when it was in the time of Uthman and wheat became abundant, the people assessed its value. So Uthman said, ‘Half a sa’ of wheat (burr) is equal to one sa’ of barley.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 105

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abbad ibn Yaqub, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
Imam (a.s) said: “The first one who made two mudds (muddayn) of Zakat equal to one sa’ of dates was Uthman.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ :»أَنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ جَعَلَ مُدَّيْنِ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ عِدْلَ صَاعٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ عُثْمَانُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abbad ibn Yaqub, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The first one who made two mudds (muddayn) of Zakat equal to one sa’ of dates was Uthman.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 105

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, Yasir al-Qummi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “Fitrah is one sa’ of wheat, one sa’ of barley, one sa’ of dates, and one sa’ of raisins. It was only Muawiyah who reduced the wheat.” (May Allah (swt) curse him)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ يَاسِرٍ اَلْقُمِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلْفِطْرَةُ صَاعٌ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ وَ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ وَ صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ وَ صَاعٌ مِنْ زَبِيبٍ وَ إِنَّمَا خَفَّفَ اَلْحِنْطَةَ مُعَاوِيَةُ« لَعَنَهُ اَللَّهُ.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, Yasir al-Qummi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Fitrah is one sa’ of wheat, one sa’ of barley, one sa’ of dates, and one sa’ of raisins. It was only Muawiyah who reduced the wheat.” (May Allah (swt) curse him)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 105

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to the man (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking him about ‘the Fitrah and how much is to be paid.’ He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: ‘Six artal of dates according to the Madani measure, and that is nine according to the Baghdadi measure.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلرَّجُلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ كَمْ تُدْفَعُ قَالَ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» سِتَّةُ أَرْطَالٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ بِالْمَدَنِيِّ وَ ذَلِكَ تِسْعَةٌ بِالْبَغْدَادِيِّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to the man (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking him about ‘the Fitrah and how much is to be paid.’ He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: ‘Six artal of dates according to the Madani measure, and that is nine according to the Baghdadi measure.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 105

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Jafar ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, and he was with us as a pilgrim, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, through my father: “May I be made your ransom, our companions have differed regarding the sa’; some of them say the Fitrah is according to the Madani sa’, And some of them say according to the Iraqi sa’.” He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) wrote to me: ‘The sa’ is six artal according to the Madani measure, and nine artal according to the Iraqi measure.” He (narrator) said: “And Imam (a.s) informed me ‘that by weight it is one thousand one hundred and seventy waznah.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْهَمَذَانِيِّ وَ كَانَ مَعَنَا حَاجّاً قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى يَدِ أَبِي جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا اِخْتَلَفُوا فِي اَلصَّاعِ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ اَلْفِطْرَةُ بِصَاعِ اَلْمَدَنِيِّ وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَقُولُ بِصَاعِ اَلْعِرَاقِيِّ قَالَ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ» اَلصَّاعُ سِتَّةُ أَرْطَالٍ بِالْمَدَنِيِّ وَ تِسْعَةُ أَرْطَالٍ بِالْعِرَاقِيِّ« قَالَ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي» أَنَّهُ يَكُونُ بِالْوَزْنِ أَلْفاً وَ مِائَةً وَ سَبْعِينَ وَزْنَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Jafar ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, and he was with us as a pilgrim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, through my father: “May I be made your ransom, our companions have differed regarding the sa’; some of them say the Fitrah is according to the Madani sa’, And some of them say according to the Iraqi sa’.” He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) wrote to me: ‘The sa’ is six artal according to the Madani measure, and nine artal according to the Iraqi measure.” He (narrator) said: “And Imam (a.s) informed me ‘that by weight it is one thousand one hundred and seventy waznah.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 106

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And as for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to the man (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about ‘the Fitrah and its Zakat, how much is to be paid?’ Imam (a.s) wrote: “Four artal according to the Madani measure.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلرَّيَّانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلرَّجُلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ زَكَاتِهَا كَمْ تُؤَدَّى فَكَتَبَ» أَرْبَعَةُ أَرْطَالٍ بِالْمَدَنِيِّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to the man (Imam (a.s)), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about ‘the Fitrah and its Zakat, how much is to be paid?’ Imam (a.s) wrote: “Four artal according to the Madani measure.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 106

chapter: Chapter on Amount of Fitrah
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, raising it (rafahu), from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man in the desert (badiyah) who is not able to pay al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Let him give four ratls (artal) of milk in charity.”
arabicText: محمد بن احمد بن يحيى عن ابراهيم بن هاشم قال: حدثنا أبو الحسن علي بن سليمان عن الحسن بن علي عن القاسم بن الحسن رفعه عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: سئل عن رجل في البادية لا يمكنه الفطرة قال :تصدق بأربعة ارطال من اللبن
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, raising it (rafahu), from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man in the desert (badiyah) who is not able to pay al-fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Let him give four ratls (artal) of milk in charity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 106

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Mansur ibn Kharijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ of dates, or half a sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of barley, and dates are more beloved to me.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» صَاعٌ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ نِصْفُ صَاعٍ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ وَاَلتَّمْرُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Mansur ibn Kharijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “One sa’ of dates, or half a sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of barley, and dates are more beloved to me.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 107

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are better.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» اَلتَّمْرُ أَفْضَلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 107

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Dates in the Fitrah are better than other than them, because they are quicker in benefit, and that is because when they fall into the hand of their owner, he eats from them.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat was revealed while the people did not have wealth, and it was only the Fitrah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلتَّمْرُ فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ لِأَنَّهُ أَسْرَعُ مَنْفَعَةً وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا وَقَعَ فِي يَدِ صَاحِبِهِ أَكَلَ مِنْهُ« وَقَالَ» نَزَلَتِ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَلَيْسَ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْوَالٌ وَإِنَّمَا كَانَتِ اَلْفِطْرَةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Dates in the Fitrah are better than other than them, because they are quicker in benefit, and that is because when they fall into the hand of their owner, he eats from them.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Zakat was revealed while the people did not have wealth, and it was only the Fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Kufi narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Samaah narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Umarah ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “For me to give one sa’ of dates is more beloved to me than to give one sa’ of gold in the Fitrah.”
arabicText: أَبُو اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنُ قُولَوَيْهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حَمْدَانَ اَلْكُوفِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :»لَأَنْ أُعْطِيَ صَاعاً مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُعْطِيَ صَاعاً مِنْ ذَهَبٍ فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Kufi narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Samaah narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Umarah ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “For me to give one sa’ of dates is more beloved to me than to give one sa’ of gold in the Fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “On behalf of every head from your family, the young among them and the old, the free and the owned slave, the rich and the poor, everyone whom you have joined to yourself; on behalf of every person is one sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of barley, or dates, or raisins.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are more beloved to me, for indeed, for every date, you will have a palm tree in Paradise.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ قَالَ» عَنْ كُلِّ رَأْسٍ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ اَلصَّغِيرِ مِنْهُمْ وَ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَ اَلْحُرِّ وَ اَلْمَمْلُوكِ وَاَلْغَنِيِّ وَ اَلْفَقِيرِ كُلِّ مَنْ ضَمَمْتَ إِلَيْكَ عَنْ كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ صَاعٌ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ أَوْ صَاعٌ مِنْ شَعِيرٍ أَوْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ زَبِيبٍ« وَ قَالَ» اَلتَّمْرُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ فَإِنَّ لَكَ بِكُلِّ تَمْرَةٍ نَخْلَةً فِي اَلْجَنَّةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “On behalf of every head from your family, the young among them and the old, the free and the owned slave, the rich and the poor, everyone whom you have joined to yourself; on behalf of every person is one sa’ of wheat, or one sa’ of barley, or dates, or raisins.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Dates are more beloved to me, for indeed, for every date, you will have a palm tree in Paradise.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding the Fitrah? Is it permissible for me to pay it in silver, according to the value of these things which you have named?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed that is more beneficial for him; he buys with it whatever he wants.”
arabicText: اِبْنُ قُولَوَيْهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ اَلصَّيْرَفِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلْفِطْرَةِ يَجُوزُ أَنْ أُؤَدِّيَهَا فِضَّةً بِقِيمَةِ هَذِهِ اَلْأَشْيَاءِ اَلَّتِي سَمَّيْتَهَا قَالَ» نَعَمْ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَنْفَعُ لَهُ يَشْتَرِي بِهَا مَا يُرِيدُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding the Fitrah? Is it permissible for me to pay it in silver, according to the value of these things which you have named?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed that is more beneficial for him; he buys with it whatever he wants.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on Best Fitrah and the Amount of the Value
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in paying the value for al-fitrah.”
arabicText: احمد بن محمد عن الحسن بن علي بن فضال عن ثعلبة بن ميمون عن إسحاق بن عمار عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: لا بأس بالقيمة في الفطرة
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in paying the value for al-fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 108

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, who are its people for whom it becomes obligatory?’ Imam (a.s) said: “One who does not find anything.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ أَبُو اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنُ قُولَوَيْهِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ نَهِيكٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ مَنْ أَهْلُهَا اَلَّذِينَ تَجِبُ لَهُمْ قَالَ» مَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ شَيْئاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: What Abu al-Qasim ibn Qulawayh narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, who are its people for whom it becomes obligatory?’ Imam (a.s) said: “One who does not find anything.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Haytham, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked: “For whom is the Fitrah lawful?” Imam (a.s) said: “For one who does not find, and whoever it is lawful for, it is not lawful upon him.” He (narrator) said: “I said to Imam (a.s): ‘Is Zakat upon one who accepts Zakat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who accepts the Zakat of wealth, then upon him is Zakat al-Fitrah, and it is not upon him because of what he accepted; and there is no Fitrah upon one who accepts the Fitrah.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْهَيْثَمِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِمَنْ تَحِلُّ اَلْفِطْرَةُ قَالَ» لِمَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ وَ مَنْ حَلَّتْ لَهُ لَمْ تَحِلَّ عَلَيْهِ« قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ أَ عَلَى مَنْ قَبِلَ اَلزَّكَاةَ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ »أَمَّا مَنْ قَبِلَ زَكَاةَ اَلْمَالِ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَا قَبِلَهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ قَبِلَ اَلْفِطْرَةَ فِطْرَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Haytham, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked: “For whom is the Fitrah lawful?” Imam (a.s) said: “For one who does not find, and whoever it is lawful for, it is not lawful upon him.” He (narrator) said: “I said to Imam (a.s): ‘Is Zakat upon one who accepts Zakat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “As for one who accepts the Zakat of wealth, then upon him is Zakat al-Fitrah, and it is not upon him because of what he accepted; and there is no Fitrah upon one who accepts the Fitrah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 109

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘Zakat al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “You give it to the Muslims; and if you do not find a Muslim, then to a weak one (mustad'af); and give from it to your relative, if you wish.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ مَالِكٍ اَلْجُهَنِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ زَكَاةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ فَقَالَ» تُعْطِيهَا اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ مُسْلِماً فَمُسْتَضْعَفاً وَ أَعْطِ ذَا قَرَابَتِكَ مِنْهَا إِنْ شِئْتَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Malik al-Juhani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘Zakat al-Fitrah.’ Imam (a.s) said: “You give it to the Muslims; and if you do not find a Muslim, then to a weak one (mustad'af); and give from it to your relative, if you wish.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi:
I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “If you do not find one in whom to place the Fitrah, then set it aside at that hour before the prayer; and the charity is one sa’ of dates, or its value in those lands as dirhams.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:» إِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ مَنْ تَضَعُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ فِيهِ فَاعْزِلْهَا تِلْكَ اَلسَّاعَةَ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ بِصَاعٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ أَوْ قِيمَتِهِ فِي تِلْكَ اَلْبِلاَدِ دَرَاهِمَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Imam (a.s) saying: “If you do not find one in whom to place the Fitrah, then set it aside at that hour before the prayer; and the charity is one sa’ of dates, or its value in those lands as dirhams.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said:
Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to Imam (a.s), asking him about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, how much is it according to the ratl of Baghdad for every head, and is it permissible to give it to other than a believer?’ Imam (a.s) wrote to him: “You must take out on behalf of yourself one sa’ according to the sa’ of the Prophet (saws), and on behalf of your dependents also. It is not proper for you to give your Zakat except to a believer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ يَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ كَمْ هِيَ بِرِطْلِ بَغْدَادَ عَنْ كُلِّ رَأْسٍ وَ هَلْ يَجُوزُ إِعْطَاؤُهَا غَيْرَ مُؤْمِنٍ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ» عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُخْرِجَ عَنْ نَفْسِكَ صَاعاً بِصَاعِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ عَنْ عِيَالِكَ أَيْضاً لاَ يَنْبَغِي لَكَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَ زَكَاتَكَ إِلاَّ مُؤْمِناً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to Imam (a.s), asking him about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, how much is it according to the ratl of Baghdad for every head, and is it permissible to give it to other than a believer?’ Imam (a.s) wrote to him: “You must take out on behalf of yourself one sa’ according to the sa’ of the Prophet (saws), and on behalf of your dependents also. It is not proper for you to give your Zakat except to a believer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Ali ibn Bilal narrated to me, and I think I had heard it from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Is it permissible that a man be in one town, and a man from his brothers be in another town, needing that Fitrah be sent to him, or not?” Imam (a.s) wrote: “Divide the Fitrah among those who are present for it, and do not send that to another town, even if you do not find one who agrees.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ وَأَرَانِي قَدْ سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي بَلْدَةٍ وَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ إِخْوَانِهِ فِي بَلْدَةٍ أُخْرَى يَحْتَاجُ أَنْ يُوَجَّهَ لَهُ فِطْرَةٌ أَمْ لاَ فَكَتَبَ» تَقْسِمُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ عَلَى مَنْ حَضَرَهَا وَلاَ تُوَجِّهْ ذَلِكَ إِلَى بَلْدَةٍ أُخْرَى وَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ مُوَافِقاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Ali ibn Bilal narrated to me, and I think I had heard it from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Is it permissible that a man be in one town, and a man from his brothers be in another town, needing that Fitrah be sent to him, or not?” Imam (a.s) wrote: “Divide the Fitrah among those who are present for it, and do not send that to another town, even if you do not find one who agrees.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 110

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah, may I give it to those other than the people of my wilayah from my neighbors?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it because of the place of public recognition.”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ أُعْطِيهَا غَيْرَ أَهْلِ وَلاَيَتِي مِنْ جِيرَانِي قَالَ» نَعَمْ اَلْجِيرَانُ أَحَقُّ بِهَا لِمَكَانِ اَلشُّهْرَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah, may I give it to those other than the people of my wilayah from my neighbors?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it because of the place of public recognition.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My grandfather (a.s), peace be upon him, used to give his Fitrah to the weak, and to one who does not find, and to one who does not profess wilayah.” He (narrator) said: “And Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘It is for its people, unless you do not find them; so if you do not find them, then to one who does not show enmity (nasb), and do not transfer it from one land to another land.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Imam knows best; he places it wherever he wishes and does with it whatever he sees.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ جَدِّي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُعْطِي فِطْرَتَهُ اَلضُّعَفَاءَ وَ مَنْ لاَ يَجِدُ وَ مَنْ لاَ يَتَوَلَّى« قَالَ وَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» هِيَ لِأَهْلِهَا إِلاَّ أَنْ لاَ تَجِدَهُمْ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْهُمْ فَلِمَنْ لاَ يَنْصِبُ وَ لاَ تَنْقُلْ مِنْ أَرْضٍ إِلَى أَرْضٍ« وَ قَالَ» اَلْإِمَامُ أَعْلَمُ يَضَعُهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ وَ يَصْنَعُ فِيهَا مَا يَرَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: What Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My grandfather (a.s), peace be upon him, used to give his Fitrah to the weak, and to one who does not find, and to one who does not profess wilayah.” He (narrator) said: “And Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘It is for its people, unless you do not find them; so if you do not find them, then to one who does not show enmity (nasb), and do not transfer it from one land to another land.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The Imam knows best; he places it wherever he wishes and does with it whatever he sees.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 111

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give anyone less than one head’s share.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تُعْطِ أَحَداً أَقَلَّ مِنْ رَأْسٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not give anyone less than one head’s share.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 112

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah, Is it from what Allah (swt), the Exalted, said: ‘Establish the prayer and give the Zakat?’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:43) Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The charity of dates is more beloved to me, because my father (a.s), the blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him, used to give charity with dates.” I (narrator) said: “Then may he make its value silver and give it to one man or two?” Imam (a.s) said: “To distribute it is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in making it silver, and dates are more beloved to me.” I asked: “Then may I give it to those other than people of wilayah from the neighbors?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it.” I (narrator) asked: “Then may I give one man three sa’s (asyu) and four sa’s (asyu)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَدَقَةِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ أَ هِيَ مِمَّا قَالَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى» أَقِيمُوا اَلصَّلاٰةَ وَآتُو ااَلزَّكٰاةَ« فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ« وَقَالَ» صَدَقَةُ اَلتَّمْرِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ لِأَنَّ أَبِي صَلَوَاتُُ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ كَانَ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِالتَّمْرِ« قُلْتُ فَيَجْعَلُ قِيمَتَهَا فِضَّةً فَيُعْطِيهَا رَجُلاً وَاحِداً أَوِ اِثْنَيْنِ فَقَالَ» يُفَرِّقُهَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ وَلاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَجْعَلَهَا فِضَّةً وَاَلتَّمْرُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ« قُلْتُ فَأُعْطِيهَا غَيْرَ أَهْلِ اَلْوَلاَيَةِ مِنْ هَذَا اَلْجِيرَانِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ اَلْجِيرَانُ أَحَقُّ بِهَا« قُلْتُ فَأُعْطِي اَلرَّجُلَ اَلْوَاحِدَ ثَلاَثَةَ أَصْيُعٍ وَ أَرْبَعَةَ أَصْيُعٍ قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the charity of al-Fitrah, Is it from what Allah (swt), the Exalted, said: ‘Establish the prayer and give the Zakat?’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:43) Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The charity of dates is more beloved to me, because my father (a.s), the blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him, used to give charity with dates.” I (narrator) said: “Then may he make its value silver and give it to one man or two?” Imam (a.s) said: “To distribute it is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in making it silver, and dates are more beloved to me.” I asked: “Then may I give it to those other than people of wilayah from the neighbors?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it.” I (narrator) asked: “Then may I give one man three sa’s (asyu) and four sa’s (asyu)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on One Entitled to Fitrah and the Least Amount of It That Is Given to the Poor Person
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in a man being given two heads, and three, and four,” meaning the Fitrah.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُعْطَى اَلرَّجُلُ اَلرَّأْسَيْنِ وَ ثَلاَثَةً وَ أَرْبَعَةً« يَعْنِي اَلْفِطْرَةَ.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in a man being given two heads, and three, and four,” meaning the Fitrah.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 113

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Giving Out Zakat to the Imam
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, for whom is it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “For the Imam.” He (narrator) said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): ‘Shall I inform my companions?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, whoever among them you want to purify.” And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it being given and the price of that being carried as silver coin (wariq).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيِّ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ لِمَنْ هِيَ قَالَ» لِلْإِمَامِ« قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَ فَأُخْبِرُ أَصْحَابِي قَالَ» نَعَمْ مَنْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُطَهِّرَهُ مِنْهُمْ« وَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُعْطَى وَ يُحْمَلَ ثَمَنُ ذَلِكَ وَرِقاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the (zakat of) Fitrah, for whom is it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “For the Imam.” He (narrator) said: “So I said to Imam (a.s): ‘Shall I inform my companions?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, whoever among them you want to purify.” And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it being given and the price of that being carried as silver coin (wariq).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 114

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Giving Out Zakat to the Imam
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Jafar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “Some people ask me about the (zakat of) Fitrah, and they ask me to carry its value to you. This man had sent to you the year before last and asked me to ask you, but I forgot that. And this year he has sent to you, on behalf of every head from his dependents, one dirham, for the value of nine artal of dates at one dirham. So your view, may Allah (swt) make me your ransom, regarding that?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “The Fitrah, questioning about it has become frequent, and I dislike everything that leads to public recognition. So cut off the mention of that. Therefore, receive from whoever pays it, and refrain from whoever does not pay.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ قَوْماً يَسْأَلُونِّي عَنِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ وَ يَسْأَلُونِّي أَنْ يَحْمِلُوا قِيمَتَهَا إِلَيْكَ وَقَدْ بَعَثَ إِلَيْكَ هَذَا اَلرَّجُلُ عَامَ أَوَّلٍ وَسَأَلَنِي أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ فَنَسِيتُ ذَلِكَ وَ قَدْ بَعَثَ إِلَيْكَ اَلْعَامَ عَنْ كُلِّ رَأْسٍ مِنْ عِيَالِهِ بِدِرْهَمٍ عَنْ قِيمَةِ تِسْعَةِ أَرْطَالِ تَمْرٍ بِدِرْهَمٍ فَرَأْيُكَ جَعَلَنِيَ اَللَّهُ فِدَاكَ فِي ذَلِكَ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» اَلْفِطْرَةُ قَدْ كَثُرَ اَلسُّؤَالُ عَنْهَا وَ أَنَا أَكْرَهُ كُلَّمَا أَدَّى إِلَى اَلشُّهْرَةِ فَاقْطَعُوا ذِكْرَ ذَلِكَ فَاقْبِضْ مِمَّنْ دَفَعَ لَهَا وَ أَمْسِكْ عَمَّنْ لَمْ يَدْفَعْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Jafar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “Some people ask me about the (zakat of) Fitrah, and they ask me to carry its value to you. This man had sent to you the year before last and asked me to ask you, but I forgot that. And this year he has sent to you, on behalf of every head from his dependents, one dirham, for the value of nine artal of dates at one dirham. So your view, may Allah (swt) make me your ransom, regarding that?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “The Fitrah, questioning about it has become frequent, and I dislike everything that leads to public recognition. So cut off the mention of that. Therefore, receive from whoever pays it, and refrain from whoever does not pay.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 114

chapter: Chapter on Obligation of Giving Out Zakat to the Imam
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his brother Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:
I (narrator) sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, dirhams belonging to me and to others, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) informing him that they were from the Fitrah of the dependents. Imam (a.s) wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received and accepted.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ قَالَ: بَعَثْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِدَرَاهِمَ لِي وَلِغَيْرِي وَ كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّهَا مِنْ فِطْرَةِ اَلْعِيَالِ فَكَتَبَ بِخَطِّهِ »قَبَضْتُ وَ قَبِلْتُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his brother Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, dirhams belonging to me and to others, and I wrote to Imam (a.s) informing him that they were from the Fitrah of the dependents. Imam (a.s) wrote in his own handwriting: “I have received and accepted.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Mukhtar ibn Ziyad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has one hundred dirhams, and ninety-nine dirhams, and thirty-nine dinars; does he pay Zakat on them?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, there is nothing of Zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until forty dinars are completed, and the dirhams are two hundred dirhams.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then a man has four she-camels (aynuq), thirty-nine sheep, and twenty-nine cows; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not pay Zakat on anything from them, because nothing from them has been completed, so Zakat is not obligatory in it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَ تِسْعَةٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ دِرْهَماً وَ تِسْعَةٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ دِينَاراً أَيُزَكِّيهَا فَقَالَ» لاَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فِي اَلدَّرَاهِمِ وَ لاَ فِي اَلدَّنَانِيرِ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ أَرْبَعُونَ دِينَاراً وَ اَلدَّرَاهِمُ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَرَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ أَرْبَعَةُ أَيْنُقٍ وَ تِسْعٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ شَاةً وَ تِسْعٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ بَقَرَةً أَيُزَكِّيهِنَّ فَقَالَ» لاَ يُزَكِّي شَيْئاً مِنْهَا لِأَنَّهَا لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنْهُنَّ قَدْ تَمَّ فَلَيْسَ تَجِبُ فِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Mukhtar ibn Ziyad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has one hundred dirhams, and ninety-nine dirhams, and thirty-nine dinars; does he pay Zakat on them?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, there is nothing of Zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until forty dinars are completed, and the dirhams are two hundred dirhams.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then a man has four she-camels (aynuq), thirty-nine sheep, and twenty-nine cows; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not pay Zakat on anything from them, because nothing from them has been completed, so Zakat is not obligatory in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s) and to his son (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has abundant produce from various kinds, or wealth in which there is no single kind in which Zakat becomes obligatory; is there upon him, in all of it, one Zakat?” So the both Imams (a.s) said: “No, it only becomes obligatory upon him when it is completed, so Zakat becomes obligatory in each kind of it. So if his land brings forth something in the amount in which charity is not obligatory, of various kinds, one Zakat is not obligatory in it.” Zurarah said: “I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), ‘A man has one hundred dirhams, and ninety-nine dirhams, and thirty-nine dinars; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, there is nothing of Zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until he completes forty dinars and two hundred dirhams.” Zurarah said: “And likewise it is in all things.” He (narrator) said: “And I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘A man had four she-camels (aynuq), thirty-nine sheep, and twenty-nine cows; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not pay Zakat on anything from them, because nothing from them has been completed, so Zakat is not obligatory in it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَلاِبْنِهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ تَكُونُ لَهُ اَلْغَلَّةُ اَلْكَثِيرَةُ مِنْ أَصْنَافٍ شَتَّى أَوْ مَالٌ لَيْسَ فِيهِ صِنْفٌ تَجِبُ فِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ فِي جَمِيعِهِ زَكَاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالاَ» لاَ إِنَّمَا تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا تَمَّ فَكَانَ تَجِبُ فِي كُلِّ صِنْفٍ مِنْهُ اَلزَّكَاةُ فَإِنْ أَخْرَجَتْ أَرْضُهُ شَيْئاً قَدْرَ مَا لاَ تَجِبُ فِيهِ اَلصَّدَقَةُ أَصْنَافاً شَتَّى لَمْ تَجِبْ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ« قَالَ زُرَارَةُ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَ تِسْعَةٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ دِرْهَماً وَ تِسْعَةٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ دِينَاراً أَيُزَكِّيهَا قَالَ» لاَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فِي اَلدَّرَاهِمِ وَ لاَ فِي اَلدَّنَانِيرِ حَتَّى يُتِمَّ أَرْبَعِينَ دِينَاراً وَ اَلدَّرَاهِمَ مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ« قَالَ زُرَارَةُ وَ كَذَلِكَ هُوَ فِي جَمِيعِ اَلْأَشْيَاءِ قَالَ وَقُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ أَرْبَعَةُ أَيْنُقٍ وَتِسْعٌ وَ ثَلاَثُونَ شَاةً وَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ بَقَرَةً أَيُزَكِّيهِنَّ فَقَالَ» لاَ يُزَكِّي شَيْئاً مِنْهَا لِأَنَّهُ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنْهُنَّ تَمَّ فَلَيْسَ تَجِبُ فِيهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s) and to his son (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man has abundant produce from various kinds, or wealth in which there is no single kind in which Zakat becomes obligatory; is there upon him, in all of it, one Zakat?” So the both Imams (a.s) said: “No, it only becomes obligatory upon him when it is completed, so Zakat becomes obligatory in each kind of it. So if his land brings forth something in the amount in which charity is not obligatory, of various kinds, one Zakat is not obligatory in it.” Zurarah said: “I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), ‘A man has one hundred dirhams, and ninety-nine dirhams, and thirty-nine dinars; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “No, there is nothing of Zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until he completes forty dinars and two hundred dirhams.” Zurarah said: “And likewise it is in all things.” He (narrator) said: “And I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: ‘A man had four she-camels (aynuq), thirty-nine sheep, and twenty-nine cows; does he pay Zakat on them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not pay Zakat on anything from them, because nothing from them has been completed, so Zakat is not obligatory in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “One hundred and ninety dirhams and nineteen dinars, is there anything upon them in Zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “When gold and silver are gathered together and that reaches two hundred dirhams, then Zakat is due in them, because the substance of wealth is dirhams, and everything besides dirhams, whether gold or goods, is merchandise (arad) returned to dirhams in Zakat and blood-money.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ تِسْعُونَ وَ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَ تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ دِينَاراً أَ عَلَيْهَا فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ »إِذَا اِجْتَمَعَ اَلذَّهَبُ وَ اَلْفِضَّةُ فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ فَفِيهَا اَلزَّكَاةُ لِأَنَّ عَيْنَ اَلْمَالِ اَلدَّرَاهِمُ وَ كُلُّمَا خَلاَ اَلدَّرَاهِمَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ فَهُوَ عَرْضٌ مَرْدُودٌ ذَلِكَ إِلَى اَلدَّرَاهِمِ فِي اَلزَّكَاةِ وَ اَلدِّيَاتِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “One hundred and ninety dirhams and nineteen dinars, is there anything upon them in Zakat?” Imam (a.s) said: “When gold and silver are gathered together and that reaches two hundred dirhams, then Zakat is due in them, because the substance of wealth is dirhams, and everything besides dirhams, whether gold or goods, is merchandise (arad) returned to dirhams in Zakat and blood-money.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has one hundred dirhams and ten dinars, Is Zakat upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he fled with them from Zakat, then Zakat is upon him.” I (narrator) asked: “He did not flee with them; he inherited one hundred dirhams and ten dinars.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Zakat upon him.” I (narrator) asked: “Then he does not break the dirhams against the dinars, nor the dinars against the dirhams?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَهُ مِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ وَ عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِيرَ أَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ فَرَّ بِهَا مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلزَّكَاةُ« قُلْتُ لَمْ يَفِرَّ بِهَا وَرِثَ مِائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ وَ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِيرَ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ« قُلْتُ فَلاَ يَكْسِرُ اَلدَّرَاهِمَ عَلَى اَلدَّنَانِيرِ وَ لاَ اَلدَّنَانِيرَ عَلَى اَلدَّرَاهِمِ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has one hundred dirhams and ten dinars, Is Zakat upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he fled with them from Zakat, then Zakat is upon him.” I (narrator) asked: “He did not flee with them; he inherited one hundred dirhams and ten dinars.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Zakat upon him.” I (narrator) asked: “Then he does not break the dirhams against the dinars, nor the dinars against the dirhams?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This is indicated by what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) the Second (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Is it permissible, may I be made your ransom, that what is obligatory from cultivation, from wheat and barley. And what is obligatory upon gold, be taken out as dirhams according to the value of what it is worth, or is it not permissible except that from each thing, what is in it be taken out?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, answered: “Whichever is easier may be taken out.”
arabicText: يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ اَلثَّانِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ مَا يَجِبُ مِنَ اَلْحَرْثِ مِنَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ وَ اَلشَّعِيرِ وَ مَا يَجِبُ عَلَى اَلذَّهَبِ دَرَاهِمَ بِقِيمَةِ مَا يَسْوَى أَمْ لاَ يَجُوزُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَا فِيهِ فَأَجَابَهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» أَيُّمَا تَيَسَّرَ يُخْرَجُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: This is indicated by what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu Ja’far (a.s) the Second (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Is it permissible, may I be made your ransom, that what is obligatory from cultivation, from wheat and barley. And what is obligatory upon gold, be taken out as dirhams according to the value of what it is worth, or is it not permissible except that from each thing, what is in it be taken out?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, answered: “Whichever is easier may be taken out.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who gives from his Zakat, for dirhams, dinars, and for dinars, dirhams, according to the value. Is that lawful for him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُعْطِي مِنْ زَكَاتِهِ عَنِ اَلدَّرَاهِمِ دَنَانِيرَ وَ عَنِ اَلدَّنَانِيرِ دَرَاهِمَ بِالْقِيمَةِ أَ يَحِلُّ ذَلِكَ لَهُ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who gives from his Zakat, for dirhams, dinars, and for dinars, dirhams, according to the value. Is that lawful for him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin ibn Abdullah ibn Zamah, from his father, from the grandfather of his father:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote for him in his letter, which he wrote for him in his own handwriting when he sent him over the charities: “Whoever has reached, among the camels with him, the charity of a four-year-old she-camel (jadhaah), but he does not have a four-year-old she-camel, and he has a three-year-old she-camel (hiqqah), then the three-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and he places with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has reached, with him, the charity of a three-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a three-year-old she-camel, and he has a four-year-old she-camel, then the four-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector (musaddiq) gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a three-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a three-year-old she-camel, and he has a two-year-old she-camel (bint labun), then it is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a two-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a two-year-old she-camel, and he has a three-year-old she-camel, then the three-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a two-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a two-year-old she-camel, and he has a one-year-old she-camel (bint makhad), then the one-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a one-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a one-year-old she-camel, and he has a two-year-old she-camel, then the two-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever does not have a one-year-old she-camel in its proper form, and he has a two-year-old male camel (ibn labun), then the two-year-old male camel is accepted from him, and there is nothing with it. And whoever has with him only four camels, and has no wealth besides them, then there is nothing due on them unless their owner wishes. Then when his wealth reaches five camels, then in it is one sheep.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُقَرِّنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ زَمْعَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّ أَبِيهِ: أَنَّ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَتَبَ لَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ اَلَّذِي كَتَبَهُ لَهُ بِخَطِّهِ حِينَ بَعَثَهُ عَلَى اَلصَّدَقَاتِ» مَنْ بَلَغَتْ عِنْدَهُ مِنَ اَلْإِبِلِ اَلصَّدَقَةُ اَلْجَذَعَةَ وَ لَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ جَذَعَةٌ وَ عِنْدَهُ حِقَّةٌ فَإِنَّهُ تُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ اَلْحِقَّةُ وَ يَجْعَلُ مَعَهَا شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَ مَنْ بَلَغَتْ عِنْدَهُ صَدَقَةُ اَلْحِقَّةِ وَ لَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ اَلْحِقَّةُ وَ عِنْدَهُ جَذَعَةٌ فَإِنَّهُ تُقْبَلُ مَعَهُ جَذَعَةٌ وَ يُعْطِيهِ اَلْمُصَدِّقُ شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَمَنْ بَلَغَتْ صَدَقَتُهُ حِقَّةً وَلَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ حِقَّةٌ وَعِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ لَبُونٍ فَإِنَّهُ يُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ وَ يُعْطِي مَعَهَا شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَمَنْ بَلَغَتْ صَدَقَتُهُ اِبْنَةَ لَبُونٍ وَ لَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ لَبُونٍ وَ عِنْدَهُ حِقَّةٌ فَإِنَّهُ تُقْبَلُ اَلْحِقَّةُ مِنْهُ وَ يُعْطِيهِ اَلْمُصَدِّقُ شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَ مَنْ بَلَغَتْ صَدَقَتُهُ اِبْنَةَ لَبُونٍ وَ لَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ لَبُونٍ وَ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ فَإِنَّهُ تُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ اِبْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ وَ يُعْطِي مَعَهَا شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَ مَنْ بَلَغَتْ صَدَقَتُهُ اِبْنَةَ مَخَاضٍ وَ لَيْسَتْ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ وَ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ لَبُونٍ فَإِنَّهُ تُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ اِبْنَةُ لَبُونٍ وَ يُعْطِيهِ اَلْمُصَدِّقُ شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَماً وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا وَ عِنْدَهُ اِبْنُ لَبُونٍ ذَكَرٌ فَإِنَّهُ يُقْبَلُ مِنْهُ اِبْنُ لَبُونٍ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ شَيْءٌ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ أَرْبَعَةٌ مِنَ اَلْإِبِلِ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهَا فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبُّهَا فَإِذَا بَلَغَ مَالُهُ خَمْساً مِنَ اَلْإِبِلِ فَفِيهِ شَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin ibn Abdullah ibn Zamah, from his father, from the grandfather of his father:
thaqalaynMatn: The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote for him in his letter, which he wrote for him in his own handwriting when he sent him over the charities: “Whoever has reached, among the camels with him, the charity of a four-year-old she-camel (jadhaah), but he does not have a four-year-old she-camel, and he has a three-year-old she-camel (hiqqah), then the three-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and he places with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has reached, with him, the charity of a three-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a three-year-old she-camel, and he has a four-year-old she-camel, then the four-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector (musaddiq) gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a three-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a three-year-old she-camel, and he has a two-year-old she-camel (bint labun), then it is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a two-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a two-year-old she-camel, and he has a three-year-old she-camel, then the three-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a two-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a two-year-old she-camel, and he has a one-year-old she-camel (bint makhad), then the one-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever has his charity reach a one-year-old she-camel, but he does not have a one-year-old she-camel, and he has a two-year-old she-camel, then the two-year-old she-camel is accepted from him, and the charity collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams. And whoever does not have a one-year-old she-camel in its proper form, and he has a two-year-old male camel (ibn labun), then the two-year-old male camel is accepted from him, and there is nothing with it. And whoever has with him only four camels, and has no wealth besides them, then there is nothing due on them unless their owner wishes. Then when his wealth reaches five camels, then in it is one sheep.”
