chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Burayd ibn Muawiyah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, sent a collector of charity (musaddiq) from al-Kufah to its desert, so Imam (a.s) said to him: ‘Go forth, O servant of Allah (swt), and upon you is the fear of Allah (swt) alone, who has no partner, and never prefer your world over your Hereafter. Be a guardian over what I have entrusted you with, observing the right of Allah (swt) in it, until you come to the assembly of the Banu ‘so-and-so’. When you arrive, then stop at their water without mixing with their houses, then proceed to them with calmness and dignity until you stand among them and greet them. Then say to them: ‘O servants of Allah (swt), the wali of Allah (swt) has sent me to you so that I may take from you the right of Allah (swt) in your wealth. Is there a right of Allah (swt) in your wealth, so that you may pay it to His (swt) wali?’ If someone says to you: ‘No’, then do not return to him. But if one of them responds affirmatively to you, then go with him without frightening him or promising him anything except good. When you come to his wealth, do not enter it except with his permission, for most of it belongs to him. So say to him: ‘O servant of Allah (swt), do you permit me to enter your wealth?’ If he permits you, then do not enter with the entry of one who dominates him in it, nor one who is harsh with him. Divide the wealth into two divisions, then give him the choice of whichever of the two divisions he wishes. Whichever of them he chooses, do not object to him. Then divide the remaining into two divisions, then give him the choice, and whichever of them he chooses, do not object to him. Continue like that until there remains that in which there is fulfilment of the right of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in his wealth. When that remains, then take the right of Allah (swt) from it. If he asks you to release him from the transaction, then release him; then mix them both together and do the like of what you did first, until you take the right of Allah (swt) in his wealth. When you have taken it, do not appoint over it except one who is sincere, compassionate, trustworthy, preserving, and not harsh with anything from it. Then bring down to us what has gathered with you from every assembly, so that we may place it where Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has commanded. When your messenger brings them down, then instruct him not to separate a she-camel from her young one (fasil), and not to separate between them, and not to withhold her milk, lest that harm her young one. He should not exhaust her (she-camel) by riding, and he should be just among them in that. He should bring them (camels) to every water he passes by, and he should not turn them away from the plants of the earth to the middle of the roads at the hour in which they rest and are milked in the evening. He should be gentle with them (camels) to the utmost of his ability until they come to us, by the permission of Allah (swt), healthy, fat, not tired and not exhausted. Then we shall divide them, by the permission of Allah (swt), according to the Book of Allah (swt) and the Sunnah of His Prophet (saws), Allah (swt) bless him and his family, among the awliya of Allah (swt). Indeed, that is greater for your reward and nearer to your right guidance. Allah (swt) looks at them, and at you, and at your effort, and your sincerity toward the one who sent you and toward whose need you were sent. For indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Allah (swt) does not look at a wali of His (swt) who exerts himself in obedience and sincerity toward his Imam, except that he will be with us in the highest company.’” He (narrator) said: “Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, wept. Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “O Burayd, by Allah (swt), no sanctity of Allah (swt) has remained except that it has been violated, and neither the Book of Allah (swt) nor the Sunnah of His Prophet (saws) has been acted upon in this world, And no legal punishment has been established among this creation since Allah (swt) took Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, and nothing of the truth has been acted upon until this day of the people.” Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, by Allah (swt), the days and nights will not pass until Allah (swt) gives life to the dead, causes the living to die, returns the truth to its people, and establishes His (swt) religion which He (swt) approved for Himself (swt) and His Prophet (saws). So rejoice, then rejoice, for by Allah (swt), the truth is only in your hands.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» بَعَثَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مُصَدِّقاً مِنَ اَلْكُوفَةِ إِلَى بَادِيَتِهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ» اِنْطَلِقْ يَا عَبْدَ اَللَّهِ وَ عَلَيْكَ بِتَقْوَى اَللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ لاَ تُؤْثِرَنَّ دُنْيَاكَ عَلَى آخِرَتِكَ وَ كُنْ حَافِظاً لِمَا اِئْتَمَنْتُكَ عَلَيْهِ رَاعِياً لِحَقِّ اَللَّهِ فِيهِ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ نَادِيَ بَنِي فُلاَنٍ فَإِذَا قَدِمْتَ فَانْزِلْ بِمَائِهِمْ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ تُخَالِطَ أَبْيَاتَهُمْ ثُمَّ اِمْضِ إِلَيْهِمْ بِسَكِينَةٍ وَ وَقَارٍ حَتَّى تَقُومَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَتُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ قُلْ لَهُمْ يَا عِبَادَ اَللَّهِ أَرْسَلَنِي إِلَيْكُمْ وَلِيُّ اَللَّهِ لآِخُذَ مِنْكُمْ حَقَّ اَللَّهِ فِي أَمْوَالِكُمْ فَهَلْ لِلَّهِ فِي أَمْوَالِكُمْ حَقٌّ فَتُؤَدُّوهُ إِلَى وَلِيِّهِ فَإِنْ قَالَ لَكَ قَائِلٌ لاَ فَلاَ تُرَاجِعْهُ فَإِنْ أَنْعَمَ لَكَ مُنْعِمٌ مِنْهُمْ فَانْطَلِقْ مَعَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ تُخِيفَهُ أَوْ تَعِدَهُ إِلاَّ خَيْراً فَإِذَا أَتَيْتَ مَالَهُ فَلاَ تَدْخُلْهُ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ فَإِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُ لَهُ فَقُلْ لَهُ يَا عَبْدَ اَللَّهِ أَتَأْذَنُ لِي فِي دُخُولِ مَالِكَ فَإِنْ أَذِنَ لَكَ فَلاَ تَدْخُلْ دُخُولَ مُتَسَلِّطٍ عَلَيْهِ فِيهِ وَ لاَ عَنِفٍ بِهِ فَاصْدَعِ اَلْمَالَ صَدْعَيْنِ ثُمَّ خَيِّرْهُ أَيَّ اَلصَّدْعَيْنِ شَاءَ فَأَيَّهُمَا اِخْتَارَ فَلاَ تَعْرِضْ لَهُ ثُمَّ اِصْدَعِ اَلْبَاقِيَ صَدْعَيْنِ ثُمَّ خَيِّرْهُ فَأَيَّهُمَا اِخْتَارَ فَلاَ تَعْرِضْ لَهُ وَ لاَ تَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَبْقَى مَا فِيهِ وَفَاءٌ لِحَقِّ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي مَالِهِ فَإِذَا بَقِيَ ذَلِكَ فَاقْبِضْ حَقَّ اَللَّهِ مِنْهُ فَإِنِ اِسْتَقَالَكَ فَأَقِلْهُ ثُمَّ اِخْلِطْهُمَا وَ اِصْنَعْ مِثْلَ اَلَّذِي صَنَعْتَ أَوَّلاً حَتَّى تَأْخُذَ حَقَّ اَللَّهِ فِي مَالِهِ فَإِذَا قَبَضْتَهُ فَلاَ تُوَكِّلْ بِهِ إِلاَّ نَاصِحاً شَفِيقاً أَمِيناً حَفِيظاً غَيْرَ مُعْنِفٍ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهَا ثُمَّ اُحْدُرْ مَا اِجْتَمَعَ عِنْدَكَ مِنْ كُلِّ نَادٍ إِلَيْنَا نُصَيِّرْهُ حَيْثُ أَمَرَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَإِذَا اِنْحَدَرَ بِهَا رَسُولُكَ فَأَوْعِزْ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ لاَ يَحُولَ بَيْنَ نَاقَةٍ وَ بَيْنَ فَصِيلِهَا وَ لاَ يُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ لاَ يَصُرَّنَّ لَبَنَهَا فَيُضِرَّ ذَلِكَ بِفَصِيلِهَا وَ لاَ يَجْهَدْ بِهَا رُكُوباً وَلْيَعْدِلْ بَيْنَهُنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ وَ لْيُورِدْهُنَّ كُلَّ مَاءٍ يَمُرُّ بِهِ وَ لاَ يَعْدِلْ بِهِنَّ عَنْ نَبْتِ اَلْأَرْضِ إِلَى جَوَادِّ اَلطُّرُقِ فِي اَلسَّاعَةِ اَلَّتِي فِيهَا تُرِيحُ وَتَغْبِقُ وَ لْيَرْفُقْ بِهِنَّ جُهْدَهُ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَنَا بِإِذْنِ اَللَّهِ صِحَاحاً سِمَاناً غَيْرَ مُتْعَبَاتٍ وَ لاَ مُجْهَدَاتٍ فَنَقْسِمَهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ اَللَّهِ عَلَى كِتَابِ اَللَّهِ وَ سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ عَلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ اَللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَعْظَمُ لِأَجْرِكَ وَ أَقْرَبُ لِرُشْدِكَ يَنْظُرُ اَللَّهُ إِلَيْهَا وَ إِلَيْكَ وَ إِلَى جُهْدِكَ وَنَصِيحَتِكَ لِمَنْ بَعَثَكَ وَ بُعِثْتَ فِي حَاجَتِهِ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ قَالَ» مَا يَنْظُرُ اَللَّهُ إِلَى وَلِيٍّ لَهُ يَجْهَدُ نَفْسَهُ بِالطَّاعَةِ وَاَلنَّصِيحَةِ لِإِمَامِهِ إِلاَّ كَانَ مَعَنَا فِي اَلرَّفِيقِ اَلْأَعْلَى««« قَالَ ثُمَّ بَكَى أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ ثُمَّ قَالَ» يَا بُرَيْدُ وَ اَللَّهِ مَا بَقِيَتْ لِلَّهِ حُرْمَةٌ إِلاَّ اُنْتُهِكَتْ وَ لاَ عُمِلَ بِكِتَابِ اَللَّهِ وَ لاَ سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ فِي هَذَا اَلْعَالَمِ وَ لاَ أُقِيمَ فِي هَذَا اَلْخَلْقِ حَدٌّ مُنْذُ قَبَضَ اَللَّهُ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ لاَ عُمِلَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْحَقِّ إِلَى يَوْمِ اَلنَّاسِ هَذَا« ثُمَّ قَالَ» أَمَا وَ اَللَّهِ لاَ تَذْهَبُ اَلْأَيَّامُ وَ اَللَّيَالِي حَتَّى يُحْيِيَ اَللَّهُ اَلْمَوْتَى وَ يُمِيتَ اَلْأَحْيَاءَ وَ يَرُدَّ اَلْحَقَّ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ وَ يُقِيمَ دِينَهُ اَلَّذِي اِرْتَضَاهُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَ نَبِيِّهِ فَأَبْشِرُوا ثُمَّ أَبْشِرُوا فَوَاَللَّهِ مَا اَلْحَقُّ إِلاَّ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Burayd ibn Muawiyah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, sent a collector of charity (musaddiq) from al-Kufah to its desert, so Imam (a.s) said to him: ‘Go forth, O servant of Allah (swt), and upon you is the fear of Allah (swt) alone, who has no partner, and never prefer your world over your Hereafter. Be a guardian over what I have entrusted you with, observing the right of Allah (swt) in it, until you come to the assembly of the Banu ‘so-and-so’. When you arrive, then stop at their water without mixing with their houses, then proceed to them with calmness and dignity until you stand among them and greet them. Then say to them: ‘O servants of Allah (swt), the wali of Allah (swt) has sent me to you so that I may take from you the right of Allah (swt) in your wealth. Is there a right of Allah (swt) in your wealth, so that you may pay it to His (swt) wali?’ If someone says to you: ‘No’, then do not return to him. But if one of them responds affirmatively to you, then go with him without frightening him or promising him anything except good. When you come to his wealth, do not enter it except with his permission, for most of it belongs to him. So say to him: ‘O servant of Allah (swt), do you permit me to enter your wealth?’ If he permits you, then do not enter with the entry of one who dominates him in it, nor one who is harsh with him. Divide the wealth into two divisions, then give him the choice of whichever of the two divisions he wishes. Whichever of them he chooses, do not object to him. Then divide the remaining into two divisions, then give him the choice, and whichever of them he chooses, do not object to him. Continue like that until there remains that in which there is fulfilment of the right of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, in his wealth. When that remains, then take the right of Allah (swt) from it. If he asks you to release him from the transaction, then release him; then mix them both together and do the like of what you did first, until you take the right of Allah (swt) in his wealth. When you have taken it, do not appoint over it except one who is sincere, compassionate, trustworthy, preserving, and not harsh with anything from it. Then bring down to us what has gathered with you from every assembly, so that we may place it where Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has commanded. When your messenger brings them down, then instruct him not to separate a she-camel from her young one (fasil), and not to separate between them, and not to withhold her milk, lest that harm her young one. He should not exhaust her (she-camel) by riding, and he should be just among them in that. He should bring them (camels) to every water he passes by, and he should not turn them away from the plants of the earth to the middle of the roads at the hour in which they rest and are milked in the evening. He should be gentle with them (camels) to the utmost of his ability until they come to us, by the permission of Allah (swt), healthy, fat, not tired and not exhausted. Then we shall divide them, by the permission of Allah (swt), according to the Book of Allah (swt) and the Sunnah of His Prophet (saws), Allah (swt) bless him and his family, among the awliya of Allah (swt). Indeed, that is greater for your reward and nearer to your right guidance. Allah (swt) looks at them, and at you, and at your effort, and your sincerity toward the one who sent you and toward whose need you were sent. For indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Allah (swt) does not look at a wali of His (swt) who exerts himself in obedience and sincerity toward his Imam, except that he will be with us in the highest company.’” He (narrator) said: “Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, wept. Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “O Burayd, by Allah (swt), no sanctity of Allah (swt) has remained except that it has been violated, and neither the Book of Allah (swt) nor the Sunnah of His Prophet (saws) has been acted upon in this world, And no legal punishment has been established among this creation since Allah (swt) took Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, and nothing of the truth has been acted upon until this day of the people.” Then Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, by Allah (swt), the days and nights will not pass until Allah (swt) gives life to the dead, causes the living to die, returns the truth to its people, and establishes His (swt) religion which He (swt) approved for Himself (swt) and His Prophet (saws). So rejoice, then rejoice, for by Allah (swt), the truth is only in your hands.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 120

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn Mammar, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Urani informed me, who said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir narrated to me, from a man from Thaqif, who said:
Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, appointed me (narrator) over Bab Baniqya (district in Baghdad) and a district from the districts of al-Kufah. Imam (a.s) said to me while the people were present: “Look to your land tax (kharaj), and strive in it, and do not leave from it a single dirham. Then when you want to go to your work, pass by me.” He (narrator) said: “So I came to Imam (a.s), and Imam (a.s) said to me: ‘Indeed, what you heard from me was a stratagem. Beware of striking a Muslim, or a Jew, or a Christian, for a dirham of land tax (kharaj), or selling a work animal for a dirham, for we have only been commanded to take from them the surplus.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مَعْمَرٍ قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْعُرَنِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُهَاجِرٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ ثَقِيفٍ قَالَ: اِسْتَعْمَلَنِي أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى بَابِ بَانِقْيَا وَ سَوَادٍ مِنْ سَوَادِ اَلْكُوفَةِ فَقَالَ لِي وَ اَلنَّاسُ حُضُورٌ» اُنْظُرْ إِلَى خَرَاجِكَ فَجِدَّ فِيهِ وَ لاَ تَتْرُكْ مِنْهُ دِرْهَماً فَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى عَمَلِكَ فَمُرَّ بِي« قَالَ فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَقَالَ لِي» إِنَّ اَلَّذِي سَمِعْتَهُ مِنِّي خُدْعَةٌ وَإِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَضْرِبَ مُسْلِماً أَوْ يَهُودِيّاً أَوْ نَصْرَانِيّاً فِي دِرْهَمِ خَرَاجٍ أَوْ تَبِيعَ دَابَّةَ عَمَلٍ فِي دِرْهَمٍ فَإِنَّمَا أُمِرْنَا أَنْ نَأْخُذَ مِنْهُمُ اَلْعَفْوَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn Mammar, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Urani informed me, who said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir narrated to me, from a man from Thaqif, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, appointed me (narrator) over Bab Baniqya (district in Baghdad) and a district from the districts of al-Kufah. Imam (a.s) said to me while the people were present: “Look to your land tax (kharaj), and strive in it, and do not leave from it a single dirham. Then when you want to go to your work, pass by me.” He (narrator) said: “So I came to Imam (a.s), and Imam (a.s) said to me: ‘Indeed, what you heard from me was a stratagem. Beware of striking a Muslim, or a Jew, or a Christian, for a dirham of land tax (kharaj), or selling a work animal for a dirham, for we have only been commanded to take from them the surplus.’”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn Khalid:
He (Muhammad ibn Khalid) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘charity.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, that is not accepted from you.” So he (narrator) said: “I carry that from my own wealth.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Command your collector of charity (musaddiq) not to gather from one water to another water, and not to join together what is separate, and not to separate what is joined together. So when he enters the wealth, let him divide the sheep into two halves and give their owner the choice of whichever of the two divisions he wishes. If he chooses, then let him hand it over to him. And if the soul of the owner of the sheep follows, from the other half of them, one sheep, or two sheep, or three, then let him hand them over to him. Then let him take his charity. When he has taken it out, let him value it among those whom he wishes. When it stands at a price, then if its owner wants it, he is more entitled to it, and if he does not want it, then let him sell it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّدَقَةِ فَقَالَ» إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لاَ يُقْبَلُ مِنْكَ« فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَحْمِلُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مَالِي فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» مُرْ مُصَدِّقَكَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْشُرَ مِنْ مَاءٍ إِلَى مَاءٍ وَ لاَ يَجْمَعَ بَيْنَ مُتَفَرِّقٍ وَ لاَ يُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَ مُجْتَمِعٍ فَإِذَا دَخَلَ اَلْمَالَ فَلْيَقْسِمِ اَلْغَنَمَ نِصْفَيْنِ وَيُخَيِّرُ صَاحِبَهَا أَيَّ اَلْقِسْمَيْنِ شَاءَ فَإِنِ اِخْتَارَ فَلْيَدْفَعْهُ إِلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ تَتَبَّعَتْ نَفْسُ صَاحِبِ اَلْغَنَمِ مِنَ اَلنِّصْفِ اَلْآخَرِ مِنْهَا شَاةً أَوْ شَاتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثاً فَلْيَدْفَعْهَا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ لْيَأْخُذْ صَدَقَتَهُ فَإِذَا أَخْرَجَهَا فَلْيُقَوِّمْهَا فِيمَنْ يُرِيدُ فَإِذَا قَامَتْ عَلَى ثَمَنٍ فَإِنْ أَرَادَهَا صَاحِبُهَا فَهُوَ أَحَقُّ بِهَا وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُرِدْهَا فَلْيَبِعْهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn Khalid:
thaqalaynMatn: He (Muhammad ibn Khalid) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about ‘charity.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, that is not accepted from you.” So he (narrator) said: “I carry that from my own wealth.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Command your collector of charity (musaddiq) not to gather from one water to another water, and not to join together what is separate, and not to separate what is joined together. So when he enters the wealth, let him divide the sheep into two halves and give their owner the choice of whichever of the two divisions he wishes. If he chooses, then let him hand it over to him. And if the soul of the owner of the sheep follows, from the other half of them, one sheep, or two sheep, or three, then let him hand them over to him. Then let him take his charity. When he has taken it out, let him value it among those whom he wishes. When it stands at a price, then if its owner wants it, he is more entitled to it, and if he does not want it, then let him sell it.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and one of them asked Imam (a.s) about ‘jewellery, Is there Zakat in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, even if it reaches one hundred thousand.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :وَ سَأَلَهُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ اَلْحُلِيِّ فِيهِ زَكَاةٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ وَ إِنْ بَلَغَ مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and one of them asked Imam (a.s) about ‘jewellery, Is there Zakat in it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, even if it reaches one hundred thousand.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Zakat in jewels and the like of them, even if they are abundant.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَيْسَ فِي اَلْجَوْهَرِ وَأَشْبَاهِهِ زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ كَثُرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Zakat in jewels and the like of them, even if they are abundant.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man left with his family maintenance of two thousand for years; is there Zakat upon it?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is present, then Zakat is upon him, and if he is absent, then there is no Zakat upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ خَلَّفَ عِنْدَ أَهْلِهِ نَفَقَةً أَلْفَيْنِ لِسِنِينَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ شَاهِداً فَعَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَائِباً فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man left with his family maintenance of two thousand for years; is there Zakat upon it?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is present, then Zakat is upon him, and if he is absent, then there is no Zakat upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man leaves for his family maintenance of three thousand dirhams, maintenance for years; ‘Is Zakat upon it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is present, then Zakat is upon it, and if he is absent, then there is nothing in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُخَلِّفُ لِأَهْلِهِ نَفَقَةً ثَلاَثَةَ آلاَفِ دِرْهَمٍ نَفَقَةَ سِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ شَاهِداً فَعَلَيْهَا زَكَاةٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَائِباً فَلَيْسَ فِيهَا شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man leaves for his family maintenance of three thousand dirhams, maintenance for years; ‘Is Zakat upon it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is present, then Zakat is upon it, and if he is absent, then there is nothing in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who took out the Zakat of his wealth, one thousand dirhams, but did not find a place for it to which he could pay that, so he looked at an owned slave who was being sold among those who bid higher, and he bought him with those one thousand dirhams which he had taken out from his Zakat, then freed him. Is that permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.” I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Then when he (the former slave) was freed and became free, he traded and worked, and acquired wealth, then died while having no heir; who inherits him when he has no heir?” Imam (a.s) said: “The poor believers who are entitled to Zakat inherit him, because he was only bought with their wealth.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَخْرَجَ زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ لَهَا مَوْضِعاً يَدْفَعُ ذَلِكَ إِلَيْهِ فَنَظَرَ إِلَى مَمْلُوكٍ يُبَاعُ فِيمَنْ يَزِيدُ فَاشْتَرَاهُ بِتِلْكَ اَلْأَلْفِ اَلدِّرْهَمِ اَلَّتِي أَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ زَكَاتِهِ فَأَعْتَقَهُ هَلْ يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ» نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ« قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا أَنْ أُعْتِقَ وَ صَارَ حُرّاً اِتَّجَرَ وَاِحْتَرَفَ فَأَصَابَ مَالاً ثُمَّ مَاتَ وَ لَيْسَ لَهُ وَارِثٌ فَمَنْ يَرِثُهُ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَارِثٌ فَقَالَ» يَرِثُهُ اَلْفُقَرَاءُ اَلْمُؤْمِنُونَ اَلَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِقُّونَ اَلزَّكَاةَ لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا اُشْتُرِيَ بِمَالِهِمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who took out the Zakat of his wealth, one thousand dirhams, but did not find a place for it to which he could pay that, so he looked at an owned slave who was being sold among those who bid higher, and he bought him with those one thousand dirhams which he had taken out from his Zakat, then freed him. Is that permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.” I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “Then when he (the former slave) was freed and became free, he traded and worked, and acquired wealth, then died while having no heir; who inherits him when he has no heir?” Imam (a.s) said: “The poor believers who are entitled to Zakat inherit him, because he was only bought with their wealth.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man with whom five hundred and six hundred from Zakat gather, and he buys from it a soul (nasamah) whom he frees.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then he would wrong other people of their rights.” Then Imam (a.s) remained silent for a while. Then Imam (a.s) said: “Except if he is a Muslim slave in necessity, then let him buy him and free him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَمْرٍو عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَجْتَمِعُ عِنْدَهُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ اَلْخَمْسُمِائَةِ وَاَلسِّتُّمِائَةِ يَشْتَرِي مِنْهَا نَسَمَةً يُعْتِقُهَا فَقَالَ» إِذاً يَظْلِمُ قَوْماً آخَرِينَ حُقُوقَهُمْ ثُمَّ مَكَثَ مَلِيّاً« ثُمَّ قَالَ» إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَبْداً مُسْلِماً فِي ضَرُورَةٍ فَلْيَشْتَرِهِ وَيُعْتِقُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man with whom five hundred and six hundred from Zakat gather, and he buys from it a soul (nasamah) whom he frees.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then he would wrong other people of their rights.” Then Imam (a.s) remained silent for a while. Then Imam (a.s) said: “Except if he is a Muslim slave in necessity, then let him buy him and free him.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “I have relatives upon whom I spend, and I give more to some of them than to others. Then the time of zakat comes to me; ‘May I give them from it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Are they entitled to it?” I (narrator) said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are better than others; give it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then who among my relatives is obligatory upon me, so that I may not count zakat for him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Your father and your mother.” I (narrator) asked: “My father and my mother?” Imam (a.s) said: “The two parents and the child.”
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن عدة من اصحابنا عن احمد بن محمد ابن عيسى عن علي بن الحكم عن عبد الملك بن عتبة عن اسحاق بن عمار عن ابي الحسن موسى عليه السلام قال: قلت له لي قرابة انفق على بعضهم فأفضل بعضهم على بعض فيأتيني إبان الزكاة أفأعطيهم منها؟ قال: أمستحقون لها؟ قلت: نعم قال: هم أفضل من غيرهم اعطهم، قال: قلت فمن الذي يلزمني من ذوي قرابتي حتى لا احتسب الزكاة عليه؟ قال: ابوك وامك ،قلت: ابي وامي؟ قال: الوالدان والولد
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “I have relatives upon whom I spend, and I give more to some of them than to others. Then the time of zakat comes to me; ‘May I give them from it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Are they entitled to it?” I (narrator) said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are better than others; give it to them.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then who among my relatives is obligatory upon me, so that I may not count zakat for him?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Your father and your mother.” I (narrator) asked: “My father and my mother?” Imam (a.s) said: “The two parents and the child.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, about ‘zakat, may some of those who are given, from among those who do not ask, be preferred over others?’ Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, the one who does not ask is preferred over the one who asks."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ يُفَضَّلُ بَعْضُ مَنْ يُعْطَى مِمَّنْ لاَ يَسْأَلُ عَلَى غَيْرِهِمْ فَقَالَ »نَعَمْ يُفَضَّلُ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَسْأَلُ عَلَى اَلَّذِي يَسْأَلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, about ‘zakat, may some of those who are given, from among those who do not ask, be preferred over others?’ Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, the one who does not ask is preferred over the one who asks."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Utbah, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan al-Sakuni, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “I sometimes divide something among my companions, maintaining ties with them through it, so how should I give it to them?” Imam (a.s) said, "Give to them according to migration (hijrah) in religion, understanding (fiqh), and intellect."
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عُتْبَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَجْلاَنَ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي رُبَّمَا قَسَمْتُ اَلشَّيْءَ بَيْنَ أَصْحَابِي أَصِلُهُمْ بِهِ فَكَيْفَ أُعْطِيهِمْ فَقَالَ» أَعْطِهِمْ عَلَى اَلْهِجْرَةِ فِي اَلدِّينِ وَاَلْفِقْهِ وَاَلْعَقْلِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Utbah, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan al-Sakuni, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “I sometimes divide something among my companions, maintaining ties with them through it, so how should I give it to them?” Imam (a.s) said, "Give to them according to migration (hijrah) in religion, understanding (fiqh), and intellect."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The charity of the ‘khuff’ (cloven hooves like sheep, cows) and the ‘zilf’ (solid hooves like horses, mules) is given to the dignified needy among the Muslims. As for the charity of gold and silver, and what is measured by the qafiz, and what the earth brings forth, it is for the severely poor." Ibn Sinan said: “I asked: ‘And how did this become like this?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Because these people are dignified needy and are shy before the people, so the more seemly of the two matters in the view of the people is given to them, and all of it is charity."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» إِنَّ صَدَقَةَ اَلْخُفِّ وَاَلظِّلْفِ تُدْفَعُ إِلَى اَلْمُتَجَمِّلِينَ مِنَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ فَأَمَّا صَدَقَةُ اَلذَّهَبِ وَ اَلْفِضَّةِ وَ مَا كِيلَ بِالْقَفِيزِ وَ مَا أَخْرَجَتِ اَلْأَرْضُ فَلِلْفُقَرَاءِ اَلْمُدْقَعِينَ« قَالَ اِبْنُ سِنَانٍ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ صَارَ هَذَا هَكَذَا فَقَالَ» لِأَنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ مُتَجَمِّلُونَ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ فَيُدْفَعُ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجْمَلُ اَلْأَمْرَيْنِ عِنْدَ اَلنَّاسِ وَ كُلٌّ صَدَقَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: "The charity of the ‘khuff’ (cloven hooves like sheep, cows) and the ‘zilf’ (solid hooves like horses, mules) is given to the dignified needy among the Muslims. As for the charity of gold and silver, and what is measured by the qafiz, and what the earth brings forth, it is for the severely poor." Ibn Sinan said: “I asked: ‘And how did this become like this?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Because these people are dignified needy and are shy before the people, so the more seemly of the two matters in the view of the people is given to them, and all of it is charity."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man dies and leaves dependants; ‘Are they to be given from the zakat?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, until they grow up and reach maturity, and they are asked from where they used to live when that is cut off from them." So I (narrator) said: “They do not know.” Imam (a.s) said: "Their deceased one is preserved through them, and the religion of their father is made beloved to them, so it will not be long before they become concerned with their religion. Then, (if) when they reach maturity and turn away to other than the religion of their father, do not give to them."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَمُوتُ وَ يَتْرُكُ اَلْعِيَالَ أَ يُعْطَوْنَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ حَتَّى يَنْشَئُوا وَ يَبْلُغُوا وَيَسْأَلُوا مِنْ أَيْنَ كَانُوا يَعِيشُونَ إِذَا قُطِعَ ذَلِكَ عَنْهُمْ« فَقُلْتُ إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يَعْرِفُونَ قَالَ» يُحْفَظُ فِيهِمْ مَيِّتُهُمْ وَيُحَبَّبُ إِلَيْهِمْ دِينُ أَبِيهِمْ فَلاَ يَلْبَثُونَ أَنْ يَهْتَمُّوا بِدِينِهِمْ فَإِذَا بَلَغُوا وَعَدَلُوا إِلَى غَيْرِ دِينِ أَبِيهِمْ فَلاَ تُعْطُوهُمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man dies and leaves dependants; ‘Are they to be given from the zakat?’” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, until they grow up and reach maturity, and they are asked from where they used to live when that is cut off from them." So I (narrator) said: “They do not know.” Imam (a.s) said: "Their deceased one is preserved through them, and the religion of their father is made beloved to them, so it will not be long before they become concerned with their religion. Then, (if) when they reach maturity and turn away to other than the religion of their father, do not give to them."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 127

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a knowledgeable, virtuous man who died and left behind a debt upon him with which he had been afflicted, and he was not corrupt, nor extravagant, nor known for asking. May one thousand and two thousand be paid on his behalf from the zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَارِفٍ فَاضِلٍ تُوُفِّيَ وَ تَرَكَ عَلَيْهِ دَيْناً قَدِ اُبْتُلِيَ بِهِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِمُفْسِدٍ وَ لاَ مُسْرِفٍ وَ لاَ مَعْرُوفٍ بِالْمَسْأَلَةِ هَلْ يُقْضَى عَنْهُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ اَلْأَلْفُ وَ اَلْأَلْفَانِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a knowledgeable, virtuous man who died and left behind a debt upon him with which he had been afflicted, and he was not corrupt, nor extravagant, nor known for asking. May one thousand and two thousand be paid on his behalf from the zakat?’ Imam (a.s) said: "Yes."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from one whom he mentioned:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), (was asked) concerning ‘a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man while he thinks that he is needy, then he finds him to be well-off.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It does not suffice for him.”
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن عدة من اصحابنا عن احمد بن محمد عن ابن ابي عمير عن الحسين بن عثمان عمن ذكره عن ابي عبد الله ع في رجل يعطي زكاة ماله رجلا وهو يرى انه معسر فوجده موسرا قال: لا يجزي عنه
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from one whom he mentioned:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), (was asked) concerning ‘a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man while he thinks that he is needy, then he finds him to be well-off.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It does not suffice for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “There is no man who withholds a dirham from a rightful due except that he spends two dirhams in other than its rightful place, and there is no man who withholds a right from his wealth except that Allah (swt), will encircle him with a serpent of fire on the Day of Resurrection.” He (narrator) said: “I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man who had recognition paid the zakat to those who were not entitled to it for a period of time; is it upon him to pay it again to those entitled to it when he comes to know them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then what if he does not know anyone entitled to it, so he does not pay it, or he does not know that it is obligatory upon him, then he comes to know after that?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He pays it to those entitled to it for what has passed.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then what if he did not know those entitled to it, so he gave it to one who was not worthy of it, while he had searched and exerted effort, then afterwards he came to know the wrongness of what he had done?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not upon him to pay it again.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يَمْنَعُ دِرْهَماً فِي حَقٍّ إِلاَّ أَنْفَقَ اِثْنَيْنِ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ وَ مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ مَنَعَ حَقّاً مِنْ مَالِهِ إِلاَّ طَوَّقَهُ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَيَّةً مِنْ نَارٍ يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ« قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ عَارِفٌ أَدَّى اَلزَّكَاةَ إِلَى غَيْرِ أَهْلِهَا زَمَاناً هَلْ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا ثَانِيَةً إِلَى أَهْلِهَا إِذَا عَلِمَهُمْ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ لَهَا أَهْلاً فَلَمْ يُؤَدِّهَا أَوْ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّهَا عَلَيْهِ فَعَلِمَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ» يُؤَدِّيهَا إِلَى أَهْلِهَا لِمَا مَضَى« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَهْلَهَا فَدَفَعَهَا إِلَى مَنْ لَيْسَ هُوَ لَهَا بِأَهْلٍ وَ قَدْ كَانَ طَلَبَ وَ اِجْتَهَدَ ثُمَّ عَلِمَ بَعْدُ سُوءَ مَا صَنَعَ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَهَا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “There is no man who withholds a dirham from a rightful due except that he spends two dirhams in other than its rightful place, and there is no man who withholds a right from his wealth except that Allah (swt), will encircle him with a serpent of fire on the Day of Resurrection.” He (narrator) said: “I said to Imam (a.s): ‘A man who had recognition paid the zakat to those who were not entitled to it for a period of time; is it upon him to pay it again to those entitled to it when he comes to know them?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then what if he does not know anyone entitled to it, so he does not pay it, or he does not know that it is obligatory upon him, then he comes to know after that?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He pays it to those entitled to it for what has passed.” He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘Then what if he did not know those entitled to it, so he gave it to one who was not worthy of it, while he had searched and exerted effort, then afterwards he came to know the wrongness of what he had done?’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not upon him to pay it again.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 128

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from Zurarah: the like of it, except that Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: "If he exerted effort (seeking those entitled to zakat), then he has become free of liability; and if he fell short in exerting effort in seeking, then no."
arabicText: وَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ: مِثْلَهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ» إِنِ اِجْتَهَدَ فَقَدْ بَرِئَ وَ إِنْ قَصَّرَ فِي اَلاِجْتِهَادِ فِي اَلطَّلَبِ فَلاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from Zurarah: the like of it, except that Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: "If he exerted effort (seeking those entitled to zakat), then he has become free of liability; and if he fell short in exerting effort in seeking, then no."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abd al-Karim ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, used to divide the charity of the people of the deserts among the people of the deserts, and the charity of the people of the towns among the people of the towns, and He (saws) would not divide it among them equally. Rather, the Prophet (saws) would divide it according to the number of them who were present before him. And He (saws) said, ‘There is nothing fixed in that.’"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يَقْسِمُ صَدَقَةَ أَهْلِ اَلْبَوَادِي فِي أَهْلِ اَلْبَوَادِي وَ صَدَقَةَ أَهْلِ اَلْحَضَرِ فِي أَهْلِ اَلْحَضَرِ وَ لاَ يَقْسِمُهَا بَيْنَهُمْ بِالسَّوِيَّةِ وَ إِنَّمَا يَقْسِمُهَا عَلَى قَدْرِ مَا يَحْضُرُهُ مِنْهُمْ وَ قَالَ» لَيْسَ فِي ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abd al-Karim ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: "The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, used to divide the charity of the people of the deserts among the people of the deserts, and the charity of the people of the towns among the people of the towns, and He (saws) would not divide it among them equally. Rather, the Prophet (saws) would divide it according to the number of them who were present before him. And He (saws) said, ‘There is nothing fixed in that.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Hilal ibn Khaqan, said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: "The one who leaves zakat, while it has become obligatory for him, is like the one who withholds it, while it has become obligatory upon him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْهَيْثَمِ بْنِ أَبِي مَسْرُوقٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» تَارِكُ اَلزَّكَاةِ وَ قَدْ وَجَبَتْ لَهُ مِثْلُ مَانِعِهَا وَ قَدْ وَجَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Hilal ibn Khaqan, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: "The one who leaves zakat, while it has become obligatory for him, is like the one who withholds it, while it has become obligatory upon him."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 129

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man from among our companions is shy to take from the zakat, so I give him from the zakat and do not name it to him that it is from the zakat.” Imam (a.s) said: "Give it to him, and do not name it (as zakat) to him, and do not humiliate the believer."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَأُعْطِيهِ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ وَ لاَ أُسَمِّي لَهُ أَنَّهَا مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ قَالَ» أَعْطِهِ وَ لاَ تُسَمِّ لَهُ وَ لاَ تُذِلَّ اَلْمُؤْمِنَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man from among our companions is shy to take from the zakat, so I give him from the zakat and do not name it to him that it is from the zakat.” Imam (a.s) said: "Give it to him, and do not name it (as zakat) to him, and do not humiliate the believer."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who is given wealth to distribute among those for whom it is lawful. Is it for him to take something from it for himself, while it was not specified for him?’ He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) said, ‘He takes from it for himself the like of what he gives to others.’"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أُعْطِيَ مَالاً يُفَرِّقُهُ فِيمَنْ يَحِلُّ لَهُ أَ لَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً لِنَفْسِهِ وَ لَمْ يُسَمَّ لَهُ قَالَ قَالَ» يَأْخُذُ مِنْهُ لِنَفْسِهِ مِثْلَ مَا يُعْطِي لِغَيْرِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who is given wealth to distribute among those for whom it is lawful. Is it for him to take something from it for himself, while it was not specified for him?’ He (narrator) said: “Imam (a.s) said, ‘He takes from it for himself the like of what he gives to others.’"

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 130

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who gives another man dirhams to divide them and place them in their proper places, while he is among those for whom charity is lawful.’ Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm in him taking for himself just as he gives to others." Imam (a.s) said: "And it is not permissible for him to take if he instructed him to place them in specified places, except with his permission."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘Charities are only for the poor and the needy.’ (Surah al-Tawbah 9:60) Imam (a.s) said: "‘The poor person’ is the one who does not ask people, and ‘the needy person’ is more distressed than him, and ‘the wretched one’ is the most distressed of them. arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» إِنَّمَا اَلصَّدَقٰاتُ لِلْفُقَرٰاءِ وَ اَلْمَسٰاكِينِ« قَالَ »اَلْفَقِيرُ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَسْأَلُ اَلنَّاسَ وَ اَلْمِسْكِينُ أَجْهَدُ مِنْهُ وَ اَلْبَائِسُ أَجْهَدُهُمْ وَ كُلُّمَا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَيْكَ فَإِعْلاَنُهُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ إِسْرَارِهِ وَ مَا كَانَ تَطَوُّعاً فَإِسْرَارُهُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ إِعْلاَنِهِ وَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً حَمَلَ زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ فَقَسَمَهَا عَلاَنِيَةً كَانَ ذَلِكَ حَسَناً جَمِيلاً«.

thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘Charities are only for the poor and the needy.’ (Surah al-Tawbah 9:60) Imam (a.s) said: "‘The poor person’ is the one who does not ask people, and ‘the needy person’ is more distressed than him, and ‘the wretched one’ is the most distressed of them. chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘To give charity publicly is good, but to give to the poor privately is better for you.’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:271) Imam (a.s) said: "It is other than zakat, for zakat is public, not secret."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» وَ إِنْ تُخْفُوهٰا وَتُؤْتُوهَا اَلْفُقَرٰاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ« فَقَالَ» هِيَ سِوَى اَلزَّكَاةِ فَإِنَّ اَلزَّكَاةَ عَلاَنِيَةٌ غَيْرُ سِرٍّ«.

thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘To give charity publicly is good, but to give to the poor privately is better for you.’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:271) Imam (a.s) said: "It is other than zakat, for zakat is public, not secret."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, said ‘Charity given in secret extinguishes the anger of the Lord (azj), Blessed and Exalted.’"
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» صَدَقَةُ اَلسِّرِّ تُطْفِئُ غَضَبَ اَلرَّبِّ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى«.

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, went out on a night when there had been a light rain, and Imam (a.s) was intending the shelter of Banu Sa'idah. So I (narrator) followed the Imam (a.s), and behold, something had fallen from Imam (a.s). Imam (a.s) said: "In the name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), return it to us." So I (narrator) came to Imam (a.s) and greeted him with peace. Imam (a.s) said: "Mu'alla?" Then I (narrator) found much scattered bread, so I began handing to Imam (a.s) what I found. Then I found a sack of bread which I was unable to carry. So I (narrator) said: “May I be made your ransom, shall I carry it on my shoulder?” Imam (a.s) said: "No, I am more entitled to it than you, but go along with me." He (narrator) said: “So we came to the shelter of Banu Sa'idah, and behold, there were people sleeping. Imam (a.s) began dividing a loaf and two loaves until he came to the last of them, then we departed.” I (narrator) asked: “May I be made your ransom, do these people know the truth?” Imam (a.s) said: "If they knew it, we would have shared with them even the duqqah." And when my father (a.s) gave something in charity, He (a.s) would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it and smell it, then return it into the hand of the beggar. arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ قَدْ رَشَّتْ وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ ظُلَّةَ بَنِي سَاعِدَةَ فَاتَّبَعْتُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ سَقَطَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ» بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ رُدَّ عَلَيْنَا« فَأَتَيْتُهُ وَ سَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ» مُعَلًّى« قُلْتُ نَعَمْ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَقَالَ لِيَ» اِلْتَمِسْ عِنْدَكَ فَمَا وَجَدْتَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَادْفَعْهُ إِلَيَّ« فَإِذَا أَنَا بِخُبْزٍ مُنْتَشِرٍ كَثِيرٍ فَجَعَلْتُ أَدْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ مَا وَجَدْتُ فَإِذَا أَنَا بِجِرَابٍ أَعْجِزُ عَنْ حَمْلِهِ مِنْ خُبْزٍ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَحْمِلُ عَلَى عَاتِقِي فَقَالَ» لاَ أَنَا أَوْلَى بِهِ مِنْكَ وَ لَكِنِ اِمْضِ مَعِي« قَالَ فَأَتَيْنَا ظُلَّةَ بَنِي سَاعِدَةَ فَإِذَا نَحْنُ بِقَوْمٍ نِيَامٍ فَجَعَلَ يَقْسِمُ اَلرَّغِيفَ وَاَلرَّغِيفَيْنِ حَتَّى أَتَى عَلَى آخِرِهِمْ ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفْنَا قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ يَعْرِفُ هَؤُلاَءِ اَلْحَقَّ فَقَالَ» لَوْ عَرَفُوهُ لَوَ اسَيْنَاهُمْ بِالدُّقَّةِ« وَاَلدُّقَّةُ هِيَ اَلْمِلْحُ» إِنَّ اَللَّهَ لَمْ يَخْلُقْ شَيْئاً إِلاَّ وَ لَهُ خَازِنٌ يَخْزُنُهُ إِلاَّ اَلصَّدَقَةَ فَإِنَّ اَلرَّبَّ يَلِيهَا بِنَفْسِهِ وَكَانَ أَبِي إِذَا تَصَدَّقَ بِشَيْءٍ وَضَعَهُ فِي يَدِ اَلسَّائِلِ ثُمَّ اِرْتَدَّهُ مِنْهُ فَقَبَّلَهُ وَشَمَّهُ ثُمَّ رَدَّهُ فِي يَدِ اَلسَّائِلِ إِنَّ صَدَقَةَ اَللَّيْلِ تُطْفِئُ غَضَبَ اَلرَّبِّ تَعَالَى وَ تَمْحُو اَلذَّنْبَ اَلْعَظِيمَ وَتُهَوِّنُ اَلْحِسَابَ وَ صَدَقَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ تُثْمِرُ اَلْمَالَ وَ تَزِيدُ فِي اَلْعُمُرِ إِنَّ عِيسَى اِبْنَ مَرْيَمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لَمَّا أَنْ مَرَّ عَلَى شَاطِئِ اَلْبَحْرِ رَمَى بِقُرْصٍ مِنْ قُوتِهِ فِي اَلْمَاءِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ اَلْحَوَارِيِّينَ يَا رُوحَ اَللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتَهُ لِمَ فَعَلْتَ هَذَا وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ قُوتِكَ قَالَ فَقَالَ فَعَلْتُ هَذَا لِدَابَّةٍ تَأْكُلُهُ مِنْ دَوَابِّ اَلْمَاءِ وَثَوَابُهُ عِنْدَ اَللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ«.

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, was asked: ‘Which charity is best?’” The Prophet (saws) said: "To the hostile relative."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَيُّ اَلصَّدَقَةِ أَفْضَلُ قَالَ» عَلَى ذِي اَلرَّحِمِ اَلْكَاشِحِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, was asked: ‘Which charity is best?’” The Prophet (saws) said: "To the hostile relative."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, said: ‘Charity is by ten, a loan is by eighteen, maintaining ties with brothers is by twenty, and maintaining ties of kinship is by twenty-four.’"
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» اَلصَّدَقَةُ بِعَشَرَةٍ وَ اَلْقَرْضُ بِثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ وَ صِلَةُ اَلْإِخْوَانِ بِعِشْرِينَ وَ صِلَةُ اَلرَّحِمِ بِأَرْبَعَةٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah's (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, said: ‘Charity is by ten, a loan is by eighteen, maintaining ties with brothers is by twenty, and maintaining ties of kinship is by twenty-four.’"

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: “And give its due on the day of its harvest.” (Surah al-An’am 6:141) They (narrators) all said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘This is from charity: he gives the needy person a handful after a handful, and at the cutting of the dates, a handful after a handful, until he finishes. He leaves for the guard a known wage, and he leaves from the palm-trees Mi'afar and Umm Ju'rur (types of palm/date); And he leaves for the guard who is in the orchard one date-cluster, two date-clusters, or three, for his guarding it.’"
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصٰادِهِ« فَقَالُوا جَمِيعاً قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» هَذَا مِنَ اَلصَّدَقَةِ يُعْطِي اَلْمِسْكِينَ اَلْقَبْضَةَ بَعْدَ اَلْقَبْضَةِ وَ مِنَ اَلْجُذَاذِ اَلْحَفْنَةَ بَعْدَ اَلْحَفْنَةِ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ وَ يَتْرُكُ لِلْحَارِسِ أَجْراً مَعْلُوماً وَ يَتْرُكُ مِنَ اَلنَّخْلِ مِعَا فَأْرَةٍ وَ أُمَّ جُعْرُورٍ وَ يَتْرُكُ لِلْحَارِسِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلْحَائِطِ اَلْعَذْقَ وَ اَلْعَذْقَيْنِ وَ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ لِحِفْظِهِ لَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: “And give its due on the day of its harvest.” (Surah al-An’am 6:141) They (narrators) all said: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘This is from charity: he gives the needy person a handful after a handful, and at the cutting of the dates, a handful after a handful, until he finishes. He leaves for the guard a known wage, and he leaves from the palm-trees Mi'afar and Umm Ju'rur (types of palm/date); And he leaves for the guard who is in the orchard one date-cluster, two date-clusters, or three, for his guarding it.’"

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: "Do not cut dates by night, do not harvest by night, do not offer sacrifice by night, and do not sow by night, for if you do that, the content one (qani) and the passer-by who asks (mu'tarr) will not come to you." I (narrator) asked: “And what are the ‘content one’ and the ‘passer-by who asks’?” Imam (a.s) said: "The ‘content one’ is the one who is content with what you give him, and the ‘passer-by who asks’ is the one who passes by you and asks you. And if you harvest by night, the beggars will not come to you. And this is the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: 'And give its due on the day of its harvest,' (Surah al-An’am 6:141) at the time of harvest, meaning a handful after a handful when you harvest it; and when it comes out, then a handful after a handful; And likewise at the time of cutting the dates; and likewise sowing: do not sow by night, because you give at the time of sowing just as you give at the time of harvest."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تَجُذَّ بِاللَّيْلِ وَلاَ تَحْصُدْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ لاَ تُضَحِّ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ لاَ تَبْذُرْ بِاللَّيْلِ فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ فَعَلْتَ لَمْ يَأْتِكَ اَلْقَانِعُ وَاَلْمُعْتَرُّ« قُلْتُ وَ مَا اَلْقَانِعُ وَاَلْمُعْتَرُّ قَالَ» اَلْقَانِعُ اَلَّذِي يَقْنَعُ بِمَا أَعْطَيْتَهُ وَاَلْمُعْتَرُّ اَلَّذِي يَمُرُّ بِكَ فَيَسْأَلُكَ وَ إِنْ حَصَدْتَ بِاللَّيْلِ لَمْ يَأْتِكَ اَلسُّؤَّالُ وَهُوَ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصٰادِهِ« عِنْدَ اَلْحَصَادِ يَعْنِي اَلْقَبْضَةَ بَعْدَ اَلْقَبْضَةِ إِذَا حَصَدْتَهُ وَ إِذَا خَرَجَ فَالْحَفْنَةَ بَعْدَ اَلْحَفْنَةِ وَ كَذَلِكَ عِنْدَ اَلصِّرَامِ وَ كَذَلِكَ اَلْبَذْرُ لاَ تَبْذُرْ بِاللَّيْلِ لِأَنَّكَ تُعْطِي فِي اَلْبَذْرِ كَمَا تُعْطِي فِي اَلْحَصَادِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: "Do not cut dates by night, do not harvest by night, do not offer sacrifice by night, and do not sow by night, for if you do that, the content one (qani) and the passer-by who asks (mu'tarr) will not come to you." I (narrator) asked: “And what are the ‘content one’ and the ‘passer-by who asks’?” Imam (a.s) said: "The ‘content one’ is the one who is content with what you give him, and the ‘passer-by who asks’ is the one who passes by you and asks you. And if you harvest by night, the beggars will not come to you. And this is the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic: 'And give its due on the day of its harvest,' (Surah al-An’am 6:141) at the time of harvest, meaning a handful after a handful when you harvest it; and when it comes out, then a handful after a handful; And likewise at the time of cutting the dates; and likewise sowing: do not sow by night, because you give at the time of sowing just as you give at the time of harvest."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: "Lending wealth is the protected enclosure of zakat."
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ فُضَيْلٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» قَرْضُ اَلْمَالِ حِمَى اَلزَّكَاةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: "Lending wealth is the protected enclosure of zakat."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 134

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Sudayr al-Sayrafi, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Shall I feed a beggar whom I do not know to be a Muslim?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, give to one whom you do not know to have allegiance (wilayah) or enmity (nasb) toward the truth. Indeed Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And speak kindly to people.' (Surah al-Baqarah 2:83) And do not feed one who shows hostility to anything of the truth (nawasib), or calls to anything of falsehood."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ سَدِيرٍ اَلصَّيْرَفِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُطْعِمُ سَائِلاً لاَ أَعْرِفُهُ مُسْلِماً فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ أَعْطِ مَنْ لاَ تَعْرِفُهُ بِوَلاَيَةٍ وَ لاَ عَدَاوَةٍ لِلْحَقِّ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ» وَقُولُوا لِلنّٰاسِ حُسْناً« وَ لاَ تُطْعِمْ مَنْ نَصَبَ لِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْحَقِّ أَوْ دَعَا إِلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلْبَاطِلِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Sudayr al-Sayrafi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Shall I feed a beggar whom I do not know to be a Muslim?” Imam (a.s) said: "Yes, give to one whom you do not know to have allegiance (wilayah) or enmity (nasb) toward the truth. Indeed Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And speak kindly to people.' (Surah al-Baqarah 2:83) And do not feed one who shows hostility to anything of the truth (nawasib), or calls to anything of falsehood."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from al-Nawfali, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a beggar who asks, while it is not known what he is.’ Imam (a.s) said: "Give to the one for whom mercy has fallen into your heart." And Imam (a.s) said: "Give less than a dirham." So I (narrator) asked: “What is the most that may be given?” Imam (a.s) said: "Four daniqs (dawaniq)."
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلسَّائِلِ يَسْأَلُ وَ لاَ يُدْرَى مَا هُوَ فَقَالَ» أَعْطِ مَنْ وَقَعَتْ فِي قَلْبِكَ لَهُ اَلرَّحْمَةُ« وَ قَالَ» أَعْطِ دُونَ اَلدِّرْهَمِ« فَقُلْتُ أَكْثَرُ مَا يُعْطَى قَالَ» أَرْبَعَةُ دَوَانِيقَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from al-Nawfali, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a beggar who asks, while it is not known what he is.’ Imam (a.s) said: "Give to the one for whom mercy has fallen into your heart." And Imam (a.s) said: "Give less than a dirham." So I (narrator) asked: “What is the most that may be given?” Imam (a.s) said: "Four daniqs (dawaniq)."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘zakat, Is it proper for the owner of a house and a servant to receive it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, unless his house is a house that produces income, from whose yield dirhams come out that suffice him and his dependants. If the yield does not suffice him and his dependants for their food, clothing, and needs, without extravagance, then zakat has become lawful for him. But if its yield suffices them, then no.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلزَّكَاةِ هَلْ تَصْلُحُ لِصَاحِبِ اَلدَّارِ وَ اَلْخَادِمِ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ دَارُهُ دَارَ غَلَّتِهَا فَيَخْرُجَ مِنْ غَلَّتِهَا دَرَاهِمُ تَكْفِيهِ وَ عِيَالَهُ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنِ اَلْغَلَّةُ تَكْفِيهِ لِنَفْسِهِ وَ عِيَالِهِ فِي طَعَامِهِمْ وَ كِسْوَتِهِمْ وَحَاجَتِهِمْ فِي غَيْرِ إِسْرَافٍ فَقَدْ حَلَّتْ لَهُ اَلزَّكَاةُ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ غَلَّتُهَا تَكْفِيهِمْ فَلاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘zakat, Is it proper for the owner of a house and a servant to receive it?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, unless his house is a house that produces income, from whose yield dirhams come out that suffice him and his dependants. If the yield does not suffice him and his dependants for their food, clothing, and needs, without extravagance, then zakat has become lawful for him. But if its yield suffices them, then no.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: "The charity of the emigrants is not lawful for the Bedouins, nor the charity of the Bedouins among the emigrants."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تَحِلُّ صَدَقَةُ اَلْمُهَاجِرِينَ لِلْأَعْرَابِ وَ لاَ صَدَقَةُ اَلْأَعْرَابِ فِي اَلْمُهَاجِرِينَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: "The charity of the emigrants is not lawful for the Bedouins, nor the charity of the Bedouins among the emigrants."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 135

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man whose father, paternal uncle, or brother suffices him in his maintenance. May he take from the zakat and thereby expand for himself, if they do not expand upon him in everything that he needs?’ Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ أَبُوهُ أَوْ عَمُّهُ أَوْ أَخُوهُ يَكْفِيهِ مَئُونَتَهُ أَ يَأْخُذُ مِنَ اَلزَّكَاةِ فَيَتَوَسَّعَ بِهِ إِنْ كَانُوا لاَ يُوَسِّعُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man whose father, paternal uncle, or brother suffices him in his maintenance. May he take from the zakat and thereby expand for himself, if they do not expand upon him in everything that he needs?’ Imam (a.s) said: "There is no harm."

chapter: Chapter on Additions Regarding Zakat
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “What is given to the collector of charity (musaddiq)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever the Imam sees fit, and nothing is fixed for him."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا يُعْطَى اَلْمُصَدِّقُ قَالَ» مَا يَرَى اَلْإِمَامُ وَ لاَ يُقَدَّرُ لَهُ شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “What is given to the collector of charity (musaddiq)?” Imam (a.s) said: "Whatever the Imam sees fit, and nothing is fixed for him."
