chapter: Chapter on Merit of Fasting the Day of Doubt and Taking Precaution for Fasting the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jafar al-Azdi, from Qutaybah al-Asha, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade fasting six days: the two Eids, the days of al-Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul Hijjah), and the day concerning which there is doubt from the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْأَزْدِيِّ عَنْ قُتَيْبَةَ اَلْأَعْشَى قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» نَهَى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ عَنْ صَوْمِ سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ وَ أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ وَ اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي يُشَكُّ فِيهِ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jafar al-Azdi, from Qutaybah al-Asha, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade fasting six days: the two Eids, the days of al-Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul Hijjah), and the day concerning which there is doubt from the month of Ramadan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 245

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Fasting the Day of Doubt and Taking Precaution for Fasting the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have made it binding upon myself that I fast until al-Qa’im (ajf), may Allah (swt) hasten his relief, rises.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not fast while traveling, nor on the two Eids, nor on the days of al-Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul Hijjah), nor on the day concerning which there is doubt.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي جَعَلْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي أَنْ أَصُومَ حَتَّى يَقُومَ اَلْقَائِمُ عَجَّلَ اَللَّهُ فَرَجَهُ فَقَالَ» لاَ تَصُمْ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ لاَ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ وَ لاَ أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ وَ لاَ اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي يُشَكُّ فِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have made it binding upon myself that I fast until al-Qa’im (ajf), may Allah (swt) hasten his relief, rises.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not fast while traveling, nor on the two Eids, nor on the days of al-Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul Hijjah), nor on the day concerning which there is doubt.”

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Fasting the Day of Doubt and Taking Precaution for Fasting the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Kasula, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadhakuni, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Mamar, from Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, who said:
I (narrator) heard Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The day of doubt (yawm al-shakk) is a day concerning which we were commanded to fast and forbidden from fasting. We were commanded that a person fast it on the basis that it is from Shaban, and we were forbidden that a person fast it on the basis that it is from the month of Ramadan while he has not seen the crescent.”
arabicText: أبو الحسن أحمد بن محمد بن الحسن بن الوليد عن أبيه عن محمد بن الحسن الصفار عن علي بن محمد القاساني عن القاسم بن محمد كاسولا عن سليمان بن داود الشاذكوني عن عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن محمد بن شهاب الزهري قال: سمعت علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام يقول: يوم الشك امرنا بصيامه ونهينا عنه أمرنا ان يصومه الانسان على انه من شعبان ونهينا عن ان يصومه الانسان على انه من شهر رمضان وهو لم ير الهلال
thaqalaynSanad: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Kasula, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Shadhakuni, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Mamar, from Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The day of doubt (yawm al-shakk) is a day concerning which we were commanded to fast and forbidden from fasting. We were commanded that a person fast it on the basis that it is from Shaban, and we were forbidden that a person fast it on the basis that it is from the month of Ramadan while he has not seen the crescent.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 246

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘It has been made lawful for you, on the night of fasting, to have relations with your women,’ the verse.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187) Imam (a.s) said: “It was revealed concerning Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, and he was with the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at al-Khandaq, while he was fasting, and he reached evening in that state. Before this verse was revealed, when one of them slept, food became forbidden for him. So Khawwat came to his family when evening came and said, ‘Do you have any food?’ They said, ‘No. Stay until we prepare food for you.’ So he (Khawwat) leaned back and slept. They said to him (Khawwat), ‘You have dozed off.’ He (Khawwat) said, ‘Yes.’ So Khawwat spent the night in that state and entered the morning. Then Khawwat went early to al-Khandaq, and he began to faint. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, passed by, and when the Prophet (saws) saw what was with him, Khawwat informed the Prophet (saws) how his affair had been. So Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him (Khawwat) the verse: ‘(You may) eat and drink until you see the light of dawn breaking the darkness of night, then complete the fast until nightfall.’” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ اَلصِّيٰامِ اَلرَّفَثُ إِلىٰ نِسٰائِكُمْ« اَلْآيَةَ فَقَالَ» نَزَلَتْ فِي خَوَّاتِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ اَلْأَنْصَارِيِّ وَكَانَ مَعَ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي اَلْخَنْدَقِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ وَ أَمْسَى عَلَى تِلْكَ اَلْحَالِ وَ كَانَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْزِلَ هَذِهِ اَلْآيَةُ إِذَا نَامَ أَحَدُهُمْ حَرُمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلطَّعَامُ فَجَاءَ خَوَّاتٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ حِينَ أَمْسَى فَقَالَ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ طَعَامٌ فَقَالُوا لاَ أَقِمْ حَتَّى نَصْنَعَ لَكَ طَعَاماً فَاتَّكَى فَنَامَ فَقَالُوا لَهُ قَدْ غَفَلْتَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَبَاتَ عَلَى تِلْكَ اَلْحَالِ وَ أَصْبَحَ ثُمَّ غَدَا إِلَى اَلْخَنْدَقِ فَجَعَلَ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ فَمَرَّ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَلَمَّا رَأَى اَلَّذِي بِهِ أَخْبَرَهُ كَيْفَ كَانَ أَمْرُهُ فَأَنْزَلَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِيهِ اَلْآيَةَ» كُلُوا وَ اِشْرَبُوا حَتّٰى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ اَلْخَيْطُ اَلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ اَلْخَيْطِ اَلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ اَلْفَجْرِ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, ‘It has been made lawful for you, on the night of fasting, to have relations with your women,’ the verse.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187) Imam (a.s) said: “It was revealed concerning Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, and he was with the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, at al-Khandaq, while he was fasting, and he reached evening in that state. Before this verse was revealed, when one of them slept, food became forbidden for him. So Khawwat came to his family when evening came and said, ‘Do you have any food?’ They said, ‘No. Stay until we prepare food for you.’ So he (Khawwat) leaned back and slept. They said to him (Khawwat), ‘You have dozed off.’ He (Khawwat) said, ‘Yes.’ So Khawwat spent the night in that state and entered the morning. Then Khawwat went early to al-Khandaq, and he began to faint. The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, passed by, and when the Prophet (saws) saw what was with him, Khawwat informed the Prophet (saws) how his affair had been. So Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him (Khawwat) the verse: ‘(You may) eat and drink until you see the light of dawn breaking the darkness of night, then complete the fast until nightfall.’” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the white thread from the black thread.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night.” Imam (a.s) said: “And Bilal used to give the call to prayer for the blessed Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when dawn rose. So the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said, ‘When you hear the voice of Bilal, then leave food and drink, for you have entered the morning.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْخَيْطِ اَلْأَبْيَضِ مِنَ اَلْخَيْطِ اَلْأَسْوَدِ فَقَالَ» بَيَاضُ اَلنَّهَارِ مِنْ سَوَادِ اَللَّيْلِ« قَالَ» وَ كَانَ بِلاَلٌ يُؤَذِّنُ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ حِينَ يَطْلُعُ اَلْفَجْرُ فَقَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ صَوْتَ بِلاَلٍ فَدَعُوا اَلطَّعَامَ وَ اَلشَّرَابَ فَقَدْ أَصْبَحْتُمْ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the white thread from the black thread.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night.” Imam (a.s) said: “And Bilal used to give the call to prayer for the blessed Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when dawn rose. So the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said, ‘When you hear the voice of Bilal, then leave food and drink, for you have entered the morning.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 247

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “When does food become forbidden for the fasting person, and prayer, the dawn prayer (fajr), become lawful?” Imam (a.s) said to me (narrator): “When dawn spreads horizontally and is like the white Coptic cloth (al-qibtiyyah), then at that point food becomes forbidden and prayer, the dawn prayer, becomes lawful.” I (narrator) asked: “So are we not within the time until the ray of the sun rises?” Imam (a.s) said: “Far from it. Where are you going (with this)? That is the prayer of children.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقُلْتُ مَتَى يَحْرُمُ اَلطَّعَامُ عَلَى اَلصَّائِمِ وَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّلاَةُ صَلاَةُ اَلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ لِي» إِذَا اِعْتَرَضَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَكَانَ كَالْقُبْطِيَّةِ اَلْبَيْضَاءِ فَثَمَّ يَحْرُمُ اَلطَّعَامُ وَ تَحِلُّ اَلصَّلاَةُ صَلاَةُ اَلْفَجْرِ« قُلْتُ فَلَسْنَا فِي وَقْتٍ إِلَى أَنْ يَطْلُعَ شُعَاعُ اَلشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ» هَيْهَاتَ أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ تِلْكَ صَلاَةُ اَلصِّبْيَانِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “When does food become forbidden for the fasting person, and prayer, the dawn prayer (fajr), become lawful?” Imam (a.s) said to me (narrator): “When dawn spreads horizontally and is like the white Coptic cloth (al-qibtiyyah), then at that point food becomes forbidden and prayer, the dawn prayer, becomes lawful.” I (narrator) asked: “So are we not within the time until the ray of the sun rises?” Imam (a.s) said: “Far from it. Where are you going (with this)? That is the prayer of children.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Dawn is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as though it is the whiteness of the river of Sura.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: »اَلْفَجْرُ هُوَ اَلَّذِي إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُ مُعْتَرِضاً كَأَنَّهُ بَيَاضُ نَهَرِ سُورَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Dawn is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as though it is the whiteness of the river of Sura.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The time of the falling of the disc and the obligation of breaking the fast from fasting is that one stands facing the qiblah and observes the redness that rises from the east. When it has passed the top of the head toward the direction of the west, then breaking the fast has become obligatory and the disc has fallen.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» وَقْتُ سُقُوطِ اَلْقُرْصِ وَ وُجُوبِ اَلْإِفْطَارِ مِنَ اَلصِّيَامِ أَنْ يَقُومَ بِحِذَاءِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ يَتَفَقَّدَ اَلْحُمْرَةَ اَلَّتِي تَرْتَفِعُ مِنَ اَلْمَشْرِقِ فَإِذَا جَازَتْ قِمَّةَ اَلرَّأْسِ إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَدْ وَجَبَ اَلْإِفْطَارُ وَ سَقَطَ اَلْقُرْصُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The time of the falling of the disc and the obligation of breaking the fast from fasting is that one stands facing the qiblah and observes the redness that rises from the east. When it has passed the top of the head toward the direction of the west, then breaking the fast has become obligatory and the disc has fallen.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 248

chapter: Chapter on Sign of the Time of the Obligation of Fasting, the Days of the Month, and the Proof of the Time of Breaking the Fast
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘breaking the fast before the prayer or after it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If there are people with him and he fears that he would keep them back from their dinner, then let him break the fast with them. But if it is other than that, then let him pray and break the fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلْإِفْطَارِ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَوْ بَعْدَهَا فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ قَوْمٌ يَخْشَى أَنْ يَحْبِسَهُمْ عَنْ عَشَائِهِمْ فَلْيُفْطِرْ مَعَهُمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُصَلِّ وَلْيُفْطِرْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘breaking the fast before the prayer or after it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If there are people with him and he fears that he would keep them back from their dinner, then let him break the fast with them. But if it is other than that, then let him pray and break the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: It has been narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that the Prophet (saws) said: “Actions are according to intentions.”
arabicText: رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:» اَلْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ«.
thaqalaynMatn: It has been narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that the Prophet (saws) said: “Actions are according to intentions.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it has been narrated with another wording, which is that the Prophet (saws) said: “Actions are only according to intentions, and for every person is what he intended.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ بِلَفْظٍ آخَرَ وَ هُوَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:» إِنَّمَا اَلْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَ لِكُلِّ اِمْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى«.
thaqalaynMatn: And it has been narrated with another wording, which is that the Prophet (saws) said: “Actions are only according to intentions, and for every person is what he intended.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And it has been narrated from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “There is no statement except with action, and no action except with intention, and no intention except by conforming to the Sunnah.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:» لاَ قَوْلَ إِلاَّ بِعَمَلٍ وَ لاَ عَمَلَ إِلاَّ بِنِيَّةٍ وَ لاَ نِيَّةَ إِلاَّ بِإِصَابَةِ اَلسُّنَّةِ«.
thaqalaynMatn: And it has been narrated from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) said: “There is no statement except with action, and no action except with intention, and no intention except by conforming to the Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the voluntary fasting person when a need arises for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He has the choice between himself and the afternoon prayer (Asr), and if he remains until the afternoon prayer (Asr), then it appears to him that he should fast, while he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ اَلْمُتَطَوِّعِ تَعْرِضُ لَهُ اَلْحَاجَةُ قَالَ» هُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اَلْعَصْرِ وَ إِنْ مَكَثَ حَتَّى اَلْعَصْرِ ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ نَوَى ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ إِنْ شَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the voluntary fasting person when a need arises for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He has the choice between himself and the afternoon prayer (Asr), and if he remains until the afternoon prayer (Asr), then it appears to him that he should fast, while he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 249

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who makes up (fasts of the month of) Ramadan. Does he have the right to break the fast after he enters the morning, before midday (al-zawal), if it occurs to him?’ So he said: “If he had intended that from the night, and it was from the makeup of (month of) Ramadan, then he must not break the fast, and he must complete his fast.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked him about ‘a man to whom it occurs, after he enters the morning and the day rises, to fast that day and make it up from (month of) Ramadan, even though he had not intended that from the night.’” He said, “Yes, he fasts it and counts it, provided that he has not brought about anything (that invalidates the fast).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْضِي رَمَضَانَ أَ لَهُ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ بَعْدَ مَا يُصْبِحُ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ إِذَا بَدَا لَهُ فَقَالَ» إِذَا كَانَ نَوَى ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ كَانَ مِنْ قَضَاءِ رَمَضَانَ فَلاَ يُفْطِرْ وَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ« قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَبْدُو لَهُ بَعْدَ مَا يُصْبِحُ وَيَرْتَفِعُ اَلنَّهَارُ أَنْ يَصُومَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ يَقْضِيَهُ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ نَوَى ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ يَصُومُهُ وَ يَعْتَدُّ بِهِ إِذَا لَمْ يُحْدِثْ شَيْئاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who makes up (fasts of the month of) Ramadan. Does he have the right to break the fast after he enters the morning, before midday (al-zawal), if it occurs to him?’ So he said: “If he had intended that from the night, and it was from the makeup of (month of) Ramadan, then he must not break the fast, and he must complete his fast.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked him about ‘a man to whom it occurs, after he enters the morning and the day rises, to fast that day and make it up from (month of) Ramadan, even though he had not intended that from the night.’” He said, “Yes, he fasts it and counts it, provided that he has not brought about anything (that invalidates the fast).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Salih ibn Abdullah, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man has made it binding upon himself for Allah (swt) to fast a month, so he enters the morning while intending to fast, then it occurs to him and he breaks the fast; and he enters the morning while not intending to fast, then it occurs to him and he fasts.” Imam (a.s) said: “All of this is permissible.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ جَعَلَ لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ صِيَامَ شَهْرٍ فَيُصْبِحُ وَ هُوَ يَنْوِي اَلصَّوْمَ ثُمَّ يَبْدُو لَهُ فَيُفْطِرُ وَ يُصْبِحُ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَنْوِي اَلصَّوْمَ فَيَبْدُو لَهُ فَيَصُومُ فَقَالَ» هَذَا كُلُّهُ جَائِزٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Salih ibn Abdullah, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man has made it binding upon himself for Allah (swt) to fast a month, so he enters the morning while intending to fast, then it occurs to him and he breaks the fast; and he enters the morning while not intending to fast, then it occurs to him and he fasts.” Imam (a.s) said: “All of this is permissible.”
