chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever enters the morning while intending to fast, then it occurs to him to break the fast, he may break the fast between himself and the middle of the day. Then he makes up that day. But if it occurs to him to fast after the day has risen, then let him fast, for it is counted for him from the hour in which he intended it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَنْ أَصْبَحَ وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ اَلصِّيَامَ ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ فَلَهُ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ نِصْفِ اَلنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَقْضِي ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ فَإِنْ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ بَعْدَ مَا اِرْتَفَعَ اَلنَّهَارُ فَلْيَصُمْ فَإِنَّهُ يُحْسَبُ لَهُ مِنَ اَلسَّاعَةِ اَلَّتِي نَوَى فِيهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever enters the morning while intending to fast, then it occurs to him to break the fast, he may break the fast between himself and the middle of the day. Then he makes up that day. But if it occurs to him to fast after the day has risen, then let him fast, for it is counted for him from the hour in which he intended it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man has not made fasting obligatory upon himself, then he remembers fasting before eating any food or drinking any drink, and he has not broken the fast, then he has the choice; if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» إِذَا لَمْ يَفْرِضِ اَلرَّجُلُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ صِيَاماً ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ اَلصِّيَامَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَطْعَمَ طَعَاماً أَوْ يَشْرَبَ شَرَاباً وَ لَمْ يُفْطِرْ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ صَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَفْطَرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If a man has not made fasting obligatory upon himself, then he remembers fasting before eating any food or drinking any drink, and he has not broken the fast, then he has the choice; if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 250

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who enters the morning and has not eaten, has not drunk, and has not intended a fast, while he has upon him a day from the month of Ramadan. Does he have the right to fast that day when most of the day has already passed?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may fast and count it as from the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصْبِحُ وَ لَمْ يَطْعَمْ وَ لَمْ يَشْرَبْ وَ لَمْ يَنْوِ صَوْماً وَ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمٌ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَ لَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ قَدْ ذَهَبَ عَامَّةُ اَلنَّهَارِ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ لَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ وَ يَعْتَدَّ بِهِ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who enters the morning and has not eaten, has not drunk, and has not intended a fast, while he has upon him a day from the month of Ramadan. Does he have the right to fast that day when most of the day has already passed?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may fast and count it as from the month of Ramadan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Samaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning the his saying, ‘The fasting person has the choice until the declining of the sun (zawal al-shams).’ Imam (a.s) said: “That is in the obligatory fast. As for the supererogatory fast, he may break the fast at any time he wishes until the setting of the sun.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِهِ اَلصَّائِمُ بِالْخِيَارِ إِلَى زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ قَالَ» إِنَّ ذَلِكَ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ أَمَّا اَلنَّافِلَةُ فَلَهُ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ أَيَّ وَقْتٍ شَاءَ إِلَى غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Samaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning the his saying, ‘The fasting person has the choice until the declining of the sun (zawal al-shams).’ Imam (a.s) said: “That is in the obligatory fast. As for the supererogatory fast, he may break the fast at any time he wishes until the setting of the sun.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man enters the morning and does not intend to fast. Then when the day rises high, an opinion occurs to him regarding fasting.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he intends the fast before the sun declines, it is counted for him from his day, and if he intends it after the decline, it is counted for him from the time in which he intended.”
arabicText: اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُصْبِحُ وَلاَ يَنْوِي اَلصَّوْمَ فَإِذَا تَعَالَى اَلنَّهَارُ حَدَثَ لَهُ رَأْيٌ فِي اَلصَّوْمِ فَقَالَ» إِنْ هُوَ نَوَى اَلصَّوْمَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ حُسِبَ لَهُ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ وَ إِنْ نَوَاهُ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ حُسِبَ لَهُ مِنَ اَلْوَقْتِ اَلَّذِي نَوَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man enters the morning and does not intend to fast. Then when the day rises high, an opinion occurs to him regarding fasting.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he intends the fast before the sun declines, it is counted for him from his day, and if he intends it after the decline, it is counted for him from the time in which he intended.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man has upon him makeup from the month of Ramadan, and he enters the morning and does not eat until the afternoon prayer. Is it permissible for him to make it makeup from the month of Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْقَضَاءُ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ يُصْبِحُ فَلاَ يَأْكُلُ إِلَى اَلْعَصْرِ أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَهُ قَضَاءً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man has upon him makeup from the month of Ramadan, and he enters the morning and does not eat until the afternoon prayer. Is it permissible for him to make it makeup from the month of Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who enters the morning without having eaten or drunk, and without having intended a fast, while he owes a day from the month of Ramadan. May he fast that day when most of the day has already passed?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may fast it and count it as being from the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: محمد بن علي بن محبوب عن معاوية بن حكيم عن صفوان عن عبد الرحمن بن الحجاج قال: سألت ابا الحسن موسى عليه السلام عن الرجل يصبح ولم يطعم ولم يشرب ولم ينو صوما وكان عليه يوم من شهر رمضان أله ان يصوم ذلك اليوم وقد ذهب عامة النهار؟ فقال: نعم له أن يصومه ويعتد به من شهر رمضان
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who enters the morning without having eaten or drunk, and without having intended a fast, while he owes a day from the month of Ramadan. May he fast that day when most of the day has already passed?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he may fast it and count it as being from the month of Ramadan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 251

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, would enter upon his family and say, ‘Do you have anything (to eat)? Otherwise, I will fast.’ If they had anything (to eat), they would bring it to him, and otherwise, Imam Ali (a.s) would fast.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَدْخُلُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ وَ يَقُولُ» عِنْدَكُمْ شَيْءٌ وَ إِلاَّ صُمْتُ« فَإِنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُمْ شَيْءٌ أَتَوْهُ بِهِ وَ إِلاَّ صَامَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, would enter upon his family and say, ‘Do you have anything (to eat)? Otherwise, I will fast.’ If they had anything (to eat), they would bring it to him, and otherwise, Imam Ali (a.s) would fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man enters the morning without intending the fast, then when the day rises, an opinion occurs to him regarding fasting.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he intends the fast before the sun passes the meridian, his day is counted for him; And if he intends it after the sun has passed the meridian, it is counted for him from the time at which he intended.”
arabicText: أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن هشام بن سالم عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: قلت له الرجل يصبح لا ينوي الصوم فإذا تعالى النهار حدث له رأى في الصوم فقال: إن هو نوى الصوم قبل أن تزول الشمس حسب ل يومه وان نواه بعد الزوال حسب له من الوقت الذى نوى
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “A man enters the morning without intending the fast, then when the day rises, an opinion occurs to him regarding fasting.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he intends the fast before the sun passes the meridian, his day is counted for him; And if he intends it after the sun has passed the meridian, it is counted for him from the time at which he intended.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on Intention of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Isa:
Isa said: “Whoever spends the night while intending to fast the next day, that becomes binding upon him. Then if he breaks the fast, he must make it up. And whoever enters the morning and had not intended the fast from the night, then he has the choice until the sun declines; if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast. Then if the sun declines and he has not eaten, then let him complete the fast until the night.”
arabicText: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ عِيسَى قَالَ:» مَنْ بَاتَ وَ هُوَ يَنْوِي اَلصِّيَامَ مِنْ غَدٍ لَزِمَهُ ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ أَفْطَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ وَ مَنْ أَصْبَحَ وَ لَمْ يَنْوِ اَلصِّيَامَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِلَى أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ إِنْ شَاءَ صَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَفْطَرَ فَإِنْ زَالَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ وَ لَمْ يَأْكُلْ فَلْيُتِمَّ اَلصَّوْمَ إِلَى اَللَّيْلِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Isa:
thaqalaynMatn: Isa said: “Whoever spends the night while intending to fast the next day, that becomes binding upon him. Then if he breaks the fast, he must make it up. And whoever enters the morning and had not intended the fast from the night, then he has the choice until the sun declines; if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast. Then if the sun declines and he has not eaten, then let him complete the fast until the night.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “Fasting is not from food and drink, and a person ought to guard his tongue from vain false speech in (month of) Ramadan and other than it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» لَيْسَ اَلصِّيَامُ مِنَ اَلطَّعَامِ وَ اَلشَّرَابِ وَ اَلْإِنْسَانُ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَحْفَظَ لِسَانَهُ مِنَ اَللَّغْوِ اَلْبَاطِلِ فِي رَمَضَانَ وَ غَيْرِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), said: “Fasting is not from food and drink, and a person ought to guard his tongue from vain false speech in (month of) Ramadan and other than it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 252

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), saying: “Nothing that the fasting person does harms him if he avoids three qualities: food, drink, (relations with) women, and immersion in water.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» لاَ يَضُرُّ اَلصَّائِمَ مَا صَنَعَ إِذَا اِجْتَنَبَ ثَلاَثَ خِصَالٍ اَلطَّعَامَ وَ اَلشَّرَابَ وَ اَلنِّسَاءَ وَاَلاِرْتِمَاسَ فِي اَلْمَاءِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), saying: “Nothing that the fasting person does harms him if he avoids three qualities: food, drink, (relations with) women, and immersion in water.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on Nature of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who lied in (month of) Ramadan.’ So he said: “He has broken the fast, and he must make it up.” I (narrator) asked: “What was his lie?” So he said: “He lies against Allah (swt) and against His Messenger (saws).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَذَبَ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» قَدْ أَفْطَرَ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ« فَقُلْتُ مَا كَذِبَتُهُ فَقَالَ» يَكْذِبُ عَلَى اَللَّهِ وَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who lied in (month of) Ramadan.’ So he said: “He has broken the fast, and he must make it up.” I (narrator) asked: “What was his lie?” So he said: “He lies against Allah (swt) and against His Messenger (saws).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
He said: “For everything there is a zakat, and the zakat of the body is fasting.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ قَالَ:» لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ زَكَاةٌ وَ زَكَاةُ اَلْأَجْسَامِ اَلصَّوْمُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He said: “For everything there is a zakat, and the zakat of the body is fasting.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The fasting person is in worship, even if he is upon his bed, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ طَلْحَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:»اَ ل صَّ ا ئِ مُ فِ ي عِ بَ ا دَ ةٍ وَ إِ نْ كَا نَ عَ لَ ى فِ رَ ا شِ هِ مَا لَمْ يَغْتَبْ مُسْلِماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The fasting person is in worship, even if he is upon his bed, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 253

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever fasts much, Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says to His (swt) angels, ‘My servant has sought refuge from My (swt) punishment, so grant him refuge.’ And Allah (swt) appoints His (swt) angels to supplicate for those who fast, and Allah (swt) has not commanded supplication for anyone except that Allah (swt) responds to them concerning him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَنْ كَثُرَ صَوْمُهُ قَالَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لِمَلاَئِكَتِهِ» عَبْدِي اِسْتَجَارَ مِنْ عَذَابِي فَأَجِيرُوهُ« وَ وَكَّلَ اَللَّهُ مَلاَئِكَتَهُ بِالدُّعَاءِ لِلصَّائِمِينَ وَ لَمْ يَأْمُرْ بِالدُّعَاءِ لِأَحَدٍ إِلاَّ اِسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ فِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever fasts much, Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says to His (swt) angels, ‘My servant has sought refuge from My (swt) punishment, so grant him refuge.’ And Allah (swt) appoints His (swt) angels to supplicate for those who fast, and Allah (swt) has not commanded supplication for anyone except that Allah (swt) responds to them concerning him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The sleep of the fasting person is worship, and his breath is glorification.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» نَوْمُ اَلصَّائِمِ عِبَادَةٌ وَ نَفَسُهُ تَسْبِيحٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The sleep of the fasting person is worship, and his breath is glorification.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from Abdullah ibn Jabir, from Uthman ibn Madhun, who said:
I (narrator) said to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), I wanted to ask you about some things.” So the Prophet (saws) said: “And what are they, O Uthman?” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘I wanted to become a monk (atarahhab).’” The Prophet (saws) said: “Do not do so, O Uthman, for the monasticism (tarahhub) of my community is sitting in the mosques and waiting for the prayer after the prayer.” He (narrator) said: “So I wanted, O Messenger of Allah (swt), to castrate myself.” The Prophet (saws) said: “Do not do so, O Uthman, for the castration (ikhtisa) of my community is fasting,” along with a lengthy statement.
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ غَالِبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ مَظْعُونٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِرَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ فَقَالَ »وَمَا هِيَ يَا عُثْمَانُ« قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنِّي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَتَرَهَّبَ قَالَ» لاَ تَفْعَلْ يَا عُثْمَانُ فَإِنَّ تَرَهُّبَ أُمَّتِي اَلْقُعُودُ فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ وَاِنْتِظَارُ اَلصَّلاَةِ بَعْدَ اَلصَّلاَةِ« قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَرَدْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَنْ أَخْتَصِيَ قَالَ» لاَ تَفْعَلْ يَا عُثْمَانُ فَإِنَّ اِخْتِصَاءَ أُمَّتِي اَلصِّيَامُ« مَعَ كَلاَمٍ طَوِيلٍ.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from Abdullah ibn Jabir, from Uthman ibn Madhun, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), I wanted to ask you about some things.” So the Prophet (saws) said: “And what are they, O Uthman?” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘I wanted to become a monk (atarahhab).’” The Prophet (saws) said: “Do not do so, O Uthman, for the monasticism (tarahhub) of my community is sitting in the mosques and waiting for the prayer after the prayer.” He (narrator) said: “So I wanted, O Messenger of Allah (swt), to castrate myself.” The Prophet (saws) said: “Do not do so, O Uthman, for the castration (ikhtisa) of my community is fasting,” along with a lengthy statement.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 254

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad al-Shairi, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to his companions: ‘Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, Satan will become distant from you just as the east is distant from the west?’” They (companions) said: “Yes.” The Prophet (saws) said: “Fasting blackens his (Satan) face, charity breaks his (Satan) back, love for the sake of Allah (swt) and mutual support in righteous action cut off his (Satan) root, and seeking forgiveness cuts off his life-vein.” And the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “For everything there is a zakat, and the zakat of the body is fasting.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ اَلشَّعِيرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:» أَنَّ اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ:» أَ لاَ أُ خْبِرُكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ فَعَلْتُمُوهُ تَبَاعَدَ اَلشَّيْطَانُ عَنْكُمْ كَمَا تَبَاعَدَ اَلْمَشْرِقُ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ« قَالُوا بَلَى قَالَ» اَلصَّوْمُ يُسَوِّدُ وَجْهَهُ وَ اَلصَّدَقَةُ تَكْسِرُ ظَهْرَهُ وَ اَلْحُبُّ فِي اَللَّهِ وَاَلْمُوَازَرَةُ عَلَى اَلْعَمَلِ اَلصَّالِحِ يَقْطَعُ دَابِرَهُ وَاَلاِسْتِغْفَارُ يَقْطَعُ وَتِينَهُ« وَ قَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ زَكَاةٌ وَ زَكَاةُ اَلْأَجْسَامِ اَلصِّيَامُ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad al-Shairi, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to his companions: ‘Shall I not inform you of something which, if you do it, Satan will become distant from you just as the east is distant from the west?’” They (companions) said: “Yes.” The Prophet (saws) said: “Fasting blackens his (Satan) face, charity breaks his (Satan) back, love for the sake of Allah (swt) and mutual support in righteous action cut off his (Satan) root, and seeking forgiveness cuts off his life-vein.” And the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “For everything there is a zakat, and the zakat of the body is fasting.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ismail ibn Yasar, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Indeed, a man may pray two rakahs, and Allah (swt) makes Paradise obligatory for him through them, Or he may fast one day voluntarily, and Allah (swt) makes Paradise obligatory for him through it.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ حَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: »إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ لَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَيُوجِبُ اَللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِمَا اَلْجَنَّةَ أَوْ يَصُومُ يَوْماً تَطَوُّعاً فَيُوجِبُ اَللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ اَلْجَنَّةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ismail ibn Yasar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Indeed, a man may pray two rakahs, and Allah (swt) makes Paradise obligatory for him through them, Or he may fast one day voluntarily, and Allah (swt) makes Paradise obligatory for him through it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muadh ibn Thabit Abu al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jumay, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said in a lengthy hadith: ‘Fasting is a shield from the Fire.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ جُمَيْعٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي حَدِيثٍ طَوِيلٍ:» اَلصِّيَامُ جُنَّةٌ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muadh ibn Thabit Abu al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jumay, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said in a lengthy hadith: ‘Fasting is a shield from the Fire.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on Reward of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Three things remove phlegm and increase memory; the tooth-stick (siwak), fasting, and recitation of the Quran.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» ثَلاَثٌ يُذْهِبْنَ اَلْبَلْغَمَ وَيَزِدْنَ فِي اَلْحِفْظِ اَلسِّوَاكُ وَ اَلصَّوْمُ وَقِرَاءَةُ اَلْقُرْآنِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Three things remove phlegm and increase memory; the tooth-stick (siwak), fasting, and recitation of the Quran.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Amr al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “‘Indeed, the number of months with Allah (swt) is twelve months in the Book of Allah (swt),’ Allah (swt) says, ‘On the day He (swt) created the heavens and the earth.’ So the first of the months is the month of Allah (swt), the month of Ramadan, And the heart of the month of Ramadan is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), And the Quran was sent down on the first night of the month of Ramadan, so receive the month (of Ramadan) with the Quran.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَمْرٍو اَلشَّامِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: » »إِنَّ عِدَّةَ اَلشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللهَِ اِثْنٰا عَشَرَ شَهْراً فِي كِتٰابِ اللهَِ « عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ »يَوْمَ خَلَقَ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ اَلْأَرْضَ« فَغُرَّةُ اَلشُّهُورِ شَهْرُ اَللَّهِ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ وَقَلْبُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ وَ نَزَلَ اَلْقُرْآنُ فِي أَوَّلِ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَاسْتَقْبِلِ اَلشَّهْرَ بِالْقُرْآنِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Amr al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “‘Indeed, the number of months with Allah (swt) is twelve months in the Book of Allah (swt),’ Allah (swt) says, ‘On the day He (swt) created the heavens and the earth.’ So the first of the months is the month of Allah (swt), the month of Ramadan, And the heart of the month of Ramadan is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), And the Quran was sent down on the first night of the month of Ramadan, so receive the month (of Ramadan) with the Quran.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 255

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from al-Mismai:
He (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) advising his children: “When the month of Ramadan enters, then exert yourselves, for in it provisions are apportioned, lifespans are written, and in it the delegation of Allah (swt) who come to Him (swt) are written. In it is a night (Al-Qadr) in which action is better than action in a thousand months.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ اَلْمِسْمَعِيِّ: أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُوصِي وُلْدَهُ» إِذَا دَخَلَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ فَأَجْهِدُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ تُقَسَّمُ اَلْأَرْزَاقُ وَتُكْتَبُ اَلْآجَالُ وَ فِيهِ يُكْتَبُ وَفْدُ اَللَّهِ اَلَّذِينَ يَفِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَ فِيهِ لَيْلَةٌ اَلْعَمَلُ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ اَلْعَمَلِ فِي أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from al-Mismai:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) advising his children: “When the month of Ramadan enters, then exert yourselves, for in it provisions are apportioned, lifespans are written, and in it the delegation of Allah (swt) who come to Him (swt) are written. In it is a night (Al-Qadr) in which action is better than action in a thousand months.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next year, unless he witnesses Arafah.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَنْ لَمْ يُغْفَرْ لَهُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ لَمْ يُغْفَرْ لَهُ إِلَى قَابِلٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ عَرَفَةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next year, unless he witnesses Arafah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah, from a man, from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
The Messenger of Allah (swt), said ‘when the month of Ramadan approached, and that was when three days remained from Shaban’, The Prophet (saws) said to Bilal: ‘Call out among the people.’ So Bilal gathered the people. The Prophet (saws) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah (swt) and extolled Him (swt), then said, “O people, indeed Allah (swt) has singled you out with this month (of Ramadan), and it is the master of the months. A night (Laylat al-Qadr) within it is better than a thousand months. In it the gates of the Fire are closed, and in it the gates of the gardens are opened. So whoever reaches this month and is not forgiven, may Allah (swt) distance him. And whoever reaches his parents and is not forgiven, may Allah (swt) distance him. And whoever I (saws) am mentioned before and does not send blessings upon Me (saws), may Allah (swt) distance him (from his mercy).’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِاَللَّهِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» لَمَّا حَضَرَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ وَذَلِكَ فِي ثَلاَثٍ بَقِينَ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ قَالَ لِبِلاَلٍ نَادِ فِي اَلنَّاسِ فَجَمَعَ اَلنَّاسَ ثُمَّ صَعِدَ اَلْمِنْبَرَ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ» أَيُّهَا اَلنَّاسُ إِنَّ هَذَا اَلشَّهْرَ قَدْ خَصَّكُمُ اَللَّهُ بِهِ وَ هُوَ سَيِّدُ اَلشُّهُورِ لَيْلَةٌ فِيهِ» خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ« تُغْلَقُ فِيهِ أَبْوَابُ اَلنَّارِ وَ تُفَتَّحُ فِيهِ أَبْوَابُ اَلْجِنَانِ فَمَنْ أَدْرَكَهُ وَ لَمْ يُغْفَرْ لَهُ فَأَبْعَدَهُ اَللَّهُ وَ مَنْ أَدْرَكَ وَالِدَيْهِ وَ لَمْ يُغْفَرْ لَهُ فَأَبْعَدَهُ اَللَّهُ وَ مَنْ ذُكِرْتُ عِنْدَهُ فَلَمْ يُصَلِّ عَلَيَّ فَأَبْعَدَهُ اَللَّهُ««.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah, from a man, from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), said ‘when the month of Ramadan approached, and that was when three days remained from Shaban’, The Prophet (saws) said to Bilal: ‘Call out among the people.’ So Bilal gathered the people. The Prophet (saws) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah (swt) and extolled Him (swt), then said, “O people, indeed Allah (swt) has singled you out with this month (of Ramadan), and it is the master of the months. A night (Laylat al-Qadr) within it is better than a thousand months. In it the gates of the Fire are closed, and in it the gates of the gardens are opened. So whoever reaches this month and is not forgiven, may Allah (swt) distance him. And whoever reaches his parents and is not forgiven, may Allah (swt) distance him. And whoever I (saws) am mentioned before and does not send blessings upon Me (saws), may Allah (swt) distance him (from his mercy).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 256

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would turn his face toward the people and say, ‘O assembly of Muslims, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises; The rebellious devils are shackled, The gates of the heaven and the gates of mercy are opened, The gates of the Fire are closed, Supplication is answered, And Allah (swt) has, at every breaking of the fast within it, freed ones whom Allah (swt) frees from the Fire. And a caller calls out every night: ‘Is there any asker? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah (swt), give every spender a replacement, and give every withholder destruction.’ Then when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are called: ‘Go early to your rewards, for it is the Day of Reward.’” Then Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, by the One (swt) in Whose hand (power) is my soul, it is not a reward of dinars and dirhams.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يُقْبِلُ بِوَجْهِهِ إِلَى اَلنَّاسِ فَيَقُولُ» يَا مَعْشَرَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ إِذَا طَلَعَ هِلاَلُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ غُلَّتْ مَرَدَةُ اَلشَّيَاطِينِ وَ فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ أَبْوَابُ اَلرَّحْمَةِ وَغُلِّقَتْ أَبْوَابُ اَلنَّارِ وَاُسْتُجِيبَ اَلدُّعَاءُ وَ كَانَ لِلَّهِ فِيهِ عِنْدَ كُلِّ فِطْرٍ عُتَقَاءُ يُعْتِقُهُمْ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ وَ يُنَادِي مُنَادٍ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ اَللَّهُمَّ أَعْطِ كُلَّ مُنْفِقٍ خَلَفاً وَ أَعْطِ كُلَّ مُمْسِكٍ تَلَفاً حَتَّى إِذَا طَلَعَ هِلاَلُ شَوَّالٍ نُودِيَ اَلْمُؤْمِنُونَ أَنِ اُغْدُوا إِلَى جَوَائِزِكُمْ فَهُوَ يَوْمُ اَلْجَائِزَةِ«« ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ »أَمَا وَ اَلَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ مَا هِيَ بِجَائِزَةِ اَلدَّنَانِيرِ وَ اَلدَّرَاهِمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would turn his face toward the people and say, ‘O assembly of Muslims, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises; The rebellious devils are shackled, The gates of the heaven and the gates of mercy are opened, The gates of the Fire are closed, Supplication is answered, And Allah (swt) has, at every breaking of the fast within it, freed ones whom Allah (swt) frees from the Fire. And a caller calls out every night: ‘Is there any asker? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah (swt), give every spender a replacement, and give every withholder destruction.’ Then when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are called: ‘Go early to your rewards, for it is the Day of Reward.’” Then Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, by the One (swt) in Whose hand (power) is my soul, it is not a reward of dinars and dirhams.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 257

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Indeed, Allah (swt) has, on every night of the month of Ramadan, freed ones and released ones from the Fire, except for one who breaks the fast upon an intoxicant. Then when it is the last night of it (month of Ramadan), Allah (swt) frees therein the like of what Allah (swt) freed throughout all of it (month of Ramadan).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» إِنَّ لِلَّهِ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ عُتَقَاءَ وَطُلَقَاءَ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَفْطَرَ عَلَى مُسْكِرٍ فَإِذَا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْهُ أَعْتَقَ فِيهَا مِثْلَ مَا أَعْتَقَ فِي جَمِيعِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Indeed, Allah (swt) has, on every night of the month of Ramadan, freed ones and released ones from the Fire, except for one who breaks the fast upon an intoxicant. Then when it is the last night of it (month of Ramadan), Allah (swt) frees therein the like of what Allah (swt) freed throughout all of it (month of Ramadan).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 257

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Torah was sent down after ‘six’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Gospel was sent down after ‘twelve’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Psalms were sent down after ‘eighteen’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Furqan (Quran) was sent down ‘on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).’”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» نَزَلَتِ اَلتَّوْرَاةُ فِي سِتٍّ مَضَيْنَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ نَزَلَ اَلْإِنْجِيلُ فِي اِثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ مَضَتْ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ نَزَلَ اَلزَّبُورُ فِي ثَمَانِي عَشْرَةَ مَضَتْ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ نَزَلَ اَلْفُرْقَانُ» فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Torah was sent down after ‘six’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Gospel was sent down after ‘twelve’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Psalms were sent down after ‘eighteen’ had passed from the month of Ramadan, And the Furqan (Quran) was sent down ‘on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, fasting is not from food and drink alone.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Mary (s.a) said, ‘Indeed, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful,’ meaning silence. (Surah Maryam 19:26) So when you fast, guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not dispute, and do not envy one another.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, heard a woman abusing a slave girl of hers while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, called for food and said to her: “Eat.” She replied: “I am fasting.” So the Prophet (saws) said: ‘How can you be fasting when you have abused your slave girl? Indeed, fasting is not (only) from food and drink.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ جَرَّاحٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِنَّ اَلصِّيَامَ لَيْسَ مِنَ اَلطَّعَامِ وَ اَلشَّرَابِ وَحْدَهُ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ» إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمٰنِ صَوْماً« أَيْ صَمْتاً فَإِذَا صُمْتُمْ فَاحْفَظُوا أَلْسِنَتَكُمْ وَغُضُّوا أَبْصَارَكُمْ وَ لاَ تَنَازَعُوا وَلاَ تَحَاسَدُوا« قَالَ» وَ سَمِعَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ اِمْرَأَةً تُسَابُّ جَارِيَةً لَهَا وَ هِيَ صَائِمَةٌ فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ بِطَعَامٍ فَقَالَ لَهَا» كُلِي« فَقَالَتْ إِنِّي صَائِمَةٌ فَقَالَ» كَيْفَ تَكُونِينَ صَائِمَةً وَ قَدْ سَبَبْتِ جَارِيَتَكِ إِنَّ اَلصَّوْمَ لَيْسَ مِنَ اَلطَّعَامِ وَ اَلشَّرَابِ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, fasting is not from food and drink alone.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Mary (s.a) said, ‘Indeed, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful,’ meaning silence. (Surah Maryam 19:26) So when you fast, guard your tongues, lower your gazes, do not dispute, and do not envy one another.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, heard a woman abusing a slave girl of hers while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, called for food and said to her: “Eat.” She replied: “I am fasting.” So the Prophet (saws) said: ‘How can you be fasting when you have abused your slave girl? Indeed, fasting is not (only) from food and drink.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you fast, then let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin fast.” And the Imam (a.s) enumerated things other than this. Imam (a.s) said: “And the day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking the fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» إِذَا صُمْتَ فَلْيَصُمْ سَمْعُكَ وَبَصَرُكَ وَشَعْرُكَ وَجِلْدُكَ وَعَدَّدَ أَشْيَاءَ غَيْرَ هَذَا قَالَ وَلاَ يَكُونُ يَوْمُ صَوْمِكَ كَيَوْمِ فِطْرِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you fast, then let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin fast.” And the Imam (a.s) enumerated things other than this. Imam (a.s) said: “And the day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast with you from what is forbidden and vile, And abandon disputation and harming the servant. Let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make the day of your fast like the day when you are not fasting.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ جَرَّاحٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» إِذَا صُمْتَ فَلْيَصُمْ مَعَكَ سَمْعُكَ وَبَصَرُكَ مِنَ اَلْحَرَامِ وَاَلْقَبِيحِ وَدَعِ اَلْمِرَاءَ وَأَذَى اَلْخَادِمِ وَلْيَكُنْ عَلَيْكَ وَقَارُ اَلصَّوْمِ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْ يَوْمَ صَوْمِكَ كَيَوْمِ فَطْرِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast with you from what is forbidden and vile, And abandon disputation and harming the servant. Let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make the day of your fast like the day when you are not fasting.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 258

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman and others, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him,:
Imam (a.s) said: “Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite (poetry) in the month of Ramadan, by night or by day.” So Ismail said to Imam (a.s): “O my father, even if it is concerning us?” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if it is concerning us.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تُنْشِدِ اَلشِّعْرَ بِلَيْلٍ وَ لاَ تُنْشِدْ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ بِلَيْلٍ وَ لاَ نَهَارٍ« فَقَالَ لَهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ يَا أَبَتَاهْ فَإِنَّهُ فِينَا قَالَ» وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِينَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman and others, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him,:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite (poetry) in the month of Ramadan, by night or by day.” So Ismail said to Imam (a.s): “O my father, even if it is concerning us?” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if it is concerning us.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 259

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When one of you fasts the three days in the month, then he must not dispute with anyone, nor act ignorantly, nor hasten to oaths and swearing by Allah (swt). And if anyone acts ignorantly toward him, then let him bear it patiently.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» إِذَا صَامَ أَحَدُكُمُ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلْأَيَّامِ فِي اَلشَّهْرِ فَلاَ يُجَادِلَنَّ أَحَداً وَ لاَ يَجْهَلْ وَ لاَ يُسْرِعْ إِلَى اَلْأَيْمَانِ وَاَلْحَلْفِ بِاللَّهِ وَ إِنْ جَهِلَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ فَلْيَتَحَمَّلْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When one of you fasts the three days in the month, then he must not dispute with anyone, nor act ignorantly, nor hasten to oaths and swearing by Allah (swt). And if anyone acts ignorantly toward him, then let him bear it patiently.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 259

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The narration of poetry is disliked for the fasting person, for the one in ihram, in the Sacred Precinct (al-haram), on Friday (Jumuah), and that it be narrated at night.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Even if it is poetry of truth?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if it is poetry of truth.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» يُكْرَهُ رِوَايَةُ اَلشِّعْرِ لِلصَّائِمِ وَلِلْمُحْرِمِ وَ فِي اَلْحَرَمِ وَ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ أَنْ يُرْوَى بِاللَّيْلِ« قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ شِعْرَ حَقٍّ قَالَ» وَ إِنْ كَانَ شِعْرَ حَقٍّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The narration of poetry is disliked for the fasting person, for the one in ihram, in the Sacred Precinct (al-haram), on Friday (Jumuah), and that it be narrated at night.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Even if it is poetry of truth?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if it is poetry of truth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 259

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Indeed, Allah (swt) disliked six qualities for Me (saws), and I (saws) disliked them for the successors from my children (the Imams (a.s)) and their followers (Shi’ah) after me; it is ‘obscene speech during fasting.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» إِنَّ اَللَّهَ كَرِهَ لِي سِتَّ خِصَالٍ وَكَرِهْتُهُنَّ لِلْأَوْصِيَاءِ مِنْ وُلْدِي وَ أَتْبَاعِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِيَ اَلرَّفَثَ فِي اَلصَّوْمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Indeed, Allah (swt) disliked six qualities for Me (saws), and I (saws) disliked them for the successors from my children (the Imams (a.s)) and their followers (Shi’ah) after me; it is ‘obscene speech during fasting.’”

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Jabir ibn Abdullah, ‘O Jabir, this is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, stands for a portion of worship from its night, keeps his stomach and his private part chaste, and restrains his tongue, exits from his sins just as he exits from the month.’ – meaning end of the month of Ramadan. So Jabir asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), how excellent this hadith is.” Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “O Jabir, and how severe these conditions are.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلنَّضْرِ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لِجَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ» يَا جَابِرُ هَذَا شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ مَنْ صَامَ نَهَارَهُ وَ قَامَ وِرْداً مِنْ لَيْلِهِ وَ عَفَّ بَطْنُهُ وَ فَرْجُهُ وَكَفَّ لِسَانَهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ ذُنُوبِهِ كَخُرُوجِهِ مِنَ اَلشَّهْرِ« فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا اَلْحَدِيثَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» يَا جَابِرُ وَمَا أَشَدَّ هَذِهِ اَلشُّرُوطَ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Jabir ibn Abdullah, ‘O Jabir, this is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, stands for a portion of worship from its night, keeps his stomach and his private part chaste, and restrains his tongue, exits from his sins just as he exits from the month.’ – meaning end of the month of Ramadan. So Jabir asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), how excellent this hadith is.” Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “O Jabir, and how severe these conditions are.”

chapter: Chapter on Sunnahs of the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the nights in which ghusl is recommended in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third.” And Imam (a.s) said: “On the night of the nineteenth, the delegation of the pilgrims is written therein, and ‘therein every wise affair is distinguished.’ (Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:4) And the night of the twenty-first, Jesus (a.s), peace be upon him, was raised therein, and therein the successor of Moses (a.s), peace be upon him, was taken, and therein the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, was taken (martyred). And the night of the twenty-third, and it is the Night of ‘al-Juhani’” And his hadith is that he said to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, ‘Indeed, my dwelling is far from Madinah, so command me with a night in which I should enter.’ So the Prophet (saws) commanded him with the night of the twenty-third.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَللَّيَالِي اَلَّتِي يُسْتَحَبُّ فِيهَا اَلْغُسْلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» لَيْلَةُ تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ وَ لَيْلَةُ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ وَ لَيْلَةُ ثَلاَثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ« وَقَالَ» فِي لَيْلَةِ تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ يُكْتَبُ فِيهَا وَفْدُ اَلْحَاجِّ وَ» فِيهٰا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ« وَلَيْلَةُ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ رُفِعَ فِيهَا عِيسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ فِيهَا قُبِضَ وَصِيُّ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ فِيهَا قُبِضَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ لَيْلَةُ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ وَ هِيَ لَيْلَةُ اَلْجُهَنِيِّ وَ حَدِيثُهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ إِنَّ مَنْزِلِي نَاءٍ عَنِ اَلْمَدِينَةِ فَمُرْنِي بِلَيْلَةٍ أَدْخُلُ فِيهَا فَأَمَرَهُ بِلَيْلَةِ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the nights in which ghusl is recommended in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third.” And Imam (a.s) said: “On the night of the nineteenth, the delegation of the pilgrims is written therein, and ‘therein every wise affair is distinguished.’ (Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:4) And the night of the twenty-first, Jesus (a.s), peace be upon him, was raised therein, and therein the successor of Moses (a.s), peace be upon him, was taken, and therein the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, was taken (martyred). And the night of the twenty-third, and it is the Night of ‘al-Juhani’” And his hadith is that he said to the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, ‘Indeed, my dwelling is far from Madinah, so command me with a night in which I should enter.’ So the Prophet (saws) commanded him with the night of the twenty-third.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 260

chapter: Chapter on the Supplication upon the Appearance of the Crescent Moon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “When the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would face the qiblah, raise his hands, and say, ‘O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, encompassing well-being, abundant provision, and the removal of illnesses. O Allah (swt), grant us its fasting, its standing, and the recitation of the Quran within it. O Allah (swt), keep it sound for us, receive it from us, and keep us safe within it.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَ اهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِبْرَ اهِيمَ بْنِ عُمَرَ اَلْيَمَانِيِّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ إِذَا هَلَّ هِلاَلُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ اَلْقِبْلَةَ وَ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَالَ» اَللَّهُمَّ أَهِلَّهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْأَمْنِ وَ اَلْإِيمَانِ وَاَلسَّلاَمَةِ وَ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ وَ اَلْعَافِيَةِ اَلْمُجَلِّلَةِ وَ اَلرِّزْقِ اَلْوَاسِعِ وَدَفْعِ اَلْأَسْقَامِ اَللَّهُمَّ اُرْزُقْنَا صِيَامَهُ وَقِيَامَهُ وَتِلاَوَةَ اَلْقُرْآنِ فِيهِ اَللَّهُمَّ سَلِّمْهُ لَنَا وَتَسَلَّمْهُ مِنَّا وَسَلِّمْنَا فِيهِ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would face the qiblah, raise his hands, and say, ‘O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, encompassing well-being, abundant provision, and the removal of illnesses. O Allah (swt), grant us its fasting, its standing, and the recitation of the Quran within it. O Allah (swt), keep it sound for us, receive it from us, and keep us safe within it.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 261

chapter: Chapter on the Supplication upon the Appearance of the Crescent Moon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, who said: Amr ibn Shimr narrated to us, saying:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), saying: “When the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, would turn toward the qiblah and say, ‘O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, and encompassing well-being. O Allah (swt), grant us its fasting, its standing, and the recitation of the Quran within it. O Allah (swt), keep it sound for us, receive it from us, and keep us safe within it.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ شِمْرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا هَلَّ هِلاَلُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَقْبَلَ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ قَالَ» اَللَّهُمَّ أَهِلَّهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْأَمْنِ وَ اَلْإِيمَانِ وَاَلسَّلاَمَةِ وَ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ وَ اَلْعَافِيَةِ اَلْمُجَلِّلَةِ اَللَّهُمَّ اُرْزُقْنَا صِيَامَهُ وَ قِيَامَهُ وَتِلاَوَةَ اَلْقُرْآنِ فِيهِ اَللَّهُمَّ سَلِّمْهُ لَنَا وَتَسَلَّمْهُ مِنَّا وَسَلِّمْنَا فِيهِ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, who said: Amr ibn Shimr narrated to us, saying:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), saying: “When the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, would turn toward the qiblah and say, ‘O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, and encompassing well-being. O Allah (swt), grant us its fasting, its standing, and the recitation of the Quran within it. O Allah (swt), keep it sound for us, receive it from us, and keep us safe within it.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Supplication upon the Appearance of the Crescent Moon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, raising it, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you see the crescent, then do not depart (without saying), and say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (swt) for the good of this month, its light, its victory, its blessing, its purity, and its provision. And I ask You (swt) for the good of what is in it and the good of what is after it, And I seek refuge in You (swt) from the evil of what is in it and the evil of what is after it. O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, blessing, God-wariness, and success in what You (swt) love and are pleased with.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ:» إِذَا رَأَيْتَ اَلْهِلاَلَ فَلاَ تَبْرَحْ وَ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هَذَا اَلشَّهْرِ وَ نُورَهُ وَنَصْرَهُ وَبَرَكَتَهُ وَطَهُورَهُ وَ رِزْقَهُ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِيهِ وَ خَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِيهِ وَ شَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ اَللَّهُمَّ أَدْخِلْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْأَمْنِ وَ اَلْإِيمَانِ وَاَلسَّلاَمَةِ وَ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ وَاَلْبَرَكَةِ وَاَلتَّقْوَى وَ اَلتَّوْفِيقِ لِمَا تُحِبُّ وَتَرْضَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, raising it, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you see the crescent, then do not depart (without saying), and say: ‘O Allah (swt), I ask You (swt) for the good of this month, its light, its victory, its blessing, its purity, and its provision. And I ask You (swt) for the good of what is in it and the good of what is after it, And I seek refuge in You (swt) from the evil of what is in it and the evil of what is after it. O Allah (swt), bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, blessing, God-wariness, and success in what You (swt) love and are pleased with.”

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Hasan, from Zurah, from Samaah, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) for one who intends to fast.’ Imam (a.s) said: “As for (month of) Ramadan, the merit is in the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), even if only with a drink of water. As for voluntary fasting outside (month of) Ramadan, whoever wishes to take the pre-dawn meal, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no problem.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسَّحُورِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ اَلصَّوْمَ فَقَالَ» أَمَّا فِي رَمَضَانَ فَإِنَّ اَلْفَضْلَ فِي اَلسَّحُورِ وَ لَوْ بِشَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَمَّا اَلتَّطَوُّعُ فِي غَيْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَمَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَتَسَحَّرَ فَلْيَفْعَلْ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Hasan, from Zurah, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) for one who intends to fast.’ Imam (a.s) said: “As for (month of) Ramadan, the merit is in the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), even if only with a drink of water. As for voluntary fasting outside (month of) Ramadan, whoever wishes to take the pre-dawn meal, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no problem.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muadh ibn Thabit Abu al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jumay, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Take the pre-dawn meal, even with mouthfuls of water. Indeed, the blessings of Allah (swt) are upon those who take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur).’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ جُمَيْعٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» تَسَحَّرُوا وَ لَوْ بِجُرَعِ اَلْمَاءِ أَلاَ صَلَوَاتُُ اَللَّهِ عَلَى اَلْمُتَسَحِّرِينَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muadh ibn Thabit Abu al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jumay, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Take the pre-dawn meal, even with mouthfuls of water. Indeed, the blessings of Allah (swt) are upon those who take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur).’”
