chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The best of your pre-dawn (al-suhur) meals is al-sawiq and dates.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: »أَفْضَلُ سَحُورِكُمُ اَلسَّوِيقُ وَ اَلتَّمْرُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The best of your pre-dawn (al-suhur) meals is al-sawiq and dates.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 262

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s), from his fathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) is a blessing.’” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘My community must not abandon the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), even if only upon a poor-quality dried date (hashafah).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» اَلسَّحُورُ بَرَكَةٌ« قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» لاَ تَدَعْ أُمَّتِيَ اَلسَّحُورَ وَ لَوْ عَلَى حَشَفَةٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s), from his fathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘The pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) is a blessing.’” Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘My community must not abandon the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), even if only upon a poor-quality dried date (hashafah).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salim, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would break the fast upon the two black things.” I (narrator) asked: “May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, and what are the two black things?” Imam (a.s) said: “Dates and water, and raisins and water, and He (saws) would take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) with them both.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلسَّلاَمِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يُفْطِرُ عَلَى اَلْأَسْوَدَيْنِ« قُلْتُ رَحِمَكَ اَللَّهُ وَ مَا اَلْأَسْوَدَانِ قَالَ» اَلتَّمْرُ وَ اَلْمَاءُ وَ اَلزَّبِيبُ وَ اَلْمَاءُ وَ يَتَسَحَّرُ بِهِمَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salim, from Sayf ibn Amirah, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would break the fast upon the two black things.” I (narrator) asked: “May Allah (swt) have mercy on you, and what are the two black things?” Imam (a.s) said: “Dates and water, and raisins and water, and He (saws) would take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) with them both.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Fudayl, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “In (month of) Ramadan, you pray (salah) and then break the fast, unless you are with people who are waiting for the breaking of the fast. If you are with the people, then do not oppose them; break the fast, then pray. Otherwise, begin with the prayer (and then break the fast).” I (narrator) asked: “And why is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because two obligations have come upon you; breaking the fast and prayer. So begin with the better of the two, and the better of the two is prayer.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “That you pray while you are fasting, so that prayer of yours is written and you seal it with fasting, is more beloved to me (the Imams (a.s)).”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ فُضَيْلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» فِي رَمَضَانَ تُصَلِّي ثُمَّ تُفْطِرُ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ يَنْتَظِرُونَ اَلْإِفْطَارَ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ مَعَهُمْ فَلاَ تُخَالِفْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ أَفْطِرْ ثُمَّ صَلِّ وَ إِلاَّ فَابْدَأْ بِالصَّلاَةِ« قُلْتُ وَ لِمَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ» لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ حَضَرَكَ فَرْضَانِ اَلْإِفْطَارُ وَ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَابْدَأْ بِأَفْضَلِهِمَا وَ أَفْضَلُهُمَا اَلصَّلاَةُ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» تُصَلِّي وَ أَنْتَ صَائِمٌ فَتُكْتَبُ صَلاَتُكَ تِلْكَ فَتَخْتِمُ بِالصَّوْمِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Fudayl, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “In (month of) Ramadan, you pray (salah) and then break the fast, unless you are with people who are waiting for the breaking of the fast. If you are with the people, then do not oppose them; break the fast, then pray. Otherwise, begin with the prayer (and then break the fast).” I (narrator) asked: “And why is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because two obligations have come upon you; breaking the fast and prayer. So begin with the better of the two, and the better of the two is prayer.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “That you pray while you are fasting, so that prayer of yours is written and you seal it with fasting, is more beloved to me (the Imams (a.s)).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Rifaah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said, ‘Assist one another, by eating the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), in fasting the day, and by sleeping at the midday nap (al-qaylulah), in standing during the night.’”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلرَّازِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» تَعَاوَنُوا بِأَكْلِ اَلسَّحُورِ عَلَى صِيَامِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَبِالنَّوْمِ عِنْدَ اَلْقَيْلُولَةِ عَلَى قِيَامِ اَللَّيْلِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Rifaah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said, ‘Assist one another, by eating the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur), in fasting the day, and by sleeping at the midday nap (al-qaylulah), in standing during the night.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 263

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Breaking the fast upon water washes away the sins of the heart.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلْإِفْطَارُ عَلَى اَلْمَاءِ يَغْسِلُ ذُنُوبَ اَلْقَلْبِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Breaking the fast upon water washes away the sins of the heart.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 264

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from some of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “If the people were to take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) and not break their fast upon water, by Allah (swt), they would not be able to fast perpetually.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَوْ أَنَّ اَلنَّاسَ تَسَحَّرُوا وَ لَمْ يُفْطِرُوا عَلَى مَاءٍ مَا قَدَرُوا وَ اَللَّهِ أَنْ يَصُومُوا اَلدَّهْرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from some of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If the people were to take the pre-dawn meal (al-suhur) and not break their fast upon water, by Allah (swt), they would not be able to fast perpetually.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 264

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Jafar, from his father:
Imam (a.s) said: “That Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to like breaking the fast upon milk.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ:» أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :كَانَ يَسْتَحِبُّ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ عَلَى اَللَّبَنِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Jafar, from his father:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “That Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to like breaking the fast upon milk.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 264

chapter: Chapter on Merit of the Pre-Dawn Meal (Suhur) and What It Is Recommended That the Breaking of the Fast Be upon
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “It is recommended for the fasting person, if he is able to do that, to pray (salah) before he breaks the fast.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَحْمَدَ اِبْنَيِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يُسْتَحَبُّ لِلصَّائِمِ إِنْ قَوِيَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “It is recommended for the fasting person, if he is able to do that, to pray (salah) before he breaks the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 264

chapter: Chapter on the Words and Supplication at the Time of Breaking the Fast (Iftar)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad (a.s), from his fathers (a.s), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) said: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, broke the fast, He (saws) would say: ‘O Allah (swt), for You (swt) we fasted, and upon Your (swt) provision we broke the fast, so accept it from us. The thirst has gone, the veins have become moist, and the reward remains.’” (Allahumma laka sumna, wa ‘ala rizqika aftarna, fa-taqabbalhu minna. Dhahaba al-zama’u, wa ibtallati al-‘uruqu, wa baqiya al-ajru)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ كَانَ إِذَا أَفْطَرَ قَالَ» اَللَّهُمَّ لَكَ صُمْنَا وَ عَلَى رِزْقِكَ أَفْطَرْنَا فَتَقَبَّلْهُ مِنَّا ذَهَبَ اَلظَّمَأُ وَاِبْتَلَّتِ اَلْعُرُوقُ وَ بَقِيَ اَلْأَجْرُ««.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad (a.s), from his fathers (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, broke the fast, He (saws) would say: ‘O Allah (swt), for You (swt) we fasted, and upon Your (swt) provision we broke the fast, so accept it from us. The thirst has gone, the veins have become moist, and the reward remains.’” (Allahumma laka sumna, wa ‘ala rizqika aftarna, fa-taqabbalhu minna. Dhahaba al-zama’u, wa ibtallati al-‘uruqu, wa baqiya al-ajru)

chapter: Chapter on the Words and Supplication at the Time of Breaking the Fast (Iftar)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa’adan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “You say on every night of the month of Ramadan at the time of breaking the fast, until its end: ‘Praise belongs to Allah (swt), who helped us, so we fasted, and provided for us, so we broke our fast. O Allah (swt), accept from us, help us in it, keep us safe in it, and receive it from us with ease from You (swt) and well-being. And praise belongs to Allah (swt), who has completed for us a day from the month of Ramadan.” (Alhamdu lillahi alladhi a‘anana fa-sumna, wa razaqana fa-aftarna. Allahumma taqabbal minna, wa a‘inna ‘alayhi, wa sallimna fihi, wa tasallamhu minna fi yusrin minka wa ‘afiyah. Walhamdu lillahi alladhi qada ‘anna yawman min shahri Ramadan)

thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa’adan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “You say on every night of the month of Ramadan at the time of breaking the fast, until its end: ‘Praise belongs to Allah (swt), who helped us, so we fasted, and provided for us, so we broke our fast. O Allah (swt), accept from us, help us in it, keep us safe in it, and receive it from us with ease from You (swt) and well-being. And praise belongs to Allah (swt), who has completed for us a day from the month of Ramadan.” (Alhamdu lillahi alladhi a‘anana fa-sumna, wa razaqana fa-aftarna. Allahumma taqabbal minna, wa a‘inna ‘alayhi, wa sallimna fihi, wa tasallamhu minna fi yusrin minka wa ‘afiyah. Walhamdu lillahi alladhi qada ‘anna yawman min shahri Ramadan)

chapter: Chapter on the Words and Supplication at the Time of Breaking the Fast (Iftar)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Qanbar, the freed slave of Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, came to Imam (a.s) with his food for breaking the fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “So he (Qanbar) came with a sack in which there was sawiq (porridge-like dish), upon which there was a seal. A man then said to Imam Ali (a.s): “O Commander of the Faithful (a.s), this is indeed miserliness, that you seal your food.’” Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, laughed. Then Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Is it other than that? I do not like anything to enter my stomach except something whose path I know.” Then Imam Ali (a.s) broke the seal, took out some sawiq from it, placed some of it in a cup, and gave it to him (the man). Imam Ali (a.s) took the cup, and when he wanted to drink, he said: ‘In the name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), for You (swt) we have fasted, and upon Your (swt) provision we have broken our fast, so accept from us. Indeed, You (swt) are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.’” (Bismillah. Allahumma laka sumna, wa ‘ala rizqika aftarna, fa-taqabbal minna. Innaka anta al-sami‘u al-‘alim)
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْجَهْمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ اَلْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» جَاءَ قَنْبَرٌ مَوْلَى عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِفِطْرِهِ إِلَيْهِ« قَالَ» فَجَاءَ بِجِرَابٍ فِيهِ سَوِيقٌ عَلَيْهِ خَاتَمٌ« قَالَ» فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ يَا أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ اَلْبُخْلُ تَخْتِمُ عَلَى طَعَامِكَ« قَالَ» فَضَحِكَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« قَالَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ» أَوَ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ لاَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بَطْنِي شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ شَيْءٌ أَعْرِفُ سَبِيلَهُ«« قَالَ» ثُمَّ كَسَرَ اَلْخَاتَمَ فَأَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ سَوِيقاً فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ فِي قَدَحٍ فَأَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ فَأَخَذَ اَلْقَدَحَ فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَشْرَبَ قَالَ» بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ لَكَ صُمْنَا وَ عَلَى رِزْقِكَ أَفْطَرْنَا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا» إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلسَّمِيعُ اَلْعَلِيمُ«««.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Qanbar, the freed slave of Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, came to Imam (a.s) with his food for breaking the fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “So he (Qanbar) came with a sack in which there was sawiq (porridge-like dish), upon which there was a seal. A man then said to Imam Ali (a.s): “O Commander of the Faithful (a.s), this is indeed miserliness, that you seal your food.’” Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, laughed. Then Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Is it other than that? I do not like anything to enter my stomach except something whose path I know.” Then Imam Ali (a.s) broke the seal, took out some sawiq from it, placed some of it in a cup, and gave it to him (the man). Imam Ali (a.s) took the cup, and when he wanted to drink, he said: ‘In the name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), for You (swt) we have fasted, and upon Your (swt) provision we have broken our fast, so accept from us. Indeed, You (swt) are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.’” (Bismillah. Allahumma laka sumna, wa ‘ala rizqika aftarna, fa-taqabbal minna. Innaka anta al-sami‘u al-‘alim)

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Volunteering in Good Deeds
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever gives a fasting person food with which to break his fast, then he shall have the like of his reward.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَلَمَةَ صَاحِبِ اَلسَّابِرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْكِنَانِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: »مَنْ فَطَّرَ صَائِماً فَلَهُ مِ ثْ لُ أَ جْ رِ هِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Volunteering in Good Deeds
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa’adan ibn Muslim, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “You giving your fasting brother food, with which to break his fast, is better than your fasting.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» فِطْرُكَ أَخَاكَ اَلصَّائِمَ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صِيَامِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa’adan ibn Muslim, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “You giving your fasting brother food, with which to break his fast, is better than your fasting.”

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Volunteering in Good Deeds
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Sadir entered upon my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) in the month of Ramadan. And Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O Sadir, do you know which nights these are?” So he (Sadir) said: “Yes, may my father be your ransom, these are the nights of the month of Ramadan. So what about it?” Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to him: “Are you able to free, on every night of these nights, ten slaves from the children of Ismail?” So Sadir said to him: “May my father and my mother be your ransom, my wealth does not reach that.” Imam al-Baqir (a.s) continued reducing it until he brought it down to one slave, and in all of that he (Sadir) would say, ‘I am not able to do it.’ Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to him: “Then are you not able to give, on every night, a Muslim man food with which to break his fast?” Sadir said to Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “Yes, and ten.” So my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said to Sadir: “That is what I intended, O Sadir. Your giving your Muslim brother food, with which to break his fast, is equal to freeing a slave from the children of Ismail.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» دَخَلَ سَدِيرٌ عَلَى أَبِي فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» يَا سَدِيرُ هَلْ تَدْرِي أَيُّ لَيَالٍ هَذِهِ« فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فِدَاكَ أَبِي هَذِهِ لَيَالِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَمَاذَا فَقَالَ لَهُ» أَ تَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَنْ تُعْتِقَ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنَ اَللَّيَالِي عَشْرَ رِقَابٍ مِنْ وُلْدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ« فَقَالَ لَهُ سَدِيرٌ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي لاَ يَبْلُغُ مَالِي ذَلِكَ فَمَا زَالَ يُنْقِصُ حَتَّى بَلَغَ بِهِ رَقَبَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي كُلِّ ذَلِكَ يَقُولُ لاَ أَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ» فَمَا تَقْدِرُ أَنْ تُفَطِّرَ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ رَجُلاً مُسْلِماً« فَقَالَ لَهُ بَلَى وَ عَشَرَةً فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبِي» فَذَاكَ اَلَّذِي أَرَدْتُ يَا سَدِيرُ إِفْطَارُكَ أَخَاكَ اَلْمُسْلِمَ يَعْدِلُ رَقَبَةً مِنْ وُلْدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Sadir entered upon my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) in the month of Ramadan. And Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “O Sadir, do you know which nights these are?” So he (Sadir) said: “Yes, may my father be your ransom, these are the nights of the month of Ramadan. So what about it?” Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to him: “Are you able to free, on every night of these nights, ten slaves from the children of Ismail?” So Sadir said to him: “May my father and my mother be your ransom, my wealth does not reach that.” Imam al-Baqir (a.s) continued reducing it until he brought it down to one slave, and in all of that he (Sadir) would say, ‘I am not able to do it.’ Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to him: “Then are you not able to give, on every night, a Muslim man food with which to break his fast?” Sadir said to Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “Yes, and ten.” So my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) said to Sadir: “That is what I intended, O Sadir. Your giving your Muslim brother food, with which to break his fast, is equal to freeing a slave from the children of Ismail.”

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Volunteering in Good Deeds
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Whoever gives a fasting person food with which to break his fast, he shall have the like of his reward, without anything being diminished from it, and whatever righteousness he does through the strength of that food.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:» مَنْ فَطَّرَ صَائِماً كَانَ لَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَنْقُصَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ وَ مَا عَمِلَ بِقُوَّةِ ذَلِكَ اَلطَّعَامِ مِنْ بِرٍّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Whoever gives a fasting person food with which to break his fast, he shall have the like of his reward, without anything being diminished from it, and whatever righteousness he does through the strength of that food.’”

chapter: Chapter on Merit of Volunteering in Good Deeds
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Jafar ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delivered a sermon on the last Friday of Shaban. The Prophet (saws) praised Allah (swt) and extolled Him (swt), and spoke some words, then said: ‘The month of Ramadan has come upon you. Whoever gives a fasting person food with which to break his fast in it, by that he shall have with Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness of his past sins.’ It was said to the Prophet (saws): “O Messenger of Allah (swt), not all of us are able to give a fasting person food with which to break his fast.” Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt) is generous. He (swt) gives this reward to one who is not able except to provide a mixture of milk (madhqah) with which he gives a fasting person to break his fast, or a drink of fresh water, or some dates, and he is not able to provide more than that.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْوَرْدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: »خَطَبَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي آخِرِ جُمُعَةٍ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ وَتَكَلَّمَ بِكَلاَمٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ »قَدْ أَظَلَّكُمْ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ مَنْ فَطَّرَ فِيهِ صَائِماً كَانَ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ عِنْدَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ وَ مَغْفِرَةُ ذُنُوبِهِ فِيمَا مَضَى« قِيلَ لَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَيْسَ كُلُّنَا نَقْدِرُ أَنْ نُفَطِّرَ صَائِماً قَالَ» إِنَّ اَللَّهَ كَرِيمٌ يُعْطِي هَذَا اَلثَّوَابَ لِمَنْ لاَ يَقْدِرُ إِلاَّ عَلَى مَذْقَةٍ مِنْ لَبَنٍ يُفَطِّرُ بِهَا صَائِماً أَوْ شَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ عَذْبٍ أَوْ تَمَرَاتٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Jafar ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delivered a sermon on the last Friday of Shaban. The Prophet (saws) praised Allah (swt) and extolled Him (swt), and spoke some words, then said: ‘The month of Ramadan has come upon you. Whoever gives a fasting person food with which to break his fast in it, by that he shall have with Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness of his past sins.’ It was said to the Prophet (saws): “O Messenger of Allah (swt), not all of us are able to give a fasting person food with which to break his fast.” Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt) is generous. He (swt) gives this reward to one who is not able except to provide a mixture of milk (madhqah) with which he gives a fasting person to break his fast, or a drink of fresh water, or some dates, and he is not able to provide more than that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 266

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Nothing harms the fasting person in what he does if he avoids three qualities; food and drink, women, and immersion in water (al-irtimas fi al-ma).”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن محمد بن ابي عمير عن حماد بن عثمان عن محمد بن مسلم قال: سمعت ابا جعفر عليه السلام يقول: لا يضر الصائم ما صنع إذا اجتنب ثلاث خصال: الطعام والشراب، والنساء، والارتماس في الماء
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “Nothing harms the fasting person in what he does if he avoids three qualities; food and drink, women, and immersion in water (al-irtimas fi al-ma).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 267

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “A lie invalidates ablution and breaks the fast.” He (narrator) said: “I said, ‘We are ruined.’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not as you think. That is only lying against Allah (swt), against His Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and against the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ يُونُسَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» اَلْكَذِبَةُ تَنْقُضُ اَلْوُضُوءَ وَ تُفَطِّرُ اَلصِّيَامَ« قَالَ قُلْتُ هَلَكْنَا قَالَ» لَيْسَ حَيْثُ تَذْهَبُ إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ اَلْكَذِبُ عَلَى اَللَّهِ وَعَلَى رَسُولِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ عَلَى اَلْأَئِمَّةِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “A lie invalidates ablution and breaks the fast.” He (narrator) said: “I said, ‘We are ruined.’” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not as you think. That is only lying against Allah (swt), against His Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and against the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 267

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who lied in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He has broken his fast, and upon him is its making up, while he is fasting; he makes up his fast and his ablution if he did so deliberately.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَذَبَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ »قَدْ أَفْطَرَ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ يَقْضِي صَوْمَهُ وَ وُضُوءَهُ إِذَا تَعَمَّدَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who lied in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He has broken his fast, and upon him is its making up, while he is fasting; he makes up his fast and his ablution if he did so deliberately.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may immerse himself in water, but he must not submerge his head.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلصَّائِمُ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ وَ لاَ يَرْمُسُ رَأْسَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may immerse himself in water, but he must not submerge his head.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person and the person in the state of ihram must not submerge his head in water.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ يَرْمُسُ اَلصَّائِمُ وَ لاَ اَلْمُحْرِمُ رَأْسَهُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person and the person in the state of ihram must not submerge his head in water.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:
He (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who administers an enema (yahtaqin), while he has an illness in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person is not permitted to administer an enema.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَحْتَقِنُ تَكُونُ بِهِ اَلْعِلَّةُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» اَلصَّائِمُ لاَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَحْتَقِنَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who administers an enema (yahtaqin), while he has an illness in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person is not permitted to administer an enema.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And that which Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his father, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s): “What do you say regarding gentle treatment with suppositories (ashyaf), which a person inserts while he is fasting?” So the Imam (a.s), wrote: “There is no harm in the solid one.”
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلتَّلَطُّفِ بِالْأَشْيَافِ يَسْتَدْخِلُهُ اَلْإِنْسَانُ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِالْجَامِدِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And that which Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s): “What do you say regarding gentle treatment with suppositories (ashyaf), which a person inserts while he is fasting?” So the Imam (a.s), wrote: “There is no harm in the solid one.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may soak himself in water, pour water over his head, cool himself with a garment, sprinkle (damp) the fan, and sprinkle (damp) the reed mat (al-buriya), but he must not immerse his head in water.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلصَّائِمُ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ وَيَصُبُّ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَيَتَبَرَّدُ بِالثَّوْبِ وَيَنْضِحُ اَلْمِرْوَحَةَ وَيَنْضِحُ اَلْبُورِيَاءَ وَ لاَ يَغْمِسُ رَأْسَهُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may soak himself in water, pour water over his head, cool himself with a garment, sprinkle (damp) the fan, and sprinkle (damp) the reed mat (al-buriya), but he must not immerse his head in water.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person undergoing cupping and pouring oil into his ear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, except snuff (al-suoot), for it is disliked.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِبَاطٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ لَيْثٍ اَلْمُرَادِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَحْتَجِمُ وَ يَصُبُّ فِي أُذُنِهِ اَلدُّهْنَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ إِلاَّ اَلسُّعُوطُ فَإِنَّهُ يُكْرَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person undergoing cupping and pouring oil into his ear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, except snuff (al-suoot), for it is disliked.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on What Invalidates Fasting, What Impairs the Conditions of Its Obligation, and Nullifies Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said:
He said: “The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may use the tooth-stick (siwak) whenever he wishes, and if he rinses his mouth at the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, then there is nothing upon him, and his fast is complete. But if he rinses his mouth at other than the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, then upon him is repetition. So it is better for the fasting person not to rinse his mouth.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اَلرَّيَّانِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ عَنْ يُونُسَ قَالَ:» اَلصَّائِمُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ يَسْتَاكُ مَتَى شَاءَ وَإِنْ تَمَضْمَضَ فِي وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ فَدَخَلَ اَلْمَاءُ حَلْقَهُ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ تَمَّ صَوْمُهُ وَ إِنْ تَمَضْمَضَ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ فَدَخَلَ اَلْمَاءُ حَلْقَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ فَالْأَفْضَلُ لِلصَّائِمِ أَنْ لاَ يَتَمَضْمَضَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He said: “The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may use the tooth-stick (siwak) whenever he wishes, and if he rinses his mouth at the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, then there is nothing upon him, and his fast is complete. But if he rinses his mouth at other than the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, then upon him is repetition. So it is better for the fasting person not to rinse his mouth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 270

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast in the month of Ramadan for one day without an excuse.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He frees a soul, or fasts two consecutive months, or feeds sixty needy persons. If he is not able, he gives charity with whatever he can bear.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً يَوْماً وَاحِداً مِنْ غَيْرِ عُذْرٍ قَالَ »يُعْتِقُ نَسَمَةً أَوْ يَصُومُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ أَوْ يُطْعِمُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ تَصَدَّقَ بِمَا يُطِيقُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast in the month of Ramadan for one day without an excuse.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He frees a soul, or fasts two consecutive months, or feeds sixty needy persons. If he is not able, he gives charity with whatever he can bear.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
That Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for a day from the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “A man came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: ‘I am ruined, O Messenger of Allah (swt).’ The Prophet (saws) said: “What is the matter with you?” He replied: “The Fire, O Messenger of Allah (swt).” So the Prophet (saws) said: “And what is the matter with you?” He said: “I had intercourse with my wife (when fasting).” So the Prophet (saws) said: “Give charity and seek forgiveness from your Lord (azj).” The man replied: “By the One (swt) who has magnified your right, I have not left in the house anything, neither little nor much (to give as charity).” The Imam (a.s) continues that ‘then a man from among the people entered with a basket (miktal) of dates, in which there were twenty sa’, which would be ten sa’ according to our sa’.’ So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to the man: “Take these dates and give them in charity.” He replied: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), to whom shall I give them in charity, when I have already informed you that there is nothing in my house, neither little nor much?” The Prophet (saws) said: “Then take it, feed it to your dependants, and seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.” He (narrator) said: “When we returned, our companions said: ‘He began with freeing.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Free (slaves), or fast (consecutively), or give charity.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ يَوْماً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً فَقَالَ» إِنَّ رَجُلاً أَتَى اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَقَالَ هَلَكْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَقَالَ» مَا لَكَ« قَالَ اَلنَّارُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَقَالَ» وَ مَا لَكَ« فَقَالَ وَقَعْتُ عَلَى أَهْلِي فَقَالَ» تَصَدَّقْ وَاِسْتَغْفِرْ رَبَّكَ« فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ فَوَاَلَّذِي عَظَّمَ حَقَّكَ مَا تَرَكْتُ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ شَيْئاً قَلِيلاً وَ لاَ كَثِيراً قَالَ فَدَخَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ بِمِكْتَلٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ فِيهِ عِشْرُونَ صَاعاً يَكُونُ عَشَرَةَ أَصْوُعٍ بِصَاعِنَا فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ» خُذْ هَذَا اَلتَّمْرَ فَتَصَدَّقْ بِهِ« فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ عَلَى مَنْ أَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ وَ قَدْ أَخْبَرْتُكَ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِي بَيْتِي قَلِيلٌ وَ لاَ كَثِيرٌ قَالَ» فَخُذْهُ فَأَطْعِمْهُ عِيَالَكَ وَاِسْتَغْفِرِ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ« قَالَ فَلَمَّا رَجَعْنَا قَالَ أَصْحَابُنَا إِنَّهُ بَدَأَ بِالْعِتْقِ قَالَ» أَعْتِقْ أَوْ صُمْ أَوْ تَصَدَّقْ««.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: That Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for a day from the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “A man came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: ‘I am ruined, O Messenger of Allah (swt).’ The Prophet (saws) said: “What is the matter with you?” He replied: “The Fire, O Messenger of Allah (swt).” So the Prophet (saws) said: “And what is the matter with you?” He said: “I had intercourse with my wife (when fasting).” So the Prophet (saws) said: “Give charity and seek forgiveness from your Lord (azj).” The man replied: “By the One (swt) who has magnified your right, I have not left in the house anything, neither little nor much (to give as charity).” The Imam (a.s) continues that ‘then a man from among the people entered with a basket (miktal) of dates, in which there were twenty sa’, which would be ten sa’ according to our sa’.’ So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to the man: “Take these dates and give them in charity.” He replied: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), to whom shall I give them in charity, when I have already informed you that there is nothing in my house, neither little nor much?” The Prophet (saws) said: “Then take it, feed it to your dependants, and seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic.” He (narrator) said: “When we returned, our companions said: ‘He began with freeing.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Free (slaves), or fast (consecutively), or give charity.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘a man who had intercourse with his wife in the month of Ramadan and did not find anything with which to give charity to sixty needy persons.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He gives charity with whatever he can bear.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ وَقَعَ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ مَا يَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ عَلَى سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً قَالَ» يَتَصَدَّقُ بِمَا يُطِيقُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘a man who had intercourse with his wife in the month of Ramadan and did not find anything with which to give charity to sixty needy persons.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He gives charity with whatever he can bear.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fondles his wife in the month of Ramadan until he ejaculates.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him is, of the expiation, the like of what is upon the one who has intercourse.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَعْبَثُ بِأَهْلِهِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ حَتَّى يُمْنِيَ قَالَ» عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ مِثْلُ مَا عَلَى اَلَّذِي يُجَامِعُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fondles his wife in the month of Ramadan until he ejaculates.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him is, of the expiation, the like of what is upon the one who has intercourse.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who was seized in the month of Ramadan, and he had broken his fast three times, and he had been brought before the (divinely appointed) Imam three times.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Let him be killed on the third.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أُخِذَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ قَدْ أَفْطَرَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ قَدْ رُفِعَ إِلَى اَلْإِمَامِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ قَالَ» فَلْيُقْتَلْ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who was seized in the month of Ramadan, and he had broken his fast three times, and he had been brought before the (divinely appointed) Imam three times.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Let him be killed on the third.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for a day from the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him are fifteen sa’, for every needy person one mudd according to the mudd of the Prophet (saws), and that is better.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ يَوْماً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً قَالَ »عَلَيْهِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ صَاعاً لِكُلِّ مِسْكِينٍ مُدٌّ بِمُدِّ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَفْضَلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Jafar, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for a day from the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him are fifteen sa’, for every needy person one mudd according to the mudd of the Prophet (saws), and that is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mashriqi, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for some days from the month of Ramadan. What expiation is upon him?’ So the Imam (a.s), wrote: “Whoever deliberately breaks his fast for a day from month of Ramadan, upon him is freeing of a believing slave, and he fasts a day in place of a day.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْمَشْرِقِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَيَّاماً مُتَعَمِّداً مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» مَنْ أَفْطَرَ يَوْماً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً فَعَلَيْهِ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ وَ يَصُومُ يَوْماً بَدَلَ يَوْمٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mashriqi, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who deliberately broke his fast for some days from the month of Ramadan. What expiation is upon him?’ So the Imam (a.s), wrote: “Whoever deliberately breaks his fast for a day from month of Ramadan, upon him is freeing of a believing slave, and he fasts a day in place of a day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ismail ibn Marrar and Abd al-Jabbar ibn Mubarak, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir and Samaah ibn Mihran, who both said:
We (narrators) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man upon whom there is the fasting of two consecutive months, but he is not able to fast, and he is not able to free a slave, and he is not able to give charity.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him fast eighteen days, for every ten needy persons, three days.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ بْنِ مُبَارَكٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالاَ: سَأَلْنَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى اَلصِّيَامِ وَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى اَلْعِتْقِ وَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى اَلصَّدَقَةِ قَالَ» فَلْيَصُمْ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً عَنْ كُلِّ عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ismail ibn Marrar and Abd al-Jabbar ibn Mubarak, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir and Samaah ibn Mihran, who both said:
thaqalaynMatn: We (narrators) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man upon whom there is the fasting of two consecutive months, but he is not able to fast, and he is not able to free a slave, and he is not able to give charity.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him fast eighteen days, for every ten needy persons, three days.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Sa’ad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said al-Madaini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who, while fasting, has intercourse with his wife.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He performs ghusl, and there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَيُجَامِعُ أَهْلَهُ فَقَالَ »يَغْتَسِلُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Sa’ad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said al-Madaini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who, while fasting, has intercourse with his wife.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He performs ghusl, and there is nothing upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurarah and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who both said:
We (narrators) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who came to his wife in the month of Ramadan, and came to his wife while he was in the state of ihram, while he did not see except that this was lawful for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him (due to their ignorance on the matter).”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ جَمِيعاً: سَأَلْنَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَتَى أَهْلَهُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَأَتَى أَهْلَهُ وَ هُوَ مُحْرِمٌ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَرَى إِلاَّ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ حَلاَلٌ لَهُ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurarah and Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who both said:
thaqalaynMatn: We (narrators) asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who came to his wife in the month of Ramadan, and came to his wife while he was in the state of ihram, while he did not see except that this was lawful for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him (due to their ignorance on the matter).”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I asked him about ‘a man who deliberately came to his wife in the month of Ramadan’. So he said: “Upon him is the freeing of a slave, And feeding sixty needy persons, And fasting two consecutive months, And making up that day; and how could he have the like of that day?” – meaning that he would still not be able to attain the reward of that singular day of fasting in the month of Ramadan.
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَتَى أَهْلَهُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً فَقَالَ» عَلَيْهِ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ وَ إِطْعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً وَ صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ أَنَّى لَهُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about ‘a man who deliberately came to his wife in the month of Ramadan’. So he said: “Upon him is the freeing of a slave, And feeding sixty needy persons, And fasting two consecutive months, And making up that day; and how could he have the like of that day?” – meaning that he would still not be able to attain the reward of that singular day of fasting in the month of Ramadan.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), it has been narrated from your fathers (a.s), peace be upon them, regarding ‘one who has intercourse in the month of Ramadan or breaks his fast in it, that there are three expiations, and it has also been narrated from them, that there is one expiation. So by which of the two hadiths should we act?’” Imam (a.s) said: “By both of them together. Whenever a man has unlawful intercourse, or breaks his fast upon something unlawful, in the month of Ramadan, then upon him are three expiations: freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty needy persons, and making up that day. But if he has married lawfully, or breaks his fast upon something lawful, then upon him is one expiation. And if he was forgetful, then there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ بَابَوَيْهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْوَاحِدِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبْدُوسٍ اَلنَّيْسَابُورِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قُتَيْبَةَ عَنْ حَمْدَانَ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلسَّلاَمِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ اَلْهَرَوِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَا اِبْنَ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ آبَائِكَ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ» فِيمَنْ جَامَعَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَوْ أَفْطَرَ فِيهِ ثَلاَثُ كَفَّارَاتٍ« وَ رُوِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَيْضاً» كَفَّارَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ« فَبِأَيِّ اَلْحَدِيثَيْنِ نَأْخُذُ قَالَ» بِهِمَا جَمِيعاً مَتَى جَامَعَ اَلرَّجُلُ حَرَاماً أَوْ أَفْطَرَ عَلَى حَرَامٍ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَعَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثُ كَفَّارَاتٍ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ وَ صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ إِطْعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً وَ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ نَكَحَ حَلاَلاً أَوْ أَفْطَرَ عَلَى حَلاَلٍ فَعَلَيْهِ كَفَّارَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ نَاسِياً فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), it has been narrated from your fathers (a.s), peace be upon them, regarding ‘one who has intercourse in the month of Ramadan or breaks his fast in it, that there are three expiations, and it has also been narrated from them, that there is one expiation. So by which of the two hadiths should we act?’” Imam (a.s) said: “By both of them together. Whenever a man has unlawful intercourse, or breaks his fast upon something unlawful, in the month of Ramadan, then upon him are three expiations: freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty needy persons, and making up that day. But if he has married lawfully, or breaks his fast upon something lawful, then upon him is one expiation. And if he was forgetful, then there is nothing upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “It is disliked for the fasting person to immerse himself in water.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يُكْرَهُ لِلصَّائِمِ أَنْ يَرْتَمِسَ فِي اَلْمَاءِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “It is disliked for the fasting person to immerse himself in water.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A fasting man deliberately immersed himself in water; is making up that day upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Making it up is not upon him, but he must certainly not return to doing it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ صَائِمٌ اِرْتَمَسَ فِي اَلْمَاءِ مُتَعَمِّداً أَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ قَالَ» لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءٌ وَ لاَ يَعُودَنَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A fasting man deliberately immersed himself in water; is making up that day upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Making it up is not upon him, but he must certainly not return to doing it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 275

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan at the beginning of the night, then delayed the ghusl until dawn rose.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and there is no making up upon him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَجْنَبَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ فَأَخَّرَ اَلْغُسْلَ حَتَّى طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لاَ قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan at the beginning of the night, then delayed the ghusl until dawn rose.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and there is no making up upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nawfali, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynabah, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, asking Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan from the beginning of the night, then delayed the ghusl until dawn rose.’ So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote to me in his own handwriting: “I know him with Musadif. He performs ghusl from his janabah, completes his fast, and there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ أَبِي زَيْنَبَةَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَجْنَبَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ فَأَخَّرَ اَلْغُسْلَ حَتَّى طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِلَيَّ بِخَطِّهِ» أَعْرِفُهُ مَعَ مُصَادِفٍ يَغْتَسِلُ مِنْ جَنَابَتِهِ وَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nawfali, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynabah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, asking Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan from the beginning of the night, then delayed the ghusl until dawn rose.’ So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote to me in his own handwriting: “I know him with Musadif. He performs ghusl from his janabah, completes his fast, and there is nothing upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Sa’ad ibn Ismail, from his father, from Ismail ibn Isa, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who was affected by janabah in the month of Ramadan, then slept until morning came; what is upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “This does not harm him, and he does not break his fast, for my father (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Aisha said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, woke in the morning while junub from intercourse, not from a wet dream.’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not break his fast, and he does not pay any attention to it.” (Narrator said) ‘And a man who was affected by janabah, then remained asleep until morning came; what is obligatory upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him; he performs ghusl.” (Narrator said) ‘And a man who was affected by janabah at the end of the night, so he rose to perform ghusl but did not find water, so he went to seek it, or sent someone to bring it to him, but it became difficult for him until morning came; how should he act?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He performs ghusl when it comes to him, then he prays.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَنَامَ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ» لاَ يَضُرُّهُ هَذَا وَ لاَ يُفْطِرُ فَإِنَّ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ »قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ أَصْبَحَ جُنُباً مِنْ جِمَاعٍ غَيْرِ اِحْتِلاَمٍ«« قَالَ» لاَ يُفْطِرُ وَلاَ يُبَالِي« وَ رَجُلٌ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فَبَقِيَ نَائِماً حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ» لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ يَغْتَسِلُ« وَ رَجُلٌ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ فَقَامَ لِيَغْتَسِلَ وَ لَمْ يُصِبْ مَاءً فَذَهَبَ يَطْلُبُهُ أَوْ بَعَثَ مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ فَعَسُرَ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ» يَغْتَسِلُ إِذَا جَاءَهُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Sa’ad ibn Ismail, from his father, from Ismail ibn Isa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who was affected by janabah in the month of Ramadan, then slept until morning came; what is upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “This does not harm him, and he does not break his fast, for my father (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Aisha said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, woke in the morning while junub from intercourse, not from a wet dream.’” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not break his fast, and he does not pay any attention to it.” (Narrator said) ‘And a man who was affected by janabah, then remained asleep until morning came; what is obligatory upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him; he performs ghusl.” (Narrator said) ‘And a man who was affected by janabah at the end of the night, so he rose to perform ghusl but did not find water, so he went to seek it, or sent someone to bring it to him, but it became difficult for him until morning came; how should he act?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He performs ghusl when it comes to him, then he prays.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who was affected by janabah in the middle of the night in (month of) Ramadan, then slept while he knew of it, and did not wake up until dawn reached him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him is that he completes his fast and makes up another day.” I (narrator) asked: “If that was from the man while he is making up (month of) Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him eat on that day of his, and let him make it up, for nothing from the months resembles (month of) Ramadan.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي جَوْفِ اَللَّيْلِ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَنَامَ وَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِهَا وَ لَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظْ حَتَّى يُدْرِكَهُ اَلْفَجْرُ فَقَالَ» عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِيَ يَوْماً آخَرَ« فَقُلْتُ إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ هُوَ يَقْضِي رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» فَلْيَأْكُلْ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ وَلْيَقْضِ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يُشْبِهُ رَمَضَانَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلشُّهُورِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who was affected by janabah in the middle of the night in (month of) Ramadan, then slept while he knew of it, and did not wake up until dawn reached him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him is that he completes his fast and makes up another day.” I (narrator) asked: “If that was from the man while he is making up (month of) Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him eat on that day of his, and let him make it up, for nothing from the months resembles (month of) Ramadan.”

chapter: Chapter on Expiation for Intentionally Breaking the Fast of a Day from the Month of Ramadan
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The man becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then wakes up, then sleeps until morning comes.” Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast and makes up another day. But if he did not wake up until morning came, he completes his day, and it is valid for him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُجْنِبُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ يَسْتَيْقِظُ ثُمَّ يَنَامُ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِي يَوْماً آخَرَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظْ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ أَتَمَّ يَوْمَهُ وَ جَازَ لَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The man becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then wakes up, then sleeps until morning comes.” Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast and makes up another day. But if he did not wake up until morning came, he completes his day, and it is valid for him.”
