chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from a man, from Safwan, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who left Baghdad intending to catch up with a man at the head of a mile, and he continued following him until he reached al-Nahrawan, and it is four farsakhs from Baghdad. Should he break the fast when he intends to return, and should he shorten (the prayer)?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He does not shorten (the prayer) and he does not break the fast, because he left his house while not intending to travel eight farsakhs. Rather, he left intending to catch up with his companion on part of the road, then the journey extended with him to the place that he reached. And if he had left his house intending al-Nahrawan, going and coming, then it would have been upon him to intend travel from the night, and to break the fast. But if he entered the morning and had not intended travel, then after he entered the morning travel occurred to him, he shortens and does not break his fast on that day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَلْحَقَ رَجُلاً عَلَى رَأْسِ مِيلٍ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَتْبَعُهُ حَتَّى بَلَغَ اَلنَّهْرَوَانَ وَ هِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ فَرَاسِخَ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ أَ يُفْطِرُ إِذَا أَرَادَ اَلرُّجُوعَ وَ يُقَصِّرُ فَقَالَ» لاَ يُقَصِّرُ وَ لاَ يُفْطِرُ لِأَنَّهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ وَ لَيْسَ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ ثَمَانِيَةَ فَرَاسِخَ وَ إِنَّمَا خَرَجَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَلْحَقَ صَاحِبَهُ فِي بَعْضِ اَلطَّرِيقِ فَتَمَادَى بِهِ اَلسَّيْرُ إِلَى اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي بَلَغَهُ وَ لَوْ أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ يُرِيدُ اَلنَّهْرَوَانَ ذَاهِباً وَ جَائِياً لَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَنْوِيَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ سَفَراً وَ اَلْإِفْطَارَ فَإِنْ هُوَ أَصْبَحَ وَ لَمْ يَنْوِ اَلسَّفَرَ فَبَدَا لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَصْبَحَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَصَّرَ وَ لَمْ يُفْطِرْ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from a man, from Safwan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who left Baghdad intending to catch up with a man at the head of a mile, and he continued following him until he reached al-Nahrawan, and it is four farsakhs from Baghdad. Should he break the fast when he intends to return, and should he shorten (the prayer)?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He does not shorten (the prayer) and he does not break the fast, because he left his house while not intending to travel eight farsakhs. Rather, he left intending to catch up with his companion on part of the road, then the journey extended with him to the place that he reached. And if he had left his house intending al-Nahrawan, going and coming, then it would have been upon him to intend travel from the night, and to break the fast. But if he entered the morning and had not intended travel, then after he entered the morning travel occurred to him, he shortens and does not break his fast on that day.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And that which Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said al-Madaini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who goes out for a need of his while he does not intend travel, then he proceeds in that and the proceeding extends with him until he proceeds eight farsakhs. What should he do regarding his prayer?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He shortens (the prayer) and does not complete the prayer until he returns to his house.”
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ فِي حَاجَةٍ لَهُ وَ هُوَ لاَ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فَيَمْضِي فِي ذَلِكَ وَيَتَمَادَى بِهِ اَلْمُضِيُّ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ بِهِ ثَمَانِيَةَ فَرَاسِخَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ» يُقَصِّرُ وَ لاَ يُتِمُّ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And that which Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Said al-Madaini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

What should he do regarding his prayer?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He shortens (the prayer) and does not complete the prayer until he returns to his house.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
The jurist, Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Shortening the prayer is required at the distance of two barids, which is twenty-four miles, or at the distance of one barid when going and returning. One barid is six miles, and that is two farsakhs. Therefore, shortening the prayer applies at four farsakhs. So when a man leaves his house intending to travel twelve miles, which is four farsakhs, and he reaches two farsakhs while still intending to return another two farsakhs, he shortens his prayer. But if he turns back from his original intention when he reaches two farsakhs, and wishes to remain there, then he must perform the prayer in full. And if he had already shortened his prayer, then turned back from his intention, he must repeat the prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ اَلْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: »اَلتَّقْصِيرُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ بَرِيدَانِ أَوْ بَرِيدٌ ذَاهِباً وَ جَائِياً وَاَلْبَرِيدُ سِتَّةُ أَمْيَالٍ وَ هُوَ فَرْسَخَانِ فَالتَّقْصِيرُ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ فَرَاسِخَ فَإِذَا خَرَجَ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ يُرِيدُ اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ مِيلاً وَ ذَلِكَ أَرْبَعَةُ فَرَاسِخَ ثُمَّ بَلَغَ فَرْسَخَيْنِ وَ نِيَّتُهُ اَلرُّجُوعُ أَوْ فَرْسَخَيْنِ آخَرَيْنِ قَصَّرَ وَ إِنْ رَجَعَ عَمَّا نَوَى عِنْدَمَا بَلَغَ فَرْسَخَيْنِ وَ أَرَادَ اَلْمُقَامَ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلتَّمَامُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَصَّرَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ عَنْ نِيَّتِهِ أَعَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The jurist, Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Shortening the prayer is required at the distance of two barids, which is twenty-four miles, or at the distance of one barid when going and returning. One barid is six miles, and that is two farsakhs. Therefore, shortening the prayer applies at four farsakhs. So when a man leaves his house intending to travel twelve miles, which is four farsakhs, and he reaches two farsakhs while still intending to return another two farsakhs, he shortens his prayer. But if he turns back from his original intention when he reaches two farsakhs, and wishes to remain there, then he must perform the prayer in full. And if he had already shortened his prayer, then turned back from his intention, he must repeat the prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who goes out on a journey that he intends, then the time enters upon him while he has gone out from the village by two farsakhs, so they prayed and departed, then some of them turned back for a need, and going out was not decreed for him. What should he do regarding the prayer that he had prayed as two rakahs?’ Imam (a.s) said: “His prayer is complete, and he does not repeat it.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ فِي سَفَرٍ يُرِيدُهُ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْوَقْتُ وَ قَدْ خَرَجَ مِنَ اَلْقَرْيَةِ عَلَى فَرْسَخَيْنِ فَصَلَّوْا وَاِنْصَرَفُوا فَانْصَرَفَ بَعْضُهُمْ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَلَمْ يُقْضَ لَهُ اَلْخُرُوجُ مَا يَصْنَعُ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلَّتِي كَانَ صَلاَّهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ» تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who goes out on a journey that he intends, then the time enters upon him while he has gone out from the village by two farsakhs, so they prayed and departed, then some of them turned back for a need, and going out was not decreed for him. What should he do regarding the prayer that he had prayed as two rakahs?’ Imam (a.s) said: “His prayer is complete, and he does not repeat it.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When a man resolves to stay for ten (days), then he must complete the prayer. But if he is in doubt, not knowing how long he will stay, and he says, ‘Today or tomorrow,’ then let him shorten between that and a month. Then if he stays in that town for more than a month, let him complete the prayer.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: »إِذَا عَزَمَ اَلرَّجُلُ أَنْ يُقِيمَ عَشْراً فَعَلَيْهِ إِتْمَامُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِي شَكٍّ لاَ يَدْرِي مَا يُقِيمُ فَيَقُولُ اَلْيَوْمَ أَوْ غَداً فَلْيُقَصِّرْ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ شَهْرٍ فَإِنْ أَقَامَ بِذَلِكَ اَلْبَلَدِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ شَهْرٍ فَلْيُتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ«
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When a man resolves to stay for ten (days), then he must complete the prayer. But if he is in doubt, not knowing how long he will stay, and he says, ‘Today or tomorrow,’ then let him shorten between that and a month. Then if he stays in that town for more than a month, let him complete the prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Sulayman ibn Jafar al-Jafari, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who intends to travel in the month of Ramadan, then leaves his family (home) after he has entered the morning.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he entered the morning among his family, then fasting that day has become obligatory upon him, unless he travels by night, a night journey (daljah).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشْيَمَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلْجَعْفَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْوِي اَلسَّفَرَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ بَعْدَ مَا يُصْبِحُ قَالَ» إِذَا أَصْبَحَ فِي أَهْلِهِ فَقَدْ وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُدْلِجَ دَلْجَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Sulayman ibn Jafar al-Jafari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who intends to travel in the month of Ramadan, then leaves his family (home) after he has entered the morning.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he entered the morning among his family, then fasting that day has become obligatory upon him, unless he travels by night, a night journey (daljah).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man to whom travel presents itself in the month of Ramadan until he enters the morning.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast on that day.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Then he comes forward in the month of Ramadan, and there is not between him and his family except the morning part of the day.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When dawn rises while he is outside, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks the fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَعْرِضُ لَهُ اَلسَّفَرُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ« قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ أَقْبَلَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ أَهْلِهِ إِلاَّ ضَحْوَةٌ مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ قَالَ فَقَالَ» إِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ هُوَ خَارِجٌ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ صَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَفْطَرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man to whom travel presents itself in the month of Ramadan until he enters the morning.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast on that day.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Then he comes forward in the month of Ramadan, and there is not between him and his family except the morning part of the day.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When dawn rises while he is outside, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks the fast.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who travels in the month of Ramadan: should he break the fast in his house?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he had spoken to himself at night about travelling, he breaks the fast when he leaves his house. But if he had not spoken to himself from the night, then travel occurred to him during his day, he completes his fast.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُسَافِرُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَ يُفْطِرُ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ قَالَ» إِذَا حَدَّثَ نَفْسَهُ بِاللَّيْلِ بِالسَّفَرِ أَفْطَرَ إِذَا خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُحَدِّثْ نَفْسَهُ مِنَ اَللَّيْلَةِ ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ أَتَمَّ صَوْمَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who travels in the month of Ramadan: should he break the fast in his house?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he had spoken to himself at night about travelling, he breaks the fast when he leaves his house. But if he had not spoken to himself from the night, then travel occurred to him during his day, he completes his fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Basir:
(Abu Basir) said: “If you leave after the rising of dawn and did not intend travel from the night, then complete the fast and count it as part of the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ:» إِذَا خَرَجْتَ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ لَمْ تَنْوِ اَلسَّفَرَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ فَأَتِمَّ اَلصَّوْمَ وَاِعْتَدَّ بِهِ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Basir:
thaqalaynMatn: (Abu Basir) said: “If you leave after the rising of dawn and did not intend travel from the night, then complete the fast and count it as part of the month of Ramadan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 297

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And that which Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who leaves his house while intending travel and while he is fasting.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he leaves before the day reaches its midpoint, then let him break the fast and make up that day. But if he leaves after midday, then let him complete his day.”
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ قَالَ» إِنْ خَرَجَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْتَصِفَ اَلنَّهَارُ فَلْيُفْطِرْ وَ لْيَقْضِ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ فَلْيُتِمَّ يَوْمَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And that which Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who leaves his house while intending travel and while he is fasting.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he leaves before the day reaches its midpoint, then let him break the fast and make up that day. But if he leaves after midday, then let him complete his day.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “When a man travels in the month of Ramadan and leaves after half of the day, then he must fast that day and count it as part of the month of Ramadan. Then, when he enters a town before the rising of dawn while intending to stay in it, then he must fast that day. But if he enters after the rising of dawn, then there is no fast upon him, though if he wishes, he may fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا سَافَرَ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَخَرَجَ بَعْدَ نِصْفِ اَلنَّهَارِ فَعَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ يَعْتَدُّ بِهِ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَإِذَا دَخَلَ إِلَى بَلَدٍ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ هُوَ يُرِيدُ اَلْإِقَامَةَ بِهَا فَعَلَيْهِ صَوْمُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ فَإِنْ دَخَلَ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَلاَ صِيَامَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ صَامَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When a man travels in the month of Ramadan and leaves after half of the day, then he must fast that day and count it as part of the month of Ramadan. Then, when he enters a town before the rising of dawn while intending to stay in it, then he must fast that day. But if he enters after the rising of dawn, then there is no fast upon him, though if he wishes, he may fast.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Samaah and Ibn Muskan, from a man, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “When you intend to travel in the month of Ramadan and you intend to leave from the night, then if you leave before dawn or after it, you are one who breaks the fast, and you must make up that day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ وَ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» إِذَا أَرَدْتَ اَلسَّفَرَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَنَوَيْتَ اَلْخُرُوجَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ فَإِنْ خَرَجْتَ قَبْلَ اَلْفَجْرِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ فَأَنْتَ مُفْطِرٌ وَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Samaah and Ibn Muskan, from a man, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “When you intend to travel in the month of Ramadan and you intend to leave from the night, then if you leave before dawn or after it, you are one who breaks the fast, and you must make up that day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 297

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Jafar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Ala, the client of the family of Sa’m:
(He was asked) regarding ‘a man who intends to travel in the month of Ramadan.’ He said: “He breaks the fast, even if he leaves shortly before the sun disappears.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْأَعْلَى مَوْلَى آلِ سَامٍ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» يُفْطِرُ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ اَلشَّمْسُ بِقَلِيلٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Jafar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Ala, the client of the family of Sa’m:
thaqalaynMatn: (He was asked) regarding ‘a man who intends to travel in the month of Ramadan.’ He said: “He breaks the fast, even if he leaves shortly before the sun disappears.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 298

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘shortening (the prayer).’ Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in the place in which you hear the call to prayer, then complete, and when you are in the place in which you do not hear the call to prayer, then shorten. And when you arrive from a journey, then it is like that.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَ انَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلتَّقْصِيرِ قَالَ» إِذَا كُنْتَ فِي اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي تَسْمَعُ فِيهِ اَلْأَذَانَ فَأَتِمَّ وَ إِذَا كُنْتَ فِي اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي لاَ تَسْمَعُ فِيهِ اَلْأَذَانَ فَقَصِّرْ وَ إِذَا قَدِمْتَ مِنْ سَفَرٍ فَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘shortening (the prayer).’ Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in the place in which you hear the call to prayer, then complete, and when you are in the place in which you do not hear the call to prayer, then shorten. And when you arrive from a journey, then it is like that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 298

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man intends to travel; when does he shorten (the prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he disappears from the houses.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘A man intends to travel, then he leaves when the sun declines.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When you leave, pray two rakahs.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ مَتَى يُقَصِّرُ قَالَ» إِذَا تَوَارَى مِنَ اَلْبُيُوتِ «قَالَ قُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلُ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فَيَخْرُجُ حِينَ تَزُولُ اَلشَّمْسُ قَالَ» إِذَا خَرَجْتَ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ«
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man intends to travel; when does he shorten (the prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he disappears from the houses.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘A man intends to travel, then he leaves when the sun declines.’” Imam (a.s) said: “When you leave, pray two rakahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 298

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘fasting while travelling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no fasting while travelling. Some people fasted during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, so the Prophet (saws) named them the ‘disobedient ones’. Thus there is no fasting while travelling except the three days which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, mentioned regarding the Hajj.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصِّيَامِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ» لاَ صِيَامَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَدْ صَامَ أُنَاسٌ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَسَمَّاهُمُ اَلْعُصَاةَ فَلاَ صِيَامَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ إِلاَّ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلْأَيَّامِ اَلَّتِي قَالَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي اَلْحَجِّ.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘fasting while travelling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no fasting while travelling. Some people fasted during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, so the Prophet (saws) named them the ‘disobedient ones’. Thus there is no fasting while travelling except the three days which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, mentioned regarding the Hajj.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 299

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:
I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who missed the fast of the three days during Hajj.’ He said: “Whoever misses the fasting of three days during Hajj, so long as he did not intentionally abandon it, then he fasts in Makkah as long as he has not left it. But if his camel-driver (jammal) refuses to stay for him, then let him fast on the road.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْجَهْمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ فَاتَهُ صَوْمُ اَلثَّلاَثَةِ اَلْأَيَّامِ فِي اَلْحَجِّ قَالَ» مَنْ فَاتَهُ صِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي اَلْحَجِّ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَمْداً تَارِكاً فَإِنَّهُ يَصُومُ بِمَكَّةَ مَا لَمْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنْ أَبَى جَمَّالُهُ أَنْ يُقِيمَ عَلَيْهِ فَلْيَصُمْ فِي اَلطَّرِيقِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked him about ‘a man who missed the fast of the three days during Hajj.’ He said: “Whoever misses the fasting of three days during Hajj, so long as he did not intentionally abandon it, then he fasts in Makkah as long as he has not left it. But if his camel-driver (jammal) refuses to stay for him, then let him fast on the road.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 299

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man performing tamattu (mutamatti) who did not have a sacrificial offering (hady) with him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts three days: one day before al-Tarwiyah, the Day of al-Tarwiyah, and the Day of Arafah.” He (narrator) said: “So I said to Imam (a.s), ‘When the Day of al-Tarwiyah enters, and it is not proper for him to fast in Mina during the days of al-Tashriq.’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then when he returns to Makkah, he fasts.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘But if his companions hasten him and refuse to stay in Makkah?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him fast on the road.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Then he fasts while travelling?’” Imam (a.s) said: “That is it; he fasts on the Day of Arafah, and the people of Arafah are travelling.”

thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated that from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Whoever did not fast the three days during Hajj until the crescent (al-hilal) was sighted for him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Upon him is a blood-sacrifice which he pours forth, and there is no fasting upon him.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَنْ لَمْ يَصُمِ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلْأَيَّامِ فِي اَلْحَجِّ حَتَّى يُهَلَّ عَلَيْهِ اَلْهِلاَلُ فَقَالَ» عَلَيْهِ دَمٌ يُهَرِيقُهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ صِيَامٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated that from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Alaa ibn Razin al-Qalla, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘zihar’ concerning a free woman and a female slave.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” He (narrator) said: “Then if he performs zihar in Shaban and does not find anything with which to free a slave?” – meaning as expiation for this sin. Imam (a.s) said: “He waits until he fasts (month of) Ramadan, then he fasts two consecutive months. And if he performs zihar while he is travelling, he breaks the fast until he arrives. And if he fasts, then comes upon wealth that he owns, then let him make up that which he began.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ اَلْقَلاَّءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلظِّهَارِ عَنِ اَلْحُرَّةِ وَ اَلْأَمَةِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قَالَ فَإِنْ ظَاهَرَ فِي شَعْبَانَ وَ لَمْ يَجِدْ مَا يُعْتِقُ قَالَ» يَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى يَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ يَصُومُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ إِنْ ظَاهَرَ وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ أَفْطَرَ حَتَّى يَقْدَمَ وَ إِنْ صَامَ فَأَصَابَ مَا لاً يَمْلِكُ فَلْيَقْضِ اَلَّذِي اِبْتَدَأَ فِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Alaa ibn Razin al-Qalla, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about ‘zihar’ concerning a free woman and a female slave.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” He (narrator) said: “Then if he performs zihar in Shaban and does not find anything with which to free a slave?” – meaning as expiation for this sin. Imam (a.s) said: “He waits until he fasts (month of) Ramadan, then he fasts two consecutive months. And if he performs zihar while he is travelling, he breaks the fast until he arrives. And if he fasts, then comes upon wealth that he owns, then let him make up that which he began.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Imam (a.s) said: “If you stay in al-Madinah for three days, then fast on the first day, Wednesday, and pray on the night of Wednesday at the column of Abu Lubabah. It is the Column of Repentance (Ustuwanah al-Tawbah), to which he tied himself until his pardon was sent down from heaven. Remain by it on Wednesday. Then, on the following night, the night of Thursday, go to the place beside the station of the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and remain there for your night and your day. Fast on Thursday. Then, on the night of Friday, go to the column that is beside the station of the blessed Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and his prayer-place. Pray beside it throughout your night and your day, and fast on Friday. If you are able, during these days, not to speak about anything except what is necessary for you, not to leave the mosque except for a need, and not to sleep by night or by day, then do so, for that is among the things in which merit is counted. Then, on Friday, praise Allah (swt), extol Him (swt), send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and ask for your need. Let the following be among what you say: ‘O almighty Allah (swt), whatever need I have with You (swt), whether I have begun to seek it and request it or have not begun, whether I have asked You (swt) for it or have not asked You (swt) for it, I turn to You (swt) through Your Prophet Muhammad (saws), the Prophet of Mercy, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, for the fulfilment of my needs, the small of them and the great.’ For it is fitting that your need will be fulfilled, if Allah (swt), Exalted is He (swt), wills.”
arabicText: مُوسَى بْنُ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِنْ كَانَ لَكَ مُقَامٌ بِالْمَدِينَةِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ صُمْتَ أَوَّلَ يَوْمٍ اَلْأَرْبِعَاءَ وَ تُصَلِّي لَيْلَةَ اَلْأَرْبِعَاءِ عِنْدَ أُسْطُوَانَةِ أَبِي لُبَابَةَ وَ هِيَ أُسْطُوَانَةُ اَلتَّوْبَةِ اَلَّتِي كَانَ رَبَطَ إِلَيْهَا نَفْسَهُ حَتَّى نَزَلَ عُذْرُهُ مِنَ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ تَقْعُدُ عِنْدَهَا يَوْمَ اَلْأَرْبِعَاءِ ثُمَّ تَأْتِي لَيْلَةَ اَلْخَمِيسِ اَلَّتِي تَلِيهَا مِمَّا يَلِي مَقَامَ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ لَيْلَتَكَ وَ يَوْمَكَ وَ تَصُومُ يَوْمَ اَلْخَمِيسِ ثُمَّ تَأْتِي اَلْأُسْطُوَانَةَ اَلَّتِي تَلِي مَقَامَ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَمُصَلاَّهُ لَيْلَةَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَتُصَلِّي عِنْدَهَا لَيْلَتَكَ وَ يَوْمَكَ وَ تَصُومُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَتَكَلَّمَ بِشَيْءٍ فِي هَذِهِ اَلْأَيَّامِ إِلاَّ مَالاَ بُدَّلَكَ مِنْهُ وَ لاَ تَخْرُجَ مِنَ اَلْمَسْجِدِ إِلاَّ لِحَاجَةٍ وَ لاَ تَنَامَ فِي لَيْلٍ وَ لاَ نَهَارٍ فَافْعَلْ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يُعَدُّ فِيهِ اَلْفَضْلُ ثُمَّ اِحْمَدِ اَللَّهَ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ أَثْنِ عَلَيْهِ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ سَلْ حَاجَتَكَ وَلْيَكُنْ فِيمَا تَقُولُ اَللَّهُمَّ مَا كَانَتْ لِي إِلَيْكَ مِنْ حَاجَةٍ شَرَعْتُ أَنَا فِي طَلَبِهَا وَاِلْتِمَاسِهَا أَوْ لَمْ أَشْرَعْ سَأَلْتُكَهَا أَوْ لَمْ أَسْأَلْكَهَا فَإِنِّي أَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْكَ بِنَبِيِّكَ مُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيِّ اَلرَّحْمَةِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي قَضَاءِ حَوَائِجِي صَغِيرِهَا وَكَبِيرِهَا فَإِنَّكَ حَرِيٌّ أَنْ تُقْضَى حَاجَتُكَ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى«.
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If you stay in al-Madinah for three days, then fast on the first day, Wednesday, and pray on the night of Wednesday at the column of Abu Lubabah. It is the Column of Repentance (Ustuwanah al-Tawbah), to which he tied himself until his pardon was sent down from heaven. Remain by it on Wednesday. Then, on the following night, the night of Thursday, go to the place beside the station of the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and remain there for your night and your day. Fast on Thursday. Then, on the night of Friday, go to the column that is beside the station of the blessed Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and his prayer-place. Pray beside it throughout your night and your day, and fast on Friday. If you are able, during these days, not to speak about anything except what is necessary for you, not to leave the mosque except for a need, and not to sleep by night or by day, then do so, for that is among the things in which merit is counted. Then, on Friday, praise Allah (swt), extol Him (swt), send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and ask for your need. Let the following be among what you say: ‘O almighty Allah (swt), whatever need I have with You (swt), whether I have begun to seek it and request it or have not begun, whether I have asked You (swt) for it or have not asked You (swt) for it, I turn to You (swt) through Your Prophet Muhammad (saws), the Prophet of Mercy, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, for the fulfilment of my needs, the small of them and the great.’ For it is fitting that your need will be fulfilled, if Allah (swt), Exalted is He (swt), wills.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Karam, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have made it binding upon myself that I fast until the Qa’im (ajf), may Allah (swt) hasten his relief, rises.” Imam (a.s) said: “Fast, but do not fast while travelling, nor on the two Eids, nor on the days of tashriq (ayyam al-tashriq), nor on the day concerning which there is doubt whether it is from the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: محمد بن يعقوب عن علي بن إبراهيم عن أبيه عن ابن ابي عمير عن كرام قال: قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام اني جعلت على نفسي ان اصوم حتى يقوم القائم عجل الله فرجه فقال: صم ولا تصم في السفر ولا العيدين ولا ايام التشريق ولا اليوم الذي يشك فيه من شهر رمضان
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Karam, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have made it binding upon myself that I fast until the Qa’im (ajf), may Allah (swt) hasten his relief, rises.” Imam (a.s) said: “Fast, but do not fast while travelling, nor on the two Eids, nor on the days of tashriq (ayyam al-tashriq), nor on the day concerning which there is doubt whether it is from the month of Ramadan.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what also indicates it is what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who made it binding upon himself to fast a month in al-Kufah, a month in al-Madinah, and a month in Makkah because of an affliction with which he was afflicted. Then it was decreed for him that he fasted a month in al-Kufah and entered al-Madinah, where he fasted eighteen days, but the camel-driver (al-jammal) did not stay for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts what remains upon him when he reaches his town.”
arabicText: وَ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ أَيْضاً مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ جَعَلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ صَوْمَ شَهْرٍ بِالْكُوفَةِ وَ شَهْرٍ بِالْمَدِينَةِ وَ شَهْرٍ بِمَكَّةَ مِنْ بَلاَءٍ اُبْتُلِيَ بِهِ فَقُضِيَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ صَامَ بِالْكُوفَةِ شَهْراً وَ دَخَلَ إِلَى اَلْمَدِينَةِ فَصَامَ بِهَا ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً وَ لَمْ يُقِمْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْجَمَّالُ فَقَالَ» يَصُومُ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا اِنْتَهَى إِلَى بَلَدِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And what also indicates it is what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who made it binding upon himself to fast a month in al-Kufah, a month in al-Madinah, and a month in Makkah because of an affliction with which he was afflicted. Then it was decreed for him that he fasted a month in al-Kufah and entered al-Madinah, where he fasted eighteen days, but the camel-driver (al-jammal) did not stay for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts what remains upon him when he reaches his town.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And also what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasts a fast which he has appointed upon himself, or fasts the sacred months, then a month and two months pass by him without him making it up.’ He (narrator) said: “So Imam (a.s) said, ‘He does not fast while travelling, and he does not make up anything from voluntary fasting except the three days which he used to fast in every month. And he should not make it like the obligatory, except that I love for you to continue upon righteous action.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the one responsible for the sacred months which he used to fast, it suffices him to fast, in place of each month from the sacred months, three days.”
arabicText: وَ أَيْضاً مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَصُومُ صَوْماً وَ قَدْ وَقَّتَهُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَوْ يَصُومُ أَشْهُرَ اَلْحُرُمِ فَيَمُرُّ بِهِ اَلشَّهْرُ وَاَلشَّهْرَ انِ لاَ يَقْضِيهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ» لاَ يَصُومُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَلاَ يَقْضِي شَيْئاً مِنْ صَوْمِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ إِلاَّ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلْأَيَّامِ اَلَّتِي كَانَ يَصُومُهَا فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ وَ لاَ يَجْعَلْهَا بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلْوَاجِبِ إِلاَّ أَنِّي أُحِبُّ لَكَ أَنْ تَدُومَ عَلَى اَلْعَمَلِ اَلصَّالِحِ« قَالَ »وَ صَاحِبُ اَلْحُرُمِ اَلَّتِي كَانَ يَصُومُهَا يُجْزِيهِ أَنْ يَصُومَ مَكَانَ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مِنْ أَشْهُرِ اَلْحُرُمِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And also what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasts a fast which he has appointed upon himself, or fasts the sacred months, then a month and two months pass by him without him making it up.’ He (narrator) said: “So Imam (a.s) said, ‘He does not fast while travelling, and he does not make up anything from voluntary fasting except the three days which he used to fast in every month. And he should not make it like the obligatory, except that I love for you to continue upon righteous action.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the one responsible for the sacred months which he used to fast, it suffices him to fast, in place of each month from the sacred months, three days.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Qasim ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Sayqal, who said:
He (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “O my master, a man vowed to fast every Friday, continuously, for as long as he remains, then that day coincided with the day of Eid al-Fitr, or Eid al-Adha, or the days of al-Tashriq, or he travelled, or he became ill. Is the fasting of that day upon him, or making it up, or what should he do, O my master?” Imam (a.s) wrote to him: “Allah (swt) has removed fasting from you in all of these days, and you fast one day in place of a day, if Allah (swt), Exalted is He (swt), wills.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْقَاسِمِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ يَا سَيِّدِي رَجُلٌ نَذَرَ أَنْ يَصُومَ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ دَائِماً مَا بَقِيَ فَوَافَقَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمُ يَوْمَ عِيدِ فِطْرٍ أَوْ أَضْحًى أَوْ أَيَّامَ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ أَوْ سَفَرَ أَوْ مَرِضَ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ أَوْ قَضَاؤُهُ أَوْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ يَا سَيِّدِي فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ» قَدْ وَضَعَ اَللَّهُ عَنْكَ اَلصِّيَامَ فِي هَذِهِ اَلْأَيَّامِ كُلِّهَا وَتَصُومُ يَوْماً بَدَلَ يَوْمٍ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Qasim ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Sayqal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “O my master, a man vowed to fast every Friday, continuously, for as long as he remains, then that day coincided with the day of Eid al-Fitr, or Eid al-Adha, or the days of al-Tashriq, or he travelled, or he became ill. chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what also indicates it is what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Jafar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “My mother had made a vow upon herself that, if Allah (swt) returned to her one of her children from something she feared for him, she would fast that day on which he arrived, for as long as she remained. Then she went out with us, travelling to Makkah, and it became unclear to us because of the vow: should she fast or break the fast?” Imam (a.s) said: “She should not fast. Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has removed His (swt) right from her, and she fasts what she made binding upon herself.” I (narrator) said: “Then what do you see, when she returns to the house, should she make it up?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Then should she leave that?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, for I fear that she may see, concerning the matter for which she made the vow, something she dislikes.”
arabicText: وَ يَدُلُّ أَيْضاً عَلَيْهِ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ أُمِّي كَانَتْ جَعَلَتْ عَلَيْهَا نَذْراً إِنِ اَللَّهُ رَدَّ عَلَيْهَا بَعْضَ وُلْدِهَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ كَانَتْ تَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ تَصُومَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ اَلَّذِي يَقْدَمُ فِيهِ مَا بَقِيَتْ فَخَرَجَتْ مَعَنَا مُسَافِرَةً إِلَى مَكَّةَ فَأَشْكَلَ عَلَيْنَا لِمَكَانِ اَلنَّذْرِ أَ تَصُومُ أَمْ تُفْطِرُ فَقَالَ» لاَ تَصُومُ وَضَعَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَنْهَا حَقَّهُ وَ تَصُومُ هِيَ مَا جَعَلَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا« قُلْتُ فَمَا تَرَى إِذَا هِيَ رَجَعَتْ إِلَى اَلْمَنْزِلِ أَتَقْضِيهِ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ أَفَتَتْرُكُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ» لاَ لِأَنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ تَرَى فِي اَلَّذِي نَذَرَتْ فِيهِ مَا تَكْرَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And what also indicates it is what Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Jafar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “My mother had made a vow upon herself that, if Allah (swt) returned to her one of her children from something she feared for him, she would fast that day on which he arrived, for as long as she remained. Then she went out with us, travelling to Makkah, and it became unclear to us because of the vow: should she fast or break the fast?” Imam (a.s) said: “She should not fast. Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has removed His (swt) right from her, and she fasts what she made binding upon herself.” I (narrator) said: “Then what do you see, when she returns to the house, should she make it up?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Then should she leave that?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, for I fear that she may see, concerning the matter for which she made the vow, something she dislikes.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sabbah, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who makes a fast of a specified day binding upon himself for Allah (swt).’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts it always, while present and while travelling.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَجْعَلُ لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمَ يَوْمٍ مُسَمًّى قَالَ» يَصُومُهُ أَبَداً فِي اَلْحَضَرِ وَ اَلسَّفَرِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sabbah, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who makes a fast of a specified day binding upon himself for Allah (swt).’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts it always, while present and while travelling.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
Bundar, the client of Idris, wrote: “O my master, I vowed to fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation becomes binding upon me?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote, and I (narrator) read it: “Do not abandon it except due to an illness, and fasting it is not upon you while travelling nor in illness, unless you had intended that. So if you have broken the fast from it without an illness, then give charity, for each day, to seven poor persons. We ask Allah (swt) for success in what He (swt) loves and is pleased with.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: كَتَبَ بُنْدَارُ مَوْلَى إِدْرِيسَ يَا سَيِّدِي نَذَرْتُ أَنْ أَصُومَ كُلَّ يَوْمِ سَبْتٍ فَإِنْ أَنَا لَمْ أَصُمْهُ مَا يَلْزَمُنِي مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» وَ قَرَأْتُهُ لاَ تَتْرُكْهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ عِلَّةٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ صَوْمُهُ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ مَرَضٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ نَوَيْتَ ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ أَفْطَرْتَ مِنْهُ فِي غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فَتَصَدَّقْ بِقَدْرِ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ مَسَاكِينَ نَسْأَلُ اَللَّهَ اَلتَّوْفِيقَ لِمَا يُحِبُّ وَيَرْضَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Bundar, the client of Idris, wrote: “O my master, I vowed to fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation becomes binding upon me?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote, and I (narrator) read it: “Do not abandon it except due to an illness, and fasting it is not upon you while travelling nor in illness, unless you had intended that. So if you have broken the fast from it without an illness, then give charity, for each day, to seven poor persons. We ask Allah (swt) for success in what He (swt) loves and is pleased with.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘fasting in Makkah and al-Madinah while we are travelling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “An obligation?” So I (narrator) asked: “No, but rather it is voluntary, just as prayer is performed voluntarily.” Imam (a.s) said: “You say, ‘Today and tomorrow’?” I (narrator) asked: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not fast.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَ عَنِ اَلصِّيَامِ بِمَكَّةَ وَ اَلْمَدِينَةِ وَ نَحْنُ فِي سَفَرٍ قَالَ »فَرِيضَةٌ« فَقُلْتُ لاَ وَ لَكِنَّهُ تَطَوُّعٌ كَمَا يُتَطَوَّعُ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ» تَقُولُ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ غَداً« قُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ» لاَ تَصُمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘fasting in Makkah and al-Madinah while we are travelling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “An obligation?” So I (narrator) asked: “No, but rather it is voluntary, just as prayer is performed voluntarily.” Imam (a.s) said: “You say, ‘Today and tomorrow’?” I (narrator) asked: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not fast.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, would not fast while travelling, neither in the month of Ramadan nor in other than it. And the Day of Badr was in the month of Ramadan, and the Conquest was in the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ يَصُومُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ لاَ غَيْرِهِ وَ كَانَ يَوْمُ بَدْرٍ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ كَانَ اَلْفَتْحُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, would not fast while travelling, neither in the month of Ramadan nor in other than it. And the Day of Badr was in the month of Ramadan, and the Conquest was in the month of Ramadan.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Rafi, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Abu Abdillah (a.s) left Madinah during days remaining from Shaban, and he was fasting. Then the month of Ramadan entered upon the Imam (a.s) while he was travelling, so the Imam (a.s) broke the fast. It was said to Imam (a.s): “Do you fast Shaban and break the fast in the month of Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Shaban is up to me; if I wish, I fast it, and if I wish, I do not. But the month of Ramadan is a firm obligation from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, to break the fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ رَافِعٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ: خَرَجَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع مِنَ اَلْمَدِينَةِ فِي أَيَّامٍ بَقِينَ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ فَكَانَ يَصُومُ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَأَفْطَرَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ أَ تَصُومُ شَعْبَانَ وَ تُفْطِرُ شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ شَعْبَانُ إِلَيَّ إِنْ شِئْتُ صُمْتُهُ وَإِنْ شِئْتُ لاَ وَشَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ عَزْمٌ مِنَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ عَلَى اَلْإِفْطَارِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Rafi, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) left Madinah during days remaining from Shaban, and he was fasting. Then the month of Ramadan entered upon the Imam (a.s) while he was travelling, so the Imam (a.s) broke the fast. It was said to Imam (a.s): “Do you fast Shaban and break the fast in the month of Ramadan?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Shaban is up to me; if I wish, I fast it, and if I wish, I do not. But the month of Ramadan is a firm obligation from Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, to break the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 305

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Traveller and the Sick Person Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Bilal, from al-Hasan ibn Bassam al-Jammal, from a man, who said:
I (narrator) was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, between Makkah and al-Madinah in Shaban, while Imam (a.s) was fasting. Then we saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, so Imam (a.s) broke the fast. I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I be made your ransom, yesterday was from Shaban and you were fasting, and today is from the month of Ramadan and you are breaking the fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, that is voluntary, and we may do whatever we wish, but this is obligatory, so we may not do except what we have been commanded.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ بِلاَلٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ بَسَّامٍ اَلْجَمَّالِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَالَ: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِيمَا بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ وَاَلْمَدِينَةِ فِي شَعْبَانَ وَهُوَ صَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَأَيْنَا هِلاَلَ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَأَفْطَرَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَمْسِ كَانَ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ وَ أَنْتَ صَائِمٌ وَ اَلْيَوْمُ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ أَنْتَ مُفْطِرٌ فَقَالَ» إِنَّ ذَاكَ تَطَوُّعٌ وَ لَنَا أَنْ نَفْعَلَ مَا شِئْنَا وَ هَذَا فَرْضٌ فَلَيْسَ لَنَا أَنْ نَفْعَلَ إِلاَّ مَا أُمِرْنَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Bilal, from al-Hasan ibn Bassam al-Jammal, from a man, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, between Makkah and al-Madinah in Shaban, while Imam (a.s) was fasting. Then we saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, so Imam (a.s) broke the fast. I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “May I be made your ransom, yesterday was from Shaban and you were fasting, and today is from the month of Ramadan and you are breaking the fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, that is voluntary, and we may do whatever we wish, but this is obligatory, so we may not do except what we have been commanded.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘an elderly man who is too weak to fast the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He gives in charity what suffices on his behalf: the food of one poor person for each day (of missed fast).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَبِيرٍ يَضْعُفُ عَنْ صَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» يَتَصَدَّقُ بِمَا يُجْزِي عَنْهُ طَعَامِ مِسْكِينٍ لِكُلِّ يَوْمٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘an elderly man who is too weak to fast the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He gives in charity what suffices on his behalf: the food of one poor person for each day (of missed fast).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 307

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, “(And upon those who are able to bear it) compensation can be made by feeding a needy person (for every day not fasted),” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:184) Imam (a.s) said: “The elderly man and the one who is afflicted by excessive thirst (al-utash).” And regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Exalted is He (swt): “But if he is unable (to fast), then let him feed sixty poor people,” (Surah Al-Mujadilah 58:4) Imam (a.s) said: “Due to illness or excessive thirst (utash).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ» وَ عَلَى اَلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعٰامُ مِسْكِينٍ« قَالَ» اَلشَّيْخُ اَلْكَبِيرُ وَ اَلَّذِي يَأْخُذُهُ اَلْعُطَاشُ« وَ عَنْ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى» فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإِطْعٰامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً« قَالَ» مِنْ مَرَضٍ أَوْ عُطَاشٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, “(And upon those who are able to bear it) compensation can be made by feeding a needy person (for every day not fasted),” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:184) Imam (a.s) said: “The elderly man and the one who is afflicted by excessive thirst (al-utash).” And regarding the saying of Allah (swt), Exalted is He (swt): “But if he is unable (to fast), then let him feed sixty poor people,” (Surah Al-Mujadilah 58:4) Imam (a.s) said: “Due to illness or excessive thirst (utash).”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the elderly man and the elderly woman who are too weak to fast in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “She gives in charity, on behalf of each day, a mudd of wheat.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلشَّيْخِ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَاَلْعَجُوزِ اَلْكَبِيرَةِ اَلَّتِي تَضْعُفُ عَنِ اَلصَّوْمِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» تَتَصَدَّقُ عَنْ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ بِمُدٍّ مِنْ حِنْطَةٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the elderly man and the elderly woman who are too weak to fast in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “She gives in charity, on behalf of each day, a mudd of wheat.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The elderly man and the one who has excessive thirst (al-utash), there is no difficulty upon them if they break the fast in the month of Ramadan, and each one of them gives in charity, for each day, a mudd of food, and there is no making up (of fasts) upon them. But if they are not able, then there is nothing upon them.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» اَلشَّيْخُ اَلْكَبِيرُ وَ اَلَّذِي بِهِ اَلْعُطَاشُ لاَ حَرَجَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُفْطِرَا فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ يَتَصَدَّقَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ بِمُدٍّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ وَ لاَ قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِمَا فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرَا فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِمَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The elderly man and the one who has excessive thirst (al-utash), there is no difficulty upon them if they break the fast in the month of Ramadan, and each one of them gives in charity, for each day, a mudd of food, and there is no making up (of fasts) upon them. But if they are not able, then there is nothing upon them.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: Jafar ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Alaa ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him; and he (narrator) mentioned the hadith, except that Imam (a.s) said: “And each one of them gives in charity, for each day, two mudds (muddayn) of food.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى هَذَا اَلْحَدِيثَ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا جَعْفَرُ بْنُ بَشِيرٍ وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: وَذَكَرَ اَلْحَدِيثَ إِلاَّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ» وَ يَتَصَدَّقُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ بِمُدَّيْنِ مِنَ اَلطَّعَامِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: Jafar ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Alaa ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him; and he (narrator) mentioned the hadith, except that Imam (a.s) said: “And each one of them gives in charity, for each day, two mudds (muddayn) of food.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Imran ibn Musa and Ali ibn Khalid, from Harun, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Samaah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “The elderly man is not able to fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “Some of his children fast on his behalf.” I (narrator) asked: “But if he has no children?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then his nearest relative.” I (narrator) asked: “But if he has no relative?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives a mudd in charity for each day. But if he does not have anything with him, then there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُوسَى وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جُنْدَبٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلشَّيْخُ اَلْكَبِيرُ لاَ يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَصُومَ فَقَالَ» يَصُومُ عَنْهُ بَعْضُ وُلْدِهِ« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وُلْدٌ قَالَ» فَأَدْنَى قَرَابَتِهِ« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ قَرَابَةٌ قَالَ» تَصَدَّقَ بِمُدٍّ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ شَيْءٌ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Imran ibn Musa and Ali ibn Khalid, from Harun, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Samaah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Imam (a.s): “The elderly man is not able to fast.” Imam (a.s) said: “Some of his children fast on his behalf.” I (narrator) asked: “But if he has no children?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then his nearest relative.” I (narrator) asked: “But if he has no relative?” Imam (a.s) said: “He gives a mudd in charity for each day. But if he does not have anything with him, then there is nothing upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from his father, who said:
Hafs al-Awar wrote to me: “Ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about three matters.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “What are they?” He (narrator) said: “One who abandoned fasting three days in a month.” Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Due to illness, or old age, or thirst?” He (narrator) replied: “Then explain to me each matter separately.” Imam (a.s) said: “If it was due to illness, then when he recovers, let him make it up (the fasts). And if it was due to old age or thirst, then in place of each day is one mudd.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: كَتَبَ حَفْصٌ اَلْأَعْوَرُ إِلَيَّ سَلْ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ ثَلاَثِ مَسَائِلَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» مَا هِيَ« قَالَ مَنْ تَرَكَ صِيَامَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي شَهْرٍ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» مِنْ مَرَضٍ أَوْ كِبَرٍ أَوْ لِعَطَشٍ« قَالَ فَاشْرَحْ لِي شَيْئاً شَيْئاً فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ مَرَضٍ فَإِذَا بَرَأَ فَلْيَقْضِهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ كِبَرٍ أَوْ لِعَطَشٍ فَبَدَلُ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مُدٌّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Hafs al-Awar wrote to me: “Ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about three matters.” So Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “What are they?” He (narrator) said: “One who abandoned fasting three days in a month.” Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Due to illness, or old age, or thirst?” He (narrator) replied: “Then explain to me each matter separately.” Imam (a.s) said: “If it was due to illness, then when he recovers, let him make it up (the fasts). And if it was due to old age or thirst, then in place of each day is one mudd.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The pregnant woman near delivery (al-hamil al-muqrib) and the breastfeeding woman with little milk, there is no difficulty upon them if they break the fast in the month of Ramadan, because they are not able to bear the fast. And it is upon them that each one of them gives in charity, for each day in which she breaks the fast, a mudd of food. And upon them is the making up of every day in which they broke the fast; they make it up afterwards.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» اَلْحَامِلُ اَلْمُقْرِبُ وَاَلْمُرْضِعُ اَلْقَلِيلَةُ اَللَّبَنِ لاَ حَرَجَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ تُفْطِرَا فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ لِأَنَّهُمَا لاَ تُطِيقَانِ اَلصَّوْمَ وَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ تَتَصَدَّقَ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ تُفْطِرُ فِيهِ بِمُدٍّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ وَ عَلَيْهِمَا قَضَاءُ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ أَفْطَرَتَا فِيهِ تَقْضِيَانِهِ بَعْدُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “The pregnant woman near delivery (al-hamil al-muqrib) and the breastfeeding woman with little milk, there is no difficulty upon them if they break the fast in the month of Ramadan, because they are not able to bear the fast. And it is upon them that each one of them gives in charity, for each day in which she breaks the fast, a mudd of food. And upon them is the making up of every day in which they broke the fast; they make it up afterwards.”

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who is afflicted by thirst until he fears for himself.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He drinks the amount by which he preserves his life (ramaq), and he does not drink until he is quenched.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْعَطَشُ حَتَّى يَخَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ قَالَ» يَشْرَبُ بِقَدْرِ مَا يُمْسِكُ رَمَقَهُ وَ لاَ يَشْرَبُ حَتَّى يَرْوَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who is afflicted by thirst until he fears for himself.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He drinks the amount by which he preserves his life (ramaq), and he does not drink until he is quenched.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on One Incapable of Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We have young men and girls who are not able to fast because of the severity of what afflicts them of thirst.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let them drink the amount by which their souls are relieved and what they fear is averted.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ لَنَا فِتْيَاناً وَبَنَاتٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى اَلصِّيَامِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَا يُصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ اَلْعَطَشِ قَالَ» فَلْيَشْرَبُوا مِقْدَارَ مَا تَرْوَى بِهِ نُفُوسُهُمْ وَ مَا يَحْذَرُونَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We have young men and girls who are not able to fast because of the severity of what afflicts them of thirst.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let them drink the amount by which their souls are relieved and what they fear is averted.”
