chapter: Chapter on Extent of Illness in Which Breaking the Fast Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s): “What is the limit of the illness whose possessor breaks the fast, and the illness whose possessor leaves prayer while standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, man is a witness over himself,” And Imam (a.s) said: “That is up to him; he is more knowledgeable of himself.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَ اهِيمَ عَنْ أَ بِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِ لَى أَ بِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرَ ضِ اَلَّذِي يُفْطِرُ صَاحِبُهُ وَ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يَدَ عُ صَاحِبُهُ اَلصَّلاَةَ مِنْ قِيَا مٍ فَقَالَ » »بَلِ اَلْإِنْسٰانُ عَلىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ« « وَ قَالَ »ذَاكَ إِلَيْهِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s): “What is the limit of the illness whose possessor breaks the fast, and the illness whose possessor leaves prayer while standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, man is a witness over himself,” And Imam (a.s) said: “That is up to him; he is more knowledgeable of himself.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 326

chapter: Chapter on Extent of Illness in Which Breaking the Fast Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man, from Samaa, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): “What is the limit of the illness in which breaking the fast becomes obligatory upon its possessor, just as it becomes obligatory upon him during travel, when whoever is sick or on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “He is entrusted with it, and it is delegated to him. So if he finds weakness, let him break the fast, and if he finds strength, let him fast it, whatever the illness may be.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يَجِبُ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ فِيهِ اَلْإِفْطَارُ كَمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ مَنْ كَانَ مَرِيضاً أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ قَالَ» هُوَ مُؤْتَمَنٌ عَلَيْهِ مُفَوَّضٌ إِلَيْهِ فَإِنْ وَجَدَ ضَعْفاً فَلْيُفْطِرْ وَ إِنْ وَجَدَ قُوَّةً فَلْيَصُمْهُ كَانَ اَلْمَرَضُ مَا كَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man, from Samaa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s): “What is the limit of the illness in which breaking the fast becomes obligatory upon its possessor, just as it becomes obligatory upon him during travel, when whoever is sick or on a journey?” Imam (a.s) said: “He is entrusted with it, and it is delegated to him. So if he finds weakness, let him break the fast, and if he finds strength, let him fast it, whatever the illness may be.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 327

chapter: Chapter on Extent of Illness in Which Breaking the Fast Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
(Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who finds pain in his head from a severe headache, Is it permissible for him to break the fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he is afflicted with a severe headache, and if he is afflicted with a severe fever, and if his eye becomes inflamed with severe inflammation, then breaking the fast has become lawful for him.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَجِدُ فِي رَأْسِهِ وَجَعاً مِنْ صُدَاعٍ شَدِيدٍ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ اَلْإِفْطَارُ قَالَ» إِذَا صُدِّعَ صُدَاعاً شَدِيداً وَإِذَا حُمَّ حُمَّى شَدِيدَةً وَإِذَا رَمِدَتْ عَيْنُهُ رَمَداً شَدِيداً فَقَدْ حَلَّ لَهُ اَلْإِفْطَارُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Said, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding ‘a man who finds pain in his head from a severe headache, Is it permissible for him to break the fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he is afflicted with a severe headache, and if he is afflicted with a severe fever, and if his eye becomes inflamed with severe inflammation, then breaking the fast has become lawful for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 327

chapter: Chapter on Extent of Illness in Which Breaking the Fast Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
The Jurist (al-Faqih) Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The sick person only prays sitting when he reaches the condition in which he is unable to walk the amount of his prayer until he finishes while standing.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ اَلْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: »اَلْمَرِيضُ إِنَّمَا يُصَلِّي قَاعِداً إِذَا صَارَ بِالْحَالِ اَلَّتِي لاَ يَقْدِرُ فِيهَا أَنْ يَمْشِيَ مِقْدَارَ صَلاَتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَفْرُغَ قَائِماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Jurist (al-Faqih) Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The sick person only prays sitting when he reaches the condition in which he is unable to walk the amount of his prayer until he finishes while standing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 327

chapter: Chapter on Extent of Illness in Which Breaking the Fast Becomes Obligatory
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who fasted (month of) Ramadan while he was ill.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and he does not repeat it; it suffices him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ وَ هُوَ مَرِيضٌ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُ يُجْزِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who fasted (month of) Ramadan while he was ill.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and he does not repeat it; it suffices him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 328

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person pouring oil into his ear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَصُبُّ فِي أُذُنِهِ اَلدُّهْنَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person pouring oil into his ear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 328

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person whose ear pains him, and he pours medicine into it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَشْتَكِي أُذُنَهُ يَصُبُّ فِيهَا اَلدَّوَاءَ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person whose ear pains him, and he pours medicine into it.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 328

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulaym al-Farra, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person applying kohl to his eyes.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it; it is neither food nor drink.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمٍ اَلْفَرَّاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَكْتَحِلُ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ لَيْسَ بِطَعَامٍ وَ لاَ شَرَابٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulaym al-Farra, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person applying kohl to his eyes.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it; it is neither food nor drink.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 328

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘kohl for the fasting person.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it; it is not food that is eaten.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي غُنْدَرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْكُحْلِ لِلصَّائِمِ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ بِطَعَامٍ يُؤْكَلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘kohl for the fasting person.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it; it is not food that is eaten.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 329

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in (applying) kohl for the fasting person.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِالْكُحْلِ لِلصَّائِمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in (applying) kohl for the fasting person.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 329

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, when his eye pains him, whether he may apply eye powder (al-dharur) and what resembles it, such as ‘kohl’, or whether that is not permissible for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not apply kuhl.” – meaning the eye-powder (kuhl) or its sharp scent may enter the throat, for that is disliked.
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ إِذَا اِشْتَكَى عَيْنَهُ يَكْتَحِلُ بِالذَّرُورِ وَ مَا أَشْبَهَهُ أَمْ لاَ يَسُوغُ لَهُ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ» لاَ يَكْتَحِلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, when his eye pains him, whether he may apply eye powder (al-dharur) and what resembles it, such as ‘kohl’, or whether that is not permissible for him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not apply kuhl.” – meaning the eye-powder (kuhl) or its sharp scent may enter the throat, for that is disliked.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 329

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man applying eye-powder (kuhl) while he is fasting.’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, for I fear that it may enter his head.” – meaning the eye-powder (kuhl) or its sharp scent may enter the throat, for that is disliked.
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكْتَحِلُ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَقَالَ» لاَ إِنِّي أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ رَأْسَهُ«.

Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Dawud al-Mustariqq, and from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, who said:

Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘cupping (al-hijamah) for the fasting person.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he does not fear weakness.” – meaning which makes him unable to keep the fast.

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Said al-Araj, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imams (a.s) said: “Three things do not break the fast of the fasting person: vomiting, nocturnal emission (al-ihtilam), and cupping (al-hijamah). The Messenger of Allah (swt), underwent cupping while the Prophet (saws) was fasting, and the Prophet (saws) did not see any harm in kohl for the fasting person.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» ثَلاَثَةٌ لاَ يُفَطِّرْنَ اَلصَّائِمَ اَلْقَيْءُ وَاَلاِحْتِلاَمُ وَ اَلْحِجَامَةُ وَ قَدِ اِحْتَجَمَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ وَ كَانَ لاَ يَرَى بَأْساً بِالْكُحْلِ لِلصَّائِمِ«.

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And that which al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in the fasting person undergoing cupping (al-hijamah), except in (month of) Ramadan, for I dislike that he should expose himself to danger, unless he fears for himself. And when we want cupping (al-hijamah) in (month of) Ramadan, we undergo cupping at night.”
arabicText: وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَحْتَجِمَ اَلصَّائِمُ إِلاَّ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَإِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُغَرِّرَ بِنَفْسِهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَخَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَ إِنَّا إِذَا أَرَدْنَا اَلْحِجَامَةَ فِي رَمَضَانَ اِحْتَجَمْنَا لَيْلاً«.

And when we want cupping (al-hijamah) in (month of) Ramadan, we undergo cupping at night.”

Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person, my he undergo cupping (al-hijamah)?’ Imam (a.s) said: “I fear for him (of weakness); does he not fear for himself?” I (narrator) asked: “What do you fear for him?” Imam (a.s) said: “Fainting (al-ghashayan), or that bile (mirrah) may be stirred up in him.” I (narrator) replied: “What do you think, if he is strong enough for that and does not fear anything?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he wishes.”

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever hour of the day he wishes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يَسْتَاكُ اَلصَّائِمُ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ أَحَبَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever hour of the day he wishes.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, all together from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever part of the day he wishes.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ جَمِيعاً عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلصَّائِمُ يَسْتَاكُ أَيَّ اَلنَّهَارِ شَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, all together from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever part of the day he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May the fasting person use the tooth-stick (siwak) with water and with the moist stick, whose taste he finds?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يَسْتَاكُ اَلصَّائِمُ بِالْمَاءِ وَ بِالْعُودِ اَلرَّطْبِ يَجِدُ طَعْمَهُ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May the fasting person use the tooth-stick (siwak) with water and with the moist stick, whose taste he finds?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the tooth-stick (siwak) for the fasting person.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever hour he wishes, from the beginning of the day to its end.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَارُودِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسِّوَاكِ لِلصَّائِمِ قَالَ» يَسْتَاكُ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شَاءَ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلنَّهَارِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the tooth-stick (siwak) for the fasting person.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever hour he wishes, from the beginning of the day to its end.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, at which hour of the day may he use the tooth-stick (siwak)?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Whenever he wishes.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ يَسْتَاكُ مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ قَالَ» مَتَى شَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, at which hour of the day may he use the tooth-stick (siwak)?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Whenever he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala al-Qalla, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever part of the day he wishes, but he should not use a moist stick. He may soak himself in water, pour it (water) over his head, cool himself with a cloth, sprinkle the fan (al-mirwahah), and sprinkle the reed mat (al-buriya) beneath him, but he should not immerse his head in water.”
arabicText: رَوَى عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلاَءٍ اَلْقَلاَّءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يَسْتَاكُ اَلصَّائِمُ أَيَّ اَلنَّهَارِ شَاءَ وَ لاَ يَسْتَاكُ بِعُودٍ رَطْبٍ وَيَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ وَ يَصُبُّ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ يَتَبَرَّدُ بِالثَّوْبِ وَيَنْضِحُ اَلْمِرْوَحَةَ وَيَنْضِحُ اَلْبُورِيَاءَ تَحْتَهُ وَ لاَ يَغْمِسُ رَأْسَهُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala al-Qalla, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may use the tooth-stick (siwak) at whichever part of the day he wishes, but he should not use a moist stick. He may soak himself in water, pour it (water) over his head, cool himself with a cloth, sprinkle the fan (al-mirwahah), and sprinkle the reed mat (al-buriya) beneath him, but he should not immerse his head in water.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Sa’ad ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: Abu Basir narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person should not use a moist stick.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ يَسْتَاكُ اَلصَّائِمُ بِعُودٍ رَطْبٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Sa’ad ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: Abu Basir narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person should not use a moist stick.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
He disliked for the fasting person to use a moist tooth-stick (siwak). And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in moistening his tooth-stick (siwak) with water, then shaking it off until nothing remains in it.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ كَرِهَ لِلصَّائِمِ أَنْ يَسْتَاكَ بِسِوَاكٍ رَطْبٍ وَ قَالَ» لاَ يَضُرُّ أَنْ يَبُلَّ سِوَاكَهُ بِالْمَاءِ ثُمَّ يَنْفُضَهُ حَتَّى لاَ يَبْقَى فِيهِ شَيْءٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: He disliked for the fasting person to use a moist tooth-stick (siwak). And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in moistening his tooth-stick (siwak) with water, then shaking it off until nothing remains in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Some of those who sat with the Imam (a.s) asked him about ‘the tooth-stick (siwak) in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is permissible.” Then some of them said: “The moisture of the tooth-stick enters the inside (of the throat).” So he (narrator) asked: “What do you say about ‘the moist tooth-stick, whose moisture enters the throat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Water for rinsing the mouth is more moist than the moist tooth-stick.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرَّازِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ بَعْضُ جُلَسَائِهِ عَنِ اَلسِّوَاكِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» جَائِزٌ« فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِنَّ اَلسِّوَاكَ تَدْخُلُ رُطُوبَتُهُ فِي اَلْجَوْفِ فَقَالَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلسِّوَاكِ اَلرَّطْبِ تَدْخُلُ رُطُوبَتُهُ فِي اَلْحَلْقِ فَقَالَ» اَلْمَاءُ لِلْمَضْمَضَةِ أَرْطَبُ مِنَ اَلسِّوَاكِ اَلرَّطْبِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Some of those who sat with the Imam (a.s) asked him about ‘the tooth-stick (siwak) in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is permissible.” Then some of them said: “The moisture of the tooth-stick enters the inside (of the throat).” So he (narrator) asked: “What do you say about ‘the moist tooth-stick, whose moisture enters the throat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Water for rinsing the mouth is more moist than the moist tooth-stick.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person soaking himself in water.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, but he should not immerse himself in it. And the woman should not soak herself in water, because she carries water with her private part.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلسَّيَّارِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْهَمَذَانِيِّ عَنْ حَنَانِ بْنِ سَدِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ يَنْغَمِسُ فِيهِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةُ لاَ تَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ لِأَنَّهَا تَحْمِلُ اَلْمَاءَ بِفَرْجِهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadhani, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person soaking himself in water.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm, but he should not immerse himself in it. And the woman should not soak herself in water, because she carries water with her private part.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “If the fasting person makes himself vomit, then he must make up that day (of fasting). But if vomiting overcomes him without him making himself vomit, then let him complete his fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا تَقَيَّأَ اَلصَّائِمُ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ فَإِنْ ذَرَعَهُ اَلْقَيْءُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَتَقَيَّأَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If the fasting person makes himself vomit, then he must make up that day (of fasting). But if vomiting overcomes him without him making himself vomit, then let him complete his fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “If the fasting person makes himself vomit, then he has broken his fast. But if it overcomes him without him making himself vomit, then let him complete his fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا تَقَيَّأَ اَلصَّائِمُ فَقَدْ أَفْطَرَ وَ إِنْ ذَرَعَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَتَقَيَّأَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If the fasting person makes himself vomit, then he has broken his fast. But if it overcomes him without him making himself vomit, then let him complete his fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits deliberately while he is fasting has broken his fast, and he must repeat it. Then if Allah (swt) wills, Allah (swt) will punish him, and if Allah (swt) wills, Allah (swt) will forgive him.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits while he is fasting must make it up.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:» مَنْ تَقَيَّأَ مُتَعَمِّداً وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَقَدْ أَفْطَرَ وَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ فَإِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ عَذَّبَهُ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ غَفَرَ لَهُ« وَ قَالَ »مَنْ تَقَيَّأَ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْقَضَاءُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits deliberately while he is fasting has broken his fast, and he must repeat it. Then if Allah (swt) wills, Allah (swt) will punish him, and if Allah (swt) wills, Allah (swt) will forgive him.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits while he is fasting must make it up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits deliberately while he is fasting must make up a day in its place.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَحْمَدَ اِبْنَيِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» مَنْ تَقَيَّأَ مُتَعَمِّداً وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ قَضَى يَوْماً مَكَانَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever vomits deliberately while he is fasting must make up a day in its place.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘regurgitation (al-qals), and it is belching (al-jushah), when food rises from the inside of a man without him having vomited, while he is standing in prayer.’ Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate his ablution, nor does it cut off his prayer, nor does it break his fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقَلْسِ وَ هُوَ اَلْجُشْأَةُ يَرْتَفِعُ اَلطَّعَامُ مِنْ جَوْفِ اَلرَّجُلِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ تَقَيَّأَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ» لاَ يَنْقُضُ ذَلِكَ وُضُوءَهُ وَ لاَ يَقْطَعُ صَلاَتَهُ وَ لاَ يُفَطِّرُ صِيَامَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘regurgitation (al-qals), and it is belching (al-jushah), when food rises from the inside of a man without him having vomited, while he is standing in prayer.’ Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate his ablution, nor does it cut off his prayer, nor does it break his fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘regurgitation (al-qals), does it break the fast of the fasting person?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقَلْسِ أَ يُفَطِّرُ اَلصَّائِمَ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘regurgitation (al-qals), does it break the fast of the fasting person?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a fasting man who regurgitates (yaqlis), and something of food comes out from him. Does that break his fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “If he swallows it after it has come onto his tongue?” Imam (a.s) said: “That does not break his fast.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَقْلِسُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ اَلشَّيْءُ مِنَ اَلطَّعَامِ أَ يُفَطِّرُهُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ »لاَ« قُلْتُ فَإِنِ اِزْدَرَدَهُ بَعْدَ أَنْ صَارَ عَلَى لِسَانِهِ قَالَ» لاَ يُفَطِّرُهُ ذَلِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about ‘a fasting man who regurgitates (yaqlis), and something of food comes out from him. Does that break his fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “If he swallows it after it has come onto his tongue?” Imam (a.s) said: “That does not break his fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a fasting person who rinses his mouth.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not swallow his saliva until he spits three times.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي صَائِمٍ يَتَمَضْمَضُ قَالَ» لاَ يَبْلَعُ رِيقَهُ حَتَّى يَبْزُقَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a fasting person who rinses his mouth.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not swallow his saliva until he spits three times.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may apply perfume oil and smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلصَّائِمُ يَدَّهِنُ بِالطِّيبِ وَ يَشَمُّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person may apply perfume oil and smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when he fasted, would perfume himself with fragrance. And Imam (a.s) would say: “Fragrance is the gift of the fasting person.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْفَضْلِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا صَامَ تَطَيَّبَ بِالطِّيبِ وَ يَقُولُ» اَلطِّيبُ تُحْفَةُ اَلصَّائِمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when he fasted, would perfume himself with fragrance. And Imam (a.s) would say: “Fragrance is the gift of the fasting person.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The fasting person smells sweet basil (al-rayhan) and fragrance.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلصَّائِمُ يَشَمُّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ وَ اَلطِّيبَ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The fasting person smells sweet basil (al-rayhan) and fragrance.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s):
The Imams (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, disliked musk being used as perfume by the fasting person.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَرِهَ اَلْمِسْكَ أَنْ يَتَطَيَّبَ بِهِ اَلصَّائِمُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: The Imams (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, disliked musk being used as perfume by the fasting person.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, do you consider it permissible for him to smell sweet basil (al-rayhan), or do you not consider that permissible for him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ أَ تَرَى لَهُ أَنْ يَشَمَّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ أَمْ لاَ تَرَى ذَلِكَ لَهُ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person, do you consider it permissible for him to smell sweet basil (al-rayhan), or do you not consider that permissible for him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa’ad ibn Sad, who said:
A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May the fasting person smell sweet basil (al-rayhan), taking pleasure in it?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ قَالَ: كَتَبَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ هَلْ يَشَمُّ اَلصَّائِمُ اَلرَّيْحَانَ يَتَلَذَّذُ بِهِ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Jafar, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa’ad ibn Sad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May the fasting person smell sweet basil (al-rayhan), taking pleasure in it?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “There is no harm in it.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhdha, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, forbidding narcissus (al-narjis). So I (narrator) asked: “May I be made your ransom, why is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because it is the sweet basil of the non-Arabs.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ اَلْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفَيْضِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع يَنْهَى عَنِ اَلنَّرْجِسِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لِمَ ذَاكَ قَالَ »لِأَنَّهُ رَيْحَانُ اَلْأَعَاجِمِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhdha, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, forbidding narcissus (al-narjis). So I (narrator) asked: “May I be made your ransom, why is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Because it is the sweet basil of the non-Arabs.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person should not smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: »اَلصَّائِمُ لاَ يَشَمُّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The fasting person should not smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Baqqah, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person wearing a wet garment.’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, and he should not smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ بَقَّاحٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَلْبَسُ اَلثَّوْبَ اَلْمَبْلُولَ فَقَالَ» لاَ وَ لاَ يَشَمُّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Baqqah, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person wearing a wet garment.’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, and he should not smell sweet basil (al-rayhan).”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of Treatment for the Fasting Person, Kohl, Cupping, the Tooth-Stick (Siwak), Entering the Bathhouse, and Other than That
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Does she make up the fast?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “From where has this come?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, the first one to use analogy (Qiyaas) was Iblis.” I (narrator) replied: “So may the fasting person soak himself in water?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Then may he wet a garment over his body?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) replied: “From where has this come?” Imam (a.s) said: “From that.” I (narrator) asked: “May the fasting person smell sweet basil (al-rayhan)?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, because it is a pleasure, and it is disliked for him to take pleasure.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْحَائِضُ تَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ تَقْضِي اَلصَّوْمَ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَ هَذَا قَالَ» إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ قَاسَ إِبْلِيسُ« قُلْتُ فَالصَّائِمُ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي اَلْمَاءِ قَالَ» نَعَمْ« قُلْتُ فَيَبُلُّ ثَوْباً عَلَى جَسَدِهِ قَالَ» لاَ« قُلْتُ مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَ هَذَا قَالَ» مِنْ ذَلِكَ« قُلْتُ اَلصَّائِمُ يَشَمُّ اَلرَّيْحَانَ قَالَ» لاَ لِأَنَّهُ لَذَّةٌ وَ يُكْرَهُ لَهُ أَنْ يَتَلَذَّذَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) asked: “Does she make up the fast?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “From where has this come?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, the first one to use analogy (Qiyaas) was Iblis.” I (narrator) replied: “So may the fasting person soak himself in water?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I (narrator) asked: “Then may he wet a garment over his body?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” I (narrator) replied: “From where has this come?” Imam (a.s) said: “From that.” I (narrator) asked: “May the fasting person smell sweet basil (al-rayhan)?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, because it is a pleasure, and it is disliked for him to take pleasure.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted in (month of) Ramadan, then ate or drank forgetfully.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and there is no making up upon him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَامَ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَأَكَلَ أَوْ شَرِبَ نَاسِياً قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءٌ«
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted in (month of) Ramadan, then ate or drank forgetfully.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, and there is no making up upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say, ‘Whoever fasts, then forgets and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because he forgot, for it is only provision that Allah (swt) has provided him, so let him complete his fast.’”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ع قَالَ كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» مَنْ صَامَ فَنَسِيَ وَ أَكَلَ وَ شَرِبَ فَلاَ يُفْطِرْ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّهُ نَسِيَ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ رِزْقٌ رَزَقَهُ اَللَّهُ فَلْيُتِمَّ صِيَامَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say, ‘Whoever fasts, then forgets and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because he forgot, for it is only provision that Allah (swt) has provided him, so let him complete his fast.’”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who forgets and eats in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, for it is only something that Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has fed him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ سِرْحَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى فَيَأْكُلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْءٌ أَطْعَمَهُ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who forgets and eats in the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast, for it is only something that Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has fed him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 339

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who ate or drank after dawn had risen in Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he had risen and looked, and did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned and saw the dawn, then let him complete his fast, and there is no repetition (qada) upon him. But if he had risen and eaten or drunk, then looked toward the dawn and saw that it had risen, then let him complete his fast and make up another day, because he began with eating before looking, so repetition (qada) is upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَكَلَ أَوْ شَرِبَ بَعْدَ مَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ قَامَ فَنَظَرَ وَ لَمْ يَرَ اَلْفَجْرَ فَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ عَادَ فَرَأَى اَلْفَجْرَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَامَ فَأَكَلَ أَوْ شَرِبَ ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى اَلْفَجْرِ فَرَآهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ طَلَعَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِي يَوْماً آخَرَ لِأَنَّهُ بَدَأَ بِالْأَكْلِ قَبْلَ اَلنَّظَرِ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who ate or drank after dawn had risen in Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he had risen and looked, and did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned and saw the dawn, then let him complete his fast, and there is no repetition (qada) upon him. But if he had risen and eaten or drunk, then looked toward the dawn and saw that it had risen, then let him complete his fast and make up another day, because he began with eating before looking, so repetition (qada) is upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 339

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who ate the pre-dawn meal, then left his house when dawn had already risen and become clear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes that fast, then let him make it up (qada). And if he ate the pre-dawn meal outside the month of Ramadan after the rising of dawn, he has broken the fast.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, one night my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) was praying while I was eating, then he turned away and said: ‘As for Ja’far (a.s), he has eaten and drunk after dawn.’ So he (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) ordered me, and I broke the fast of that day outside the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَسَحَّرَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ وَ قَدْ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ تَبَيَّنَ فَقَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ لْيَقْضِهِ وَ إِنْ تَسَحَّرَ فِي غَيْرِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ أَفْطَرَ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» إِنَّ أَبِي كَانَ لَيْلَةً يُصَلِّي وَ أَنَا آكُلُ فَانْصَرَفَ فَقَالَ» أَمَّا جَعْفَرٌ فَقَدْ أَكَلَ وَ شَرِبَ بَعْدَ اَلْفَجْرِ« فَأَمَرَنِي فَأَفْطَرْتُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ فِي غَيْرِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘a man who ate the pre-dawn meal, then left his house when dawn had already risen and become clear.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes that fast, then let him make it up (qada). And if he ate the pre-dawn meal outside the month of Ramadan after the rising of dawn, he has broken the fast.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, one night my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) was praying while I was eating, then he turned away and said: ‘As for Ja’far (a.s), he has eaten and drunk after dawn.’ So he (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) ordered me, and I broke the fast of that day outside the month of Ramadan.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar:
I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I order the slave-girl to look whether dawn has risen or not, and she says: ‘It has not risen, so I eat.’ Then I look and find that it had already risen when she looked.” Imam (a.s) said: “You complete your day and make it up (qada). Indeed, had you been the one who looked, there would have been no making it up upon you.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ آمُرُ اَلْجَارِيَةَ أَنْ تَنْظُرَ طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ أَمْ لاَ فَتَقُولُ لَمْ يَطْلُعْ فَآكُلُ ثُمَّ أَنْظُرُ فَأَجِدُهُ قَدْ طَلَعَ حِينَ نَظَرَتْ قَالَ» تُتِمُّ يَوْمَكَ وَتَقْضِيهِ أَ مَا أَنَّكَ لَوْ كُنْتَ أَنْتَ اَلَّذِي نَظَرْتَ مَا كَانَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاؤُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I order the slave-girl to look whether dawn has risen or not, and she says: ‘It has not risen, so I eat.’ Then I look and find that it had already risen when she looked.” Imam (a.s) said: “You complete your day and make it up (qada). Indeed, had you been the one who looked, there would have been no making it up upon you.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who went out in the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating the pre-dawn meal in a house. He looked toward the dawn and called out to them, so some of them stopped, while some of them thought that he was mocking, so he ate.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast and makes it up.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ خَرَجَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ أَصْحَابُهُ يَتَسَحَّرُونَ فِي بَيْتٍ فَنَظَرَ إِلَى اَلْفَجْرِ فَنَادَاهُمْ فَكَفَّ بَعْضُهُمْ وَ ظَنَّ بَعْضُهُمْ أَنَّهُ يَسْخَرُ فَأَكَلَ قَالَ» يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِي«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who went out in the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating the pre-dawn meal in a house. He looked toward the dawn and called out to them, so some of them stopped, while some of them thought that he was mocking, so he ate.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He completes his fast and makes it up.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Basir and Samaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a people who fasted the month of Ramadan, then a black cloud covered them at the setting of the sun, so they thought that it was night.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon the one who broke the fast is the fasting of that day (qada). Indeed Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Then complete the fast until the night.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187) So whoever eats before the night enters, then making it up is upon him, because he ate deliberately.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْمٍ صَامُوا شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ فَغَشِيَهُمْ سَحَابٌ أَسْوَدُ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَرَأَوْا أَنَّهُ اَللَّيْلُ فَقَالَ» عَلَى اَلَّذِي أَفْطَرَ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ» ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا اَلصِّيٰامَ إِلَى اَللَّيْلِ« فَمَنْ أَكَلَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ اَللَّيْلُ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ لِأَنَّهُ أَكَلَ مُتَعَمِّداً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Basir and Samaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a people who fasted the month of Ramadan, then a black cloud covered them at the setting of the sun, so they thought that it was night.’ Imam (a.s) said: “Upon the one who broke the fast is the fasting of that day (qada). Indeed Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Then complete the fast until the night.’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187) So whoever eats before the night enters, then making it up is upon him, because he ate deliberately.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted, then thought that the sun had set while there was cloud in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the cloud cleared, and behold, the sun had not set.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast has been completed, and he does not make it up.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ اَلْكِنَانِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَامَ ثُمَّ ظَنَّ أَنَّ اَلشَّمْسَ قَدْ غَابَتْ وَ فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ غَيْمٌ فَأَفْطَرَ ثُمَّ إِنَّ اَلسَّحَابَ اِنْجَلَى فَإِذَا اَلشَّمْسُ لَمْ تَغِبْ فَقَالَ »قَدْ تَمَّ صَوْمُهُ وَ لاَ يَقْضِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted, then thought that the sun had set while there was cloud in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the cloud cleared, and behold, the sun had not set.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast has been completed, and he does not make it up.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a fasting man who thought that the night had already entered and that the sun had set, while there was cloud in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the cloud cleared, and behold, the sun had not set.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast is complete, and he does not make it up.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَائِمٍ ظَنَّ أَنَّ اَللَّيْلَ قَدْ كَانَ دَخَلَ وَ أَنَّ اَلشَّمْسَ قَدْ غَابَتْ وَ كَانَ فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ سَحَابٌ فَأَفْطَرَ ثُمَّ إِنَّ اَلسَّحَابَ اِنْجَلَى فَإِذَا اَلشَّمْسُ لَمْ تَغِبْ فَقَالَ» تَمَّ صَوْمُهُ وَ لاَ يَقْضِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a fasting man who thought that the night had already entered and that the sun had set, while there was cloud in the sky, so he broke his fast. Then the cloud cleared, and behold, the sun had not set.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast is complete, and he does not make it up.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The time of Maghrib is when the disc (of sun) disappears. So if you see it after that, and you have already prayed, you repeat the prayer, while your fast has passed, and you refrain from food if you had taken anything of it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» وَقْتُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا غَابَ اَلْقُرْصُ فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ أَعَدْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ مَضَى صَوْمُكَ وَتَكُفُّ عَنِ اَلطَّعَامِ إِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ أَصَبْتَ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “The time of Maghrib is when the disc (of sun) disappears. So if you see it after that, and you have already prayed, you repeat the prayer, while your fast has passed, and you refrain from food if you had taken anything of it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 342

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadalah, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “A kiss does not invalidate the fast.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ:» لاَ تَنْقُضُ اَلْقُبْلَةُ اَلصَّوْمَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadalah, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “A kiss does not invalidate the fast.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a kiss in the month of Ramadan for the fasting person, does it break his fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقُبْلَةِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ لِلصَّائِمِ أَتُفَطِّرُهُ قَالَ» لاَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah ibn Mihran, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a kiss in the month of Ramadan for the fasting person, does it break his fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked whether the fasting person may have physical contact or kiss in the month of Ramadan. Imam (a.s) said: “I fear for him, so let him keep away from that, unless he is confident that his semen (lustful desires) will not overcome him.”
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ هَلْ يُبَاشِرُ اَلصَّائِمُ أَوْ يُقَبِّلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَنَزَّهْ عَنْ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَثِقَ أَنْ لاَ يَسْبِقَهُ مَنِيُّهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked whether the fasting person may have physical contact or kiss in the month of Ramadan. Imam (a.s) said: “I fear for him, so let him keep away from that, unless he is confident that his semen (lustful desires) will not overcome him.”

chapter: Chapter on Ruling of the Forgetful One and the Mistaken One Regarding Fasting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa’ad ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, may I kiss while I am fasting?” Imam (a.s) said to him: “Keep your fast chaste, for the beginning of fighting is slapping (al-litam).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ ظَرِيفٍ عَنِ اَلْأَصْبَغِ بْنِ نُبَاتَةَ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أُقَبِّلُ وَ أَنَا صَائِمٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ» عِفَّ صَوْمَكَ فَإِنَّ بَدْءَ اَلْقِتَالِ اَللِّطَامُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa’ad ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, may I kiss while I am fasting?” Imam (a.s) said to him: “Keep your fast chaste, for the beginning of fighting is slapping (al-litam).”
