thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘the fasting person who performs wudu (ablution) for prayer, and water enters his throat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If his wudu (ablution) was for an obligatory prayer, then there is no making up upon him, but if his wudu was for a supererogatory prayer, then upon him is the making up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Jamilah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said,
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a fasting person deliberately immersed himself in water. Is he required to make up that day?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He is not required to make it up, but he must not do it again."
arabicText: محمد بن الحسين عن ابي جميلة عن اسحاق بن عمار قال: قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام صائم ارتمس في الماء متعمدا أعليه قضاء ذلك اليوم؟ قال: ليس عليه قضاء ولا يعودن
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Jamilah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said,
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a fasting person deliberately immersed himself in water. Is he required to make up that day?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He is not required to make it up, but he must not do it again."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘the man who becomes thirsty in (month of) Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in sucking the ring.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَعْطَشُ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يَمَصَّ اَلْخَاتَمَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘the man who becomes thirsty in (month of) Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in sucking the ring.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person chewing gum (ilk)’. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he wishes.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ أَ بِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَمْضَغُ اَلْعِلْكَ فَقَالَ» نَعَمْ إِنْ شَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person chewing gum (ilk)’. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person fumigating himself with aloeswood or with something other than that, and the smoke enters his throat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is permissible, there is no harm in it.” He said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person when dust enters his throat.’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَتَدَخَّنُ بِعُودٍ أَوْ بِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَيَدْخُلُ اَلدُّخْنَةُ فِي حَلْقِهِ فَقَالَ» جَائِزٌ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ« قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَدْخُلُ اَلْغُبَارُ فِي حَلْقِهِ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person fumigating himself with aloeswood or with something other than that, and the smoke enters his throat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is permissible, there is no harm in it.” He said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the fasting person when dust enters his throat.’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 405

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I ask Imam (a.s) about ‘a fasting person tasting drink or food, with its taste in his throat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not do so.” I (narrator) asked: “So if he does it, what is upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him, and he should not return to it.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَذُوقُ اَلشَّرَابَ وَ اَلطَّعَامَ يَجِدُ طَعْمَهُ فِي حَلْقِهِ قَالَ» لاَ يَفْعَلُ« قُلْتُ فَإِنْ فَعَلَ فَمَا عَلَيْهِ قَالَ» لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لاَ يَعُودُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I ask Imam (a.s) about ‘a fasting person tasting drink or food, with its taste in his throat.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He should not do so.” I (narrator) asked: “So if he does it, what is upon him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him, and he should not return to it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the man and the woman, is it proper for them to insert medicine while they are both fasting?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُمَا أَنْ يَسْتَدْخِلاَ اَلدَّوَاءَ وَ هُمَا صَائِمَانِ قَالَ »لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘the man and the woman, is it proper for them to insert medicine while they are both fasting?’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ammar al-Sabati said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the cupper performing cupping while he is fasting.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate.” And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘the fasting person undergoing cupping.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: عَمَّارٌ اَلسَّابَاطِيُّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّامِ يَحْجُمُ وَهُوَ صَائِمٌ قَالَ» لاَ يَنْبَغِي« وَعَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يَحْتَجِمُ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ammar al-Sabati said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the cupper performing cupping while he is fasting.’ Imam (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate.” And (Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘the fasting person undergoing cupping.’ Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who travelled in (month of) Ramadan, then death overtook him before he could make it up.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The most virtuous of his household should make it up for him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَافَرَ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَأَدْرَكَهُ اَلْمَوْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقْضِيَهُ قَالَ» يَقْضِيهِ أَفْضَلُ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Samaah, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who travelled in (month of) Ramadan, then death overtook him before he could make it up.’ Imam (a.s) said: “The most virtuous of his household should make it up for him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted while he was sick.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast is complete, and he does not repeat it; it suffices him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَامَ وَ هُوَ مَرِيضٌ قَالَ» تَمَّ صَوْمُهُ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُ يُجْزِيهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who fasted while he was sick.’ Imam (a.s) said: “His fast is complete, and he does not repeat it; it suffices him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
My father asked Imam (a.s), while I was listening, about ‘the limit of the illness in which fasting is to be left.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When he is not able to take the pre-dawn meal.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ أَبِي وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ عَنْ حَدِّ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يُتْرَكُ فِيهِ اَلصَّوْمُ فَقَالَ» إِذَا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يَتَسَحَّرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: My father asked Imam (a.s), while I was listening, about ‘the limit of the illness in which fasting is to be left.’ Imam (a.s) said: “When he is not able to take the pre-dawn meal.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 406

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘an elderly man who becomes weak from fasting the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: ‘He should give in charity what suffices on his behalf: the food of one poor person for each day.’
arabicText: عنه عن ابن ابي عمير عن حماد عن الحلبي عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: سألته عن رجل كبير يضعف عن صوم شهر رمضان قال: يتصدق بما يجزي عنه، طعام مسكين لكل يوم
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘an elderly man who becomes weak from fasting the month of Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: ‘He should give in charity what suffices on his behalf: the food of one poor person for each day.’

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ammar al-Sabati said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person who is afflicted by thirst until he fears for himself (from death).’ Imam (a.s) said: “He drinks the amount by which he preserves his remaining life, and he does not drink until he is quenched.”
arabicText: عَمَّارٌ اَلسَّابَاطِيُّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّائِمِ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْعَطَشُ حَتَّى يَخَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ قَالَ »يَشْرَبُ بِقَدْرِ مَا يُمْسِكُ رَمَقَهُ وَ لاَ يَشْرَبُ حَتَّى يَرْوَى«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ammar al-Sabati said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the fasting person who is afflicted by thirst until he fears for himself (from death).’ Imam (a.s) said: “He drinks the amount by which he preserves his remaining life, and he does not drink until he is quenched.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, ‘at what age is the boy taken (made) to fasting?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Between him and fifteen years and fourteen years, and if he fasts before that, then leave him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي كَمْ يُؤْخَذُ اَلصَّبِيُّ بِالصِّيَامِ فَقَالَ» مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً وَ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً وَ إِنْ هُوَ صَامَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ فَدَعْهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, ‘at what age is the boy taken (made) to fasting?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Between him and fifteen years and fourteen years, and if he fasts before that, then leave him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
Imam (a.s) said: “The boy, when he is able to fast three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan has become obligatory upon him.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلسَّكُونِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» اَلصَّبِيُّ إِذَا أَطَاقَ اَلصَّوْمَ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ مُتَتَابِعَةٍ فَقَدْ وَجَبَ عَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: As for what al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father, Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The boy, when he is able to fast three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan has become obligatory upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘the boy, when does he (made to) fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “When he is able to bear it.”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلصَّبِيِّ مَتَى يَصُومُ قَالَ» إِذَا أَطَاقَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And what Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about ‘the boy, when does he (made to) fast?’ Imam (a.s) said: “When he is able to bear it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said: “Upon the boy, when he has a wet dream, is (obligation of) fasting, And upon the girl, when she menstruates, is (obligation of) fasting and the veil (khimar), unless she is an owned slave-woman (mamlukah), for there is no veil (khimar) upon her unless she likes to veil herself, and fasting is (still) upon her.”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن القاسم بن محمد عن علي عن ابي بصير عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: على الصبي إذا احتلم الصيام وعلى الجارية إذا حاضت الصيام والخمار إلا أن تكون مملوكة فانه ليس عليها خمار إلا ان تحب ان تختمر وعليها الصيام
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Upon the boy, when he has a wet dream, is (obligation of) fasting, And upon the girl, when she menstruates, is (obligation of) fasting and the veil (khimar), unless she is an owned slave-woman (mamlukah), for there is no veil (khimar) upon her unless she likes to veil herself, and fasting is (still) upon her.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 407

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaa ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a woman who makes it upon herself for Allah (swt) to fast two consecutive months, then she menstruates.’ Imam (a.s) said: “She fasts what she menstruated, and it suffices her.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اِمْرَأَةٍ تَجْعَلُ لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوْمَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ فَتَحِيضُ قَالَ» تَصُومُ مَا حَاضَتْ فَهُوَ يُجْزِيهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaa ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a woman who makes it upon herself for Allah (swt) to fast two consecutive months, then she menstruates.’ Imam (a.s) said: “She fasts what she menstruated, and it suffices her.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Do not go out in (month of) Ramadan except for Hajj, or Umrah, or wealth which you fear may be lost, or for crops whose harvest time has arrived.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ تَخْرُجْ فِي رَمَضَانَ إِلاَّ لِلْحَجِّ أَوِ اَلْعُمْرَةِ أَوْ مَالٍ تَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ اَلْفَوْتَ أَوْ لِزَرْعٍ يَحِينُ حَصَادُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Do not go out in (month of) Ramadan except for Hajj, or Umrah, or wealth which you fear may be lost, or for crops whose harvest time has arrived.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘going out when (month of) Ramadan has entered.’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, except in what I inform you of: going out to Makkah, or fighting in the way of Allah (swt), or wealth whose destruction you fear, or a brother whose destruction you fear.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, it is not a brother from the father and the mother.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْخُرُوجِ إِذَا دَخَلَ رَمَضَانُ فَقَالَ» لاَ إِلاَّ فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكَ بِهِ خُرُوجاً إِلَى مَكَّةَ أَوْ غَزْواً فِي سَبِيلِ اَللَّهِ أَوْ مَالاً تَخَافُ هَلاَكَهُ أَوْ أَخاً تَخَافُ هَلاَكَهُ« وَ قَالَ» إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَخٌ مِنَ اَلْأَبِ وَ اَلْأُمِّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘going out when (month of) Ramadan has entered.’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, except in what I inform you of: going out to Makkah, or fighting in the way of Allah (swt), or wealth whose destruction you fear, or a brother whose destruction you fear.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, it is not a brother from the father and the mother.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaa ibn Musa, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who wants to travel in (month of) Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he begins the morning in his town and then goes out, then if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ اَلسَّفَرَ فِي رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» إِذَا أَصْبَحَ فِي بَلَدِهِ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ فَإِنْ شَاءَ صَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَفْطَرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifaa ibn Musa, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who wants to travel in (month of) Ramadan.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If he begins the morning in his town and then goes out, then if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 408

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about the man, ‘what should he do when he wants to travel?’ Imam (a.s) said: “When dawn rises and he has not departed (his home town), then upon him is the fasting of that day. But if he goes out from his family before the rising of dawn, then let him break the fast, and there is no fast upon him. And if he arrives after the sun has passed the meridian, he breaks the fast and does not eat openly. And if he arrives from his journey before the sun has passed the meridian, then upon him is the fasting of that day, if he wishes.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ إِذَا أَرَادَ اَلسَّفَرَ قَالَ »إِذَا طَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ لَمْ يَشْخَصْ فَعَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ اَلْفَجْرِ فَلْيُفْطِرْ وَ لاَ صِيَامَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ قَدِمَ بَعْدَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ أَفْطَرَ وَ لاَ يَأْكُلُ ظَاهِراً وَ إِنْ قَدِمَ مِنْ سَفَرِهِ قَبْلَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَعَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ إِنْ شَاءَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about the man, ‘what should he do when he wants to travel?’ Imam (a.s) said: “When dawn rises and he has not departed (his home town), then upon him is the fasting of that day. But if he goes out from his family before the rising of dawn, then let him break the fast, and there is no fast upon him. And if he arrives after the sun has passed the meridian, he breaks the fast and does not eat openly. And if he arrives from his journey before the sun has passed the meridian, then upon him is the fasting of that day, if he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 409

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Samaah said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever wants to travel in (month of) Ramadan, and dawn rises while he is among his family, then upon him is the fasting of that day. And when he travels, it is not appropriate that he alone should break the fast on that day. Shortening (the prayer) and breaking the fast do not separate; so whoever shortens (the prayer), let him break the fast.”
arabicText: سَمَاعَةُ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ : »مَنْ أَرَادَ اَلسَّفَرَ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَطَلَعَ اَلْفَجْرُ وَ هُوَ فِي أَهْلِهِ فَعَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ وَ إِذَا سَافَرَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُفْطِرَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ وَحْدَهُ وَ لَيْسَ يَفْتَرِقُ اَلتَّقْصِيرُ وَ اَلْإِفْطَارُ فَمَنْ قَصَّرَ فَلْيُفْطِرْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Samaah said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever wants to travel in (month of) Ramadan, and dawn rises while he is among his family, then upon him is the fasting of that day. And when he travels, it is not appropriate that he alone should break the fast on that day. Shortening (the prayer) and breaking the fast do not separate; so whoever shortens (the prayer), let him break the fast.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the man who says, ‘For Allah (swt) upon me is that I fast a month, or more than that, or less,’ then a matter arises for him in which he has no choice but to travel. Should he fast while he is a traveller?’ Imam (a.s) said: “When he travels, let him break the fast, because fasting during travel is not lawful for him, whether it is obligatory or other than that, and fasting during travel is disobedience.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُولُ لِلَّهِ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَصُومَ شَهْراً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَقَلَّ فَعَرَضَ لَهُ أَمْرٌ لاَ بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ أَنْ يُسَافِرَ أَ يَصُومُ وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ قَالَ» إِذَا سَافَرَ فَلْيُفْطِرْ لِأَنَّهُ لاَ يَحِلُّ لَهُ اَلصَّوْمُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَرِيضَةً كَانَ أَوْ غَيْرَهُ وَ اَلصَّوْمُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ مَعْصِيَةٌ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the man who says, ‘For Allah (swt) upon me is that I fast a month, or more than that, or less,’ then a matter arises for him in which he has no choice but to travel. chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who fasted the month of Ramadan while traveling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If it had not reached him that the blessed Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade that, then there is no make-up fast upon him, and the fast has sufficed on his behalf.”
arabicText: محمد بن علي بن محبوب عن عبد الرحمن بن ابى نجران عن حماد بن عيسى عن عبد الرحمن بن ابي عبد الله عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: سألته عن رجل صام شهر رمضان في السفر قال: ان كان لم يبلغه ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله نهى عن ذلك فليس عليه القضاء وقد أجزأ عنه الصوم
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who fasted the month of Ramadan while traveling.’ Imam (a.s) said: “If it had not reached him that the blessed Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade that, then there is no make-up fast upon him, and the fast has sufficed on his behalf.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the man who travels in (month of) Ramadan and has a slave girl (jariyah) with him, may he have intercourse with her?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُسَافِرُ فِي رَمَضَانَ وَ مَعَهُ جَارِيَةٌ أَ يَقَعُ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ» نَعَمْ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘the man who travels in (month of) Ramadan and has a slave girl (jariyah) with him, may he have intercourse with her?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man upon whom there are days from the month of Ramadan: how should he make them up?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If there are two days (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for one day. And if there are five days (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for two days. And if there is a month (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for some days. And he does not have the right to fast more than eight days (of qada fasts), meaning consecutively. So if there are eight days or ten days (of qada fasts) upon him, he breaks the fast between them for one day.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّامٌ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ كَيْفَ يَقْضِيهَا قَالَ» إِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَانِ فَلْيُفْطِرْ بَيْنَهُمَا يَوْماً وَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ خَمْسَةُ أَيَّامٍ فَلْيُفْطِرْ بَيْنَهَا يَوْمَيْنِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ شَهْرٌ فَلْيُفْطِرْ بَيْنَهَا أَيَّاماً وَ لَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثَمَانِيَةِ أَيَّامٍ يَعْنِي مُتَوَالِيَةً فَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ ثَمَانِيَةُ أَيَّامٍ أَوْ عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ أَفْطَرَ بَيْنَهَا يَوْماً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man upon whom there are days from the month of Ramadan: how should he make them up?’ Imam (a.s) said: “If there are two days (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for one day. And if there are five days (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for two days. And if there is a month (of qada fasts) upon him, then let him break the fast between them for some days. And he does not have the right to fast more than eight days (of qada fasts), meaning consecutively. So if there are eight days or ten days (of qada fasts) upon him, he breaks the fast between them for one day.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali and Ishaq, the two sons of Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad:
He (narrator) said: “A man wrote to al-Faqih (a.s), ‘O my master, I vowed that whenever the night prayer missed me, I would fast on its morning’, but that missed him. What should he do, and is there a way out for him from that, and how much expiation is obligatory upon him for the fast of each day that he left, if he wishes to make expiation for that?” He (narrator) said: “So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote, ‘He distributes (charity), for each day, a mudd of food as expiation.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيٍّ وَ إِسْحَاقَ اِبْنَيْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: كَتَبَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى اَلْفَقِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَا مَوْلاَيَ نَذَرْتُ أَنِّي مَتَى فَاتَتْنِي صَلاَةُ اَللَّيْلِ صُمْتُ فِي صَبِيحَتِهَا فَفَاتَهُ ذَلِكَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ وَ هَلْ لَهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَخْرَجٌ وَكَمْ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ فِي صَوْمِ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ تَرَكَهُ أَنْ كَفَّرَ إِنْ أَرَادَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ »يُفَرِّقُ عَنْ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مُدّاً مِنْ طَعَامٍ كَفَّارَةً«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali and Ishaq, the two sons of Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) said: “A man wrote to al-Faqih (a.s), ‘O my master, I vowed that whenever the night prayer missed me, I would fast on its morning’, but that missed him. What should he do, and is there a way out for him from that, and how much expiation is obligatory upon him for the fast of each day that he left, if he wishes to make expiation for that?” He (narrator) said: “So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote, ‘He distributes (charity), for each day, a mudd of food as expiation.’”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘a man on whom was fasting of two straight months in zihar, so he fasted Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah entered on him. What can he do?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts all of Dhu al-Hijjah except the days of al-tashriq, then he makes them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so he will have fasted two consecutive months.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And it is not appropriate for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three days of al-tashriq which he did not fast. And there is no harm if he fasts a month, then fasts some days from the month that follows it, then an illness occurs to him that causes him to cut it off, then he makes it up after the completion of the month.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمُ» شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتٰابِعَيْنِ« فِي ظِهَارٍ فَصَامَ ذَا اَلْقَعْدَةِ وَ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ ذُو اَلْحِجَّةِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ» يَصُومُ ذَا اَلْحِجَّةِ كُلَّهُ إِلاَّ أَيَّامَ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ ثُمَّ يَقْضِيهَا فِي أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ مِنَ اَلْمُحَرَّمِ حَتَّى يُتِمَّ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَيَكُونَ قَدْ صَامَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ« ثُمَّ قَالَ» وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَقْرَبَ أَهْلَهُ حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ اَلثَّلاَثَةَ اَلْأَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ اَلَّتِي لَمْ يَصُمْهَا وَ لاَ بَأْسَ إِنْ صَامَ شَهْراً ثُمَّ صَامَ مِنَ اَلشَّهْرِ اَلَّذِي يَلِيهِ أَيَّاماً ثُمَّ عَرَضَتْ لَهُ عِلَّةٌ أَنْ يَقْطَعَهُ ثُمَّ يَقْضِيَ بَعْدُ تَمَامَ اَلشَّهْرِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) about ‘a man on whom was fasting of two straight months in zihar, so he fasted Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah entered on him. What can he do?’ Imam (a.s) said: “He fasts all of Dhu al-Hijjah except the days of al-tashriq, then he makes them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so he will have fasted two consecutive months.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And it is not appropriate for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three days of al-tashriq which he did not fast. And there is no harm if he fasts a month, then fasts some days from the month that follows it, then an illness occurs to him that causes him to cut it off, then he makes it up after the completion of the month.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
(Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who appoints for himself known, named days in every month, then travels for the number of the months.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He does not fast, because he is on a journey, and he does not make them up when he is present.”
arabicText: هَارُونُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُوَقِّتُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَيَّاماً مَعْرُوفَةً مُسَمَّاةً فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ فَيُسَافِرُ بِعِدَّةِ اَلشُّهُورِ قَالَ» لاَ يَصُومُ لِأَنَّهُ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ يَقْضِيهَا إِذَا شَهِدَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Harun ibn Muslim, from Masadah ibn Sadaqah, from Imam Jafar al-Sadiq (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: (Imam (a.s) was asked) concerning ‘a man who appoints for himself known, named days in every month, then travels for the number of the months.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He does not fast, because he is on a journey, and he does not make them up when he is present.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Ubayd, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s), meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him: “O my master, a man vowed to fast a day for Allah (swt), then on that day he had intercourse with his wife; what expiation is upon him?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, answered him: “He fasts one day in place of a day, and the freeing of a slave.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ يَعْنِي أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَا سَيِّدِي رَجُلٌ نَذَرَ أَنْ يَصُومَ يَوْماً لِلَّهِ فَوَقَعَ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلْكَفَّارَةِ فَأَجَابَهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» يَصُومُ يَوْماً بَدَلَ يَوْمٍ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Ubayd, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s), meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him: “O my master, a man vowed to fast a day for Allah (swt), then on that day he had intercourse with his wife; what expiation is upon him?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, answered him: “He fasts one day in place of a day, and the freeing of a slave.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Harun ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salih ibn Abdillah, who said:
I (narrator) said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him: “Indeed, my brother was imprisoned, so I made upon myself the fasting of a month. So I fasted, but sometimes some of my brothers would come to me so that I would break the fast, and I broke the fast for some days. Should I make it up” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: هَارُونُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ أَخِي حُبِسَ فَجَعَلْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي صَوْمَ شَهْرٍ فَصُمْتُ فَرُبَّمَا أَتَانِي بَعْضُ إِخْوَانِي لِأُفْطِرَ فَأَفْطَرْتُ أَيَّاماً أَ فَأَ قْضِيهِ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Harun ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salih ibn Abdillah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (a.s), peace be upon him: “Indeed, my brother was imprisoned, so I made upon myself the fasting of a month. So I fasted, but sometimes some of my brothers would come to me so that I would break the fast, and I broke the fast for some days. Should I make it up” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 412

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Do not fast for three days after Eid al-Adha, and nor for three days after Eid al-Fitr. Indeed, they are days of eating and drinking.”
arabicText: اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْحَلاَّلِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» لاَ تَصُمْ بَعْدَ اَلْأَضْحَى ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَ لاَ بَعْدَ اَلْفِطْرِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِنَّهَا أَيَّامُ أَكْلٍ وَ شُرْبٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Do not fast for three days after Eid al-Adha, and nor for three days after Eid al-Fitr. Indeed, they are days of eating and drinking.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 412

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from his father, who said:
I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), saying: “Indeed, al-Juhani came to the Prophet (saws), and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), indeed I have camels, sheep, young servants, and workers, so I would like you to command me with a night in which I may enter and witness (attend) the prayer’, and that was in the month of Ramadan. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, called him and whispered secretly into his ear. So al-Juhani, when it was the night of twenty-three (of the month of Ramadan), would enter with his camels, his sheep, and his family to his place (to attend to prayer).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:» إِنَّ اَلْجُهَنِيَّ أَتَى اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ لِي إِبِلاً وَغَنَماً وَ غِلْمَةً وَ عَمَلَةً فَأُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْمُرَنِي بِلَيْلَةٍ أَدْخُلُ فِيهَا فَأَشْهَدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ ذَلِكَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَدَعَاهُ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَسَارَّهُ فِي أُذُنِهِ فَكَانَ اَلْجُهَنِيُّ إِذَا كَانَ لَيْلَةُ ثَلاَثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ دَخَلَ بِإِبِلِهِ وَغَنَمِهِ وَأَهْلِهِ إِلَى مَكَانِهِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), saying: “Indeed, al-Juhani came to the Prophet (saws), and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), indeed I have camels, sheep, young servants, and workers, so I would like you to command me with a night in which I may enter and witness (attend) the prayer’, and that was in the month of Ramadan. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), Allah’s (swt) blessings be upon him and his family, called him and whispered secretly into his ear. So al-Juhani, when it was the night of twenty-three (of the month of Ramadan), would enter with his camels, his sheep, and his family to his place (to attend to prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 412

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Night of Qadr is in every year, and its day is like its night.”
arabicText: اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ:» لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ وَ يَوْمُهَا مِثْلُ لَيْلَتِهَا«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Night of Qadr is in every year, and its day is like its night.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad ibn Isa, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
He (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘two men, one of whom stood praying until morning, while the other was sitting supplicating; which of them is better?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Supplication is better.”
arabicText: حَمَّادُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ قَامَ أَحَدُهُمَا يُصَلِّي حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ وَ اَلْآخَرُ جَالِسٌ يَدْعُو أَيُّهُمَا أَفْضَلُ قَالَ» اَلدُّعَاءُ أَفْضَلُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad ibn Isa, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: He (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘two men, one of whom stood praying until morning, while the other was sitting supplicating; which of them is better?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Supplication is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from Dawud and Ali, his two brothers, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Burayd, who said:
I (narrator) saw Imam (a.s) perform ghusl on the night of the twenty-third (of the month of the Ramadan) twice; once at the beginning of the night and once at the end of the night.
arabicText: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ دَاوُدَ وَ عَلِيٍّ أَخَوَيْهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ بُرَيْدٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُهُ اِغْتَسَلَ فِي لَيْلَةِ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مَرَّتَيْنِ مَرَّةً مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ وَ مَرَّةً مِنْ آخِرِ اَللَّيْلِ.
thaqalaynSanad: Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from Dawud and Ali, his two brothers, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Burayd, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) saw Imam (a.s) perform ghusl on the night of the twenty-third (of the month of the Ramadan) twice; once at the beginning of the night and once at the end of the night.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Asim ibn Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam (a.s) used to give sugar in charity. So it was said to Imam (a.s): “You give sugar in charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing more beloved to me than it, so I love to give in charity the most beloved of things to me.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَاصِمِ بْنِ يُونُسَ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: كَانَ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِالسُّكَّرِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ تَتَصَدَّقُ بِالسُّكَّرِ فَقَالَ» لَيْسَ شَيْ ءٌأَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِنْهُ فَأَنَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَتَصَدَّقَ بِأَحَبِّ اَلْأَشْيَاءِ إِلَيَّ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Asim ibn Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) used to give sugar in charity. So it was said to Imam (a.s): “You give sugar in charity?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing more beloved to me than it, so I love to give in charity the most beloved of things to me.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a newborn who was born on the night of Eid al-Fitr, Is there fitrah upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, he has already exited the month.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ مَوْلُودٍ وُلِدَ لَيْلَةَ اَلْفِطْرِ أَ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةٌ قَالَ» لاَ قَدْ خَرَجَ عَنِ اَلشَّهْرِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a newborn who was born on the night of Eid al-Fitr, Is there fitrah upon him?’ Imam (a.s) said: “No, he has already exited the month.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in a man giving on behalf of his dependents while they are absent from him, or ordering them so they give on his behalf while he is absent from them,” meaning al-fitrah.
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُعْطِيَ اَلرَّجُلُ عَنْ عِيَالِهِ وَ هُمْ غُيَّبٌ عَنْهُ أَوْ يَأْمُرُهُمْ فَيُعْطُونَ عَنْهُ وَ هُوَ غَائِبٌ عَنْهُمْ« يَعْنِي اَلْفِطْرَةَ.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in a man giving on behalf of his dependents while they are absent from him, or ordering them so they give on his behalf while he is absent from them,” meaning al-fitrah.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 413

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “A man pays the zakat al-fitrah on behalf of his mukatab (slave who has entered into a contractual agreement), the slaves of his wife, his Christian slave, his Magian slave, and whoever his door has closed upon (inside his house).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» يُؤَدِّي اَلرَّجُلُ زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ وَ رَقِيقِ اِمْرَأَتِهِ وَعَبْدِهِ اَلنَّصْرَانِيِّ وَاَلْمَجُوسِيِّ وَ مَا أَغْلَقَ عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “A man pays the zakat al-fitrah on behalf of his mukatab (slave who has entered into a contractual agreement), the slaves of his wife, his Christian slave, his Magian slave, and whoever his door has closed upon (inside his house).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 414

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a mukatab (slave who has entered into a contractual agreement), Is the fitrah of the month of Ramadan upon him or upon the one who entered into a mukatabah with him? And is his testimony permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “The fitrah is upon him, and his testimony is not permissible.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ مُكَاتَبٍ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ فِطْرَةُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَوْ عَلَى مَنْ كَاتَبَهُ وَ هَلْ تَجُوزُ شَهَادَتُهُ قَالَ» اَلْفِطْرَةُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لاَ تَجُوزُ شَهَادَتُهُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a mukatab (slave who has entered into a contractual agreement), Is the fitrah of the month of Ramadan upon him or upon the one who entered into a mukatabah with him? And is his testimony permissible?’ Imam (a.s) said: “The fitrah is upon him, and his testimony is not permissible.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 414

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has a guest with him from among his brothers, and the day of al-Fitrah arrives. Does he pay the fitrah on his behalf?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The fitrah is obligatory upon everyone whom he supports, male or female, free or owned, young or old.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May he give the fitrah as flour in place of wheat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm. The cost of its grinding is according to the amount between the wheat and the flour.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May a man give the fitrah as dirhams, the price of dates and wheat, when that would be more beneficial for the household of the believer?’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ اَلضَّيْفُ مِنْ إِخْوَانِهِ فَيَحْضُرُ يَوْمُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ أَ يُؤَدِّي عَنْهُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ قَالَ» نَعَمْ اَلْفِطْرَةُ وَاجِبَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مَنْ يَعُولُ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى حُرٍّ أَوْ مَمْلُوكٍ صَغِيرٍ أَوْ كَبِيرٍ« قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ أَ يُعْطِي اَلْفِطْرَةَ دَقِيقاً مَكَانَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ يَكُونُ أَجْرُ طَحْنِهِ بِقَدْرِ مَا بَيْنَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ وَاَلدَّقِيقِ« قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ أَ يُعْطِي اَلرَّجُلُ اَلْفِطْرَةَ دَرَاهِمَ ثَمَنَ اَلتَّمْرِ وَ اَلْحِنْطَةِ يَكُونُ أَنْفَعَ لِأَهْلِ بَيْتِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِ قَالَ» لاَ بَأْسَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who has a guest with him from among his brothers, and the day of al-Fitrah arrives. Does he pay the fitrah on his behalf?’ Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. The fitrah is obligatory upon everyone whom he supports, male or female, free or owned, young or old.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May he give the fitrah as flour in place of wheat?’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm. The cost of its grinding is according to the amount between the wheat and the flour.” He (narrator) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May a man give the fitrah as dirhams, the price of dates and wheat, when that would be more beneficial for the household of the believer?’” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 414

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from Rifaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The beginning of the year is the Night of Qadr (Laylat al-Qadr); in it is written what will occur from the year to the year.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» رَأْسُ اَلسَّنَةِ لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ يُكْتَبُ فِيهَا مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ اَلسَّنَةِ إِلَى اَلسَّنَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from Rifaah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The beginning of the year is the Night of Qadr (Laylat al-Qadr); in it is written what will occur from the year to the year.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 414

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then forgets all of that until the month of Ramadan ends.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer and the fast.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَيَنْسَى ذَلِكَ جَمِيعَهُ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ» يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ اَلصَّوْمَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about ‘a man who becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then forgets all of that until the month of Ramadan ends.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer and the fast.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 415

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Qa’im (ajf), peace be upon him, will rise on Saturday, the day of Ashura, the day on which Imam al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, was killed. And the Qa’im (ajf) will cut off the hands of the Banu Shaybah and hang them in the Kabah.” – meaning a historic Arab clan and the hereditary guardians of the keys to the Holy Ka'bah.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:» يَخْرُجُ اَلْقَائِمُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْمَ اَلسَّبْتِ يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ اَلْيَوْمَ اَلَّذِي قُتِلَ فِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ يَقْطَعُ أَيْدِيَ بَنِي شَيْبَةَ وَيُعَلِّقُهَا فِي اَلْكَعْبَةِ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Qa’im (ajf), peace be upon him, will rise on Saturday, the day of Ashura, the day on which Imam al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him, was killed. And the Qa’im (ajf) will cut off the hands of the Banu Shaybah and hang them in the Kabah.” – meaning a historic Arab clan and the hereditary guardians of the keys to the Holy Ka'bah.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 415

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Yunus ibn Hisham, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would often spit on the day of Ashura into the mouths of nursing children from the descendants of Sayyidah Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, from his saliva. And the Prophet (saws) would say, ‘Do not feed them anything until the night.’ And they would be quenched by the saliva of the blessed Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the wild animals used to fast on the day of Ashura during the time of Dawud (a.s), peace be upon him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ هِشَامٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ كَثِيراً مَا يَتْفُلُ يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ فِي أَفْوَاهِ أَطْفَالِ اَلْمَرَاضِعِ مِنْ وُلْدِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ مِنْ رِيقِهِ وَ يَقُولُ» لاَ تُطْعِمُوهُمْ شَيْئاً إِلَى اَللَّيْلِ« وَ كَانُوا يَرْوَوْنَ مِنْ رِيقِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ «قَالَ» وَ كَانَتِ اَلْوَحْشُ تَصُومُ يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ عَلَى عَهْدِ دَاوُدَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Yunus ibn Hisham, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, would often spit on the day of Ashura into the mouths of nursing children from the descendants of Sayyidah Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her, from his saliva. And the Prophet (saws) would say, ‘Do not feed them anything until the night.’ And they would be quenched by the saliva of the blessed Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.” Imam (a.s) said: “And the wild animals used to fast on the day of Ashura during the time of Dawud (a.s), peace be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 415

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “When the month of Ramadan is safe (is observed), the year is safe.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The beginning of the year is the month of Ramadan.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا سَلِمَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ سَلِمَتِ اَلسَّنَةُ« وَ قَالَ» رَأْسُ اَلسَّنَةِ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “When the month of Ramadan is safe (is observed), the year is safe.” And Imam (a.s) said: “The beginning of the year is the month of Ramadan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 416

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Kindi al-Raqqi, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam (a.s) said: “Look for the old crescent in the east in the morning. If it is not seen, then the crescent here is a new crescent, regardless of whether people later see it or do not see it.”
arabicText: اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكِنْدِيِّ اَلرَّقِّيِّ عَنْ دَاوُدَ اَلرَّقِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:» إِذَا طُلِبَ اَلْهِلاَلُ فِي اَلْمَشْرِقِ غُدْوَةً فَلَمْ يُرَ فَهُوَ هَا هُنَا هِلاَلٌ جَدِيدٌ رُئِيَ أَوْ لَمْ يُرَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Kindi al-Raqqi, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Look for the old crescent in the east in the morning. If it is not seen, then the crescent here is a new crescent, regardless of whether people later see it or do not see it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 416

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said:
Abbad ibn Maymun asked (Abdullah ibn Jundab), while I (narrator) was present, about ‘a man who had imposed upon himself a vow (nadhr) of fasting and wanted to go out for the Hajj.’ So Abdullah ibn Jundab said: “I heard from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he (Zurarah) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who had imposed upon himself a vow of fasting, then he formed an intention to visit Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He goes out and does not fast it on the road, then when he returns, he makes that up.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ اَلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ جُنْدَبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ عَبَّادُ بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ عَنْ رَجُلٍ جَعَلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ نَذْرَ صَوْمٍ وَ أَرَادَ اَلْخُرُوجَ فِي اَلْحَجِّ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ جُنْدَبٍ سَمِعْتُ مِنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ جَعَلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ نَذْرَ صَوْمٍ فَحَضَرَتْهُ نِيَّةٌ فِي زِيَارَةِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ» يَخْرُجُ وَ لاَ يَصُومُهُ فِي اَلطَّرِيقِ فَإِذَا رَجَعَ قَضَى ذَلِكَ«.
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abbad ibn Maymun asked (Abdullah ibn Jundab), while I (narrator) was present, about ‘a man who had imposed upon himself a vow (nadhr) of fasting and wanted to go out for the Hajj.’ So Abdullah ibn Jundab said: “I heard from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, that he (Zurarah) asked Imam (a.s) about ‘a man who had imposed upon himself a vow of fasting, then he formed an intention to visit Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.’ Imam (a.s) said: “He goes out and does not fast it on the road, then when he returns, he makes that up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 417

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Does the executor pay zakat al-fitrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “There is no zakat upon an orphan.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ اَلْوَصِيُّ يُزَكِّي زَكَاةَ اَلْفِطْرَةِ عَنِ اَلْيَتَامَى إِذَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مَالٌ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» لاَ زَكَاةَ عَلَى يَتِيمٍ«.
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (narrator) wrote to Imam (a.s): “Does the executor pay zakat al-fitrah on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote: “There is no zakat upon an orphan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 4, p. 418

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ammar al-Sabati said:
I (narrator) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “How much does a man give?” Imam (a.s) said: “Every town according to their measure (mikyal): half of a quarter for every head.”

chapter: Chapter on Additions
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, through my father: “May I be made your ransom, our companions have differed concerning the sa’. Some of them say that the fitrah is by the Madinese sa’, and some of them say by the Iraqi sa’.” So the Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, wrote to me: “The sa’ is six rotls (artal) by the Madinese measure and nine rotls by the Iraqi measure.” He said: “And by weight it is one thousand, one hundred and seventy weights (waznah).”
arabicText: محمد بن أحمد عن جعفر بن محمد الهمداني قال: كتبت إلى ابي الحسن عليه السلام على يد ابي جعلت فداك ان أصحابنا اختلفوا في الصاع بعضهم يقول الفطرة بصاع المدنى وبعضهم يقول بصاع العراقى فكتب عليه السلام الي: الصاع ستة ارطال بالمدني وتسعة ارطال بالعراقى، قال: ويكون بالوزن الفا ومائة وسبعين وزنة
